# Every finding, as the run produced it

> Part of the [Vulkan backend review](README.md). 2026-08-21, against the tree
> at `4d91b91`. **Not updated as findings are fixed.**

The [README](README.md) is the review: merged, ranked, argued, and checked
against a run of the suite. This file is the material underneath it — every
finding that survived refutation in the words triage merged it into, with its
refuters' reasoning printed beneath it and an adjudicator's where the two
disagreed; then the ones that did not survive, with the reasoning that killed
them; and last the sixty-five nobody ever checked.

Where the README merges several of these into one section, each appears here
separately — seven agents reaching the same branch by seven routes is the
strongest signal a run of this shape can produce, and collapsing it in both
documents would hide it.

Severities are the verified ones where a refuter corrected them. The word in
backticks after the severity is the triage area the finding was ranked in —
`core`, `seam`, `tests`, `docs`, `build`, or `probe` for a gap probe — and
`raised by` names the raw candidate findings, `R1`…`R167` and `P1`…`P9`, that
triage merged into the entry.

---

## Confirmed — survived two adversarial refuters

34 findings. Both refuters were told to default to *refuted*; where they disagreed an adjudicator read the code and decided.

### C1. create_swapchain's zero-extent early return leaves the stale swapchain installed, so present()'s two minimised guards are dead code and end_frame throws on every frame while the window is minimised

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059`** · must-fix · `core` · raised by R2, R17, R51, R163 · run id `V1`

FOUR LENSES (timeline-sync, swapchain, errors, degenerate) landed on this same line independently, which is the strongest signal in the run. create_swapchain()'s only early return does not touch swapchain_: lines 1059-1067 read `if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u) { // A minimised window. There is nothing to present into and there // will be again; present() answers this by doing nothing rather // than by refusing, because a shell that keeps drawing while // minimised is the ordinary case and not a mistake. this->swapchain_extent_ = extent; return; }`. The return sits ABOVE `VkSwapchainKHR previous = this->swapchain_;` (1110) and above `this->destroy_swapchain();` (1140), and destroy_swapchain() (1195-1210) is the only place that assigns VK_NULL_HANDLE to swapchain_. So after the first successful create_swapchain, a zero extent can never produce the state present() tests for at 1495 (`if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)  // Minimised, or a swapchain that could not be made at this size.`) or at 1523 after rebuild_swapchain(). RULE BROKEN: docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard, which CLAUDE.md names as live - a comment in engine/render/ that the code no longer matches is a defect - and here the false comment is the load-bearing statement of the error path. Also T6 (PHILOSOPHY.md:106-119): renderer.h documents no throw from end_frame, and device_resources.h:320-326 already names a window procedure as the place where a throw does more damage than the failure it reports. FAILURE (verified against the shell in this tree): minimise any client. engine/app/window.cpp:379-397 turns WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED into on_suspending and forwards no size; Window::pump_until_quit (window.cpp:234-248) calls notify_->tick() on every idle iteration; Application::tick (application.cpp:254-258) is `this->timer_.Tick(...); this->render();` with no suspend gate, and Application::render (application.cpp:280-300) runs begin_frame/submit/end_frame unconditionally. The surface's currentExtent is now {0,0}, so vkAcquireNextImageKHR at 1509 returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR; present() calls rebuild_swapchain() (1522) -> create_swapchain(), which returns at 1066 with the SAME stale swapchain installed and swapchain_extent_ = {0,0}; the guard at 1523 is false; the retry acquire at 1530 hits the same stale swapchain and returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again; check_vk at 1542 throws std::runtime_error("No swapchain image could be acquired (VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR).") out of Renderer::end_frame, through Application::render and pump_until_quit, with no handler anywhere - minimising the window kills the process. FIX: call this->destroy_swapchain() immediately before the early return at 1066 (both callers of create_swapchain have already run vkDeviceWaitIdle, at 1182 and 1234, so it is safe), which makes swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE really mean 'nothing to present into' and gives both guards the behaviour their comments claim. That fix requires the separately-ranked 'no way back from a null swapchain' finding to be fixed with it.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

Every quote checks out character for character and every link in the chain holds.

device_resources.cpp:1059-1067 is exactly as quoted, comment included. The return sits above `VkSwapchainKHR previous = this->swapchain_;` (1110) and above `this->destroy_swapchain();` (1140). A grep of every `swapchain_` reference confirms only two assignments exist: 1143 (`= fresh`) and 1208 (`= VK_NULL_HANDLE`, inside destroy_swapchain, 1186-1210). destroy_swapchain's other call sites are teardown (388) and handle_device_lost (1283) — neither on the minimise path. So the early return provably leaves the prior swapchain installed while setting swapchain_extent_ = {0,0}, and create_swapchain has no other early exit (1023-1067 read in full: only the surface-capabilities check at 1032-1039, which throws).

present() at 1493-1543 matches: guard at 1495-1504, acquire at 1509, OUT_OF_DATE branch at 1513, rebuild_swapchain at 1522, guard at 1523-1528, retry acquire at 1530, check_vk at 1542. check_vk (212-221) is `if (result == VK_SUCCESS) return; throw std::runtime_error(std::string(what) + " (" + vk_result_name(result) + ").");` and 206 maps VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR to its name, so the thrown text is exactly the string the finding gives.

Reachability from a real entry point: window.cpp WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED calls on_suspending() and forwards no size (confirmed, and docs/review/backend-equivalence/README.md:97 independently confirms restore-from-minimise forwards none either); pump_until_quit (234-248) calls notify_->tick() every idle iteration; Application::tick (254-258) is `this->timer_.Tick(...); this->render();`; Application::render (280-300) has only a frame-count-zero guard, no suspend gate; Renderer::end_frame (vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867) calls device_resources.present() directly. The only handlers anywhere are samples/minimal/main.cpp:48 and samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49 — catch, MessageBox, return 1. The process dies.

Determinism of the second acquire: an out-of-date swapchain stays out of date by spec, so the retry at 1530 on the same unchanged handle cannot succeed — the throw is not a race. The present-side route at 1634-1641 also calls rebuild_swapchain() into the same early return, so the next frame's acquire throws instead; both routes converge.

Rules invoked are real: PHILOSOPHY.md:106-119 T6 says "Not a licence for: throwing on the way out ... nor for treating expected absence as failure ... Loud is for broken contracts, not for the world being the world". device_resources.h:320-326 names the resize path reached from a window procedure as the place where a throw does more damage. d3d12/device_resources.cpp:468-490 presents with Present(1,0) + ThrowIfFailed, which a minimised window returns a success code from, so the other backends genuinely survive what this one dies on.

The suggested fix's premise also checks out: rebuild_swapchain runs vkDeviceWaitIdle at 1182 and create_window_size_dependent_resources at ~1234, both before create_swapchain.

*Correction:* Two imprecisions survive, neither refuting.

(1) The headline "present()'s two minimised guards are dead code" overstates by one word. The guard at 1495 is live before the first successful create_swapchain — a client shown minimised, or any pre-creation state. Only 1523 is genuinely unreachable. The finding's body scopes this correctly ("after the first successful create_swapchain"), so this is headline wording only. Strengthening the finding: the 1497 comment is wrong in a second way it does not claim — "a swapchain that could not be made at this size" also cannot leave swapchain_ null, because 1140 destroys and 1141's check_vk(created, ...) throws instead.

(2) The failure chain requires the Win32 WSI to report VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR while the client rect is 0x0, which the finding asserts without flagging as a driver-observable. It is the canonical behaviour (it is why the standard recreate-swapchain loop must wait for a non-zero extent), it is reached from both the acquire (1513) and the present (1634) side, and once it arrives the throw is deterministic. But on an implementation that keeps returning VK_SUCCESS while minimised, create_swapchain is never entered at all — minimise forwards no size — and nothing throws; the defect then degrades to the comment at 1061-1064 describing a state the code never enters, plus a stale swapchain_extent_ = {0,0} that sends the compare at 1568 down the blit branch with dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1}, a zero-extent blit region. Either way the early return leaves the object inconsistent, so the fix is the same and the severity is unchanged.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried four refutation routes and all closed.

(1) Does the early return really leave the swapchain installed? Yes. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067 is `if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u) { ...comment...; this->swapchain_extent_ = extent; return; }` and touches nothing else. It returns above `VkSwapchainKHR previous = this->swapchain_;` (1110) and above `this->destroy_swapchain();` (1140). destroy_swapchain's body at 1205-1209 (`if (this->swapchain_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE) { vkDestroySwapchainKHR(...); this->swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE; }`) is the only assignment of VK_NULL_HANDLE to swapchain_ in the file; grep for destroy_swapchain gives exactly three call sites — 388 (destructor), 1140 (successful-create path), 1283 (handle_device_lost). So after one successful creation, no zero-extent path can null it. The guards at 1495 (`if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)` / "// Minimised, or a swapchain that could not be made at this size.") and 1523 (same test after rebuild_swapchain at 1522) are therefore unreachable for a minimise, and the comment at 1061-1064 ("present() answers this by doing nothing rather than by refusing") describes behaviour the code does not have. Structural, confirmed, needs no driver knowledge.

(2) Can the failure be reached from a caller? Yes. window.cpp:380 `case WM_SIZE:` — 387-397 handle SIZE_MINIMIZED by calling notify_->on_suspending() and forwarding no size; on_window_size_changed at 410 is in the `else if (self && !self->in_sizemove_)` branch only, and the restore path (402-407) also forwards no size. Application::on_suspending (application.cpp:352-364) suspends the gamepad reader, drops input focus and suspends audio — it gates no rendering. Window::pump_until_quit (window.cpp:234-248) calls notify_->tick() on every idle iteration; Application::tick (254-258) is `timer_.Tick(...); this->render();`; Application::render (280-300) runs begin_frame/submit/end_frame with only a frame-count-zero guard. Renderer::end_frame (renderer.cpp:856-866) calls device_resources.present() unconditionally. check_vk (device_resources.cpp:212-221) throws std::runtime_error for anything but VK_SUCCESS, and the guard at 1540 (`acquired != VK_SUCCESS && acquired != VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR`) lets VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR through to check_vk at 1542. The quoted message is exact: what + " (" + vk_result_name + ")." with VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR spelled at 206.

(3) Is the Vulkan rule real? The finding needs only that a Win32 implementation is permitted to return VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR from vkAcquireNextImageKHR (1509/1530) or vkQueuePresentKHR (1626) once the window is minimised. It is: VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR is defined as the surface having changed so it is no longer compatible with the swapchain, and on Win32 VkSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR::currentExtent is the client rect with minImageExtent == maxImageExtent == currentExtent, so a swapchain at the pre-minimise size is by definition incompatible once the client rect is 0x0. That is also why the guard at 1059 exists at all — VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR::imageExtent must be non-zero. This is the one link not verifiable from source (an implementation may instead return VK_SUCCESS or VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR), so the crash is driver-dependent in principle and usual in practice. The SUBOPTIMAL alternative is not clean either: present's rebuild at 1641 leaves swapchain_extent_ = {0,0} while colour_extent_ is clamped to >= 1 at 914/919, so the next frame fails the equality test at 1568-1569 and takes vkCmdBlitImage at 1590-1595 with dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1} — a degenerate destination region and a frozen image.

(4) Do the other backends have the same shape? No. d3d12/device_resources.cpp:472-487 presents and calls ThrowIfFailed(hr); DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED is a success HRESULT so FAILED() is false and nothing throws, and d3d11 presents the same way at 396. The D3D backends survive minimise; this shape is unique to vulkan/.

Rules invoked check out. T6 at docs/design/PHILOSOPHY.md:106-119 reads "Not a licence for: throwing on the way out ... nor for treating expected absence as failure ... Loud is for broken contracts, not for the world being the world" — a minimised window is expected absence, so T6 argues against the throw rather than merely being name-dropped. device_resources.h:320-326 does name the window-procedure-throw hazard in this same file ("THE SAME WAIT, FOR THE PLACES WHERE THROWING DOES MORE DAMAGE THAN THE FAILURE IT REPORTS"). CLAUDE.md does describe backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md as a live list of comments in engine/render/ that the code no longer matches, so a false load-bearing comment is a tracked defect class here.

The proposed fix's safety premise also checks out: rebuild_swapchain runs vkDeviceWaitIdle at 1182 before create_swapchain at 1183, and create_window_size_dependent_resources runs it at 1234 before create_swapchain at 1240.

*Correction:* Three refinements, none of which touch the conclusion.

1. "end_frame throws on every frame while the window is minimised" overstates the count. There is no handler anywhere on the path, so the first throwing frame ends the process — it throws once, fatally, not repeatedly.

2. The finding presents acquire-reports-first as the only order. There are two, and both end the same way. vkQueuePresentKHR at 1626 may be what first reports VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR; 1636-1642 answers that by calling rebuild_swapchain(), which is equally ineffective at zero extent, so the throw lands on the next frame's retry acquire instead of this one's. Either entry reaches check_vk at 1542.

3. The failure is driver-conditional, which the finding does not say. An implementation may return VK_SUCCESS or VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR on a minimised Win32 surface instead of VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR; VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR is explicitly let past at 1540, so on such a driver the outcome is not a crash but the degenerate blit at 1590-1595 (dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1}, since colour_extent_ is clamped to >= 1 at 914-919 while swapchain_extent_ was set to {0,0} at 1065). Severity stays must-fix: returning OUT_OF_DATE is permitted by the specification and is the ordinary Windows behaviour, the action that triggers it is a user minimising a window, and the state that is provably wrong regardless of driver — two guards that cannot fire and a comment stating the error path they do not implement — is the load-bearing statement of this backend's minimise handling.

### C2. create_swapchain's minimised early return leaves the stale swapchain in place, so present()'s "minimised, do nothing" guard is dead and end_frame throws out of the message loop

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059`** · must-fix · `seam` · raised by R75 · run id `V43`

CLAIM: The minimised branch of create_swapchain returns BEFORE the destroy_swapchain() further down, so swapchain_ keeps its old, now-out-of-date handle. present()'s minimised guard tests `swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE`, which after a minimise of a running window can never be true - so the guard the comment names as the answer to minimisation is unreachable, and the acquire retry falls through to a throw.

EVIDENCE, verbatim:

engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1066:

```
    if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u)
    {
        // A minimised window. There is nothing to present into and there
        // will be again; present() answers this by doing nothing rather
        // than by refusing, because a shell that keeps drawing while
        // minimised is the ordinary case and not a mistake.
        this->swapchain_extent_ = extent;
        return;
    }
```

The only destroy_swapchain() in this function is at :1142, below that return; destroy_swapchain (:1186-1209) is the only place swapchain_ is set to VK_NULL_HANDLE.

engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1493-1543, present():

```
    if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE) { ... this->execute(); frame_index_ = ...; return; }
    ...
    if (acquired == VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR)
    {
        this->rebuild_swapchain();
        if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE) { this->execute(); ...; return; }
        acquired = vkAcquireNextImageKHR(this->owner_->device,
            this->swapchain_, UINT64_MAX, this->frame().acquired, ...);
    }
    ...
    if (acquired != VK_SUCCESS && acquired != VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR)
    { check_vk(acquired, "No swapchain image could be acquired"); }
```


RULE BROKEN: docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md makes a comment the code does not match a defect in its own right, and renderer.h:545-557 states the uniformity term - "a caller must not be able to tell which backend it has", with gl/renderer.cpp and null/renderer.cpp cited as backends that pay a price to keep it. D3D11 and D3D12 survive a minimise: engine/app/window.cpp:387-412 swallows the SIZE_MINIMIZED WM_SIZE (verified - it takes the on_suspending branch and never reaches on_window_size_changed), so their swap chains are never resized, and IDXGISwapChain::Present returns DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED, a SUCCEEDED HRESULT.

FAILURE SCENARIO: Run MinimalSample or LineSweeperSample on x64-debug-vulkan and minimise the window. Verified in the tree: Application::on_suspending (application.cpp:352-358) only suspends the gamepad reader, and Application::render (application.cpp) has no minimised gate - it calls begin_frame / submit / end_frame unconditionally after the first update. So the shell keeps drawing, which is exactly the client :1063 describes. end_frame -> present(): swapchain_ is the live pre-minimise swapchain, so :1495 is false; vkAcquireNextImageKHR returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR because the Win32 surface now reports currentExtent {0,0}; rebuild_swapchain() -> create_swapchain() takes the :1059 branch and returns with swapchain_ UNCHANGED; :1523 is false; the retry acquires from the same out-of-date swapchain and returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again; :1542 throws std::runtime_error("No swapchain image could be acquired") out of Renderer::end_frame, out of Application::render, out of the pump. The same early return also writes swapchain_extent_ = {0,0} while swapchain_ still names a swapchain of the old extent, so present()'s copy-vs-blit test at :1567 reads a member that no longer describes the object it is used with.

FIX: Make the minimised branch reach the state present() tests for - call destroy_swapchain() before returning at :1066. It already sets swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE, clears swapchain_images_ and the presentable_ semaphores, so both :1495 and :1523 become true and the frame is submitted without a present, as the comment says. It is safe there: rebuild_swapchain() has just run vkDeviceWaitIdle (:1182) and create_window_size_dependent_resources runs one at :1234.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I attacked this on five fronts and it survived all of them.

EVIDENCE IS VERBATIM. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067 is exactly as quoted: the minimised branch sets `this->swapchain_extent_ = extent;` (:1065) and `return;` (:1066), touching nothing else. The only `destroy_swapchain()` inside create_swapchain is at :1140, thirty lines below that return (grep for destroy_swapchain in the file gives :388, :1140, :1186 the definition, :1283 in handle_device_lost - nowhere else). destroy_swapchain (:1186-1210) is the only writer of `swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE` (:1208). present() at :1493-1543 is as quoted, including the guard `if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)` at :1495, the post-rebuild retest at :1523, the retry acquire at :1530-1532 against `this->swapchain_`, and the throw path `check_vk(acquired, "No swapchain image could be acquired")` at :1542. check_vk (:212-221) throws std::runtime_error on anything that is not VK_SUCCESS. So the retry, if it returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again, throws - there is no third chance.

THE STATE MODEL CONTRADICTS ITSELF, INDEPENDENT OF ANY DRIVER. :1061-1064 says the minimised case is answered "by present() doing nothing"; :1497 says the swapchain_==NULL guard is what "minimised" looks like. Those two comments describe a state the code never constructs on the running-window path, because the early return is the one exit from create_swapchain that leaves swapchain_ alone. That alone is a comment the code does not match, which docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md treats as a defect in its own right.

THE PATH IS REACHABLE FROM A REAL ENTRY POINT. I followed every link. engine/app/window.cpp:387-397: `w_param == SIZE_MINIMIZED` sets minimized_/in_suspend_ and calls on_suspending() only - on_window_size_changed is in the third branch (:408-412) and is never reached, so no backend hears about a minimise. Application::on_suspending (application.cpp:352-364) suspends the gamepad reader, drops input focus and suspends audio; it does not gate rendering. Window::pump_until_quit (window.cpp:234-250) calls notify_->tick() on every empty PeekMessage, and tick() (application.cpp:254-258) calls render() unconditionally. Application::render (:280-300) has one gate, `GetFrameCount() == 0`, and then calls begin_frame/submit/end_frame. Renderer::end_frame (vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867) calls device_resources.present() with no try/catch. So a minimised sample keeps entering present() with the pre-minimise swapchain live - exactly the client :1063 calls "the ordinary case".

I COULD NOT FIND A MISSING LINK. The only escape would be an implementation that never reports out-of-date while minimised - but a Win32 surface reports currentExtent {0,0} when minimised (which is precisely why :1059 exists, since VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR forbids a zero imageExtent), and the file's own header states the premise at device_resources.h:50-52. If that escape held, the :1059 branch and the :1495 guard would both be unreachable dead code, which is not a defence of the code.

Nor is the damage confined to the throw: once create_swapchain has taken the early return, `swapchain_extent_` is {0,0} (:1065) while `swapchain_` still names images of the old size, and the copy-vs-blit test at :1568-1569 compares those two members. The blit branch then builds dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1} at :1589-1591. That half is deterministic the moment the branch runs, with no second acquire needed.

THE FIX AS STATED IS SOUND. vkDeviceWaitIdle sits at :1182 in rebuild_swapchain immediately before create_swapchain, and at :1234 in create_window_size_dependent_resources - the two callers - so destroy_swapchain() at :1066 would run behind a full device wait in both. destroy_swapchain clears presentable_ (:1195-1202), swapchain_images_ (:1203) and swapchain_ (:1205-1209), which is exactly the state :1495 and :1523 test for.

*Correction:* Three refinements, none of which rescue the code:

1. "Throws out of the message loop" understates where it stops. It unwinds out of present() -> Renderer::end_frame -> Application::render -> tick() -> Window::pump_until_quit -> Application::run, and is caught by the sample's own top-level handler - samples/minimal/main.cpp:48-56 and samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49 - which prints to stderr, shows a MessageBoxA titled "Sample - startup failure" and returns 1. So the observable symptom is not an unhandled-exception crash dialog but the game dying on minimise with a startup-failure box, which is arguably worse to diagnose.

2. The guard at :1495 is not dead in the absolute sense, only on the path the finding describes. swapchain_ is VK_NULL_HANDLE before the first create_swapchain, and again after handle_device_lost's destroy_swapchain (:1283), so a device created or lost while the window is already minimised does reach it. The finding's own wording ("after a minimise of a running window can never be true") is the accurate form and is correct.

3. The mechanism is broader than the finding states, in the finding's favour. present() has a second door into rebuild_swapchain: :1634-1642 calls it when vkQueuePresentKHR returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR or VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR. On a minimise that fires first, reaching the same corrupted state (stale swapchain_ plus swapchain_extent_ {0,0}) one frame before any acquire fails, so the throw lands on the following frame rather than the current one. Both doors lead to the same :1059 early return.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

CONFIRMED at HEAD; every link in the chain reads as the finding says.

1. The early return is real and leaves the handle live. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1058-1066 is `if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u) { ...comment...; this->swapchain_extent_ = extent; return; }`. The only `destroy_swapchain()` inside `create_swapchain` is at :1142 ("The old one is retired whether or not the new one was made"), below that return. A grep of every `swapchain_` reference in the file gives assignments at :1143 (`swapchain_ = fresh`) and :1208 (`swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE`, inside destroy_swapchain :1186-1209) and nowhere else — so destroy_swapchain is indeed the only writer of the null handle, and the minimised path never reaches it. `rebuild_swapchain` (:1171-1184) is just vkDeviceWaitIdle + create_swapchain, so it cannot null it either.

2. The guards present() tests are therefore unreachable via minimisation. :1495 `if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)` and :1523 (the identical test after rebuild_swapchain at :1522) both stay false, so the "Minimised, or a swapchain that could not be made at this size" comment at :1497-1500 and the "present() answers this by doing nothing rather than by refusing" comment at :1061-1064 both name a path the code cannot take. That alone is the DRIFT.md class of defect (docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md preamble: "The comments in engine/render/ are held to the same standard... Each item is a claim that the code no longer matches").

3. Reachability verified end to end, not assumed. engine/app/window.cpp:387-398: WM_SIZE with w_param == SIZE_MINIMIZED sets minimized_/in_suspend_ and calls on_suspending(); the `else if (self && !self->in_sizemove_)` at :408-412 that calls on_window_size_changed is not reached. Application::on_suspending (engine/app/application.cpp:352-364) suspends the gamepad reader, drops input focus and suspends audio — nothing touches the renderer. Window::pump_until_quit (engine/app/window.cpp:234-250) calls this->notify_->tick() on every idle PeekMessage pass, unconditionally. Application::tick (application.cpp:254-258) always calls render(); Application::render (application.cpp:280-300) gates only on GetFrameCount() == 0 and then calls begin_frame/submit/end_frame. Renderer::end_frame (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867) calls impl.device_resources.present(). So the shell does keep drawing while minimised, which is exactly the client :1063 describes.

4. The Vulkan premise is correct for the objects in question. VK_KHR_win32_surface specifies VkSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR::currentExtent as the window's client area, and minImageExtent/maxImageExtent equal it; a minimised HWND has a 0x0 client rect, so currentExtent is {0,0}. VUID-VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR-imageExtent-01689 requires imageExtent.width and .height to be non-zero, so declining to create a swapchain there is the right call — the defect is purely that the function returns without putting the object into the state present() was written to test. VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR is a documented return of vkAcquireNextImageKHR ("A surface has changed in such a way that it is no longer compatible with the swapchain... applications must query the new surface properties and recreate their swapchain"), and a minimise on Win32 is the canonical producer of it — it is the reason the standard minimisation wait loop exists in every Vulkan sample. So :1513 fires, rebuild_swapchain no-ops, and :1530's retry runs against the same out-of-date object.

5. The backend comparison does not excuse it — it indicts it. engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.cpp:396 and engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:472 both call Present(1, 0); a minimised DXGI swap chain returns DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED, 0x087A0001, severity bit clear, so SUCCEEDED is true and the ThrowIfFailed at d3d11:416 / d3d12:487 passes. Their swap chains are never resized because window.cpp swallows the minimise. GL's SwapBuffers on a 0x0 window is benign and null has no window at all. Four of five backends survive a minimise and the fifth does not, which is precisely the term engine/render/renderer.h:550-557 states: "A seam whose caller contract changed per backend is the thing this file exists to prevent... gl/renderer.cpp and null/renderer.cpp both drop a frame on a resize that destroys nothing of theirs, because a caller must not be able to tell which backend it has."

6. The stale-extent half is real too. colour_extent_ is only reset by destroy_colour_target (:1020-1021), which runs from create_window_size_dependent_resources (:1212-1240) — never called on a minimise. So after the early return, swapchain_extent_ is {0,0} while colour_extent_ is still the pre-minimise size and swapchain_ still names a swapchain of that old extent; the copy-vs-blit test at :1568-1569 then takes the blit branch with dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1} (:1589-1591) against a real image of the old size. The member no longer describes the object it is used with, exactly as claimed.

*Correction:* Three things the finding gets slightly wrong; none of them rescue the code.

(a) The throw is the likely outcome, not the guaranteed one, and the finding presents it as the only one. Nothing in the specification obliges the second vkAcquireNextImageKHR at :1530 to return VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again — a driver may hand back VK_SUCCESS or VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR from an out-of-date swapchain whose images still exist. On such a driver there is no throw: present() proceeds to the blit at :1581-1597 with dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1} (a degenerate destination region computed from the {0,0} the early return wrote), vkQueuePresentKHR then returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR, :1634-1642 calls rebuild_swapchain(), which no-ops through the same early return, and the loop repeats every frame. So the defect has two faces — a crash on one driver and a silently degraded present loop on another — and the write of swapchain_extent_ = {0,0} beside a live swapchain of the old extent is the part that is unconditional. The fix is the same either way.

(b) "Throws out of the message loop" is right about the unwind but overstates the end state. It does escape Renderer::end_frame, Application::render, Application::tick and Window::pump_until_quit, but samples/minimal/main.cpp:48 and samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49 both catch const std::exception&, print to stderr, put up a MessageBoxA and return 1. The observable failure is that minimising the window ends the game with "No swapchain image could be acquired" in a message box, not an unhandled terminate. Still must-fix: minimising a window is the most ordinary thing a player does, and it is survivable on the other four backends.

(c) The finding does not mention that restoring the window does not deliberately repair the state either. engine/app/window.cpp:399-407 takes the `else if (self && self->minimized_)` branch on the un-minimise WM_SIZE and calls on_resuming(), so on_window_size_changed is never called on the way back up and create_window_size_dependent_resources never runs. Recovery depends entirely on the presentation engine reporting OUT_OF_DATE once more after the restore, at which point rebuild_swapchain finally sees a non-zero extent. That strengthens the case for the proposed fix rather than weakening it.

---

### C3. create_swapchain's zero-extent branch leaves swapchain_ stale, so minimising a Vulkan window throws out of end_frame()

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059`** · must-fix · `tests` · raised by R121 · run id `V76`

CLAIM: the minimised-window branch of DeviceResources::create_swapchain never produces the state present() is written against, so a minimise on the Vulkan backend ends in std::runtime_error out of Renderer::end_frame rather than in a no-op.

EVIDENCE (verified in the tree). device_resources.cpp:1059-1067:


```
		if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u)
		{
			// A minimised window. There is nothing to present into and there
			// will be again; present() answers this by doing nothing rather
			// than by refusing, because a shell that keeps drawing while
			// minimised is the ordinary case and not a mistake.
			this->swapchain_extent_ = extent;
			return;
		}
```


The branch returns WITHOUT calling destroy_swapchain(), and destroy_swapchain() (:1186-1209) is the only writer of `this->swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE` (:1207). present() is written entirely against that null state: :1495 `if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)` -> execute, advance frame index, return; :1520 on VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR -> `this->rebuild_swapchain();` then :1523 `if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE) { ... return; }`; otherwise :1530 re-acquires against `this->swapchain_`; :1541-1542 `if (acquired != VK_SUCCESS && acquired != VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR) check_vk(acquired, "No swapchain image could be acquired");`. rebuild_swapchain() (:1171-1184) is vkDeviceWaitIdle + create_swapchain() and nothing more, so after a minimise `swapchain_` still holds the pre-minimise handle while `swapchain_extent_` is {0,0}.

RULE BROKEN: docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard, restated in CLAUDE.md — a comment the code does not match is a defect. The comment at :1061-1064 states the behaviour ('present() answers this by doing nothing rather than by refusing') and present()'s two guards implement exactly that behaviour for a state this branch cannot reach once a swapchain exists. It also breaks backend equivalence: d3d11/device_resources.cpp:396 and d3d12/device_resources.cpp:472 both Present a minimised window, get a success HRESULT, and survive.

FAILURE SCENARIO: engine/app keeps rendering while minimised by design — window.cpp:236-247 calls notify_->tick() whenever the queue is empty regardless of minimized_, WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED (window.cpp:387-397) fires only on_suspending(), and Application::on_suspending (application.cpp:352-364) suspends audio and gamepads but not rendering, so Application::render() reaches end_frame() at application.cpp:299 on every tick (both confirmed by reading those files). Build any sample with x64-debug-vulkan and minimise it: the surface now reports currentExtent {0,0}; vkAcquireNextImageKHR returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR; rebuild_swapchain -> create_swapchain takes the branch above and returns with the stale handle; the :1523 guard sees a non-null swapchain, so the second acquire runs against the same stale object, returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again, and :1542 throws std::runtime_error("No swapchain image could be acquired (VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR).") out of Renderer::end_frame, through Application::render, tick and DispatchMessage, to the top-level catch at samples/minimal/main.cpp:48 — a 'startup failure' MessageBox and exit code 1 because the player minimised the game. On a driver where the acquire instead returns VK_SUCCESS or VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR the second consequence bites: swapchain_extent_ is {0,0} while colour_extent_ is not, so present() takes the blit path at :1585-1598 with dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1} — a zero-area blit region into a stale image.

FIX: call `this->destroy_swapchain();` before the `return` in the zero-extent branch, so the state both present() guards are written for is the state that actually occurs. That alone leaves the window black on restore, because WM_SIZE/SIZE_RESTORED after a minimise takes window.cpp:399-406 and delivers no on_window_size_changed — so also make present()'s :1495 guard attempt a rebuild before giving up.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried to kill this on four fronts — the quote, the state machine, the reachability, and the shell — and it survived all four.

THE QUOTE IS EXACT. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067 is character-for-character what the finding quotes, comment included: `if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u) { ... this->swapchain_extent_ = extent; return; }`. The `return` is at :1066; `this->destroy_swapchain();` is at :1140, seventy-four lines below it, unreachable from that branch.

THE STATE MACHINE IS AS CLAIMED. `grep -n "swapchain_ ="` over the whole tree returns exactly two writers: :1143 `this->swapchain_ = fresh;` and :1208 `this->swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;` inside `destroy_swapchain` (plus the `= VK_NULL_HANDLE` initialiser at device_resources.h:429). So the finding's "destroy_swapchain is the only writer of the null state" is right, and the zero-extent branch reaches neither writer. `rebuild_swapchain` (:1171-1184) is `vkDeviceWaitIdle` + `create_swapchain()` and nothing else — confirmed by reading it in full — so it cannot null the handle either. Meanwhile both of `present()`'s no-op doors are keyed on the null handle: :1495 `if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)` and :1523 the same test after the rebuild. The branch's comment ("present() answers this by doing nothing rather than by refusing") therefore describes a contract the branch does not deliver whenever a swapchain already exists.

THE THROW IS REAL AND UNCAUGHT. `check_vk` (:212-220) throws `std::runtime_error` for every result that is not `VK_SUCCESS`; :1540-1542 routes anything that is not `VK_SUCCESS`/`VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR` into it. `grep -rn "catch\s*(" engine/app/*.cpp engine/render/vulkan/*.cpp` finds exactly one catch in the whole path and it is in texture_factory.cpp:320 — nothing between `DeviceResources::present()` and `samples/minimal/main.cpp`'s handler. Renderer::end_frame calls straight through (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:866 `impl.device_resources.present();`).

THE SHELL REALLY DOES KEEP RENDERING, AND REALLY DOES NOT RESIZE. Application::tick (application.cpp:254-258) is `timer_.Tick(update); this->render();` with no suspend gate, and render() reaches `end_frame()` at :299. `Application::on_suspending` (:352-363) touches gamepads, focus and audio only. window.cpp's WM_SIZE: `SIZE_MINIMIZED` fires `on_suspending()` only, and the restore arm (`else if (self && self->minimized_)`) fires `on_resuming()` only — `on_window_size_changed` is in the third arm and is never reached by either edge of a minimise. `Application::on_resuming` (:366-379) does nothing to the renderer. So `window_size_changed(0,0)` is never delivered, which matters twice: it kills the benign reading of the branch, and it means the only reachable caller that can hand `create_swapchain` a {0,0} extent is `rebuild_swapchain` from present's two OUT_OF_DATE/SUBOPTIMAL paths (:1522, :1641) — i.e. the branch exists *for* exactly the case that breaks it. (The third caller, handle_device_lost -> create_window_size_dependent_resources at :1240, is preceded by `destroy_swapchain()` at :1283, so that route reaches the branch with a null handle and behaves correctly. That is the only case the comment is true for.)

THE FAILURE CONSTRUCTS. Minimise; the Win32 surface's `currentExtent` becomes {0,0} (this is why the branch was written at all); the presentation engine reports the swapchain no longer matches its surface via `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR` from acquire (:1513) or from `vkQueuePresentKHR` (:1636-1641). Either way `rebuild_swapchain` -> `create_swapchain` takes :1059 and returns with the pre-minimise handle intact and `swapchain_extent_` clobbered to {0,0}. The :1523 guard sees non-null, so :1530 re-acquires the *same* swapchain, which is still out of date (out-of-dateness is a property of swapchain-vs-surface and does not clear itself), so :1542 throws `std::runtime_error("No swapchain image could be acquired (VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR).")` out of end_frame to main.cpp's "startup failure" MessageBox and exit 1.

THE SECOND CONSEQUENCE ALSO CONSTRUCTS, and it is the one that bites on drivers where the acquire comes back VK_SUCCESS: `swapchain_extent_` is now permanently {0,0} while `colour_extent_` is not, so :1568's copy/blit test always takes the blit arm and :1589-1591 sets `dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1}` — a zero-area destination. Nothing ever repairs it, because on restore no `on_window_size_changed` arrives and a swapchain that matches the restored window is not out of date, so `create_swapchain` is never called again. The window presents an image nothing wrote into, forever. The finding's proposed two-part fix is correct for the same reason: `destroy_swapchain()` alone would park present() in the :1495 no-op with no event able to leave it.

THE EQUIVALENCE CLAIM CHECKS OUT. d3d11/device_resources.cpp:396 `HRESULT hr = m_swapChain->Present(1, 0);` and d3d12/device_resources.cpp:472 `const HRESULT hr = this->swap_chain_->Present(1, 0);` both take a success HRESULT while minimised and fall through to `ThrowIfFailed(hr)` without throwing. Four backends survive a minimise; the fifth does not.

Index safety was my last refutation hope and it fails too: the early return leaves `swapchain_images_` and `presentable_` populated and consistent with the surviving handle, so there is no out-of-bounds — the damage is confined to the two consequences above.

*Correction:* Substance stands; three qualifications a reader should carry.

(1) Line-number drift in the finding's citations, all trivially off: `this->swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE` is at :1208 not :1207 (destroy_swapchain spans :1186-1210); the `rebuild_swapchain()` call in the OUT_OF_DATE arm is at :1522 not :1520, and the arm opens at :1513. The quoted 1059-1067 block is exact.

(2) The crash is driver-conditional, not unconditional. Every consequence is gated on the presentation engine reporting VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR (or SUBOPTIMAL from present) for the minimised surface. The spec permits that and it is the ordinary Windows behaviour — it is the reason every Vulkan codebase has a "wait while the extent is zero" path in its swapchain-recreation routine — but a driver that keeps returning VK_SUCCESS while minimised never enters the branch and never fails. This does not soften the verdict: on such a driver the :1059 branch is simply dead code whose comment describes a state the function cannot produce, so :1059-1067 is wrong either way, and on the drivers that do report it the process dies. It does mean "reproduce by minimising" may come back clean on one adapter and crash on the next, and it explains why the validation-layer pass that checked this backend never saw it — validation layers do not exercise a minimise.

(3) One mechanism detail to state more precisely than the finding does: the two consequences are alternatives selected by the *second* acquire, not a sequence. If it returns OUT_OF_DATE the process throws; if it returns VK_SUCCESS/SUBOPTIMAL the process survives with `swapchain_extent_` permanently {0,0}, which is not merely a bad frame while minimised — nothing in the shell can ever call create_swapchain again after a restore (window.cpp's restore arm delivers on_resuming only), so the zero-area blit persists for the life of the window and the game comes back from a minimise showing undefined swapchain contents. That second outcome is a silent永-black window rather than a crash, which is arguably the worse of the two to diagnose.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

Every asserted fact checks out, and I could not find a break in the chain.

STATE. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067 returns from the zero-extent branch with no destroy_swapchain(); the only destroy_swapchain() call inside create_swapchain is at :1140, after the branch, and destroy_swapchain (:1186-1210) is the sole writer of swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE (:1208). rebuild_swapchain (:1171-1184) is vkDeviceWaitIdle + create_swapchain and nothing else. So a rebuild taken while minimised leaves swapchain_ holding the pre-minimise handle with swapchain_extent_ = {0,0} (:1065). Verified the branch is reachable on Win32: VK_KHR_win32_surface derives currentExtent from the client rect, which is 0x0 for a minimised HWND, and :1049's 0xFFFFFFFF escape does not fire there.

GUARDS. present() is written only against the null state: :1495 and :1523 both test swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE, and after this branch it is not null, so :1530's second acquire runs against the same object the first one just declared out of date. check_vk (:212-219) throws std::runtime_error on every non-VK_SUCCESS, VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR included, so :1540-1542 is a throw. That is the state the comment at :1061-1064 claims present() handles, and the two guards are the code implementing that claim - so the comment describes behaviour the branch itself makes unreachable once a swapchain exists.

VULKAN. VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR means the surface is no longer compatible with the swapchain and further presentation using it will fail; a 0x0 surface whose minImageExtent == maxImageExtent == {0,0} is exactly that against a non-zero swapchain, and the condition is not transient - re-acquiring on the same handle gives the same answer. Minimise-to-zero-extent is the standard Windows case for this, not folklore. It is driver-visible behaviour rather than a spec guarantee, but even a driver that only reports it at present rather than acquire lands in the same state via :1634-1641, which also calls rebuild_swapchain().

REACHABILITY. Rendering does continue while minimised: window.cpp:387-397 fires only on_suspending() on SIZE_MINIMIZED, Application::on_suspending (application.cpp:350-364) touches gamepads, focus and audio only, pump_until_quit calls notify_->tick() on every empty queue (window.cpp:245-247), tick calls render() unconditionally (application.cpp:254-258) and render() ends at end_frame() (application.cpp:299), which is impl.device_resources.present() (vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867). There is no catch anywhere in engine/app - grep for "catch" over engine/app/*.cpp is empty - so the throw reaches samples/minimal/main.cpp:47-56 and exits 1 with a "startup failure" message box.

EQUIVALENCE. Not a seam-wide shape: d3d11/device_resources.cpp:396 and d3d12/device_resources.cpp:472 both call Present(1, 0) on a minimised window, get a success HRESULT (DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED is 0x087A0001, SUCCEEDED), and carry on; ThrowIfFailed never fires. Only the Vulkan backend dies.

*Correction:* Three things the finding gets wrong or understates, none of which touch its conclusion.

1. The unwind path is not through DispatchMessage. For a minimise, tick() runs from the empty-queue branch of pump_until_quit (window.cpp:245-247), so the throw leaves pump_until_quit and run() normally and reaches main's catch cleanly. tick() is called from inside a window procedure only during a drag-resize (WM_PAINT while in_sizemove_, window.cpp:344-350). The destination - main.cpp's message box and exit 1 - is right; the route named is not.

2. The "acquire returns VK_SUCCESS instead" second consequence is not reachable by the sequence the finding gives, because entering :1522 requires the first acquire on that very handle to have returned OUT_OF_DATE, and a driver does not then answer SUCCESS on the same swapchain. The equivalent state does arise, by the other door: vkQueuePresentKHR returning OUT_OF_DATE or SUBOPTIMAL on minimise takes :1634-1641 into the same rebuild, leaving the stale handle with swapchain_extent_ = {0,0}. And there the consequence is worse than "a zero-area blit into a stale image": nothing recomputes swapchain_extent_ afterwards, because SIZE_RESTORED after a minimise takes window.cpp:399-407 and delivers no on_window_size_changed, so the blit path at :1581-1597 keeps writing a zero-area destination on every subsequent frame - the window is black permanently after the restore, not only while minimised.

3. Whether the crash or the black window fires depends on where the driver reports staleness, so this is a defect whose symptom varies by driver rather than one that is identical everywhere. It stays must-fix: on the common Windows drivers the symptom is an error dialog and exit 1 because the player pressed minimise, and the alternative symptom is a permanently dead window.

Also, the area label "tests" is wrong - nothing about this lives in tests/; it is engine/render/vulkan/ runtime behaviour that no test can currently reach, since RenderPixelTests uses a hidden window and never minimises.

### C4. abandon_commands resets colour_layout_ to UNDEFINED on every ordinary frame, so the frame's first barrier has an empty first synchronisation scope and the clear is not ordered after the previous frame's present blit of the same image

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1488`** · must-fix · `core` · raised by R13, R31 · run id `V2`

TWO LENSES (barriers-layouts, pipeline-state) reached this from opposite ends - one blaming stage_of(UNDEFINED), one blaming abandon_commands - and they are one defect. abandon_commands ends with `this->colour_layout_ = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;` (device_resources.cpp:1488) under the comment 'AND THE LAYOUT TRACKING IS FORGOTTEN, WHICH IS NOT TIDINESS. The barriers that moved the colour target into a layout were IN the commands this just threw away, so the member saying where it is has stopped being true'. That premise is false for the caller that matters: abandon_commands has exactly two callers, device_resources.cpp:1237 (resize, which then destroys the target) and Renderer::Impl::abandon_recording (renderer.cpp:658-662), whose sole caller is renderer.cpp:840 inside Renderer::begin_frame - i.e. EVERY frame. In an ordinary frame nothing is thrown away: present() left colour_layout_ = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL and execute() (1412) submitted the barrier that put it there, so the member is TRUE at the top of the next frame and is discarded anyway. The consequence: transition_colour (1708-1722) builds its barrier as `image_barrier(this->colour_image_, this->colour_layout_, layout)` and issues `vkCmdPipelineBarrier(this->commands(), stage_of(this->colour_layout_), stage_of(layout), ...)`, and stage_of(VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED) returns VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT (device_resources.cpp:64-66) with access_of returning 0 (87-89). A srcStageMask of TOP_OF_PIPE waits for nothing, so open_frame's UNDEFINED -> TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL barrier orders nothing at all. RULE BROKEN: the file's own, at device_resources.cpp:48-52 - 'a barrier whose source mask does not match the layout it is leaving is the class of mistake that produces a frame that is right on one driver and torn on another' - violated once per frame by the function written to prevent it. FAILURE: FRAME_COUNT is 2 (device_resources.h:196) and there is one colour_image_ shared by both frames in flight (device_resources.h:443); begin_frame's wait_for_frame() waits on frames_[frame_index_].timeline_value, i.e. frame N-2's submit, so frame N-1 is deliberately still in flight. Frame N-1's present() recorded vkCmdCopyImage/vkCmdBlitImage READING colour_image_ (1577/1593). Frame N's open_frame (renderer.cpp:672-692) emits the empty-scope barrier and then vkCmdClearColorImage WRITES the whole image. Nothing orders that write after the still-executing read: a write-after-read hazard across two batches on one queue, which Vulkan permits to overlap, plus an UNDEFINED transition that additionally licenses the implementation to discard the contents the blit is reading. On screen: intermittent black or torn frames. Invisible to RenderPixelTests, which never presents. Had the tracker been left alone, the barrier would have been TRANSFER_SRC -> TRANSFER_DST with srcStageMask TRANSFER and srcAccessMask TRANSFER_READ, whose first scope does cover frame N-1's blit - so the reset is the whole of the bug. FIX: forget the layout only when something unexecuted is actually discarded - record the layout at each successful submit (`submitted_colour_layout_ = colour_layout_` in execute()) and roll back to it at line 1488 instead of writing UNDEFINED; or, if the UNDEFINED marker is kept, make stage_of/access_of return VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT and the two write bits for it, since UNDEFINED is only ever used on the src side.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried to kill this and could not; every quoted line matches character for character and the failure path is reachable from a real entry point.

EVIDENCE CHECKED, LINE BY LINE:
- `device_resources.cpp:1488` is exactly `this->colour_layout_ = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;`, the last statement of `abandon_commands` (1434-1489), under the quoted "AND THE LAYOUT TRACKING IS FORGOTTEN" comment (1465-1487).
- Callers: `grep -rn abandon_commands engine/ tests/ samples/` returns exactly two call sites — `device_resources.cpp:1237` (inside `create_window_size_dependent_resources`, 1212-1240) and `renderer.cpp:661` (inside `Impl::abandon_recording`, 658-662). `abandon_recording`'s only call site is `renderer.cpp:840`, inside `Renderer::begin_frame` (826-854). `Application::render` calls `begin_frame` at `engine/app/application.cpp:292` and `end_frame` at 299, so both samples take this path every frame.

A srcStageMask of TOP_OF_PIPE is defined by the spec as equivalent to naming no stages, so this barrier carries no execution dependency against anything submitted earlier.

Frame N-1's submit is deliberately still pending.

That is a write-after-read across two batches on one queue with no semaphore and no non-empty barrier between them — Vulkan permits those to overlap, and the UNDEFINED oldLayout additionally licenses discarding the contents the blit is reading.

1. The line and its comment are as quoted: engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1488 `this->colour_layout_ = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;` under the comment at 1466-1487 ("The barriers that moved the colour target into a layout were IN the commands this just threw away").

So it runs once per frame.

3. The comment's premise is false for the per-frame caller. execute() sets `recording_ = false` at device_resources.cpp:1380 and `submitted_ = true` at 1422; present() ran transition_colour(TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL) at 1548, which sets colour_layout_ = TRANSFER_SRC at 1721 and then submits at 1607. At the top of frame N nothing is unexecuted (recording_ == false), the member is TRUE, and it is overwritten with UNDEFINED anyway.

4. Consequence as claimed. transition_colour (1708-1722) builds `image_barrier(colour_image_, colour_layout_, layout)` and issues `vkCmdPipelineBarrier(commands(), stage_of(colour_layout_), stage_of(layout), ...)`. stage_of(VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED) returns VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT (64-66); access_of returns 0 (87-89). Vulkan rule, stated precisely: vkCmdPipelineBarrier's first synchronization scope includes all commands earlier in *submission order* — which spans earlier vkQueueSubmit batches on the same queue — restricted to the stages in srcStageMask. TOP_OF_PIPE is the stage every command trivially reaches immediately, so as a source mask it is equivalent to no execution dependency (the spec says so explicitly). Had colour_layout_ been left at TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, stage_of/access_of would have produced VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT / VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT (59-61, 81-82), whose first scope does cover the previous submission's blit. So the reset is the whole of the bug, as the finding says.

5. Hazard is reachable from the ordinary present path. FRAME_COUNT = 2 (device_resources.h:197); a single colour_image_ shared by both frames in flight (device_resources.h:443 — it is not per-frame-index, unlike D3D12's back buffer); wait_for_frame (1653-1669) waits on frames_[frame_index_].timeline_value, written at each submit (1430), i.e. frame N-2's value, so frame N-1 is deliberately still executing. Frame N-1's vkCmdCopyImage (1577) / vkCmdBlitImage (1593) READ colour_image_; frame N's open_frame (renderer.cpp:663-692) emits the empty-scope barrier and then vkCmdClearColorImage WRITES the whole image (renderer.cpp:687). Write-after-read across two batches on one queue with no execution dependency — Vulkan permits these to overlap. The UNDEFINED oldLayout additionally licenses the implementation to discard contents (legal per VUID-VkImageMemoryBarrier-oldLayout-01197, which allows UNDEFINED or the current layout) while the blit is reading them.

6. No compensating wait exists on that path. The only device-wide waits are device_resources.cpp:381/385 (device loss), 1182 and 1223-1234 (resize/swapchain teardown), 1280, 1348 (second opening in one frame), and renderer.cpp:1224 (read_back_buffer). None runs on an ordinary draw-and-present frame.

7. The nearest accidental serialisation does not save it. Frame N's submit waits on frame.acquired at VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT (present() 1607, execute() 1404-1406), which does block the clear until frame N's own image is acquired. But the swapchain is created with `minImageCount + 1` images (1103) in VK_PRESENT_MODE_FIFO_KHR (1129); with three images the image acquired for frame N is not the one frame N-1 just presented, so its semaphore can signal without frame N-1's submit having completed.

8. Not a seam issue and not shared with the other backends. D3D12 keeps back_buffer_states_[FRAME_COUNT] per back buffer (d3d12/device_resources.h:212, set at d3d12/renderer.cpp:610) and its abandon_recording (d3d12/renderer.cpp:506-525) never forgets it; ID3D12CommandQueue::ExecuteCommandLists is documented to guarantee the first workload finishes before the second starts, so the analogous hazard cannot arise. The Vulkan file itself concedes the asymmetry at 1483-1487.

9. Why it was not caught. Only VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation is enabled (458-478); there is no VkValidationFeaturesEXT anywhere in engine/render/vulkan/, so synchronization validation — which is opt-in and off by default — never ran, and core validation is silent because UNDEFINED as oldLayout is legal. tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:305 ("Deliberately no end_frame()") and :505 ("read_back_buffer, which drains the GPU, so no frame here has ever...") confirm the suite neither presents nor leaves work in flight.

10. The file's own rule at device_resources.cpp:48-52 ("a barrier whose source mask does not match the layout it is leaving is the class of mistake that produces a frame that is right on one driver and torn on another"), repeated at device_resources.h:369-375, is the rule broken — and it is broken once per frame by the function written to prevent it.

*Correction:* Mechanism and conclusion both stand; three refinements.

(a) "Empty first synchronisation scope" is loose phrasing. TOP_OF_PIPE's first scope formally contains the top-of-pipe stage of every earlier command; the spec's point is that as a *source* mask it is equivalent to no dependency. Conclusion unchanged.

(b) The finding omits the one mechanism that comes closest to hiding the race, and should say why it does not: frame N's entire command buffer waits on frame.acquired with pWaitDstStageMask = VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT (device_resources.cpp:1607, consumed at 1404-1406), so the TRANSFER-stage clear cannot start before frame N's swapchain image is acquired. That is not the required ordering, because the swapchain takes minImageCount + 1 images (1103) in FIFO (1129), so the acquired image is generally not the one frame N-1 just presented and its semaphore can signal while N-1 is still running. Only with a two-image FIFO swapchain would the serialisation be incidental — which is precisely the "right on one driver, torn on another" shape.

(c) The defect is slightly broader than the WAR-against-the-blit the finding describes. On the minimised / no-swapchain path present() returns at 1495-1504 without transitioning, leaving colour_layout_ = COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL (set by renderer.cpp:1154 after vkCmdEndRenderPass), so the next frame's same empty-scope barrier is an unordered write-after-write against the previous frame's render pass output as well.

Also worth noting for whoever fixes it: the reset is harmless at the resize caller (1237), which sits behind vkDeviceWaitIdle at 1234 and is followed by create_colour_target's own reset at 986. The line only ever does damage on the begin_frame path, so guarding it on `recording_` (or the finding's submitted_colour_layout_ rollback) is sufficient and loses nothing.

WHY IT IS WRONG: The comment's own justification - "the barriers ... were IN the commands this just threw away" - is true for exactly one of abandon_commands' two callers. On the frame path the previous frame's commands were EXECUTED, not thrown away, so colour_layout_ was still true when it was discarded. Because there is one colour_image_ shared by both frame indices, and wait_for_frame only waits frames_[index].timeline_value (two frames back), the wait never covers the immediately preceding frame's present blit, which was submitted under the other index. A vkCmdPipelineBarrier's first synchronization scope covers commands submitted earlier to the same queue as limited by srcStageMask; TOP_OF_PIPE as a source stage limits that scope to nothing. The rule this breaks is written in this same file at device_resources.cpp:47-52: "a barrier whose source mask does not match the layout it is leaving is the class of mistake that produces a frame that is right on one driver and torn on another", and renderer.h:364-365/473-474 make begin_frame's clear and end_frame's present two terms of one seam.

FAILURE SCENARIO: MinimalSample or LineSweeperSample on x64-debug-vulkan, ordinary loop (Application::render, application.cpp: begin_frame / submit / end_frame, no minimised gate). Frame N (index 0) end_frame records transition_colour(TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL) + vkCmdCopyImage/vkCmdBlitImage reading colour_image_ (device_resources.cpp:1546-1608) and submits batch B_N; colour_layout_ is left TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, which is TRUE. Frame N+1 (index 1) begin_frame calls wait_for_frame(), which waits frames_[1].timeline_value - frame N-1's value, not frame N's - then abandon_commands() sets colour_layout_ = UNDEFINED, then open_frame() (renderer.cpp:664-673) emits image_barrier(colour_image_, UNDEFINED -> TRANSFER_DST) with srcStageMask = TOP_OF_PIPE and srcAccessMask = 0, followed immediately by vkCmdClearColorImage on colour_image_ (renderer.cpp:687-689), submitted as B_{N+1}. On any implementation that lets two transfer submissions on one queue overlap, the image handed to vkQueuePresentKHR for frame N is a mixture of frame N and black. RenderPixelTests cannot see it: every Harness::end() goes through read_back_buffer -> wait_for_gpu() (renderer.cpp:1224), and pixel_tests.cpp calls end_frame exactly once (line 1767), so frame_index_ never leaves 0 and wait_for_frame degenerates into full serialisation for the whole suite.

FIX (two independent ones, either closes it): (a) forget the layout only for commands actually discarded - guard the tail of abandon_commands with `if (this->recording_) { this->colour_layout_ = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED; }`; the resize caller does not need the unconditional form because destroy_colour_target (:1019) and create_colour_target (:986) both set UNDEFINED themselves. (b) make a barrier out of UNDEFINED honest about what it does not know - return VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT for VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED in stage_of (device_resources.cpp:63-66), since UNDEFINED here means "this class stopped tracking", not "the image is brand new", and the one site where it genuinely is new pays nothing for the stronger scope.

1. So at the next `abandon_commands` the member is accurate, and the tail throws away accurate information. The comment's own justification ("the barriers ... were IN the commands this just threw away") is false on this path: `execute()` set `recording_ = false` at :1380, so `abandon_commands`' `vkResetCommandPool` at :1451 discards an already-submitted, already-executed buffer.

3. Nothing else supplies the dependency. `wait_for_frame()` (device_resources.cpp:1653-1655) waits `this->frame().timeline_value` only. `frame.timeline_value` is written in `execute()` (:1429) for the index current at submit, and `frame_index_` advances only inside `present()` (:1502, :1526, :1648), with `FRAME_COUNT = 2` (device_resources.h:197). So frame N+1's wait targets frame N-1's value, never frame N's. The submit itself (:1400-1412) waits on exactly one binary semaphore, `current.acquired` from `vkAcquireNextImageKHR` (:1607), and signals timeline + `presentable_[image]` — there is no GPU-side timeline wait anywhere. 4. The Vulkan rule is stated correctly. Batches submitted to one queue are not implicitly ordered against each other — submission order defines synchronization scopes, not execution order, and without an explicit dependency commands from separate batches may execute concurrently. `vkCmdPipelineBarrier`'s first synchronization scope is "all commands that occur earlier in submission order", limited to srcStageMask — which does reach across batches on the same queue, so the *correct* barrier (TRANSFER_SRC -> TRANSFER_DST, srcStage=TRANSFER via stage_of at :59-61) would genuinely have covered frame N's blit. With srcStageMask=TOP_OF_PIPE the first scope contains only the top-of-pipe stage of earlier commands, which performs no work, so no execution dependency is created at all. The hazard is write-after-read plus an unordered layout transition (a transition is itself a write); WAR needs only an execution dependency, and there is none. This holds at the 1.2 floor (device_resources.cpp:31) and at every later version.

Nor would the layers catch it: `create_instance` enables `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` (device_resources.cpp:457-461) but never populates `VkValidationFeaturesEXT`, so synchronization validation — the only thing that finds a cross-submission WAR — is off.

6. The proposed fix (a) checks out too: the resize caller at device_resources.cpp:1237 calls `abandon_commands()` and then `destroy_colour_target()` (:1019 sets UNDEFINED) and `create_colour_target()` (:986 sets UNDEFINED) immediately after, so it does not depend on the unconditional form; and on the frame path `recording_` is false at that point while on the "begun and never submitted" path it is true, which is exactly the discrimination the guard needs.

*Correction:* Two things the finding gets wrong, neither of which saves it.

AREA IS NOT "SEAM". Nothing in renderer.h's contract is broken — "a frame begun and never submitted contributes nothing to the next one" is honoured, and the fix keeps honouring it. This is a defect internal to `vulkan/`, and it exists because of a structure unique to that backend: one `VkImage colour_image_` (device_resources.h:443) and one `VkImageLayout colour_layout_` (device_resources.h:448) sitting outside `Frame frames_[FRAME_COUNT]` (device_resources.h:463), shared by both frames in flight. The comparison backend does not have the shape: d3d12 carries `back_buffers_[FRAME_COUNT]` and `back_buffer_states_[FRAME_COUNT]` (engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.h:211-212), so frame N+1's clear never touches the resource frame N presented; d3d11 and gl present the buffer they drew into. The file's own comment at device_resources.cpp:1483-1486 already identifies d3d12 as immune, it just attributes the difference to the wrong thing (immediate clear execution, rather than one shared image plus a two-frame-old wait). Relabel this vulkan/sync, not seam — otherwise a reader goes looking for it in the other four.

IT IS SLIGHTLY BROADER THAN THE BLIT. When the swapchain is gone — minimised, or unmakeable at this size — `present()` takes the early return at device_resources.cpp:1496-1503, which calls `execute()` and advances `frame_index_` without ever transitioning to TRANSFER_SRC or blitting. `colour_layout_` is then COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL and still true, and the same line at :1488 forgets it, so the next frame's barrier loses a COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT source scope against the previous frame's render-pass attachment writes rather than a TRANSFER one against a blit read. Same line, same fix, one more shape it fails in.

One imprecision worth not repeating: "empty first synchronization scope" is loose. The scope contains the TOP_OF_PIPE stage of earlier commands, which executes no work — the effect is identical, but the phrasing invites a rebuttal that does not exist.

### C6. The stated justification for the SDK install — that without the loader none of the eleven other test executables would start — is false for two of them, and is repeated in three documents

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml:65`** · should-fix · `build` · raised by R109, R102 · run id `V67`

EVIDENCE. ci.yml:63-65:


tests/math/CMakeLists.txt:15-19 — target_link_libraries(MattMathTests PRIVATE MattMath doctest::doctest labrador_settings), with engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:24 linking MattMath PRIVATE labrador_settings only;
tests/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt:5-7 and 20-24 — "NOTE WHAT IS NOT LINKED: LabradorEngine. RULE. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard, restated in CLAUDE.md: a comment the code does not match is a defect. This number is not decoration — it is the load-bearing half of the argument that the install is not optional.

Correct all three places: "...and for the Vulkan loader the same installer puts in System32, without which the nine test executables here that link LabradorEngine would not start at all — MattMathTests and LineSweeperTests link no engine and are unaffected, which is the property tests/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt was written for." **Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this and could not. Every load-bearing link verified at HEAD.

THE SENTENCE, character for character. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:64-65` reads "...and for the Vulkan / # loader the same installer puts in System32, without which none of the / # eleven other test executables in this preset would start at all." The universal ("none of the eleven ... would start at all") is quoted accurately, and the finding's cited line 65 is exactly where "eleven other test executables" sits.

THE COUNT IS RIGHT, THE UNIVERSAL IS NOT. Vulkan reaches an executable through exactly one edge: `engine/CMakeLists.txt:184`, `target_link_libraries(LabradorEngine PUBLIC Vulkan::Vulkan)`, inside the `elseif(LABRADOR_RENDER_BACKEND STREQUAL "vulkan")` branch at `:166`. I enumerated every ctest entry and its link line:

THE REPETITION IS REAL. `docs/port/android.md:553`, inside the `> **Decided 2026-08-21:**` blockquote: "supplies the loader without which none of the *other* eleven test executables". And `git log -1 --format=%B 4d91b91` line 121: "installer supplies the loader without which none of the eleven other test".

This target has LineSweeperRules, / doctest and the settings interface, so there is no window to open, no device / to create and no renderer to fail." Two comments in one tree assert opposite things about the same binary.

THE RULE INVOKED IS THIS CODEBASE'S OWN. `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:1-17` states the standard exactly as the finding paraphrases it — comments "are held to the same standard" as the design documents, and "Each item is a claim that the code no longer matches, with the line that contradicts it. This is a work item". Its existing entries are the same species (three translation units vs four, RGBA vs BGRA).

I could not construct any reading under which MattMathTests fails to start without vulkan-1.dll.

*Correction:* Three refinements, none of which touch the conclusion.

1. Two citation slips. `engine/math/CMakeLists.txt` links MattMath at **:27**, not :24. `tests/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt`'s `target_link_libraries` is at **:18-22**, not :20-24 (the :5-7 comment citation is exact). Cosmetic.

2. Only ONE of the three sites is actually fixable, so "correct all three places" is the wrong prescription. The commit message of 4d91b91 is immutable history and rewriting it is off the table. `docs/port/android.md:553` sits inside a `> **Decided 2026-08-21:**` blockquote that reads as a dated decision record rather than present-tense specification — amending it means editing a record of what was decided, which is the thing `docs/review/` is explicitly forbidden from doing (CLAUDE.md: "historical ... not updated as findings are fixed"). The live, unambiguously-fixable site is `.github/workflows/ci.yml:64-65`; the android.md line at most earns a bracketed correction beneath the blockquote, not a silent rewrite.

3. The finding's own alternative fix is the better one, and it should be the primary rather than the fallback. Replacing a false eleven with an unverified nine reproduces the defect one digit smaller.
