### C21. device_resources.h's commands() contract states the opposite of this backend's frame shape: it says every entry point executes before returning, and neither begin_frame nor submit does

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:275`** · should-fix · `docs` · raised by R127 · run id `V89`

CLAIM: the contract on `commands()` describes D3D12's open/execute protocol transplanted onto a backend that deliberately does not use it, and it denies the exact hazard class the validation layers caught in this same commit.

EVIDENCE, device_resources.h:270-277:

```
		// The frame's command buffer, begun if it is not already recording.
		// [...] It is not a way to add to what an
		// earlier entry point recorded - every entry point executes before it
		// returns, so there is never an open buffer between them.
		VkCommandBuffer commands();
```


Against the code. Every call site of `execute()` in the folder: device_resources.cpp:1501, 1525 and 1607, all three inside `present()`, plus renderer.cpp:1221 inside `read_back_buffer`. `Renderer::begin_frame` (renderer.cpp:826-854) ends at `impl.open_frame();`, which records a barrier, `vkCmdClearColorImage` and a barrier into `commands()` and never executes — I confirmed open_frame at renderer.cpp:664-701. `Renderer::submit` (renderer.cpp:915-1156) ends at `device_resources.set_colour_layout(...)` after `vkCmdEndRenderPass` and never executes. Both return with `recording_ == true`.

The same folder says the opposite outright at device_resources.cpp:1485-1487: "This backend records the whole frame into one command buffer and submits once, which is cheaper and puts the burden here." And `commands()` itself (device_resources.cpp) opens with "A SECOND OPENING IN ONE FRAME, WHICH IS NOT A BEGIN", handling exactly the case the comment says cannot occur.

RULE: DRIFT.md's standard, restated in CLAUDE.md — a comment the code does not match is a defect. This is not a stale count but an inverted description of the backend's frame shape, in the header CLAUDE.md holds up as the contract.

FAILURE: a maintainer adding an entry point — a second clear, a marker implementation — reads this and concludes the buffer is closed between calls, so nothing they record can be dropped by a later `abandon_commands` and no layout tracking can go stale. That is precisely the assumption the validation layers caught here: device_resources.cpp:1466-1481 records that the clear `open_frame` writes IS dropped by `abandon_commands`, taking the layout tracking with it, on the case "a frame that is never submitted contributes nothing", and that "every assertion in that case passed while it was wrong". The comment tells the next reader the bug class does not exist on this backend.

FIX: replace the last sentence with what the code does: "One buffer holds the whole frame - open_frame's clear, submit()'s render pass and present()'s blit - and it stays open across entry points. Only read_back_buffer and present() execute it, which is why commands() has to handle being called after a submit and why abandon_commands has to forget the layout."

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I attacked this from five angles and every one failed.

1. EVIDENCE, CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:270-277` reads exactly as quoted. Line 275 is the offending clause: "earlier entry point recorded - every entry point executes before it" / 276 "returns, so there is never an open buffer between them." The cited line number is precise.

2. THE BEHAVIOURAL CLAIM. Confirmed at every link.
- `Renderer::begin_frame` (renderer.cpp:825-854) ends at `impl.open_frame();` (:853). `Impl::open_frame` (renderer.cpp:664-701) calls `transition_colour`, then `vkCmdClearColorImage(this->device_resources.commands(), ...)` at :688, then `transition_colour` again, then `reset_views()`. No `execute()`. `commands()` sets `recording_ = true` (device_resources.cpp:1362), so begin_frame returns with the buffer open.
- `Renderer::submit` takes the buffer at renderer.cpp:982 (`VkCommandBuffer commands = device_resources.commands();`), begins a render pass at :1000, ends it at :1146 (`vkCmdEndRenderPass`), and ends the function at :1152-1153 with `device_resources.set_colour_layout(VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL);`. No `execute()`. Returns with the buffer open.
- The complete set of `execute()` call sites in the folder is exactly as the finding states: device_resources.cpp:1501, 1525, 1607 — `present()` begins at device_resources.cpp:1493, so all three are inside it — plus renderer.cpp:1221 inside `read_back_buffer`. No others exist.
So the buffer is open between begin_frame and submit, and between submit and present, in every ordinary frame. This is the normal path, not a corner case, and the sentence's stated consequence ("there is never an open buffer between them") is false on the main line.

3. IS "ENTRY POINT" BEING MISREAD? No. The preceding sentence sets the granularity with its own two examples — "the barrier and the clear of a begin_frame" and "the transition, the copy and the transition back of a read-back" — so `begin_frame` is explicitly one of the things being quantified over. Narrowing "entry point" to DeviceResources' own methods does not save it either: `transition_colour` records a barrier and returns without executing, as does `commands()` itself.

4. THE MECHANISM CLAIM ("D3D12 transplanted"). Confirmed verbatim. `engine/render/d3d12/backend.h:358-366` is the same paragraph with "list"→"buffer": "...It is not a way to add to what begin_frame recorded - every entry point executes and closes the list before it returns, so there is never an open one between them." On D3D12 that is TRUE, because `Impl::open_frame` calls `this->execute_frame_list();` at d3d12/renderer.cpp:547, one line after the clear. The Vulkan file's own `abandon_commands` says precisely this at device_resources.cpp:1483-1486: "THE D3D12 BACKEND CANNOT HAVE THIS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ONE LINE OF ITS open_frame: it executes the clear immediately... This backend records the whole frame into one command buffer and submits once, which is cheaper and puts the burden here." The folder contradicts its own header outright.

5. THE RULE. Real and in-tree. `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:8-17` sets the standard the finding invokes: "The comments in engine/render/ are held to the same standard — renderer.h is not a header with comments, it is the specification of the seam... Each item is a claim that the code no longer matches, with the line that contradicts it." CLAUDE.md calls DRIFT.md a live list of exactly this defect class.

6. THE CONSEQUENCE. Corroborated by the folder itself. device_resources.cpp:1466-1481 records the hazard the header denies: "FOUND BY THE VALIDATION LAYERS AND BY NOTHING ELSE, on tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp's 'a frame that is never submitted contributes nothing' - a frame whose clear is recorded and dropped, followed by one that begins a render pass expecting the layout the dropped clear would have left. Every assertion in that case passed while it was wrong." A reader who believes "every entry point executes before it returns" believes begin_frame's clear has already reached the queue and cannot be dropped — the exact false belief that bug came from.

Also confirmed: `commands()` at device_resources.cpp:1338-1352 opens with "A SECOND OPENING IN ONE FRAME, WHICH IS NOT A BEGIN", a code path that only exists because the buffer's open/submitted state genuinely varies across entry points.

No link in the chain is missing. This is a docs finding, so there is no runtime scenario to reach and none is claimed.

*Correction:* Two refinements, both strengthening it.

(a) The mechanism is stronger than "describes D3D12's protocol" — it is a literal copy-paste. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:270-276` is `engine/render/d3d12/backend.h:358-366` with "list"→"buffer" and "open_frame"→"a begin_frame". The suggested fix should therefore say what differs from D3D12, not merely what Vulkan does, because the next person to port a backend will copy this paragraph again. The one-line difference is already written down at device_resources.cpp:1483-1486 and the header should point at it.

(b) Scope the fix to the last sentence only. Sentences one and two (device_resources.h:270-274, "begun if it is not already recording... idempotent WITHIN one operation", with the begin_frame and read-back examples) are accurate and are the useful half — `commands()` really is idempotent within one operation. Only :274-276, from "It is not a way to add to what an earlier entry point recorded" onward, inverts. Replacing the whole paragraph would throw away a correct contract.

Severity confirmed at should-fix, not minor. This is not a stale count of the kind that fills most of DRIFT.md — it is an inverted statement of the backend's central frame shape, sitting in the header CLAUDE.md singles out as carrying "the largest decision in the port", denying a hazard class that was actually hit during this commit and that `abandon_commands`' layout-forgetting exists to answer.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to refute this on four independent lines and it survived all four.

1. IS THE SENTENCE FALSE? Yes, and on the main frame path. device_resources.h:274-276 reads "It is not a way to add to what an earlier entry point recorded - every entry point executes before it returns, so there is never an open buffer between them." Renderer::begin_frame ends at `impl.open_frame();` (renderer.cpp:853). open_frame (renderer.cpp:664-701) records transition_colour -> vkCmdClearColorImage into device_resources.commands() (renderer.cpp:688) -> transition_colour, and returns without executing; commands() sets recording_ = true at device_resources.cpp:1362 and nothing clears it. Renderer::submit then calls device_resources.commands() at renderer.cpp:982, which returns that same still-open buffer — i.e. it IS "a way to add to what an earlier entry point recorded". submit ends at device_resources.set_colour_layout(...) after vkCmdEndRenderPass (renderer.cpp:1150-1156), again without executing. So the buffer is open across begin_frame -> submit -> present.

2. IS THE CALL-SITE INVENTORY RIGHT? Yes, exactly. grep for execute( across engine/render/vulkan/ gives the declaration (device_resources.h:292), the definition (device_resources.cpp:1368) and exactly four call sites: device_resources.cpp:1501, 1525, 1607 — all three inside present() — plus renderer.cpp:1221 inside read_back_buffer (confirmed by reading renderer.cpp:1195-1225). Neither begin_frame nor submit executes.

3. IS THE "TRANSPLANTED FROM D3D12" MECHANISM REAL? Yes, and I located the donor text. engine/render/d3d12/backend.h:359-366: "Opens the frame list for recording, resetting it onto this frame's allocator if it is closed. Returns the same list either way, which is what makes it idempotent WITHIN one operation: the barrier and the clear of open_frame are two calls to this and one list, as are the transition, the copy and the transition back of read_back_buffer. It is not a way to add to what begin_frame recorded - every entry point executes and closes the list before it returns, so there is never an open one between them." That is the Vulkan paragraph almost word for word. On d3d12 the claim is TRUE: Renderer::Impl::open_frame calls this->execute_frame_list(); at d3d12/renderer.cpp:547. So this is not a shape the other backends share and get away with — it is a sentence that is correct for d3d12 and inverted for vulkan. The Vulkan copy also generalised d3d12's "what begin_frame recorded" into "what an earlier entry point recorded", which makes it strictly more wrong, since submit() adds to exactly what begin_frame recorded.

4. DOES THE FOLDER CONTRADICT ITSELF? Yes, explicitly. device_resources.cpp:1484-1487: "THE D3D12 BACKEND CANNOT HAVE THIS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ONE LINE OF ITS open_frame: it executes the clear immediately, so its back_buffer_state is true the moment it is written. This backend records the whole frame into one command buffer and submits once, which is cheaper and puts the burden here." That is the frame shape stated correctly, in the .cpp, contradicting the .h.

5. IS THE RULE A REAL RULE HERE? Yes. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:8-11: "The comments in `engine/render/` are held to the same standard — `renderer.h` is not a header with comments, it is the specification of the seam, and several of its paragraphs are the only place a rule is written down." Every entry in that document is of this exact shape (a claim the code no longer matches, with the contradicting line). CLAUDE.md likewise treats vulkan/device_resources.h as a contract document ("`vulkan/device_resources.h` carries that argument and it is the largest decision in the port").

6. IS THE FAILURE SCENARIO REACHABLE? Yes, and it has already been hit once in this commit. device_resources.cpp:1466-1481 records that abandon_commands must reset colour_layout_ to UNDEFINED because "The barriers that moved the colour target into a layout were IN the commands this just threw away", that this was "FOUND BY THE VALIDATION LAYERS AND BY NOTHING ELSE" on the pixel test "a frame that is never submitted contributes nothing", and that "Every assertion in that case passed while it was wrong". That hazard class exists precisely because the buffer stays open across entry points — the state the header tells the reader never occurs.

No reading of "entry point" rescues the sentence. The paragraph names "a begin_frame" and "a read-back" as its two examples, and the d3d12 original names begin_frame outright, so "entry point" unambiguously means the seam's entry points, two of which do not execute.

Severity: this is a documentation defect, not a behavioural one — no runtime path is wrong — so not must-fix. But it is an inversion (not a stale count) in the backend's contract header, about a hazard class the same commit was demonstrably bitten by, so not minor either. should-fix is correct as raised.

*Correction:* Two things in the finding need correcting; neither touches the conclusion.

(1) The third evidence item is wrong. The finding says commands() "opens with 'A SECOND OPENING IN ONE FRAME, WHICH IS NOT A BEGIN', handling exactly the case the comment says cannot occur." It does not. That branch (device_resources.cpp:1338-1350) is guarded by `!this->recording_ && this->submitted_` — a CLOSED buffer that has already been to the queue. A closed-and-submitted buffer between entry points is entirely consistent with "there is never an open buffer between them"; if anything that branch is the one part of the file that agrees with the header. The reachable path there is present()'s commands() at device_resources.cpp:1546 after read_back_buffer executed at renderer.cpp:1221, exactly as its own comment says. Drop this item — the begin_frame and submit evidence is decisive without it.

(2) The mechanism is right but the citation is under-specified. "D3D12's open/execute protocol transplanted" is literally true, and the donor is engine/render/d3d12/backend.h:359-366 (not d3d12/device_resources.h, which has no commands() at all). Worth naming, because it is what proves this is not a shared seam shape the reviewer should leave alone: the identical sentence is TRUE on d3d12, whose open_frame executes at d3d12/renderer.cpp:547, and FALSE only here. The Vulkan copy also broadened d3d12's "what begin_frame recorded" to "what an earlier entry point recorded", which is what turns a correct sentence into an inverted one.

The proposed FIX text is accurate against the code as it stands (four execute() call sites, all in present() and read_back_buffer) and can be taken as written.

### C22. handle_device_lost destroys every device-dependent resource before its vkDeviceWaitIdle, and the ~Impl comment that would have caught it says the wait is inside a function that has none

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:271`** · should-fix · `core` · raised by R38, R6 · run id `V12`

TWO LENSES (lifetimes, timeline-sync). renderer.cpp:271-274 reads 'The wait is inside destroy_device_dependent_resources for the same reason ~DeviceResources has one: nothing may be freed while the GPU is reading it, and this API tracks none of that for you.' The body is renderer.cpp:280-281: `std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu(); this->destroy_device_dependent_resources();` - and destroy_device_dependent_resources (renderer.cpp:602-660) contains no wait of any kind; it goes straight to destroy_vulkan_buffer / vkDestroyPipeline / vkDestroyPipelineLayout / vkDestroyDescriptorSetLayout / vkDestroySampler. The D3D12 destructor this is transliterated from (d3d12/renderer.cpp:440-459) makes no such claim - it calls try_wait_for_gpu and stops, because ComPtr members do the rest. The comment matters because the function's OTHER caller has no wait either: Renderer::Impl::on_device_lost (renderer.cpp:703-705) calls it, and it is reached from device_resources.cpp:1265-1268 `this->notify_->on_device_lost();`, which is the FIRST statement of handle_device_lost - nine lines BEFORE its own `std::ignore = vkDeviceWaitIdle(this->owner_->device);` at 1277-1280. RULE BROKEN: DRIFT.md's standard as CLAUDE.md restates it, on the one ordering rule this backend's teardown depends on. FAILURE: handle_device_lost has a call site that is not a submit failure - device_resources.cpp:1223-1226, `if (!this->try_wait_for_gpu()) { this->handle_device_lost(); return; }`. try_wait_for_gpu (1688-1703) answers false for ANY non-VK_SUCCESS from vkWaitSemaphores, including VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY and VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY, neither of which means the device is lost. On those, a WM_EXITSIZEMOVE resize enters handle_device_lost with the last frame still executing, and the first thing it does is destroy the VkPipeline, both VkSamplers and the index VkBuffer - all named by a command buffer that is still running - eleven lines before the wait. FIX: move `std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu();` from renderer.cpp:280 into the top of destroy_device_dependent_resources so both callers get it (~Impl's behaviour is unchanged and the comment becomes true), or hoist device_resources.cpp:1277-1280's vkDeviceWaitIdle above the notify_->on_device_lost() call at 1268 and rewrite renderer.cpp:271-274 to say where the wait really is.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

Every quoted line matches character for character, and the chain holds.

The body is renderer.cpp:280-281: `std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu();` then `this->destroy_device_dependent_resources();`. The wait is at the call site, not inside. Its only reachable caller is device_resources.cpp:1275 `this->notify_->on_device_lost();` (grep: the sole notify_->on_device_lost() in the vulkan folder), which is the first statement of handle_device_lost (:1265-1281) — the vkDeviceWaitIdle sits at :1278-1281, after it. On an OOM return the device is not lost and the last submit may still be executing, yet handle_device_lost then destroys the VkPipeline, both VkSamplers, the index VkBuffer and its VkDeviceMemory before any wait — vkFreeMemory and vkDestroyPipeline on objects a submitted command buffer still names is UB (VUID-vkDestroyPipeline-pipeline-00765 and the vkFreeMemory in-use rule), exactly what the ~Impl comment says this API does not track for you.

*Correction:* Four corrections, none of which unseat it.

(1) The headline overstates. handle_device_lost does NOT destroy every device-dependent resource before its wait: its own swapchain, colour target and frames go after it (device_resources.cpp:1283-1285), as do the render pass and upload pool (:1291-1299). Only what the notify chain reaches goes before it. Say "the resources the notify chain destroys", not "every".

(2) The mechanism is wider than the finding scopes it. The same pre-wait chain continues past renderer.cpp:705 to :709 -> Application::on_device_lost (application.cpp:414-426) -> RenderResources::release_device_resources (vulkan/render_resources.cpp:121-124) -> release_all_textures, so the VkImages the in-flight command buffer samples are destroyed pre-wait too. The sharpest violation is vkFreeMemory on memory still bound to work in flight (device_resources.cpp:355-359), not vkDestroyPipeline.

(3) Reachability is narrower than "any non-VK_SUCCESS" implies. Three of the four handle_device_lost call sites (device_resources.cpp:1417 submit, :1537 acquire, :1631 present) are guarded by `== VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`, and on a genuinely lost device the vkDeviceWaitIdle at :1278-1281 is itself a no-op that returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST without flushing — so the ordering costs nothing on those three. The entire behavioural consequence rests on the OOM branch of :1223-1226, which is why should-fix rather than must-fix is right; no test in tests/ reaches any of these paths.

(4) The finding's first proposed fix does not close its own scenario. Moving `try_wait_for_gpu()` to the top of destroy_device_dependent_resources leaves the OOM path broken: vkWaitSemaphores fails again for the same reason, the result is std::ignore'd, and the destroys proceed regardless. Only the second fix works — hoist device_resources.cpp:1278-1281's vkDeviceWaitIdle above the notify_->on_device_lost() at :1275, which does not fight the :1269-1274 comment (owner_ holds the VulkanDevice alive across the whole function, so the textures are still destroyed against their own device) — and then rewrite renderer.cpp:271-274 to say where the wait actually is.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *refuted*, severity `minor`

I checked every quotation and then the two things the finding needs to be true: that the ordering is a defect, and that it is *this backend's* defect.

WHAT IS QUOTED CORRECTLY. `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:266-282` reads as claimed — the comment at :271-274 says "The wait is inside destroy_device_dependent_resources", and the wait is at :280, in `~Impl`, not inside it. `destroy_device_dependent_resources` (renderer.cpp:602-643) contains no wait: it early-outs on a null device, then `destroy_vulkan_buffer` (device_resources.cpp:337-359 — vkUnmapMemory/vkDestroyBuffer/vkFreeMemory, no wait), `vkDestroyPipeline` :620, `vkDestroyPipelineLayout` :625, `vkDestroyDescriptorSetLayout` :630, two `vkDestroySampler` :635/:640. `Renderer::Impl::on_device_lost` (renderer.cpp:703-711) calls it with no wait, and `DeviceResources::handle_device_lost` (device_resources.cpp:1265-1285) calls `notify_->on_device_lost()` at :1275, nine lines before `vkDeviceWaitIdle` at :1280. All of that is accurate.

WHY THE DEFECT DOES NOT STAND.

(1) It is verbatim the d3d12 shape, and Vulkan's is the stronger of the two. `d3d12/device_resources.cpp:317-321` is the same call site — `if (!this->try_wait_for_gpu()) { this->handle_device_lost(); return; }` inside `create_window_size_dependent_resources`, with the same comment about WM_EXITSIZEMOVE. `d3d12/device_resources.cpp:439-444` is `handle_device_lost` calling `notify_->on_device_lost()` first — and then it destroys everything with **no wait of any kind**, where Vulkan at :1280 at least has a `vkDeviceWaitIdle`. What that notify runs is `d3d12/renderer.cpp:964-1000`: `view->list.Reset()`, every `view->allocators[i].Reset()`, `view->pages[i].clear()` (the mapped vertex pages), `indices.Reset()`, `pipeline_state.Reset()`, `root_signature.Reset()`, `texture_heap.Reset()`, `sampler_heap.Reset()` — D3D12 command lists hold no reference to the resources they name, so that is the identical hazard on the identical path, in a shipped backend whose review (`docs/review/d3d12/`, all findings applied per CLAUDE.md) read this exact ordering and called it correct: all-findings.md:3382-3386, "DeviceResources::handle_device_lost (d3d12/device_resources.cpp:410-436) calls notify_->on_device_lost() first, then rebuilds… In-tree reachability is nil and correctly ordered." d3d11 (renderer.cpp:637) has no such hazard because its runtime tracks lifetimes; gl and null have no `on_device_lost` at all. So the shape is either a seam-level question or an accepted one — it is not something `render/vulkan/` introduced.

(2) The one reachable path needs an OOM return from a semaphore wait. Three of the four `handle_device_lost` call sites gate strictly on `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`: device_resources.cpp:1415-1418 (vkQueueSubmit), :1535-1538 (vkAcquireNextImageKHR), :1629-1632 (vkQueuePresentKHR). On a genuinely lost device, destroying the objects *is* the specified recovery — pending work is not guaranteed ever to complete, so the "all submitted commands that refer to it must have completed execution" conditions cannot be satisfied by waiting, and `vkDeviceWaitIdle` itself returns `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` there and establishes no idleness. The wait at :1280 therefore buys nothing on those three paths and hoisting it above :1275 would change nothing. That leaves only :1223, and only through `try_wait_for_gpu` (:1688-1703) returning false for `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY`/`VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` — the timeout is `UINT64_MAX`, so `VK_TIMEOUT` is not in play. That conflation is legal to worry about, but it is the same conflation `d3d12/device_resources.cpp:556-571` makes (false on any FAILED from `record_signal` or `block_until`, E_OUTOFMEMORY included), on the same resize path, and it was not raised there.

(3) The finding's own primary fix does not close its own scenario. The wait is `std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu();` — the result is discarded. Moving that line into the top of `destroy_device_dependent_resources` gives `on_device_lost` a best-effort wait whose failure is ignored, so in the OOM scenario the second wait fails for the same reason the first one did and the pipeline, samplers and index buffer are destroyed regardless. It makes the comment true; it does not make the teardown safe.

WHAT I DID CHECK AND FOUND REAL. The comment at renderer.cpp:271-272 is factually wrong about where the wait lives, and DRIFT.md's preamble (docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:8-11) does establish that comments in `engine/render/` are held to the design documents' standard — so the drift half is a genuine item, at the severity DRIFT.md's own entries carry. It is also true that `~DeviceResources` (device_resources.cpp:370-390) does try_wait → vkDeviceWaitIdle → destroy, while `handle_device_lost` puts the notify's destruction ahead of its `vkDeviceWaitIdle`; but the notify-first order is deliberately argued at :1269-1274 (it keeps the old `VulkanDevice` alive through the texture table's shared_ptrs) and hoisting the `vkDeviceWaitIdle` above :1275 would not disturb that argument. That is the cheap belt-and-braces change if anyone wants one — not the fix the finding leads with.

*Correction:* The should-fix correctness claim is refuted; one factual half survives at minor. Surviving: renderer.cpp:271-272 mislocates the wait — `destroy_device_dependent_resources` (renderer.cpp:602-643) has none, the wait is at renderer.cpp:280 in `~Impl`. That is comment drift of one clause, fixable with a word, and belongs on a DRIFT-style list rather than being carried as a teardown-ordering defect. Not surviving: the failure scenario. The notify-before-vkDeviceWaitIdle ordering in device_resources.cpp:1265-1285 is the same ordering d3d12 ships with no wait at all (d3d12/device_resources.cpp:439-444 + renderer.cpp:964-1000), from the same resize call site (d3d12/device_resources.cpp:317-321), and the d3d12 review read that ordering and passed it (all-findings.md:3382-3386) — so it is a seam-level question about `try_wait_for_gpu` conflating OOM with device loss, not a defect in `render/vulkan/`, and Vulkan is the stronger of the two implementations of it. On the three device-lost call sites (1415, 1535, 1629) destroying without a completed-execution guarantee is the specified recovery and `vkDeviceWaitIdle` guarantees nothing anyway, so moving it changes nothing there. If it is raised again, raise it against `try_wait_for_gpu`'s inability to distinguish OOM from loss in both backends, not against this comment. Note also that the finding's preferred fix (move the wait into `destroy_device_dependent_resources`) cannot close the scenario it describes, because the wait's result is `std::ignore`d and destruction proceeds either way.

The wait is at renderer.cpp:280 (`std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu();`), one line above the call at :281 — at the call site, not inside. I CHECKED REFUTER B'S AUTHORITY AND IT DOES NOT SAY WHAT B SAYS. docs/review/d3d12/all-findings.md:3378-3386 ("In-tree reachability is nil and correctly ordered") is adjudicating whether a stale GPU descriptor handle can survive a heap remake — it says the allocator reset "always follows the table being emptied". It is about table-emptying order versus descriptor allocation, not about destroying objects a submitted command list still names. Nothing in docs/review/d3d12/ adjudicates GPU-in-flight destruction on the notify path (I grepped the folder). B is right about the rest of the comparison — d3d12/device_resources.cpp:317-321 is the same ungated resize call site, :439-444 is notify-first with no wait at all, d3d12/renderer.cpp:964-1000 resets the lists/allocators/pages/PSO/heaps, and d3d12's try_wait_for_gpu (:556-571) makes the same OOM/loss conflation. That is a fair argument that the ordering half is seam-wide and pre-existing, and it correctly caps the severity. It is not a reason to kill a finding whose surviving half is a false new sentence about GPU synchronisation in a backend whose stated reason for existing is that "this API tracks none of that for you".

### C23. read_back_buffer discards execute()'s documented device-lost answer, then reads a mapping and frees handles belonging to a VkDevice that has been destroyed

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221`** · should-fix · `core` · raised by R24, R37, R46, R52, R166 · run id `V3`

> Raised as must-fix; a refuter corrected it to should-fix.

FIVE LENSES (memory, lifetimes, readback, errors, degenerate) hit this one line independently. renderer.cpp:1221 is `device_resources.execute();` with the bool return dropped. device_resources.h:283-291 makes that return a contract: 'ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out. That is not a courtesy' - and present(), the only other caller, honours it (device_resources.cpp:1607-1615). The buffer is `VulkanBuffer readback = create_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.owner(), ...)` (renderer.cpp:1184); create_vulkan_buffer takes `const VulkanDevice& owner` (device_resources.h:177), so the buffer holds NO reference on the device - unlike VulkanTexture, which device_resources.h:113-131 says holds a shared_ptr precisely because 'A texture destroyed after the device would be a call into a device that has gone, which is the one shape of undefined behaviour this API gives no diagnostic for'. RULE BROKEN: that stated class invariant, plus Vulkan's own requirement that a handle only be passed to the device that created it (VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-parent, VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-parent) and that all child objects be destroyed before vkDestroyDevice (VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-00378). FAILURE: a TDR or driver reset while a client (or RenderPixelTests) reads a frame back. vkQueueSubmit at device_resources.cpp:1412 returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, execute() calls handle_device_lost() (1265) which first runs notify_->on_device_lost() - emptying the texture table and dropping every shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> - then `this->owner_.reset();` (1317), so ~VulkanDevice calls vkDestroyDevice while readback.buffer, readback.memory and its live mapping are still children of it; then create_device_resources() installs a NEW VkDevice and sets timeline_value_ = 0. execute() returns false; read_back_buffer ignores it. wait_for_gpu() at 1224 returns instantly (timeline_value_ == 0). renderer.cpp:1230-1238 then reads width*height*4 bytes through readback.mapped - freed, unmapped memory - filling `pixels` with garbage or faulting, and renderer.cpp:1240 `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback)` hands the NEW device the OLD device's handles. RenderPixelTests reports a golden mismatch rather than a device loss. The D3D12 sibling cannot reach this state: its readback is a ComPtr (d3d12/renderer.cpp:1296) and its wait_for_gpu throws GetDeviceRemovedReason (d3d12/device_resources.cpp:541-554). FIX: capture `const std::shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> owner = device_resources.shared_device();` (the accessor already exists, device_resources.h:330) before line 1221; take the answer - `if (!device_resources.execute()) { destroy_vulkan_buffer(owner->device, readback); throw std::runtime_error("The device was lost while the back buffer was being read."); }` - and free against owner->device at 1240. Mark DeviceResources::execute [[nodiscard]] so no caller can drop it again.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this on five separate angles and could not. Every load-bearing line is verbatim what the finding says it is.

THE QUOTED EVIDENCE, checked character for character:
- `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221` is exactly `device_resources.execute();` — a `bool`-returning call with the answer dropped.
- `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:287-291` reads "ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out. That is not a courtesy: ..." — verbatim, and it documents `bool execute(...)` declared at 292-294.
- `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1184` is `VulkanBuffer readback = create_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.owner(), ...)`. `owner()` is `const VulkanDevice&` (device_resources.h:345) and `create_vulkan_buffer` takes `const VulkanDevice& owner` (device_resources.h:177). `struct VulkanBuffer` (device_resources.h:164-175) has four PODs and no `shared_ptr`. So the readback buffer holds no reference on the device. Confirmed.
- The texture contrast is real: device_resources.h:111-113 "A texture destroyed after the device would be a call into a device that has gone, which is the one shape of undefined behaviour this API gives no diagnostic for", and `VulkanTexture` does hold `std::shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> owner_` (backend.h:104), handed in at texture_factory.cpp:353 from `device_resources.shared_device()`.

THE FAILURE CHAIN, followed callee by callee:
1. `vkQueueSubmit` at device_resources.cpp:1411-1412; `if (submitted == VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) { this->handle_device_lost(); return false; }` at 1414-1418. `execute()` genuinely returns false having rebuilt.

3. `~VulkanDevice` (device_resources.cpp:225-241) calls `vkDestroyDevice` — so when the refcount reaches zero at 1318, the readback buffer, its memory and its live mapping become children of a destroyed device.
4. `wait_for_gpu()` (device_resources.cpp:1671-1675) returns immediately on `timeline_value_ == 0`, so nothing throws and nothing signals the caller. Confirmed — this is the missing tripwire.
5. renderer.cpp:1230-1238 dereferences `readback.mapped`, which `create_vulkan_buffer` mapped once at device_resources.cpp:330-331 and never unmapped.
6. renderer.cpp:1240 `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback)` — `device()` (device_resources.h:335-338) now returns the NEW `owner_->device`, and `destroy_vulkan_buffer` (device_resources.cpp:337-361) calls `vkUnmapMemory`/`vkDestroyBuffer`/`vkFreeMemory` on it with the old device's handles. That is VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-parent / VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-parent, unconditionally, regardless of whether the old device was destroyed.

I could not find a missing link. `recording_` is definitely true at 1221 (vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer at 1206 goes through `device_resources.commands()`), so `execute()` does not early-out at device_resources.cpp:1371-1374. The proposed accessor `shared_device()` does exist at device_resources.h:330-333, so the suggested fix compiles as written.

The D3D12 contrast is fair: d3d12/renderer.cpp:1297 makes the readback a `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource>`, and d3d12/device_resources.cpp:541-553 `wait_for_gpu` throws `GetDeviceRemovedReason()` rather than returning quietly.

*Correction:* Two supporting claims are wrong, and neither rescues the code.

1. "present(), the only other caller, honours it" is inaccurate. `execute()` has three call sites in `present()` — device_resources.cpp:1501, 1525 and 1607 — and only 1607 checks the answer. At 1501 and 1525 the return is dropped and the very next statement is `this->frame_index_ = (this->frame_index_ + 1) % FRAME_COUNT;`, which walks past the `frame_index_ = 0` that handle_device_lost() just set at device_resources.cpp:1320. So the contract is dropped in three places, not one, which strengthens the [[nodiscard]] half of the fix rather than weakening the finding.

2. The stated outcome in RenderPixelTests is wrong. Nothing in tests/ or samples/ ever calls `Renderer::set_device_notify` (engine/render/renderer.h:342) — the only `register_device_notify` in the tree is Impl registering itself with DeviceResources at vulkan/renderer.cpp:263. So in the test harness `Impl::notify` is null and `Impl::on_device_lost()` (vulkan/renderer.cpp:703-711) runs `destroy_device_dependent_resources()` only; it never empties the RenderResources texture table. The harness's `quad` and `font` (pixel_tests.cpp:258-272) are live `VulkanTexture`s each holding a `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>` (backend.h:104), so `owner_.reset()` at device_resources.cpp:1318 does NOT reach zero and the old VkDevice survives. In RenderPixelTests, therefore, what happens is stale/garbage pixels (the copy never executed), the old buffer and memory leaked, and the cross-device destroy at renderer.cpp:1240 — not a fault. The full use-after-free of a destroyed device needs a client that honours DeviceNotify by releasing its textures, i.e. a real game, not this test. The mechanism is real in both cases; the pixel test is the milder of the two.

Severity lowered from must-fix to should-fix, narrowly. It is genuine UB with a three-line fix and it sits in a file that built explicit machinery for exactly this event, but the trigger is a device loss landing inside one specific submit in a function renderer.h:479 calls "NOT A FRAME-PATH CALL", whose only in-tree caller is pixel_tests.cpp:496. Nothing a shipping frame executes reaches it — `present()`'s own submit at device_resources.cpp:1607 is checked.

*Correction:* Three corrections, none of which touches the conclusion.

1. "present(), the only other caller, honours it" is half right. present() contains THREE execute() calls: device_resources.cpp:1501 and :1525 (the minimised and the no-swapchain-after-rebuild paths) also drop the return, and only :1607 honours it. Those two are harmless — all that follows is `frame_index_ = (frame_index_ + 1) % FRAME_COUNT`, and handle_device_lost has already reset it to 0 — but the claim that only read_back_buffer ignores the answer is not exact. It is the only site where ignoring it is a defect.

2. Line cites drift by a line or two: `this->owner_.reset();` is device_resources.cpp:1318 (not 1317), and the VulkanTexture shared_ptr paragraph runs device_resources.h:102-118 (not 113-131). The execute() contract paragraph is device_resources.h:287-291 with the declaration at :292-294. Note also that the contract paragraph gives a PRESENT-specific reason for the return value ("the caller that passes semaphores is present()"), so read_back_buffer is not the case the sentence was written for — the class invariant at :102-118 is the stronger ground and the finding is right to lean on it too.

3. The consequence has two branches and the finding states only the first. If the texture-table release drops the last other reference, ~VulkanDevice runs vkDestroyDevice with the readback buffer, its memory and its live mapping outstanding (VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-00378) and renderer.cpp:1230-1238 reads unmapped memory — fault or garbage. If some VulkanTexture outlives the release and keeps the old device alive, the read instead yields stale bytes the copy never wrote, and renderer.cpp:1240 still hands old handles to the new VkDevice. Both are UB and in both the caller is told nothing.

Impact bound worth recording: read_back_buffer has no caller outside tests/ in this tree (grep over all .cpp/.h: only tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp, golden_image.cpp, dds_file_tests.cpp, null_tests.cpp), so today's trigger is a TDR during RenderPixelTests rather than a shipping client. renderer.h:467-480 exposes it as public seam API, and the repo's own must-fix precedent (d3d12 review §2.2, §2.3) is device-loss lifetime UB of exactly this shape, so the severity stands.

### C24. read_back_buffer maps and reads the staging buffer with no TRANSFER_WRITE -> HOST_READ barrier, which HOST_COHERENT does not supply and a timeline wait does not perform

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221`** · should-fix · `core` · raised by R27, R47 · run id `V4`

> Raised as must-fix; a refuter corrected it to should-fix.

TWO LENSES (memory, readback) independently. renderer.cpp:1206-1208 records `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer(device_resources.commands(), device_resources.colour_target(), VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, readback.buffer, 1, &copy);`. The only thing recorded after it is `device_resources.transition_colour(previous)` (renderer.cpp:1216-1219), an IMAGE barrier on colour_image_ whose stages come from stage_of() (device_resources.cpp:53-68) and can never be VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT. Then `device_resources.execute(); device_resources.wait_for_gpu();` (1221-1224), where wait_for_gpu is `vkWaitSemaphores(..., UINT64_MAX)` on the timeline (device_resources.cpp:1671-1686), and then the host reads every byte through readback.mapped (1230-1238). `grep -rn "HOST_READ\|HOST_BIT" engine/render/vulkan/` returns NOTHING - there is no VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT, no VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT and no vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges anywhere in the folder. RULE BROKEN: the Vulkan specification separates host cache management from availability. VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT (renderer.cpp:1188) removes the need for vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges; it does not perform the availability operation that moves device transfer writes into the host domain. The spec states this for a host wait directly: 'Signaling a fence and waiting on the host does not guarantee that the results of memory accesses will be visible to the host, as the access scope of a memory dependency defined by a fence only includes device access. A memory barrier or other memory dependency must be used to guarantee this.' The same holds for vkWaitSemaphores. Khronos' own read-back recipe is copy -> TRANSFER_WRITE-to-HOST_READ barrier -> wait -> map. renderer.h:448-456 makes read_back_buffer the whole basis of the pixel contract ('a seam whose output nothing can read cannot be held to a contract'). FAILURE: on any implementation that holds transfer writes in a device cache until an availability operation drains them - the tile-based mobile hardware docs/port/android.md says this backend exists to reach - the loop at renderer.cpp:1232 reads stale or partially-written bytes, so RenderPixelTests fails its golden comparison with nothing wrong on screen, or passes intermittently inside ALLOWED_CHANNEL_DRIFT. Neither the core validation layers nor any assertion in pixel_tests.cpp can see it. FIX: between renderer.cpp:1208 and the execute() at 1221, record `vkCmdPipelineBarrier(device_resources.commands(), VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT, 0, ...)` with a VkBufferMemoryBarrier over readback.buffer, srcAccessMask VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT, dstAccessMask VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT, VK_WHOLE_SIZE. One call, on a path the seam already says stalls.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this on four fronts — quoted evidence, callee chain, the Vulkan rule, and reachability — and it survived all four.

EVIDENCE IS EXACT. Every citation matches character for character. renderer.cpp:1188 is `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT`. renderer.cpp:1206-1208 is the `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` as quoted. renderer.cpp:1216-1219 is the `transition_colour(previous)` guard. renderer.cpp:1221 is `device_resources.execute();`, 1224 `wait_for_gpu();`, and the host read loop is 1230-1238 reading `readback.mapped`. `grep -rn "HOST_READ\|HOST_BIT" engine/render/vulkan/` returns nothing (exit 1); so does a grep for Invalidate/FlushMappedMemoryRanges. The line spans given for the callees are right to the line: `stage_of` is device_resources.cpp:53-68 (`access_of` begins at 70) and `wait_for_gpu` is 1671-1686.

NO CALLEE SUPPLIES THE DEPENDENCY. `transition_colour` (device_resources.cpp:1708-1723) records a single `VkImageMemoryBarrier` on `colour_image_` via `vkCmdPipelineBarrier(commands(), stage_of(old), stage_of(new), 0, 0,nullptr, 0,nullptr, 1,&barrier)` — an image barrier, not a buffer one, and `stage_of` (53-68) has four cases returning COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT / TRANSFER / FRAGMENT_SHADER / TOP_OF_PIPE, so it can never name HOST_BIT. `execute()` (device_resources.cpp:1368-1432) records nothing: `vkEndCommandBuffer`, timeline increment, `vkQueueSubmit`. `wait_for_gpu()` (1671-1686) is a bare `vkWaitSemaphores(..., UINT64_MAX)`. So between the copy at 1208 and the host read at 1232 there is no memory dependency of any kind touching `readback.buffer`.

THE RULE IS REAL VULKAN. `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT` is defined solely as removing the need for the host cache management *commands* (vkFlush/vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges); it performs no availability or domain operation. The spec's fence note says a host wait does not make device writes visible to the host because the access scope of that dependency covers device accesses only, and a timeline host wait is the same case. The decisive structural argument is the asymmetry: the spec grants an *implicit* dependency for the host-write-to-device direction at vkQueueSubmit (Host Write Ordering Guarantees) and grants nothing for device-write-to-host-read. If a host wait sufficed, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT and VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT would have no purpose in the API. Khronos' own read-back recipe is copy -> TRANSFER_WRITE-to-HOST_READ barrier -> wait -> map, exactly as the finding states.

REACHABLE FROM A REAL ENTRY POINT. tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:492-497 `Harness::read_frame()` is `renderer_.submit(); renderer_.read_back_buffer(pixels_); buffer_ = back_buffer_size();`, and the comment at pixel_tests.cpp:503-506 confirms "every end() routes through read_back_buffer". So every frame RenderPixelTests reads under x64-debug-vulkan takes this path. renderer.h:445-456 does say what the finding quotes: "A seam whose output nothing can read cannot be held to a contract."

ONE AGGRAVATING FACT THE FINDING MISSED. `VulkanDevice::memory_type` (device_resources.cpp:265-275) returns the *first* memory type whose flags contain the requested set. Nothing excludes VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_CACHED_BIT, so the readback allocation can land in host-cached memory — the case where a missing availability operation is most likely to hand back stale bytes.

WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM is the failure as literally written. RenderPixelTests runs only on Windows (CLAUDE.md: "Windows-only"), where desktop drivers flush at submission end, so the golden comparison will not fail on anything this repo builds or CIs. The defect is latent UB, not an active failure — which is why I moved severity rather than leaving must-fix.

*Correction:* The mechanism and the conclusion both stand; the fix as proposed is correct and belongs in the code. Three corrections, none of them refutations:

1. SEVERITY, must-fix -> should-fix. The stated failure ("RenderPixelTests fails its golden comparison ... or passes intermittently inside ALLOWED_CHANNEL_DRIFT") is not reachable on any configuration this repository builds. The engine is Windows-only and RenderPixelTests runs under x64-debug-vulkan on desktop drivers that drain caches at submission end. The finding's reachability rests entirely on docs/port/android.md, which is labelled "Scoping only, 2026-08-21 ... **Nothing here has been built**" (android.md:3-4) and which argues mobile as a destination ("mobile is where 2D games are", line 8-9) but nowhere makes the tile-based-cache claim the finding attributes to it. This is a latent conformance defect on an unbuilt target, not a live one — correct, cheap, worth fixing, but not blocking. The distinction is largely academic given the fix is one call.

2. THE ANCHOR LINE IS WRONG, and "maps" is wrong. renderer.cpp:1221 is `device_resources.execute();`. The host read is 1230-1238. Nothing maps at 1221: create_vulkan_buffer maps once at allocation (device_resources.cpp:327-331, "MAPPED ONCE AND NEVER UNMAPPED"), so the pointer is established at renderer.cpp:1183, before the copy is even recorded. The finding should anchor at 1232 (the read) or 1208 (the unbarriered copy).

3. ONE FACT MISSED THAT STRENGTHENS IT. VulkanDevice::memory_type (device_resources.cpp:265-275) returns the first memory type containing the requested flags and does not exclude VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_CACHED_BIT, so the readback buffer can be allocated from host-cached memory — the configuration in which a missing availability operation most readily yields stale bytes. Worth adding to the finding.

Also worth noting for whoever applies the fix: the barrier must be recorded after line 1208 but its position relative to the transition_colour at 1216-1219 is immaterial (independent resources), and the transition is conditional, so on the previous==UNDEFINED path nothing whatsoever is recorded between the copy and execute().

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried to kill this three ways — the code, the rule, and the seam — and it survived all three.

THE CODE. Every line number the finding gives is exact at HEAD (4d91b91).
- `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1184-1190` creates the read-back buffer with `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT | VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT`.
- `renderer.cpp:1206-1208` records `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer(...)` into it.
- `renderer.cpp:1216-1219` is the only thing recorded afterwards, and it is *conditional* (`if (previous != VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED)`) and itself early-returns when the layout already matches (`device_resources.cpp:1710-1713`) — so on some paths literally nothing is recorded after the copy. When it does record, it is `vkCmdPipelineBarrier(..., stage_of(colour_layout_), stage_of(layout), 0, 0, nullptr, 0, nullptr, 1, &barrier)` (`device_resources.cpp:1718-1720`) — one *image* barrier on `colour_image_`, with no buffer barrier and no memory barrier, and `stage_of` (`device_resources.cpp:53-68`) returns only COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT / TRANSFER / FRAGMENT_SHADER / TOP_OF_PIPE. It can never name HOST.
- `renderer.cpp:1221` calls `execute()`, which is `vkEndCommandBuffer` then a plain `vkQueueSubmit` with a timeline signal and nothing else (`device_resources.cpp:1376-1412`) — no trailing barrier of any kind.
- `renderer.cpp:1224` calls `wait_for_gpu()`, which is `vkWaitSemaphores(device, &wait, UINT64_MAX)` on the timeline (`device_resources.cpp:1671-1686`).
- `renderer.cpp:1230-1239` then reads every byte through `readback.mapped`, which is a map taken at creation and never unmapped (`device_resources.cpp:324-332`) — so there isn't even a post-wait `vkMapMemory` call in the path.

I checked the only other two `vkCmdPipelineBarrier` sites in the folder (`device_resources.cpp:1554` and `:1603`): both are image barriers on the swapchain image inside the present path, and the read-back path never goes through present — it calls `execute()` directly. My own grep confirms the finding's: no `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT`, no `VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT`, no `vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` anywhere under `engine/render/vulkan/` (the only HOST_ hits are the two memory *property* bits at `device_resources.cpp:328,1754-1755`, `renderer.cpp:585-586,1187-1188`, `texture_factory.cpp:233-234`).

THE RULE, stated from the specification rather than from the finding. Vulkan's memory model separates *availability* (getting a write out of the writer's caches into a domain) from *visibility*, and the host is its own memory domain. An availability + domain operation to the host domain is performed only by a memory dependency whose destination stage mask includes `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT` and whose destination access mask includes `VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT`; `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT` is the pseudo-stage for host reads/writes of device memory and is never invoked by any recorded command. The spec makes the host-wait point explicitly under fences: "Signaling a fence and waiting on the host does not guarantee that the results of memory accesses will be visible to the host, as the access scope of a memory dependency defined by a fence only includes device access. A memory barrier or other memory dependency must be used to guarantee this." The same holds for a host wait on a timeline semaphore — a semaphore signal's availability operation is to the device domain, and `vkWaitSemaphores` carries no host-domain guarantee; the asymmetry is deliberate, which is why the spec has a whole clause ("Host Write Ordering Guarantees") granting the *opposite* direction automatically at `vkQueueSubmit` and no reciprocal clause for device→host. That clause is also why the texture-upload direction in this backend needs nothing and is correctly bare.

I specifically tried to refute on HOST_COHERENT, which is the strongest available defence, and it does not hold. `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT` is defined in terms of the host *cache management commands*: it means `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges`/`vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` are not needed. It removes a call, not a memory dependency; it does not perform an availability or domain operation, and nothing in the coherent-memory wording exempts a device write from needing one. Khronos' own synchronisation-examples recipe for GPU→CPU read-back is copy → barrier `srcStageMask TRANSFER / srcAccessMask TRANSFER_WRITE` to `dstStageMask HOST / dstAccessMask HOST_READ` → wait → read, with no coherent-memory carve-out. So this is a genuine specification requirement, not folklore, and it applies at the 1.2 floor this backend sets (`device_resources.cpp` MIN_API_VERSION = VK_API_VERSION_1_2).

THE SEAM TEST — is this shape accepted in another backend? No. `engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp:1272-1340` is the closest analogue and it is correct in its own API's terms: a READBACK-heap resource in `D3D12_RESOURCE_STATE_COPY_DEST`, fence wait, then `Map(0, &everything, &mapped)` with an explicit read range — D3D12 places the coherency obligation on the runtime for readback heaps, and the read range is the mechanism. There is no missing step there and no equivalent host-domain concept to omit. The GL backend reads with `glReadPixels`, where the GL spec makes the read a client-side synchronising operation. This defect exists in exactly one backend and is not a property of the seam.

REACHABILITY AND CONSEQUENCE. `read_back_buffer` is not dead code and is not incidental: `engine/render/renderer.h:446-456` makes it the whole basis of the pixel contract ("A seam whose output nothing can read cannot be held to a contract"), and `tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:496` calls it once per frame in the harness — the entire `RenderPixelTests` binary and every golden comparison in `tests/render/golden/` reads through this pointer. An implementation is permitted to leave the transfer writes in a device cache until an availability operation drains them, and the loop at `renderer.cpp:1232` would then copy stale or partially-written bytes. Nothing in the tree detects it: the buffer is persistently mapped, so there is no `vkMapMemory` for a layer to hook, and core validation does not model host-domain hazards.

The one honest calibration: no configuration this repository builds today is known to fail. On the desktop Windows drivers and on WARP-class software implementations the caches are flushed at end-of-submit as a matter of driver behaviour, so `x64-debug-vulkan` passes and will keep passing. The failure is spec-permitted rather than observed. That is exactly the class the backend was added to care about, though — `CLAUDE.md` says `render/vulkan/` exists because it is "the single API that reaches Android, Linux and, through MoltenVK, the Apple platforms", and MoltenVK is a concrete case where a `HOST_READ` barrier is what triggers the underlying `synchronizeResource` for managed-storage buffers. The file's own barrier comment (`device_resources.cpp:48-52`) names precisely this hazard class as the thing to guard against: "the class of mistake that produces a frame that is right on one driver and torn on another."

The fix the finding proposes is right, and a `VkMemoryBarrier` would serve equally: between `renderer.cpp:1208` and the `execute()` at `:1221`, one `vkCmdPipelineBarrier` from `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT` to `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT` with `VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT` → `VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT` over `readback.buffer`, `VK_WHOLE_SIZE`. One call, on a path the seam already documents as stalling.

*Correction:* Two details in the finding's mechanism to tighten, neither of which weakens it. (1) The `transition_colour(previous)` at renderer.cpp:1216-1219 is conditional on `previous != VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED`, and `transition_colour` early-returns when the layout already matches (device_resources.cpp:1710-1713) — so on some paths nothing at all is recorded after the copy, which makes the gap wider than "one image barrier that cannot name HOST", not narrower. (2) The finding's fix names a VkBufferMemoryBarrier; a plain VkMemoryBarrier with the same masks is equally sufficient and avoids the queue-family-index fields.

Severity calibration, stated so a reader can re-rank it against their own bar: this fails no configuration the repository currently builds. Desktop Windows drivers and WARP-class software implementations drain transfer writes at end-of-submit as driver behaviour, so `x64-debug-vulkan` passes today and the golden set is not currently at risk — the finding's "RenderPixelTests fails, or passes intermittently inside ALLOWED_CHANNEL_DRIFT" is a spec-permitted possibility, not an observed failure. I keep must-fix anyway because it is a missing specification-required synchronisation (undefined behaviour, not a style point) on the single function that constitutes the pixel contract, in the one backend whose stated reason for existing is the platforms where this class actually bites. A reviewer whose must-fix bar is strictly "breaks a configuration we build" should read it as should-fix; the code change is identical either way.

### C25. read_back_buffer discards execute()'s device-lost bool, then reads and frees old-device resources against the new device

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221`** · should-fix · `docs` · raised by R148 · run id `V86`

> Raised as must-fix; a refuter corrected it to should-fix.

CLAIM: `Renderer::read_back_buffer` ignores the bool `DeviceResources::execute()` returns, so a device loss inside that submit is followed by a read of freed host memory and by handing old-device handles to a new VkDevice.

EVIDENCE, renderer.cpp:1219-1240:

```
		device_resources.execute();
		// It stalls on the GPU by construction, and the seam says so.
		device_resources.wait_for_gpu();
		...
		const unsigned char* bytes = static_cast<const unsigned char*>(readback.mapped);
		...
		destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback);
```


The contract it ignores, device_resources.h:287-294: "ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out." The implementation, device_resources.cpp:1415-1419: `if (submitted == VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) { this->handle_device_lost(); return false; }`. I read `handle_device_lost` (device_resources.cpp:1265ff) and confirmed it calls `notify_->on_device_lost()`, destroys the swapchain, colour target, frames, render pass, upload pool and timeline, then `this->owner_.reset();`, `this->timeline_value_ = 0;`, then `create_device_resources()` and `create_window_size_dependent_resources()` — a brand-new VkInstance/VkDevice/timeline.

RULE: the seam's own written contract at device_resources.h:287, which `present()` honours at device_resources.cpp:1607 (`if (!this->execute(current.acquired, ...)) { ... return; }` with a comment saying why). read_back_buffer is the only caller of `execute()` that neither checks nor marks the discard. This folder's convention for a deliberate discard is `std::ignore =`, used at device_resources.cpp:381, 385, 512, 1182, 1234, 1280, 1349, 1451, 1461 and renderer.cpp:206, 228, 280, 1257, 1267, so a bare call reads as an oversight.

FAILURE: a TDR or driver reset during the read-back submit. `execute()` rebuilds the device and returns false; the false is dropped. `wait_for_gpu()` returns immediately because `timeline_value_ == 0` (device_resources.cpp, first lines of wait_for_gpu). The loop then dereferences `readback.mapped`, host memory mapped from a VkDeviceMemory of a VkDevice that `owner_.reset()` destroyed — nothing in read_back_buffer holds a shared_ptr keep-alive, since `create_vulkan_buffer` is handed `device_resources.owner()` as a bare reference. Finally `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback)` passes the OLD VkBuffer and VkDeviceMemory to vkUnmapMemory/vkDestroyBuffer/vkFreeMemory on the NEW VkDevice. Undefined behaviour on both halves, and the caller silently receives garbage pixels rather than an error.

FIX: check it the way present() does — `if (!device_resources.execute()) { std::fill(pixels.begin(), pixels.end(), 0u); return; }`, deliberately without touching `readback`, whose buffer and memory went with the device that made them. Spell any genuinely intended discard `std::ignore = device_resources.execute();`; the same applies to the two bare `this->execute();` calls at device_resources.cpp:1501 and 1525.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this and could not. Every quoted line is accurate character for character, and every link in the failure chain is present in the code at HEAD.

THE EVIDENCE, VERIFIED LINE BY LINE
- `C:\VSProjects\Labrador\engine\render\vulkan\renderer.cpp:1221` is exactly `device_resources.execute();` — a bare call, return value discarded. It is the only call to `execute()` anywhere in that file (grep for `execute()` in renderer.cpp returns line 1221 and nothing else).
- `renderer.cpp:1223-1224` is the `wait_for_gpu()` with its comment; `renderer.cpp:1230-1231` is `const unsigned char* bytes = static_cast<const unsigned char*>(readback.mapped);`; `renderer.cpp:1240` is `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback);`. The finding's quoted block is the real block.
- `device_resources.h:287-291` reads "ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out." — verbatim.
- `device_resources.cpp:1415-1419` is `if (submitted == VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) { this->handle_device_lost(); return false; }` — verbatim.

THE CHAIN, FOLLOWED CALLEE BY CALLEE
1. `execute()` reaches `vkQueueSubmit` because `recording_` is true: `transition_colour` and `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` at `renderer.cpp:1206-1208` both went through `commands()`. `execute()`'s early-out at `device_resources.cpp:1370` (`if (!this->recording_) return true;`) is not taken.
2. `handle_device_lost()` (`device_resources.cpp:1265-1329`) does exactly what the finding says: `notify_->on_device_lost()`, `vkDeviceWaitIdle`, destroys swapchain/colour target/frames/render pass/upload pool/timeline/surface, then `this->owner_.reset();` (line ~1317), `this->frame_index_ = 0; this->timeline_value_ = 0;`, then `create_device_resources()` and `create_window_size_dependent_resources()`.
3. `owner_.reset()` really destroys the VkDevice. `VulkanDevice::~VulkanDevice()` at `device_resources.cpp:225-241` calls `vkDestroyDevice`. The only other shared_ptr holders are `VulkanTexture` (`backend.h:104`), and the texture table is emptied first by `notify_->on_device_lost()` — the comment at `device_resources.cpp:1267-1274` says so explicitly. `Renderer::Impl` holds no shared_ptr: `Impl::on_device_lost` (`renderer.cpp:703-711`) calls `destroy_device_dependent_resources()`, which frees the index buffer, pipeline, layouts and samplers as raw handles. So at `vkDestroyDevice` the readback buffer created at `renderer.cpp:1184` is the *only* live child object of the dying device — a VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-00378 violation in its own right, on top of everything else.
4. `create_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.owner(), ...)` — `owner()` at `device_resources.h:345` returns `*this->owner_`, a bare `const VulkanDevice&`. `VulkanBuffer` (`device_resources.h:164-176`) holds only `VkBuffer`, `VkDeviceMemory`, `VkDeviceSize` and `void* mapped`. No keep-alive whatsoever. The finding is right.
5. `wait_for_gpu()` at `device_resources.cpp:1671-1676` returns immediately: `if (this->timeline_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE || this->timeline_value_ == 0) return;`. I checked whether the rebuild could bump the counter back above zero — `create_window_size_dependent_resources()` (`device_resources.cpp:1212-1241`) submits nothing; it waits, abandons commands, and creates the colour target and swapchain. `timeline_value_` is still 0. No protection.
6. `bytes[i * 4 + …]` at `renderer.cpp:1234-1237` then reads a host mapping made by `vkMapMemory` at `device_resources.cpp:331` against a VkDevice that no longer exists.
7. `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback)` at `renderer.cpp:1240` — `device()` (`device_resources.h:335`) returns `owner_->device`, which is now the NEW device — and `destroy_vulkan_buffer` (`device_resources.cpp:337-360`) hands it the OLD `VkDeviceMemory` to `vkUnmapMemory`, the OLD `VkBuffer` to `vkDestroyBuffer`, the OLD memory to `vkFreeMemory`. Both halves confirmed.

THE RULE IS A RULE OF THIS CODEBASE
`present()` at `device_resources.cpp:1607-1615` is `if (!this->execute(current.acquired, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT, this->presentable_[...])) { … return; }` with the comment "The device went away inside that submit and everything has been rebuilt". That is the same contract honoured. The `std::ignore =` discard convention is real at every line cited: `device_resources.cpp:381, 385, 512, 1182, 1234, 1280, 1349, 1451, 1461` and `renderer.cpp:206, 228, 280, 1257, 1267`.

The comparison to the other backends confirms rather than weakens it. D3D11's `read_back_buffer` wraps `context->Map` in `ThrowIfFailed` (`d3d11/renderer.cpp:977`), so a removed device becomes an exception, and its ComPtrs keep the staging resource and device alive regardless. D3D12 holds the readback in a `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource>` (`d3d12/renderer.cpp:1296`). Vulkan's own `handle_device_lost` comment at `device_resources.cpp:1310-1314` names this exact difference: "anything still holding one of these … keeps the old device alive until it does, which is exactly the guarantee COM gives the D3D12 backend for free." `read_back_buffer` is the one place in this backend that takes that guarantee without paying for it.

REACHABILITY — the one soft link, and it does not break the finding
`Renderer::read_back_buffer` is public seam (`engine/render/renderer.h:480`); its only caller in this tree is `tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:496`. The trigger is a TDR or driver reset landing inside that one `vkQueueSubmit` — a hardware event, not caller-controllable, so no test can reach it deterministically. That bears on severity, not on truth: device loss is an event this backend is built to survive everywhere else, and this is the single place it does not.

*Correction:* Three corrections, none of which touch the conclusion.

1. SEVERITY, must-fix → should-fix. The defect and its undefined behaviour are exactly as described, but the path needs a hardware fault at one precise instant inside a function that renderer.h itself marks "NOT A FRAME-PATH CALL" and that no shipping client in this repository calls — `tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:496` is the only caller. Nothing in the frame path (begin_frame/submit/end_frame/present) is affected, and `present()` already guards the same hazard correctly. It should be fixed — a four-line check with the pattern already written three lines away in the same class — but it does not break any run that happens today.

2. The FIX section overreaches when it sweeps in "the two bare `this->execute();` calls at device_resources.cpp:1501 and 1525." I read both. They are the minimised branch and the no-swapchain-after-rebuild branch of `present()`, and each is followed only by `this->frame_index_ = (this->frame_index_ + 1) % FRAME_COUNT; return;`. Nothing after them touches the old device or any old handle, so a device loss there is fully absorbed by `handle_device_lost()`. The worst consequence is that `frame_index_`, reset to 0 by the rebuild, is then advanced to 1 — which frame is next, not a correctness problem. Adding `std::ignore =` there is a readability improvement, not a bug fix, and pairing them with line 1221 under one finding invites a reader to think three sites are broken when one is.

3. The finding is filed under area "docs". It is not a docs finding — it is a code defect in `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp`. The documentation it cites (`device_resources.h:287`) is correct as written; the code is what fails to honour it.

One thing the finding understates rather than overstates: on the device-lost path the readback buffer is the only child object still alive when `owner_.reset()` triggers `vkDestroyDevice` (`device_resources.cpp:225-241`), because `Impl::on_device_lost` at `renderer.cpp:703-711` has already freed everything else the renderer owns. So the violation begins one step earlier than the finding says — at `vkDestroyDevice` itself, not at the `readback.mapped` read.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried to kill this on four routes — the contract, the reachability, the "other backends do the same" defence, and the Vulkan rules invoked — and it survived all four.

THE DISCARD IS THERE AND IS UNMARKED. `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221` is a bare `device_resources.execute();`. It is the only call to `execute()` in that file (grep: `execute(` appears in the folder at device_resources.cpp:1368 (definition), :1501, :1525, :1607 and renderer.cpp:1221 only).

THE CONTRACT SAYS WHAT THE FINDING QUOTES. device_resources.h:287-291: "ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out." device_resources.cpp:1412-1419: `vkQueueSubmit(...)`, then `if (submitted == VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) { this->handle_device_lost(); return false; }`. The only caller that honours it is present(), device_resources.cpp:1607.

THE REBUILD REALLY DESTROYS THE DEVICE. handle_device_lost, device_resources.cpp:1265-1330: `notify_->on_device_lost()` (:1275) → Renderer::Impl::on_device_lost (renderer.cpp:703-711) destroys device-dependent resources and forwards to the shell, which empties the texture table; then destroy_swapchain/colour target/frames, render pass, upload pool, timeline, surface; then `this->owner_.reset();` (:1318), `timeline_value_ = 0;` (:1321), then create_device_resources() + create_window_size_dependent_resources() (:1323-1324). The only other holders of `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>` are VulkanTextures (backend.h:104, handed one at texture_factory.cpp:353), and those are exactly what on_device_lost releases — so the reset drops the last reference and `VulkanDevice::~VulkanDevice` (device_resources.cpp:225-241) runs `vkDestroyDevice`.

THE READBACK HAS NO KEEP-ALIVE. `create_vulkan_buffer(const VulkanDevice& owner, ...)` (device_resources.h:177, called at renderer.cpp:1184 with `device_resources.owner()`, which returns `*this->owner_` — a bare reference, device_resources.h:345). `struct VulkanBuffer` (device_resources.h:164-175) is four POD fields, no owner, no destructor. `mapped` is a live `vkMapMemory` pointer (device_resources.cpp:328-332).

SO THE FAILURE CHAIN IS AS DESCRIBED. `wait_for_gpu` early-outs on `timeline_value_ == 0` (device_resources.cpp:1673-1676), so nothing intervenes; renderer.cpp:1230-1238 dereferences `readback.mapped` after `vkDestroyDevice`; renderer.cpp:1240 calls `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback)` where `device()` (device_resources.h:335-338) now returns the NEW `owner_->device`, and destroy_vulkan_buffer (device_resources.cpp:337-361) hands the OLD VkDeviceMemory/VkBuffer to vkUnmapMemory/vkDestroyBuffer/vkFreeMemory on it.

THE VULKAN RULES CHECKED FROM THE SPEC, NOT FROM THE FINDING. (a) `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` is a documented return code of vkQueueSubmit, so the entry condition is real, not folklore. (b) VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-00378 — all child objects created on a device must be destroyed before vkDestroyDevice; the readback VkBuffer and VkDeviceMemory are live children at :1318, so the rebuild itself is already a violation and the mapping goes with the device. (c) The parent VUs — VUID-vkUnmapMemory-memory-parent, VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-parent, VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-parent — each require the handle to have come from the `device` argument, which is precisely what renderer.cpp:1240 breaks. All three hold at the 1.2 floor and apply to these objects. `recording_` is guaranteed true at :1221 (commands() is called at :1206 for the copy regardless of what transition_colour does), so execute() cannot early-out at :1371.

THE "OTHER BACKENDS DO THE SAME" DEFENCE FAILS. d3d12/renderer.cpp:1272-1355 has the same shape but a different outcome: `device_resources.wait_for_gpu()` (d3d12/device_resources.cpp:541-554) throws on a removed device rather than continuing, and its `readback` is a ComPtr whose COM reference keeps the resource alive. d3d11/renderer.cpp:957-977 routes CreateTexture2D and Map through ThrowIfFailed, so removal surfaces as an exception. The Vulkan header itself states the difference at device_resources.h:102-118 — the reference COM gives D3D12 for free "is supplied here by hand: every VulkanTexture holds a shared_ptr" — and read_back_buffer's buffer is the one device-owned object in the folder that was not given one. This is a Vulkan-specific gap, not a seam issue.

THE CONVENTION CITED IS REAL. I opened all nine sites at device_resources.cpp:381, 385, 512, 1182, 1234, 1280, 1349, 1451, 1461: every one is `std::ignore =` on a discarded return value (try_wait_for_gpu, vkDeviceWaitIdle, vkResetCommandPool, vkResetDescriptorPool, a messenger create). renderer.cpp:1221 is the only discarded return value in the folder that is not spelt that way.

SEVERITY CALIBRATED AGAINST THE REPO'S OWN REVIEW. docs/review/d3d12/README.md:89-310 puts two device-loss-path defects in "Must fix" — §2.2 (a throw on the removal path, plus terminate sites) and §2.3 (resources released before the GPU is idled). A use-after-free of mapped memory plus cross-device object destruction sits alongside those, so must-fix stands.

*Correction:* Three corrections, none fatal.

1. THE HARM IS ORDERED WRONG. "the caller silently receives garbage pixels rather than an error" is the benign branch, and it is the unlikely one. In the dominant case the last shared_ptr went at device_resources.cpp:1318, vkDestroyDevice ran, and the read at renderer.cpp:1230-1238 faults on unmapped pages — a crash, not garbage. Silent garbage requires some VulkanTexture to have outlived the shell's release and kept the old VulkanDevice alive, in which case the pixels are the pre-loss contents of a copy that never executed and renderer.cpp:1240 is still three parent-VU violations. Lead with the use-after-free and the cross-device destroy; the garbage-pixel wording undersells it.

2. THE `wait_for_gpu` STEP IS INCIDENTAL. The claim is correct as written (device_resources.cpp:1673-1676 early-outs on `timeline_value_ == 0`, which handle_device_lost set at :1321), but nothing turns on it: had it waited, it would have waited on the NEW timeline, which covers no work the readback cares about. The defect is the discarded bool and the missing keep-alive, not the wait.

3. THE TAIL OF THE FIX OVERREACHES. The two bare `this->execute();` at device_resources.cpp:1501 and 1525 are not the same defect. Both sit in present()'s no-swapchain paths, where nothing local survives the call to be used against the new device, so the discard there is defensible and only wants the `std::ignore =` spelling for consistency. The one real oddity at those sites is separate: handle_device_lost sets `frame_index_ = 0` (:1320) and the next line advances it to 1 against freshly created frames — noise, not a fault. Raising them alongside :1221 as "the same applies" conflates a use-after-free with a style point.

One thing the finding does not claim but that strengthens it: VulkanBuffer has no destructor (device_resources.h:164-175), so any throw between renderer.cpp:1184 and :1240 leaks the buffer and its memory — and `execute()`'s rebuild can throw, since create_device_resources goes through check_vk. Whatever fix lands should give the readback a scope-bound owner rather than a second manual destroy path.
