### C26. read_back_buffer reads mapped device memory after only a timeline-semaphore wait, with no memory dependency into the host domain

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1224`** · should-fix · `seam` · raised by R85 · run id `V45`

CLAIM: The vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer whose result read_back_buffer memcpys out is followed by no pipeline barrier to VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT / VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT. Waiting on the host for device work does not make device writes visible to the host; HOST_COHERENT removes the need for vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges, not the need for the availability/visibility operation.

EVIDENCE, verbatim and verified at renderer.cpp:1205-1238:

```
    vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer(device_resources.commands(),
        device_resources.colour_target(),
        VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, readback.buffer, 1, &copy);
    ...
    if (previous != VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED) { device_resources.transition_colour(previous); }
    device_resources.execute();
    // It stalls on the GPU by construction, and the seam says so.
    device_resources.wait_for_gpu();
    ...
    const unsigned char* bytes =
        static_cast<const unsigned char*>(readback.mapped);
```

readback is created HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT and permanently mapped (renderer.cpp:1183-1187); wait_for_gpu is a plain vkWaitSemaphores on the timeline (device_resources.cpp:1671-1686). No vkCmdPipelineBarrier naming HOST appears anywhere in engine/render/vulkan/.

RULE BROKEN: the Vulkan synchronisation chapter, quoted by the lens: "Signaling a fence and waiting on the host does not guarantee that the results of memory accesses will be visible to the host, as the access scope of a memory dependency defined by a fence only includes device access. A memory barrier or other memory dependency must be used to guarantee this." The same applies to a timeline semaphore wait. This file's own habit elsewhere is to record the barrier the layout implies (transition_colour, device_resources.cpp:1708-1722); here nothing is recorded at all. Every other host-touched buffer in this backend goes the other way - host writes before vkQueueSubmit, which the host-write ordering guarantee does cover - so this is the backend's only device-to-host read and the only place that needs it.

FAILURE SCENARIO: RenderPixelTests under x64-debug-vulkan on an implementation that does not implicitly flush transfer writes into the host domain at queue completion: the memcpy loop at renderer.cpp:1231-1238 reads whatever was in the mapped allocation before the copy landed - the previous frame, or uninitialised bytes - and golden::check_frame compares that against the checked-in PNG. This is the single channel through which all fifty golden comparisons and every at(x, y) assertion in pixel_tests.cpp observe this backend, so the symptom is a whole frame wrong, or intermittently wrong, with no other diagnostic. CI does not rasterise the Vulkan preset, so a developer's machine is the only place it would ever show.

FIX: Record the dependency before submitting. Between the vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer at renderer.cpp:1205 and device_resources.execute() at :1221, add vkCmdPipelineBarrier(commands, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT, 0, ...) carrying a VkBufferMemoryBarrier on readback.buffer with srcAccessMask = VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT and dstAccessMask = VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT (a plain VkMemoryBarrier with the same masks would do).

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this on four fronts — the quoted evidence, an incidentally-covering barrier, an unreachable failure path, and the Vulkan rule itself — and it survived all four.

EVIDENCE, checked character for character. `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` is at engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1206 (finding says 1205 — off by one, text is identical), `device_resources.execute()` at :1221, `device_resources.wait_for_gpu()` at :1224 under the comment "It stalls on the GPU by construction, and the seam says so.", and the memcpy loop reads `static_cast<const unsigned char*>(readback.mapped)` at :1231. The readback buffer is created at renderer.cpp:1183-1188 with `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT | VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT` and `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`. `DeviceResources::wait_for_gpu` (engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1671-1686) is exactly a `vkWaitSemaphores` on `this->timeline_` and nothing else.

NO BARRIER EXISTS. `grep -rn "HOST_BIT\|HOST_READ\|HOST_WRITE\|vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges"` over engine/render/vulkan/ returns nothing at all. `DeviceResources::execute` (device_resources.cpp:1368-1432) records no barrier — it is `vkEndCommandBuffer`, a timeline increment, and `vkQueueSubmit`. The four `vkDeviceWaitIdle` calls in the backend (device_resources.cpp:385, 1182, 1234, 1280) are all in the destructor, resize and device-loss paths; none is in read_back_buffer's chain, and a device-wait-idle would carry the same fence-like semantics anyway.

THE ONE BARRIER THAT IS RECORDED CANNOT COVER IT. `transition_colour(previous)` at renderer.cpp:1216-1219 does record a `vkCmdPipelineBarrier` (device_resources.cpp:1715-1719), but it is a `VkImageMemoryBarrier` on `colour_image_` with `srcAccessMask = access_of(TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL) = VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT` and `dstStage = stage_of(COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL) = VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT` (device_resources.cpp:53-91, 93-110). An image barrier's access scopes are limited to that image's subresources, so it cannot reach the buffer's `TRANSFER_WRITE` even incidentally, and no mask in it names HOST.

THE FAILURE PATH IS REACHABLE. `read_back_buffer` has exactly one real caller: `Harness::read_frame` at tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:493-498, which every `end()` in the file routes through (the comment at :505 says so in as many words). No engine or sample code calls it. `ls tests/render/golden/*.png` is 50 files — the finding's "all fifty golden comparisons" is exact. And .github/workflows/ci.yml:89-91 sets `x64-debug-vulkan` with `skip_tests: '-E RenderPixelTests'`, so the finding's "CI does not rasterise the Vulkan preset" is confirmed from the workflow.

THE ONLY DEVICE-TO-HOST READ. Every other use of `.mapped` in the backend is a host write before submit — renderer.cpp:589 (index staging), :958 and :960 (vertex/transform ring), texture_factory.cpp:237 (texture staging). renderer.cpp:1231 is the sole read, so the finding's framing is right.

THE RULE. The quoted note is real Vulkan spec text from the fence section, and its mechanism — the memory dependency's second access scope is empty, so no visibility operation into the host domain occurs — applies identically to a timeline `vkWaitSemaphores`. `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT` is specified in terms of the host cache management commands `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges`/`vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges`; it removes the invalidate, not the barrier. Khronos's own synchronization examples give this exact readback pattern a barrier with `dstStageMask = VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT`, `dstAccessMask = VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT`, with no carve-out for coherent memory.

WHY IT IS PLAUSIBLY AN OVERSIGHT RATHER THAN A DECISION. engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp:1272-1327 is the structural template — same "Made per call and thrown away" comment, same "PUT BACK WHERE IT WAS", same "It stalls on the GPU by construction". In D3D12 the fence wait plus Map genuinely is sufficient; the one thing Vulkan requires that D3D12 has no concept of is precisely the missing host barrier. And this backend argues every decision it makes at length — `grep -i host` over the vulkan headers and renderer.cpp turns up no argument for the omission, in a file whose own barrier helper is prefaced (device_resources.cpp:48-52) with "a barrier whose source mask does not match the layout it is leaving is the class of mistake that produces a frame that is right on one driver and torn on another."

The fix as proposed is sound and may be placed anywhere between renderer.cpp:1206 and :1221; a plain `VkMemoryBarrier` is the better spelling, since the access scopes need to be global to reach the buffer.

*Correction:* Three mechanism details are wrong; none touches the conclusion.

1. "the previous frame, or uninitialised bytes" — the previous-frame half is unreachable. `readback` is a fresh `vkCreateBuffer` + `vkAllocateMemory` per call (renderer.cpp:1183-1188) and is destroyed at renderer.cpp:1240, so no prior frame's pixels can live in it. Only stale/uninitialised bytes of the new allocation are reachable, which means the symptom is garbage rather than a plausible-looking wrong frame.

2. "here nothing is recorded at all" is loose. A barrier IS recorded after the copy — `transition_colour(previous)` at renderer.cpp:1216-1219 — it is simply the wrong barrier on the wrong resource (image barrier on `colour_image_`, `TRANSFER_READ` to `COLOR_ATTACHMENT_WRITE|READ`, device_resources.cpp:1715-1719). The accurate statement is that nothing naming the buffer or the host domain is recorded.

3. "permanently mapped" describes the per-frame vertex/transform buffers, not this one. The readback is mapped at creation (device_resources.cpp:328-331) and unmapped by `destroy_vulkan_buffer` within the same call (device_resources.cpp:345-348).

On severity: should-fix stands, but for a different reason than the finding gives, and the finding oversells one thing while underselling another. It oversells the practical risk — no desktop implementation this repository builds against is known to fail this, and `read_back_buffer` has no engine or sample caller (tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:493-498 is the only one), so the worst case today is a wrong test result and not a shipped rendering defect. That is what keeps it off must-fix. It undersells the reason it matters: CLAUDE.md puts this backend here because it "reaches Android, Linux and, through MoltenVK, the Apple platforms", and mobile tilers and MoltenVK are exactly the implementation class where host-domain assumptions stop being free. A latent spec violation sitting on the sole channel through which all 50 golden comparisons observe this backend, on the platforms the backend was added to reach, with a two-line fix, is should-fix rather than minor.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this on four fronts — hidden barrier, an implicit spec guarantee, folklore rule, and "the other backends do it too" — and it survived all four.

CODE, verified at HEAD (4d91b91):
- `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1184-1189` creates the readback buffer HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT, TRANSFER_DST only; `device_resources.cpp:328-332` maps it permanently at creation and it is never invalidated (`vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` appears nowhere in the tree).
- `renderer.cpp:1206-1208` records `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` into it. The only thing recorded afterwards is `transition_colour(previous)` at `renderer.cpp:1216-1219`, which is `device_resources.cpp:1706-1723` — an image barrier on the colour image between `stage_of(old)` and `stage_of(new)`, i.e. device-domain stages only, and not naming the readback buffer at all. When `previous == VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED` nothing is recorded at all.
- `renderer.cpp:1221` → `DeviceResources::execute` (`device_resources.cpp:1368-1432`) is a plain `vkQueueSubmit` with **no fence** (`device_resources.cpp:1411-1412` passes `VK_NULL_HANDLE`) that signals the timeline.
- `renderer.cpp:1224` → `wait_for_gpu` (`device_resources.cpp:1668-1686`) is a bare `vkWaitSemaphores` on the timeline.
- `renderer.cpp:1230-1238` then memcpys straight out of `readback.mapped`.
- Grep confirms the negative: the only five `vkCmdPipelineBarrier` calls in the backend are `device_resources.cpp:1554,1603,1718` and `texture_factory.cpp:283,297`, none with `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT`; grep for `HOST` in `engine/render/vulkan/` returns only error strings, memory-property flags and the property test at `device_resources.cpp:328`. No host-domain dependency exists anywhere in the backend.

THE RULE, stated from the specification rather than from the finding. Vulkan's memory model (§7.9, unchanged 1.0→1.4, so it holds at the 1.2 floor) separates availability from domain: device writes must be made available, and then a *memory domain operation* must move them from the device domain to the host domain before the host may read them. That domain operation is performed by a memory dependency whose dst stage mask includes `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT` and whose dst access mask includes `VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT` — and only by that. The spec states the consequence explicitly in the fence section: "Signaling a fence and waiting on the host does not guarantee that the results of memory accesses will be visible to the host, as the access scope of a memory dependency defined by a fence only includes device access. A memory barrier or other memory dependency must be used to guarantee this." A semaphore is no better: a signal operation's first access scope is all device memory accesses and its **second access scope is empty**; a wait operation's first access scope is empty. Neither reaches the host domain. `HOST_COHERENT` is defined as removing the need for `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges`/`vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` — the host cache-management commands — which is the second of the two steps, not the first. This is also the exact case in Khronos' own synchronization examples ("CPU read back data written by the GPU": src TRANSFER/TRANSFER_WRITE → dst HOST/HOST_READ). So the rule the finding invokes is real, current, and says what the finding needs it to say.

NOT REACHABLE-ONLY-IN-THEORY: `tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:493-497` routes every frame in `RenderPixelTests` through `submit()` then `read_back_buffer()`, so this is the sole channel through which every golden comparison and every `at(x,y)` assertion observes this backend. Validation layers — the way MEMORY.md records this backend was checked — do not instrument a memcpy through a persistent mapping, so the check that was run could not have caught it.

NOT A SEAM FINDING: the sibling backends each perform their own API's host-visibility step. `d3d12/renderer.cpp:1338-1341` maps the readback resource with an explicit read range `{0, total_bytes}`, which is precisely D3D12's cache-invalidation mechanism, and unmaps with `{0,0}` at :1354-1355; GL's path is `glReadPixels`, synchronous by definition. Every other host-visible allocation in the Vulkan backend (`renderer.cpp:585-586`, `device_resources.cpp:1754,1777`, `texture_factory.cpp:233`) is host-write-then-submit, which the host write ordering guarantee at `vkQueueSubmit` genuinely does cover. This really is the backend's only device-write→host-read, and the only one missing the step.

Nor is it a decision the file made and defended: grep for "coherent", "invalidate", "host domain", "HOST_READ" across `engine/render/vulkan/*.h` finds nothing on this subject, in a backend whose habit is to write down every such choice (`device_resources.h:466-476` explains the mid-frame submit in detail and says nothing about visibility).

*Correction:* Three corrections, none of which touch the conclusion.

1. Mechanism, sharpened: the finding quotes the spec's *fence* note, but there is no fence anywhere in this path — `execute()` passes `VK_NULL_HANDLE` as the fence at `device_resources.cpp:1411-1412` and the wait is `vkWaitSemaphores` on the timeline (`device_resources.cpp:1668-1686`). The fence note therefore applies by analogy rather than directly. The direct argument is the access scopes of semaphore operations: a signal's second access scope is empty and a wait's first access scope is empty, so no device-to-host memory domain operation is defined by either. Same conclusion, stronger footing.

2. Line drift, immaterial: `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` is at `renderer.cpp:1206-1208`, not :1205 (blank); the buffer creation is :1184-1189, not :1183-1187; `wait_for_gpu` begins at `device_resources.cpp:1668`; `transition_colour` is :1706-1723.

3. Failure scenario, slightly overstated: the readback buffer is allocated fresh at `renderer.cpp:1184` and destroyed at :1240, so a stale read yields whatever a recycled allocation holds — plausibly the previous read-back's bytes given the identical size, but "the previous frame" is not guaranteed. "Stale or uninitialised" is the accurate wording.

Severity holds at should-fix rather than must-fix: on the desktop drivers `x64-debug-vulkan` runs against today, queue completion does in practice flush transfer writes to memory, which is why the goldens pass — the exposure is a spec-legal staleness the implementation is permitted to exhibit, on a path the seam itself calls "NOT A FRAME-PATH CALL" (`renderer.h:477-480`). It is not minor either: this backend exists in this tree specifically to reach Android and, via MoltenVK, the Apple platforms (CLAUDE.md; docs/port/android.md), and MoltenVK's `synchronizeResource` for managed-storage buffers is emitted in response to exactly the host barrier that is missing here — so this is the one omission most likely to turn into garbage pixels on the platforms the port was argued for, with no diagnostic and no CI coverage. The fix the finding gives (a `VkMemoryBarrier` or `VkBufferMemoryBarrier`, `TRANSFER` → `HOST`, `TRANSFER_WRITE` → `HOST_READ`, recorded between :1208 and :1221) is correct as written.

### C27. Every VulkanBuffer local leaks its VkBuffer and VkDeviceMemory on any throw, including in the catch block whose own comment says every failure puts everything back

**`engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:230`** · should-fix · `core` · raised by R25, R39, R42, R53, R165, R49 · run id `V6`

SIX LENSES (memory, lifetimes, texture-upload, errors, degenerate, readback) on the same class of defect, three sites. VulkanBuffer is a plain aggregate with no destructor (device_resources.h:164-175). texture_factory.cpp:208-211 states the rule: 'FROM HERE THE IMAGE IS OWNED BY NOBODY UNTIL THE LAST LINE, so every failure between the two has to put it back. There is no ComPtr in this API and no destructor to lean on'. In-repo the consequence is one leak per failure plus a vkDestroyDevice run with live children during unwind. The repeated-leak scaling depends on ColourWars, which is out of this tree, so treat it as a possible amplifier rather than an established one. This is why should-fix is the right rank and must-fix is not: nothing here reaches the leak without an OOM or a device loss.

*Correction:* Three corrections; none of them saves the code.

1. The accumulation in the failure scenario is not reachable. "a device that keeps failing leaks one per texture per attempt" is wrong: ResourceLoader::reload_device_resources (assets/resource_loader.cpp:96-108) has no catch, so the first throw ends the replay loop after one leak, and no caller retries - Application::on_device_restored (app/application.cpp:428-439) does not catch, and the only catches in engine/ and samples/ are resource_loader.cpp:152 (sound banks only), core/thread_pool.cpp:144, and the two mains (samples/minimal/main.cpp:48, samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49), which print and return 1. The true cost is bounded at one VkBuffer plus one VkDeviceMemory per process, on a path that is already terminating. The consequence that survives is the teardown one: unwinding out of main destroys the Application local, which reaches VulkanDevice::~VulkanDevice (device_resources.cpp:239) and calls vkDestroyDevice with a live child - VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-00378, an error the debug build's validation layers (device_resources.cpp:451-467) are configured to report.

2. The comment is paraphrased more strongly than it reads. texture_factory.cpp:208-211 states the rule about the IMAGE ("FROM HERE THE IMAGE IS OWNED BY NOBODY UNTIL THE LAST LINE, so every failure between the two has to put it back"), and the catch's own comment at :332-335 is about the table, not about everything being released. The finding's "the catch block whose own comment says every failure puts everything back" is not what either comment says. The rule extends fairly to the staging buffer - it is in the identical position - but quote it as it stands.

3. There is a fourth site of the same class the finding does not name: create_vulkan_buffer (device_resources.cpp:286-334) undoes only the vkAllocateMemory failure (:314-319); a throw from vkBindBufferMemory (:321) or from vkMapMemory (:330) strands both the VkBuffer and the VkDeviceMemory it just made. The proposed owning holder fixes that one too, which makes the holder the better of the two suggested fixes rather than merely the tidier.

Severity holds at should-fix, but for the spec-conformance reason rather than the memory-exhaustion one: the leak makes the eventual vkDestroyDevice a VUID violation in a backend whose debug configuration exists to catch exactly that, and the file states the rule twenty lines above breaking it.

### C28. Vulkan::Vulkan is linked PUBLIC, putting the SDK's include directory on every consumer's command line and opening a hole check_engine_includes.cmake cannot see

**`engine/CMakeLists.txt:184`** · minor · `build` · raised by R100 · run id `V65`

> Raised as should-fix; a refuter corrected it to minor.

CLAIM: engine/CMakeLists.txt:183-184 links the Vulkan imported target PUBLIC, so $VULKAN_SDK/Include becomes a usage requirement of LabradorEngine and lands on the command line of every sample, every test and every downstream client — the exact leak the rapidjson paragraph 35 lines below rejects, and the one way a graphics API can escape the backend seam without any file naming a backend header.

EVIDENCE. engine/CMakeLists.txt:183-184:

```
    find_package(Vulkan REQUIRED)
    target_link_libraries(LabradorEngine PUBLIC Vulkan::Vulkan)
```

engine/CMakeLists.txt:219-227, same file: "rapidjson is PRIVATE and SYSTEM. It used to be PUBLIC, so a sample that / parses nothing still had a JSON parser's headers on its command line, and / their warnings were measured against /W4 /WX. // PRIVATE now means what it says: assets/json.h hands out JsonDocument and / JsonValue, whose only rapidjson is a void* recovered inside json.cpp, so no / engine header names the parser and no client needs it to include one."
CMake's FindVulkan defines Vulkan::Vulkan as an IMPORTED target carrying INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES (${Vulkan_INCLUDE_DIRS}), so PUBLIC propagates the include path. That is a real behavioural difference from the three sibling branches this line was copied from — `PUBLIC d3d11 dxgi dxguid` (line 111), `PUBLIC d3d12 dxgi dxguid` (line 138), `PUBLIC opengl32` (line 160) — which are bare library names with no usage requirements at all, so PUBLIC and PRIVATE are indistinguishable there. This is the first backend whose link line carries a header path, which is precisely what the block's own comment (engine/CMakeLists.txt:175-182, "THE ONLY BACKEND WHOSE DEPENDENCY IS NOT ALREADY ON THE MACHINE") says makes it special — and it then treats it identically.

RULE. CLAUDE.md and ARCHITECTURE: "Everything a backend owns lives in render/<backend>/. Nothing outside that folder includes anything from it" — plus this file's own stated rapidjson policy.

FAILURE. Configure x64-debug-vulkan. Add `#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>` and a vkCreateInstance call to engine/app/application.h, to samples/minimal/*.cpp, or to ColourWars' client code. Everything compiles and links. cmake/check_engine_includes.cmake cannot catch it: the second-wall regex at line 82 is `^[  ]*#[  ]*include[  ]*[\"<](\.\./)*(engine/)?render/[A-Za-z0-9_]+/[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.h[\">]` (verified in the tree), which `<vulkan/vulkan.h>` does not match. The graphics API is then above the seam with no file naming a backend header. Switch to x64-debug and the same tree stops compiling — the backend choice, which the seam exists to hide, has become visible above it via the build.

FIX. `target_link_libraries(LabradorEngine PRIVATE Vulkan::Vulkan)`. For a STATIC library CMake records PRIVATE entries as $<LINK_ONLY:Vulkan::Vulkan> in INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES, so vulkan-1.lib still reaches every executable's link line; only the include directory stops propagating, and no engine header outside engine/render/vulkan/ names a Vulkan type. Note the asymmetry with the d3d11/d3d12/gl lines in a comment, since those are PUBLIC only because it makes no difference there.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

The mechanical claim survives, verified end to end, but two of its supporting arguments do not.

VERIFIED TRUE. engine/CMakeLists.txt:183-184 is exactly as quoted: `find_package(Vulkan REQUIRED)` then `target_link_libraries(LabradorEngine PUBLIC Vulkan::Vulkan)`. CMake's FindVulkan (CMake 4.3, at .../VS18/Common7/IDE/CommonExtensions/Microsoft/CMake/CMake/share/cmake-4.3/Modules/FindVulkan.cmake:720-725) creates `add_library(Vulkan::Vulkan UNKNOWN IMPORTED)` with `INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${Vulkan_INCLUDE_DIRS}"`, so PUBLIC does put $VULKAN_SDK/Include on every consumer's command line. The consumers exist and link the engine: samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:23-26 (`target_link_libraries(MinimalSample PRIVATE LabradorEngine ...)`), tests/render/CMakeLists.txt:20-24 and :79-93. Since x64-debug-vulkan configures and builds green (CMakePresets.json:45-52, CLAUDE.md's 12-entry table), the imported target resolves in those sibling directory scopes, so its usage requirements really do reach them. check_engine_includes.cmake:82's second-wall regex is character-for-character as the finding quotes it (`^[  ]*#[  ]*include[  ]*["<](\.\./)*(engine/)?render/[A-Za-z0-9_]+/[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.h[">]`) and cannot match `<vulkan/vulkan.h>` — no `render/` segment. The failure scenario is constructible from a real entry point: add `#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>` to samples/minimal/main.cpp under x64-debug-vulkan and it resolves and links; under x64-debug it stops compiling.

THE FIX IS SOUND. No engine header outside engine/render/vulkan/ names a Vulkan type — grepping `\bVk[A-Z]` across the tree outside that folder yields exactly three hits, all inside comments: engine/render/renderer.h:421 ("a VkCommandPool may not"), engine/render/render_resources.h:135 ("A VkImage is a handle"), tests/render/renderer_seam_tests.cpp:54 ("a VkDevice"). No `#include <vulkan/...>` exists anywhere outside engine/render/vulkan/. So PRIVATE would not break a compile, and for a STATIC library CMake still records `$<LINK_ONLY:Vulkan::Vulkan>` in INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES so vulkan-1.lib keeps reaching every executable. FindVulkan's own documented example, FindVulkan.cmake:300 and :307, is `target_link_libraries(project_target PRIVATE Vulkan::Vulkan)`.

THE FILE'S POLICY IS REAL AND APPLIED ELSEWHERE WITH INTENT. engine/CMakeLists.txt:219-230 makes rapidjson PRIVATE because no engine header names it; engine/CMakeLists.txt:232 keeps `Microsoft::DirectXTK` PUBLIC, and that one is justified — engine/app/application.h:19, engine/assets/resource_loader.h:7, engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.h:4 and engine/audio/sound_bank.h:3 all `#include <Audio.h>`, so a consumer genuinely needs the path. Vulkan is in rapidjson's position, not DirectXTK's, and is spelt like DirectXTK's. That is a genuine deviation from the file's own demonstrated rule.

WHAT THE FINDING GETS WRONG. (1) It invokes the rapidjson paragraph's stated harm — "their warnings were measured against /W4 /WX" — but that does not transfer. Include directories coming from the interface of a consumed IMPORTED target are treated as system directories by default (CMake docs, Help/prop_tgt/NO_SYSTEM_FROM_IMPORTED.rst:1-7), so the Vulkan headers arrive as external/system includes and their warnings are not measured against /W4 /WX. Only the second half of that paragraph — "no engine header names the parser and no client needs it to include one" — applies. (2) "the one way a graphics API can escape the backend seam without any file naming a backend header" is false. d3d11.h, d3d12.h, dxgi.h and gl/GL.h live in the Windows SDK (verified present at C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/Include/10.0.26100.0/um/d3d11.h and .../um/gl/GL.h), which is unconditionally on every MSVC command line regardless of any target_link_libraries line, and engine/CMakeLists.txt:109/:137/:159 propagate d3d11/d3d12/dxgi/opengl32 PUBLIC. So under x64-debug a sample can already `#include <d3d11.h>`, call D3D11CreateDevice, compile AND link, with no file naming a backend header and check_engine_includes silent — the identical escape, in the default configuration, since before this commit. Vulkan makes a fourth API reachable that way; it does not open the class of hole, and the "first backend whose link line carries a header path" observation, while literally true, does not carry the consequence the finding hangs on it.

NET. The defect is really there and the one-word fix is correct, but nothing in the tree exploits it, no compile/link/runtime behaviour is wrong today, there is no warning exposure, and the seam-escape it enables already exists three other ways that no build change can close. That is hygiene against the file's own stated policy, not a should-fix consequence.

*Correction:* Mechanism and fix stand; the severity rationale does not. Two claims must be struck. First, the /W4 /WX half of the rapidjson analogy is wrong: an IMPORTED target's INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES are treated as SYSTEM by default (NO_SYSTEM_FROM_IMPORTED), so unlike rapidjson's plain path the Vulkan headers are not measured against the warning settings. Only "no engine header names it, so no client needs it" survives — and that half is verified: the sole Vk mentions outside engine/render/vulkan/ are comments at engine/render/renderer.h:421, engine/render/render_resources.h:135 and tests/render/renderer_seam_tests.cpp:54. Second, "the one way a graphics API can escape the backend seam" is wrong: d3d11.h/d3d12.h/dxgi.h/gl/GL.h ship in the Windows SDK and are on every MSVC command line unconditionally, and engine/CMakeLists.txt:109/:137/:159 propagate the matching import libraries PUBLIC, so under x64-debug a sample can already include <d3d11.h> and link D3D11CreateDevice with check_engine_includes silent. The Vulkan line widens an existing, unclosable class of hole to a fourth API rather than opening a new one — which is why this is minor rather than should-fix. The remaining case for fixing it is the file's own demonstrated policy (rapidjson PRIVATE at :219-230 because nothing names it, Microsoft::DirectXTK PUBLIC at :232 because engine/app/application.h:19 includes <Audio.h>) and FindVulkan's own documented usage at FindVulkan.cmake:300, which is PRIVATE. The proposed fix is safe as written: PRIVATE on a STATIC library still records $<LINK_ONLY:Vulkan::Vulkan>, so vulkan-1.lib keeps reaching every executable's link line.

Everything past that fails.

1. "THE ONE WAY A GRAPHICS API CAN ESCAPE THE SEAM" IS FALSE, AND THE FINDING QUOTES ITS OWN REFUTATION. engine/CMakeLists.txt:109 (`PUBLIC d3d11 dxgi dxguid`), :137 (`PUBLIC d3d12 dxgi dxguid`) and :159 (`PUBLIC opengl32`) link those import libraries PUBLIC to every consumer. It is the opposite: indistinguishable means the hole is unclosable there, and it is standing open on three of five backends.

2. THE FIX DOES NOT CLOSE THE HOLE, BY THE FINDING'S OWN ADMISSION. A consumer therefore recovers the entire escape with one line of its own — `find_package(Vulkan)` — against a library the engine still hands it. What PRIVATE buys is that a would-be violator must type one extra line. That is not a hole closed.

THE WALL IS NOT FAULTED FOR WHAT IT CLAIMS. check_engine_includes.cmake:70-74 states in its own words that it is "Deliberately not a compiler error" and that "there is no include path that admits it there and refuses it next door". Further, CMakeLists.txt:21 sets `-DENGINE_DIR=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/engine`, so the wall never scanned samples/ or tests/ for any backend — half the stated failure scenario ("add it to samples/minimal/*.cpp", "to ColourWars' client code") is outside its territory by design, not by this line's fault.

4. THE RAPIDJSON PARAGRAPH IS BORROWED WITHOUT ITS HARM, AND THE SAME FILE CONTRADICTS THE GENERALISATION THREE LINES BELOW IT. The harm engine/CMakeLists.txt:219-221 names is "their warnings were measured against /W4 /WX" — rapidjson was a hand-written plain include path (now SYSTEM PRIVATE at :228-230). Vulkan::Vulkan is an IMPORTED target, and CMake treats an imported target's INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES as system includes by default (NO_SYSTEM_FROM_IMPORTED defaults off), so cmake/settings.cmake's /W4 /WX exposure does not arise. And this file's actual policy is plainly "PUBLIC when a public header needs it", not "no imported target may be PUBLIC": engine/CMakeLists.txt:232 links `Microsoft::DirectXTK` PUBLIC — a vcpkg imported target carrying its own INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES — because engine/app/application.h:19, engine/assets/resource_loader.h:7, engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.h:4 and engine/audio/sound_bank.h:3 all include `<Audio.h>`. So "a third-party imported target's include dir on every consumer's command line" is what the file deliberately does immediately below the paragraph cited as forbidding it.

5. NO CONSEQUENCE AT HEAD. Nothing outside engine/render/vulkan/ includes a Vulkan header. There is no install() or export() anywhere in the tree (grep over all CMakeLists.txt and *.cmake returns nothing), so no exported package config bakes in a stale absolute SDK path. The include arrives as a system include, so no warning exposure. Vulkan is not in vcpkg.json, so nothing else can supply the header behind the engine's back either. The claimed defect is entirely a hypothetical about a future author deliberately writing a seam violation that the build already permits three other ways and will still permit after the fix.

CLAUDE.md's own statement of how this boundary is held — "the walls are include discipline plus review" — is what actually governs here, and check_engine_includes.cmake:70-74 says the same thing about this specific wall.

*Correction:* What survives is an accurate but consequence-free observation, not the defect claimed. It is true that PUBLIC is unnecessary on engine/CMakeLists.txt:184 — only engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:13 names a Vulkan header — and changing the word to PRIVATE would be harmless one-word tidying that keeps vulkan-1.lib on every link line. But it closes nothing: the same escape survives via `find_package(Vulkan)` in any consumer, and it is standing wide open on d3d11, d3d12 and gl (engine/CMakeLists.txt:109, :137, :159) where the Windows SDK puts the headers on every command line unconditionally and PRIVATE could not change it. Anyone raising this again should raise it as a five-backend consistency question about how the seam is actually held, not as a Vulkan build defect — and should expect the answer check_engine_includes.cmake:70-74 already gives, that this wall is a grep over backend-header includes on purpose because no include path can admit "engine/render/vulkan/backend.h" inside the folder and refuse it next door.

**Adjudicator** — the two disagreed, so a third read the code. *confirmed*

MECHANICS — CONFIRMED, and confirmed harder than either refuter managed. engine/CMakeLists.txt:183-184 is `find_package(Vulkan REQUIRED)` / `target_link_libraries(LabradorEngine PUBLIC Vulkan::Vulkan)`. FindVulkan.cmake:721-724 (CMake 4.3, VS18 Community install) creates `add_library(Vulkan::Vulkan UNKNOWN IMPORTED)` with `INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${Vulkan_INCLUDE_DIRS}"`. I did not have to reason about whether that reaches consumers across directory scopes: out/build/x64-debug-vulkan/build.ninja already exists, and MinimalSample's own main.cpp compile statement (build.ninja:1087-1092) carries `-external:IC:\VulkanSDK\1.4.357.0\include`. 142 compile lines in that file carry it — samples/minimal, samples/linesweeper, every tests/* target, bench. rapidjson does NOT appear on that same sample line (it is on the engine's own TUs only, engine/CMakeLists.txt:228-230). So the file applies its stated policy to one third-party dependency and not to the other, and the difference is visible in the generated build.

THE FINDING'S TWO SUPPORTING ARGUMENTS ARE BOTH FALSE, and both refuters are right about that. (1) The /W4 /WX harm named in the rapidjson comment (engine/CMakeLists.txt:219-221) does not transfer: the same ninja line shows the Vulkan path arriving as `-external:I` alongside `-external:W0` while `/W4 /WX` apply to the engine-root `-I` paths only. NO_SYSTEM_FROM_IMPORTED.rst:1-12 in the same CMake install states the rule — SYSTEM defaults true for imported targets. Zero warning exposure, measured not inferred. (2) "the one way a graphics API can escape the backend seam" is plainly false: d3d11.h, d3d12.h and gl/GL.h are present at C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/Include/10.0.26100.0/um/, unconditionally on every MSVC command line, and engine/CMakeLists.txt:109/:137/:159 hand the matching import libraries to every consumer PUBLIC. Under x64-debug a sample can already include <d3d11_1.h>, call D3D11CreateDevice, compile and link, with check_engine_includes.cmake silent. The class of hole is three backends old and no CMake word can close it.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHY IT IS NOT NOTHING. The claim in the finding's headline — Vulkan::Vulkan is PUBLIC and puts the SDK include directory on every consumer's command line — is true, verified, and unnecessary. Only engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:13 includes <vulkan/vulkan.h>; the sole `Vk*` mentions outside that folder are three comments (engine/render/renderer.h:421, engine/render/render_resources.h:135, tests/render/renderer_seam_tests.cpp:54). FindVulkan's own documented example (FindVulkan.cmake:300, :307) is PRIVATE. The fix is safe as written: for a STATIC library PRIVATE is recorded as $<LINK_ONLY:Vulkan::Vulkan>, so vulkan-1.lib keeps reaching every executable, and the name resolves in the same scope it resolves in today. And the propagated directory is not merely vulkan/ — $VULKAN_SDK/Include also holds dxc, glslang, shaderc, slang, spirv, spirv_cross, spirv-tools and vk_video, so every sample and test is handed a shader-toolchain's headers by name. Neither refuter noticed that.

WHERE I PART FROM REFUTER B. B's decisive argument is "the fix does not close the hole, therefore not-a-finding" — a consumer can write its own find_package(Vulkan). That proves too much: the same is true of rapidjson, and this file deliberately made rapidjson PRIVATE anyway (:219-227), so the file itself rejects that reasoning. B's point 4 also inverts: Microsoft::DirectXTK PUBLIC at :232 does not contradict the policy, it IS the policy — engine/app/application.h:19, engine/assets/resource_loader.h:7, engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.h:4 and engine/audio/sound_bank.h:3 all include <Audio.h>, so a consumer genuinely needs that path. Vulkan fails the same test, which is exactly what the finding says. B is right that every stated harm is wrong; B is wrong that nothing is left. Refuter A gets the disposition right.

WHERE I PART FROM THE FINDING. should-fix is unearned. Nothing at HEAD includes a Vulkan header outside the folder, there is no install()/export() anywhere in the source tree (the only hits are generated cmake_install.cmake under out/), Vulkan is absent from vcpkg.json so no stale absolute path is baked into anything shipped, and the include is SYSTEM so /W4 /WX never sees it. Nothing compiles, links or runs differently. check_engine_includes.cmake:70-74 says in its own words that this wall is deliberately not a compiler error and that "there is no include path that admits it there and refuses it next door" — so faulting line 184 for a hole that grep was never built to see is faulting the wrong artefact. This is a one-word deviation from the file's own demonstrated rule, worth fixing when the file is next touched, with the d3d11/d3d12/gl asymmetry noted in a comment because in this repository that comment is the actual deliverable. Minor.

### C29. renderer.h states 'presenting discards the back buffer' as a flat term of the seam, and the backend this commit added makes it false

**`engine/render/renderer.h:473`** · minor · `tests` · raised by R117 · run id `V80`

> Raised as should-fix; a refuter corrected it to minor.

CLAIM: the seam header gives one flat reason for the read_back_buffer interval, the new test case declares that same reason backend-specific, and on the Vulkan backend the reason is simply false — neither was amended.

EVIDENCE (verified). engine/render/renderer.h:473-474: '// BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame(). Presenting discards the back // buffer's contents, so after end_frame there is nothing left to read.' tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:1750-1752, added by this commit: 'What a present does to the buffer it presented is // a backend's business and differs - two of the four discard it -'. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1533-1600: present() blits or copies `this->colour_image_` INTO a swapchain image and its only change to the colour target is `transition_colour(VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL)`; engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1206-1208 reads back from that same `device_resources.colour_target()`. So on Vulkan the contents survive end_frame, exactly because the engine owns the image (device_resources.h:31-33, 'THE IMAGE THE FRAME IS DRAWN INTO IS NOT A SWAPCHAIN IMAGE' — the file's largest decision). The two that do discard are d3d11/device_resources.cpp:285 and d3d12/device_resources.cpp:369, the two DISCARD swap effects.

RULE BROKEN: CLAUDE.md — a design statement 'changes by amendment in the same commit as the change that fights it'. renderer.h is the seam and is mostly comment because the comment is the contract; this commit rewrote parts of renderer.h and left the one sentence its own new test case contradicts.

FAILURE SCENARIO: a client author reads renderer.h, believes reading after end_frame yields nothing on every backend, and writes the screenshot path accordingly. It behaves as documented on d3d11/d3d12, is undefined on gl, and returns the correct frame on vulkan — so a bug that depends on the read being empty is invisible on the platform the port exists to reach. Conversely a reader who trusts pixel_tests.cpp:1751 concludes the seam permits reading after end_frame on some backends, which renderer.h forbids.

FIX: amend renderer.h:473-474 where the rule lives: keep 'BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame()' as the rule, and state the reason as per-backend — two of the four discard the buffer at present, GL leaves it undefined, and the Vulkan backend keeps it only because the engine owns the image, which is not something a caller may rely on. Then pixel_tests.cpp:1750-1752 and the harness note at :305-306 ('Presenting a FLIP_DISCARD swap chain throws the back buffer's contents away') agree with it rather than with each other.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

EVERY QUOTED LINE CHECKS OUT CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER.

engine/render/renderer.h:473-474 reads exactly "// BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame(). Presenting discards the back // buffer's contents, so after end_frame there is nothing left to read." `git show 4d91b91 -- engine/render/renderer.h` shows this commit touched renderer.h in fourteen hunks (:40, :281-284, :366-369, :391-394, :406-426, :484-487, :515-519, :535-541, :565-568, :573-583, :583-604, :619-625, :632-649, :659) — including the paragraph immediately below this one at :484-487 — and the read_back_buffer paragraph at :445-480 is in none of them. Pre-existing sentence, untouched by the commit that fights it.

THE MECHANISM IS REAL. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1493 `void DeviceResources::present()`; its only write to the colour target is :1548 `this->transition_colour(VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL)`, after which `this->colour_image_` is the SOURCE of a vkCmdCopyImage or vkCmdBlitImage into the acquired swapchain image (:1560-1596). Nothing writes colour_image_. The clear is elsewhere: vkCmdClearColorImage at engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:688, inside `Renderer::Impl::open_frame()` (:664), reached from `Renderer::begin_frame()` (:826, calling open_frame at :853) — so between end_frame and the NEXT begin_frame the image still holds the presented frame. engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1207 reads from `device_resources.colour_target()`, that same image, and engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1334-1352 `commands()` explicitly handles being called after the frame has already been to the queue ("A SECOND OPENING IN ONE FRAME, WHICH IS NOT A BEGIN"). So a post-end_frame read on Vulkan returns the frame, and engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:31-32 is the reason: "THE IMAGE THE FRAME IS DRAWN INTO IS NOT A SWAPCHAIN IMAGE."

The contrast is as stated: engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.cpp:285 `swapChainDesc.SwapEffect = m_flipPresent ? DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_DISCARD : DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_DISCARD;` and engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:369 `description.SwapEffect = DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_DISCARD;`. GL presents with SwapBuffers (engine/render/gl/renderer.cpp:756), where the back buffer is undefined afterwards rather than discarded. So renderer.h's "Presenting discards the back buffer's contents" is a universal mechanism claim that is true on two of five, vacuous on null, near-enough on gl, and FALSE on the backend this commit added.

THE TWO SENTENCES REALLY CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE. tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:1751-1752, added here, says "What a present does to the buffer it presented is // a backend's business and differs - two of the four discard it -". renderer.h:473 says presenting discards, full stop. That is a live contradiction of fact between a comment this commit wrote and a comment it left alone, and the harness note at tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:305-306 ("Deliberately no end_frame(). Presenting a FLIP_DISCARD swap chain // throws the back buffer's contents away") is a third, D3D-shaped, statement of the same thing.

THE CLASS OF FINDING IS ONE THIS TREE ALREADY RECOGNISES. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:9-12 states the standard: "The comments in `engine/render/` are held to the same standard — `renderer.h` is not a header with comments, it is the specification of the seam." Its item on `:327-330` is the exact analogue — "A per-backend sentence on the shared seam, false in two of three configurations" — and that one was fixed; renderer.h:458-465 now defers to the backend for the swizzle instead of asserting it. So the finding is not inventing a rule.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE IS THE CONSEQUENCE. See correction.

*Correction:* The defect is real and the FIX is right; the FAILURE SCENARIO and the RULE BROKEN are both wrong, and they are what carried the severity.

1. The failure scenario is not constructible. "A client author... believes reading after end_frame yields nothing... so a bug that depends on the read being empty is invisible" — nobody writes code that depends on a read returning nothing. An over-broad prohibition makes a caller decline a legal operation; it cannot make a caller write a defect. The real (and much smaller) harm runs the other way: a developer who tries a post-end_frame read on Vulkan finds it works, ships it, and gets an empty buffer on d3d11/d3d12 — which is precisely what renderer.h:473's rule already warns them off, so the stale because-clause did not cause it.

2. The claimed contradiction with the new test is overstated. tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:1750-1754 does not "conclude the seam permits reading after end_frame on some backends"; it DECLINES to assert anything about the post-present buffer and pins "the frame after one is clean" instead. Its own header at :1731-1738 restates the seam's interval correctly as "draw, submit, read, present" — read BEFORE present — and the case at :1755-1780 never reads after end_frame. The two files agree about the rule; they disagree only about the word "discards".

3. The rule cited is misattributed. CLAUDE.md's "changes by amendment in the same commit as the change that fights it" sits under "Reading the documents correctly" and is scoped to `docs/design/`. renderer.h is not in docs/design/. The citation that actually supports this finding is docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:9-12, which extends that standard to `engine/render/` comments by name.

4. The rule the stale sentence heads is still correct and still unamended for a reason: "BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame()" holds on all five backends, and a caller obeying it is correct everywhere. Only the justification clause went one-backend-specific. Nothing in engine/, samples/ or tests/ behaves wrongly; `end_frame` has exactly one non-test caller (engine/app/application.cpp) and no read follows it. This is documentation drift in the seam spec with no reachable behavioural consequence — minor, not should-fix.

One line-number nit: the present() body the finding cites as :1533-1600 actually begins at :1493, and the transition_colour it names is at :1548. The range still contains the evidence.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

CONFIRMED on every load-bearing point, and I verified the mechanism further than the finding did.

1. The seam sentence is exactly as quoted and is flat. engine/render/renderer.h:473-474: "// BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame(). Presenting discards the back // buffer's contents, so after end_frame there is nothing left to read." Nothing in the surrounding paragraph (renderer.h:445-480) qualifies it per backend, and end_frame's own paragraph (renderer.h:364-381) says only "end_frame presents".

2. The commit ran a renderer.h amendment pass and skipped this paragraph. `git show 4d91b91 -- engine/render/renderer.h` changes 87 lines and rewrites fourteen count-sentences: renderer.h:37 (four->five backends), :284-285, :368, :394, :409-423, :487, :518-522, :538-543, :568. The read_back_buffer paragraph, renderer.h:445-480, has no hunk at all. The commit message states the policy itself: "renderer.h counted four in fourteen places and the other four backends counted each other in nine more."

3. On the Vulkan backend the clause is false, and I checked the whole path, not only that present() does not destroy its source. present() (engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1493-1649) touches the colour target once, at :1548, `this->transition_colour(VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL)`; the image is only a copy source (vkCmdCopyImage, :1577) or blit source (vkCmdBlitImage, :1594) into the acquired swapchain image, and the tail (:1626-1647) presents and advances frame_index_. Renderer::end_frame (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:855-866) is `impl.frame_begun = false; impl.device_resources.present();` and nothing else. The clear is in Impl::open_frame (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:664-694, vkCmdClearColorImage at :688), which is reached only from begin_frame (:853) and the resize restart (:810) - never from commands(). So in the interval after end_frame and before the next begin_frame the engine-owned image still holds the presented frame.

4. And it is readable, not merely resident. Renderer::read_back_buffer (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1171-1240) copies from device_resources.colour_target() at :1207 with no check of frame_begun, saves and restores the previous layout (:1191, :1217-1220 - `previous` would be TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, set by present at :1548), then execute() and wait_for_gpu(). DeviceResources::commands() (engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1334-1352) contains precisely the branch that makes this legal after a submit: `if (!this->recording_ && this->submitted_)` -> wait_for_frame(), vkResetCommandPool, then vkBeginCommandBuffer. So "after end_frame there is nothing left to read" is false on this backend in the strongest sense: the read succeeds and returns the presented frame.

5. The reading that could have saved the sentence - "back buffer" meaning the swapchain image - is closed by the backend itself. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:32 ("THE IMAGE THE FRAME IS DRAWN INTO IS NOT A SWAPCHAIN IMAGE") and device_resources.cpp:1519-1521 ("what it invalidates is not what the seam calls the back buffer") both make the seam's back buffer the engine-owned colour image on this backend.

6. The two that do discard are as cited: engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.cpp:285 (`DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_DISCARD`) and engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:369 (same, with :352-354 arguing it is not optional there). So this is not a shape d3d12/ or gl/ already has and gets away with - it is new with the fifth backend, which is why the finding is about this commit rather than about the seam.

7. The contradiction is internal to the commit. `git show 4d91b91 -- tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp` shows tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:1729-1754 as wholly added text, including :1750-1752 "What a present does to the buffer it presented is // a backend's business and differs - two of the four discard it". The same commit therefore added a statement that a present's effect on the buffer is backend-specific while leaving the seam header asserting it flatly. The pre-existing harness note at tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:304-307 ("Presenting a FLIP_DISCARD swap chain throws the back buffer's contents away") was extended by this commit (the "ONE CASE CALLS IT ITSELF" paragraph, :309-314) without its D3D-specific justification being generalised either.

I could not find a refutation. The failure scenario is reachable exactly as stated for a caller who steps outside the documented interval, and the file's own standard is the one the finding is applying.

*Correction:* Three corrections, none of which touch the conclusion.

(a) The rule is cited from the wrong place. CLAUDE.md's "changes by amendment in the same commit as the change that fights it" is scoped to `docs/design/` ("docs/design/ is written in the present tense of the target... and changes by amendment..."), and renderer.h is not in docs/design/. The finding does not need that citation and is stronger without it. The authority that actually applies is in renderer.h itself, sixteen lines above the sentence at issue: renderer.h:319-322, "The term is right; the reasoning under it was not, and a false justification is worse than none because it reads as though the case had been considered." That paragraph is the file striking out an earlier justification it found to be untrue while keeping the rule - which is exactly the fix this finding asks for, in the same file. Secondary support: the commit's own stated policy in its message, and docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md, which CLAUDE.md describes as "a live list of comments in engine/render/ that the code no longer matches" - i.e. this repository already treats stale comments in this folder as a tracked defect class.

(b) The proposed amendment should be a three-way split, not two-and-a-half. Two discard (d3d11, d3d12, both FLIP_DISCARD); GL leaves the back buffer UNDEFINED after SwapBuffers rather than preserving it, so it is not a counter-example, only not a guarantee; Vulkan preserves it as a consequence of the engine owning the image; and the null backend is outside the sentence entirely because read_back_buffer throws there (renderer.h:467-471). Only one of the five actually falsifies the clause, and it falsifies it completely.

(c) The finding asserts the Vulkan read "returns the correct frame" from present() not destroying its source. That inference is right but under-evidenced as written; the load-bearing checks are that end_frame does nothing but present (vulkan/renderer.cpp:855-866), that the clear is in open_frame and reachable only from begin_frame (vulkan/renderer.cpp:664-694, :853), and that commands() explicitly supports reopening a buffer that has already been submitted (vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1337-1352). Quote those rather than present() alone.

On severity: should-fix stands. Two considerations pull down - no runtime defect exists, the normative half of the sentence ("BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame()") is still correct and still obeyed by every backend, and only an out-of-contract caller is affected. Three pull up harder: renderer.h is the contract and is mostly comment for that reason; the commit performed the amendment pass and missed the one paragraph its own new test case contradicts, so this is a gap in work that was done rather than work not attempted; and the file has already ruled, at :321, that a false justification in it is worse than no justification. Adjacent note for whoever fixes it - the same untouched paragraph enumerates read-back formats at renderer.h:461-465 ("both Direct3D back buffers are BGRA... the GL one is asked for as RGBA and only flipped") and omits Vulkan, which vulkan/renderer.cpp:1235-1240 says is B8G8R8A8 and swapped on the way out. That is an omission rather than a falsehood and is a separate item, but it confirms the paragraph as a whole was skipped.

### C30. sprite.hlsl still says the negative y term is because clip space's y runs up and that this is the single line where the flip is decided; the third reader this commit added has clip y running down and decides it in a second place

**`engine/render/sprite.hlsl:68`** · minor · `seam` · raised by R82 · run id `V50`

> Raised as should-fix; a refuter corrected it to minor.

CLAIM: This commit made sprite.hlsl a three-backend file and rewrote five of its header paragraphs to say so, but left untouched the one paragraph whose premise the third backend falsifies.

EVIDENCE, verbatim and verified at sprite.hlsl:63-69:

```
    // Pixels to clip space, as two multiply-adds rather than a 4x4 matrix.
    ...
    // and offset is fifteen more than the arithmetic needs. The values are
    // (2/width, -2/height, -1, 1): the y term is negative because the seam's y runs
    // down the screen and clip space's runs up, which is the single line in this
    // engine where that is decided.
```


The same commit added, at engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:50-56:

```
    // THE SAME FOUR NUMBERS THE DIRECT3D BACKENDS WRITE, AND THAT IS A
    // CLAIM ABOUT THE VIEWPORT RATHER THAN ABOUT THE SHADER. Vulkan's clip
    // space has y increasing DOWN where D3D's and GL's increase up, so this
    // shader - which is theirs, unchanged - would draw every frame upside
    // down here. What puts it right is a negative viewport height in
    // replay() below ...
```


and the second deciding site itself, verified at renderer.cpp:1046-1054:

```
    pane.y = static_cast<float>(pixels.y + pixels.height);
    pane.height = -static_cast<float>(pixels.height);
```

with renderer.cpp:1037-1046 calling it "THIS BACKEND'S WHOLE SHARE OF THE ONE TERM renderer.h SAYS A BACKEND STILL DECIDES".

RULE BROKEN: CLAUDE.md, "Reading the documents correctly" - documents change by amendment in the same commit as the change that fights them - and docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md extends that to comments in engine/render/. On the Vulkan build the shader's y term is negative DESPITE clip space running down, and the flip is decided in two lines that cancel, not one.

FAILURE SCENARIO: The literal reading is a trap for the next person who touches this shader. Believing this is "the single line in this engine where that is decided", they flip the sign here to fix an inverted frame (or to serve a sixth API) and check it against the D3D11 or the GL golden run, which passes. The Vulkan build then renders every frame upside down, because the negative viewport height was compensating for a term that is no longer there - and CI does not rasterise the Vulkan preset (this commit's own decision, renderer.h:641-647), so nothing catches it.

FIX: Amend sprite.hlsl:66-69 in the style the rest of the file was amended in: the y term is the seam's y-down convention expressed once; D3D and GL clip space run up so it lands correctly there; Vulkan's runs down and its backend negates the viewport height to cancel - naming engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp's submit() as the second half. Delete "which is the single line in this engine where that is decided".

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this and could not. Every quoted line is exact and the contradiction is stated by the commit itself, not inferred.

VERIFIED EVIDENCE. engine/render/sprite.hlsl:63-69 reads character for character as quoted, ending "...the y term is negative because the seam's y runs / down the screen and clip space's runs up, which is the single line in this / engine where that is decided." (:67-69). engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:50-60 reads as quoted, including ":52 Vulkan's clip / space has y increasing DOWN where D3D's and GL's increase up, so this / shader - which is theirs, unchanged - would draw every frame upside / down here." And renderer.cpp:1037-1046 reads "THE NEGATIVE HEIGHT IS THE Y FLIP, AND IT IS THIS BACKEND'S / WHOLE SHARE OF THE ONE TERM renderer.h SAYS A BACKEND STILL / DECIDES", with the code at :1047-1051 setting pane.y = pixels.y + pixels.height and pane.height = -height, inside Renderer::submit().

So the file all three HLSL backends compile states as unqualified fact that clip space's y runs up, and the same commit states twice, in capitals, that Vulkan's runs down and that the shader alone would draw upside down. That is a verbal contradiction in one commit, not a matter of reading.

I tried the strongest defence available: that the negative viewport height is merely "where a pane sits in the buffer" (the one term renderer.h leaves to a backend), so Vulkan normalises its clip space to the engine's and the shader comment stays true. The code refuses that reading. If Vulkan's clip space ran up, the natural pane placement would be pane.y = pixels.y with a positive height; the deviation to bottom-edge-plus-negative-height IS the direction flip, and vulkan/renderer.cpp:1037 says so in its own heading. GL is not a counter-example: GL's clip space genuinely does run up, and gl/renderer.cpp:590-598 adjusts only the framebuffer origin (drawable_height - (pixels.y + pixels.height)) while writing the identical four numbers at :603-605. Vulkan is the first reader where the premise itself is false.

RULE IS REAL AND NOT ALREADY SATISFIED. CLAUDE.md's amendment rule is extended to comments in engine/render/ by docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:6-12 ("renderer.h is not a header with comments, it is the specification of the seam"). DRIFT.md:3-4 dates itself 2026-08-19 against 57b65b3 and says it is not updated, so it predates this commit and does not already carry the item. git show 4d91b91 --format="" -- engine/render/sprite.hlsl confirms the commit rewrote the surrounding header paragraphs and left :63-69 untouched, while its own message claims "The documents change by amendment in the commit that earns it, which is most of the diff."

CI CLAIM CHECKS OUT. .github/workflows/ci.yml:89-91 sets skip_tests: '-E RenderPixelTests' for x64-debug-vulkan, and engine/render/renderer.h:641-648 gives the reason ("Vulkan has no in-box fallback at all"). So CI would not catch a Vulkan-only inversion.

WHERE IT IS REACHABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT. The literal action in the failure scenario cannot be performed: sprite.hlsl:95-97 is "input.position * pixels_to_clip.xy + pixels_to_clip.zw" with no sign in it. The constant is written by CPU code in four places (d3d11/renderer.cpp:85-87, d3d12/renderer.cpp:122-124, gl/renderer.cpp:603-605, vulkan/renderer.cpp:66-67), and the Vulkan one sits twelve lines below the comment at :48-60 that names the viewport negation and points at replay(). A maintainer changing the convention must edit that function, standing on the warning. What survives is the narrower and still real hazard: sprite.hlsl is the shared file a reader goes to for this term, and what it tells them is false for one of its three readers and tells them not to look further.

*Correction:* The conclusion stands; three things in the write-up do not.

1. MECHANISM. "they flip the sign here" is not possible. sprite.hlsl:95-97 is a bare multiply-add; the four numbers come from CPU code in four per-backend sites (d3d11/renderer.cpp:85-87, d3d12/renderer.cpp:122-124, gl/renderer.cpp:603-605, vulkan/renderer.cpp:66-67). The Vulkan site is directly under vulkan/renderer.cpp:48-60, which names the negative viewport height and points at replay(), so the person doing the edit is warned at the edit site. The hazard is to the reader of sprite.hlsl, not to the editor of the constant.

2. CONSEQUENCE OVER-STATED. CI does skip it (ci.yml:89-91), but tests/render/golden/ would catch an inverted Vulkan frame the moment anyone ran ctest --preset x64-debug-vulkan, which CLAUDE.md already requires for any change to engine/render/. "Nothing catches it" should read "CI does not catch it".

3. THE FIX UNDER-SCOPES. Two more comments carry the same falsified premise and the finding names neither. gl/sprite_shader.h:38-39 repeats "the seam's y runs down the screen and clip space's runs up" verbatim. d3d11/renderer.cpp:71-77 calls its own to_transform "THE ONE LINE WHERE Y RUNNING DOWN IS DECIDED" and predicts "one whose framebuffer origin is at the bottom writes them differently, and this is the only place it has to" - which GL falsified before this commit (gl/renderer.cpp:603-605 writes the same four numbers; the difference is at glViewport, :590-598) and Vulkan falsifies again from the other direction. So "the single line" was never literally one line even at HEAD~1; it was one decision transliterated four times, and Vulkan is the first genuine second decision. An amendment to sprite.hlsl:66-69 alone leaves two copies of the false premise standing.

4. Count nit: the commit edited four paragraph regions of the header (one newly added), not five.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *refuted*, severity `minor`

QUOTES VERIFIED. sprite.hlsl:63-69 is verbatim as the finding gives it and was untouched by 4d91b91 (the commit's diff on that file is four hunks, all in the lines above :62). vulkan/renderer.cpp:50-60 and :1037-1054 are quoted correctly. DRIFT.md:6-11 does hold comments in engine/render/ to the design documents' amendment standard, so the rule invoked is a real rule. renderer.h:648 confirms CI rasterises only twice, both Direct3D.

REFUTATION 1 - THE PREMISE IS NOT FALSIFIED. The constant does not assume "Vulkan's NDC"; it assumes "clip y of +1 is the top of the viewport", which is the engine's own wording at gl/sprite_shader.h:41-42. Vulkan's viewport transform is p_y = (h/2)*y_ndc + (y_vp + h/2). With pane.y = pixels.y + pixels.height and pane.height = -pixels.height (vulkan/renderer.cpp:1049-1051), y_ndc = +1 maps to p_y = pixels.y, the pane's TOP - identical to D3D. Negative VkViewport::height is core since 1.1 (maintenance1 promotion) and the floor here is 1.2, so this is legal, not a trick. Every rasterising backend therefore presents the shader a clip space whose +1 is the top; none falsifies "clip space's runs up" as the shader means it, they satisfy it by different means. vulkan/renderer.cpp:50-51 says so explicitly: "THE SAME FOUR NUMBERS THE DIRECT3D BACKENDS WRITE, AND THAT IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE VIEWPORT RATHER THAN ABOUT THE SHADER", and :59-60 "Neither reaches engine/render/sprite.hlsl, which is the test that they belong to a backend". The backend was written to preserve the shader paragraph, not in defiance of it.

REFUTATION 2 - GL IS THE SAME SHAPE AND IT WAS ACCEPTED. gl/renderer.cpp:587-588 says "the clip-space y flip in the shader and GL's origin cancel exactly" and :590-591 calls its glViewport line "THE ONE PLACE A BACKEND DECIDES WHERE A PIXEL GOES". gl/sprite_shader.h:38-42 says "the two cancel". GL landed at 091c8f4; `git log -S "single line in this"` returns 1370fc0 and 3dda092, so the sentence was last rewritten in the D3D12 commit with GL and both of those comments already in the tree, and was deliberately kept. A second file participating in where a pane's rows land, documented in that backend rather than in the shader, is the seam's pre-existing pattern - CLAUDE.md and renderer.h both assign "where a pane sits in the buffer" to the backend. That makes this a question about the seam's vocabulary, not a defect this commit introduced.

REFUTATION 3 - THE FAILURE SCENARIO IS UNREACHABLE AS WRITTEN. There is no sign in sprite.hlsl to flip: sprite.hlsl:95-96 is `input.position * pixels_to_clip.xy + pixels_to_clip.zw`, pure multiply-add. The -2/height is a CPU value written in four independent places - d3d11/renderer.cpp:87, d3d12/renderer.cpp:124, gl/renderer.cpp:604, vulkan/renderer.cpp:67 - three of which predate this commit, so "the single line" was never a line count even before Vulkan existed. Anyone changing the y convention must edit all four fill_transform sites, one of which is vulkan/renderer.cpp:61-70 sitting under twenty lines of capitalised comment explaining exactly this coupling. And the finding's "check it against the D3D11 or the GL golden run, which passes" is false: a change to the shared term inverts D3D11 and D3D12 as well, and renderer.h:648 says CI rasterises the whole contract twice on those two presets. The claimed trap does not spring.

MECHANISM ERROR: the finding says the two lines "cancel". They compose to one net flip; a cancellation would leave the frame inverted.

AMENDMENT OBLIGATION: it was discharged where the design vocabulary lives. 4d91b91's CLAUDE.md hunk rewrites "one term a backend still decides is where a pane sits in the buffer, because Direct3D measures down from the top and GL up from the bottom" into the three-answer form naming Vulkan's negative viewport height "so that one shader serves all three".

*Correction:* One residue survives, well below should-fix. This commit added vulkan/renderer.cpp:51-52 ("Vulkan's clip space has y increasing DOWN where D3D's and GL's increase up", repeated at :1038-1040) while leaving sprite.hlsl:67-68 saying "clip space's runs up". Both sentences are true - one about the API's default NDC-to-framebuffer mapping, the other about the mapping the backend hands the shader - but they use the same two words for opposite things in the same commit with no cross-reference. gl/sprite_shader.h:38-42 spends four lines resolving that same clash for GL ("GL's window origin is at the bottom left where Direct3D's is at the top, and the two cancel - clip y of +1 is the top of the viewport in both"); the HLSL file spends none for Vulkan. Adding a clause of that kind is worth doing. What should NOT be done is the finding's proposed deletion of "which is the single line in this engine where that is decided" on the grounds that the paragraph is false - it is not false, and the same sentence already survived GL, whose backend documents an identical interaction.

**Adjudicator** — the two disagreed, so a third read the code. *confirmed*

VERIFIED TEXT. engine/render/sprite.hlsl:63-69 reads exactly as quoted, ending "the y term is negative because the seam's y runs / down the screen and clip space's runs up, which is the single line in this / engine where that is decided." `git show 4d91b91 -- engine/render/sprite.hlsl` has four hunks, the last one ending at the "COMPILED AT BUILD TIME" paragraph (line ~55); the transform paragraph at :63-69 was untouched while the header around it was rewritten. The same commit added engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:50-60 ("Vulkan's clip space has y increasing DOWN where D3D's and GL's increase up, so this shader - which is theirs, unchanged - would draw every frame upside down here") and :1037-1051 ("THE NEGATIVE HEIGHT IS THE Y FLIP, AND IT IS THIS BACKEND'S WHOLE SHARE OF THE ONE TERM renderer.h SAYS A BACKEND STILL DECIDES", with pane.y = pixels.y + pixels.height and pane.height = -height). `grep -rn "single line in this"` returns exactly one hit, sprite.hlsl:68.

THE ARITHMETIC. Refuter B is right that nothing renders wrong. Vulkan's viewport transform is y_f = (h/2)*y_ndc + (y_vp + h/2); with y_vp = py+ph and h = -ph, y_ndc=+1 lands at py (the pane's top) and -1 at py+ph, identical to D3D. So the composed mapping the shader is handed does have +1 at the top on all four rasterising backends, and the goldens reproducing on vulkan is consistent with that. There is no behavioural defect and no code fix here.

WHY THAT DOES NOT REFUTE IT. The sentence does not say "clip y of +1 is the top of the viewport" — that is Refuter B's charitable reconstruction, and the project already writes it that way when it means it (gl/sprite_shader.h:38-42 spends four lines: "GL's window origin is at the bottom left where Direct3D's is at the top, and the two cancel - clip y of +1 is the top of the viewport in both"). sprite.hlsl says flatly that clip space's y runs up and that this is "the single line in this engine where that is decided". As a statement about the API's clip space that is false for one of its three readers, and the same commit says so twice in capitals, in the same words. GL is not the precedent B claims: GL's clip y genuinely does run up, and gl/renderer.cpp:590-598 converts a framebuffer origin, not a direction — it writes the identical four numbers at :603-605. Vulkan is the first reader whose clip space actually inverts, and the backend's own heading calls the compensating line "THE Y FLIP". So on that build the direction is settled by two lines that compose, and the shared file whose paragraph a reader goes to for this term denies the second one exists. That is squarely CLAUDE.md's amendment rule as docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:6-12 extends it to engine/render/ comments; DRIFT dates itself 2026-08-19 against 57b65b3, so it does not already carry the item. B's own correction concedes the clause is worth adding, which is a finding with a textual fix, not a refutation.

SEVERITY DOWN TO MINOR. The finding's failure scenario does not spring. sprite.hlsl:95-96 is `input.position * pixels_to_clip.xy + pixels_to_clip.zw` — there is no sign in the shader to flip. The constant is CPU-side in four places (d3d11/renderer.cpp:85-87, d3d12/renderer.cpp:122-124, gl/renderer.cpp:603-605, vulkan/renderer.cpp:66-67), and the Vulkan one sits directly under the twenty-line comment that names the viewport negation and points at replay(), so the editor is warned at the edit site. And "check it against the D3D11 or the GL golden run, which passes" is wrong: a change to the shared term inverts D3D11 and D3D12 too, and ci.yml:82-85 rasterises both. What survives is a real but narrow hazard — a false premise plus a finality clause in the one shared file, telling a reader not to look further — whose fix is one paragraph.
