### C31. HLSL member order is now a silent Vulkan ABI term, stated only inside the backend, in a file that claims no backend difference reaches it

**`engine/render/sprite.hlsl:78`** · minor · `build` · raised by R104 · run id `V64`

> Raised as should-fix; a refuter corrected it to minor.

CLAIM: after 4d91b91 the declaration order of sprite.hlsl's VertexIn is a load-bearing interface term for the Vulkan backend, and the only file that says so is the backend's own renderer.cpp — the shared file where the breaking edit would be made says the opposite.

EVIDENCE. engine/render/sprite.hlsl:78-83:

```
    struct VertexIn
    {
        float2 position : POSITION;
        float4 colour   : COLOR;
        float2 texcoord : TEXCOORD;
    };
```

engine/render/sprite.hlsl:28-33, the paragraph enumerating what a backend owns: "The binding / is in each backend's renderer.cpp, because it is a call and not a build / setting: ... No difference reaches / this file, which is the test that it belongs above all three."
engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:382-385: "The three fields of SpriteVertex, located by offsetof rather than by / position, which is why sprite_vertex.h is free to declare them in any / order it likes. The locations are the shader's, assigned by dxc in / the order the HLSL struct declares its semantics." — followed at 386-402 by attributes[0].location=0 -> offsetof(SpriteVertex, position), attributes[1].location=1 with VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32A32_SFLOAT -> offsetof(SpriteVertex, colour), attributes[2].location=2 with VK_FORMAT_R32G32_SFLOAT -> offsetof(SpriteVertex, texcoord). No semantic string and no name appears anywhere in that table.
The original lens also read the generated header out/build/x64-debug-vulkan/generated/engine/render/vulkan/sprite_vertex_shader.h, which carries "OpDecorate %in_var_POSITION Location 0 / OpDecorate %in_var_COLOR Location 1 / OpDecorate %in_var_TEXCOORD Location 2" — declaration order, not alphabetical order of the semantic strings (alphabetical would put COLOR at 0), so the member order above is the only determinant.

RULE. sprite.hlsl:24-35 is a closed enumeration of what a backend owns — "THE PROFILE AND THE BINDING" — sealed by "No difference reaches this file". A third term now reaches it. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard, restated in CLAUDE.md, is that a comment the code does not match is a defect; and this repository's own practice is to put the constraint where the edit happens (engine/render/sprite_vertex.h:10 does exactly that for the C++ half).

FAILURE. Swap the `colour` and `texcoord` members of VertexIn — an edit sprite_vertex.h:10-13 declares safe for the C++ half, which genuinely is safe for d3d11/ and d3d12/ (they bind by semantic string) and irrelevant to gl/ (its own GLSL, bound by glBindAttribLocation). All five presets still compile. On x64-debug-vulkan dxc now assigns POSITION 0, TEXCOORD 1, COLOR 2, while engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:393-402 still ties location 1 to a 4-component format at offsetof(colour) and location 2 to a 2-component format at offsetof(texcoord). Vulkan fills the shader input's missing components with (0,0,0,1) and ignores surplus attribute components, so pipeline creation raises no validation error: every sprite is then sampled at texture coordinate (colour.r, colour.g) and tinted with (texcoord.x, texcoord.y, 0, 1). The one test that would catch it, RenderPixelTests, is the one CI skips on this preset (.github/workflows/ci.yml:88-90), so it fails silently and only on a developer machine with a driver.

FIX. Add a paragraph immediately above VertexIn saying that the member order is the SPIR-V location order for the Vulkan backend and must stay in step with the attribute table in engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:386-402, and amend "No difference reaches this file" at line 32 to name this one. Say also that [[vk::location]] is not the escape, for the reason vulkan/renderer.cpp:307-312 already gives about [[vk::push_constant]]: fxc cannot parse the annotation, so it would be the first compiler-conditional line in a shared source.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

Verified every link. (1) sprite.hlsl:78-83 declares position:POSITION, colour:COLOR, texcoord:TEXCOORD in that order, quoted correctly. (2) vulkan/renderer.cpp:382-385 states the term verbatim as quoted ("The locations are the shader's, assigned by dxc in the order the HLSL struct declares its semantics"), and the table at :387-402 hard-codes location 0 -> R32G32 at offsetof(position), location 1 -> R32G32B32A32 at offsetof(colour), location 2 -> R32G32 at offsetof(texcoord), with no semantic string anywhere in it. (3) The asymmetry is real: d3d11/renderer.cpp:442-448 and d3d12/renderer.cpp:711-717 bind by semantic string plus offsetof, so reordering VertexIn leaves them correct; gl/renderer.cpp:431-433 binds by name into gl/sprite_shader.h:47-49, its own GLSL inside the backend folder. Vulkan is the only backend keyed on a positional property of the shared file. (4) grep over engine/, docs/, cmake/, tests/ returns exactly one statement of the term in the repository: vulkan/renderer.cpp:385. sprite.hlsl (read in full, 115 lines) says nothing about it. (5) The failure fires silently: all three locations remain provided after a swap, so no "input not consumed/not provided" VUID triggers, and Vulkan's (0,0,0,1) fill plus surplus-component discard are spec behaviour, so pipeline creation is clean and the pixels are wrong. (6) .github/workflows/ci.yml:89-91 confirms x64-debug-vulkan carries skip_tests: '-E RenderPixelTests', so the only test that could catch it does not run on the only preset that could run it. (7) The house rule invoked is a real one: engine/app/application.h:229 and engine/app/window.h:183 both use the literal form "DECLARATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING BELOW THIS LINE" at the point of edit. (8) The one premise I could not test read-only is dxc's implicit location-assignment order (compile_shaders.cmake passes no -fvk-stage-io-order, so the default governs). It resolves in the finding's favour by elimination: alphabetical assignment would give COLOR location 0, which would already mis-wire the table at renderer.cpp:387-402 today, and the commit message's "Six configurations green: 12/12/12/12/11 debug" plus the shared golden set rule that out.

*Correction:* Two corrections, one to the mechanism's framing and one to severity.

FRAMING. The finding's headline charge — that the shared file "claims no backend difference reaches it" and is therefore contradicted — misreads sprite.hlsl:32. In context from :24 ("WHAT A BACKEND DOES OWN IS THE PROFILE AND THE BINDING... D3D11 gives the vertex shader its b0 through a constant buffer, D3D12... four root constants, and Vulkan as a uniform buffer in a descriptor set. No difference reaches this file"), the antecedent of "difference" is the profile/b0-binding difference just enumerated, and that sentence is still literally true: `git show 4d91b91 -- engine/render/sprite.hlsl` shows Vulkan required no change to the shader body, only to the comment header. The file also already carries cross-file interface terms the enumeration never covered — the semantic strings "POSITION"/"COLOR"/"TEXCOORD" are hard-coded in both D3D input layouts and must match the shader, or CreateInputLayout fails. So the accurate statement is narrower than "the file says the opposite": what is new in 4d91b91 is not that a term reaches the shared file, but that this is the first such term whose violation is SILENT (Vulkan matches by location only, never by name) rather than loud at device creation, on the one preset CI cannot rasterise. The conclusion — an undocumented cross-file constraint stated only at the consuming end — stands on that narrower ground.

SEVERITY. should-fix overstates it. No defect exists at HEAD; no failure is reachable from any test in tests/render/, any sample, or any engine call site; the constraint is written down once, immediately above the code that depends on it (vulkan/renderer.cpp:382-385), which is where a reader debugging the breakage would land. The harm requires a future editor to make a gratuitous edit — reordering HLSL struct members is not an edit any feature requires. That is a documentation gap, hence minor.

ONE ADDITION, arguably stronger than the item raised. engine/render/sprite_vertex.h was not touched by 4d91b91 at all (confirmed by the commit's file list), and :10-13 still reads "Every backend with a vertex buffer builds its offsets from offsetof and binds by semantic (the two Direct3D ones) or by name (gl)". Vulkan is a backend with a vertex buffer and binds by neither. Its conclusion survives — Vulkan does use offsetof, so reordering the C++ SpriteVertex remains safe on all five — but the enumeration is now incomplete in exactly the file that invites the reordering, which is the plausible route to the fatal edit: reorder SpriteVertex as that paragraph blesses, then mirror it into VertexIn for tidiness. If a paragraph is added anywhere, sprite_vertex.h:10 needs Vulkan named in the enumeration at least as much as sprite.hlsl:78 needs the new warning.

The finding's proposed fix is otherwise sound, including the [[vk::location]] caveat: vulkan/renderer.cpp:306-311 makes exactly that argument for [[vk::push_constant]] ("reaching them from HLSL needs a [[vk::push_constant]] annotation, which is an edit to a file two other backends compile").

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

I checked the four things the finding needs, and three of them hold.

1. The coupling is real and is new with this commit. `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:386-403` hardcodes `attributes[0].location = 0` / `[1] = 1` (`VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32A32_SFLOAT`, `offsetof(SpriteVertex, colour)`) / `[2] = 2` (`VK_FORMAT_R32G32_SFLOAT`, `offsetof(SpriteVertex, texcoord)`). No semantic string appears in that table. The SPIR-V Location decorations those numbers must match are assigned by dxc, and `cmake/compile_shaders.cmake:125-136` passes only `-spirv -T -E -fvk-b-shift -fvk-t-shift -fvk-s-shift -Fh -Vn` — no `-fvk-stage-io-order`, so dxc's documented default (`decl`, declaration order) applies. `engine/render/sprite.hlsl:78-83` is therefore the file that decides which location is which. (I did not re-read the generated header under `out/`, per the read-only constraint; the flag's absence and dxc's default agree with the lens's observation that COLOR lands at Location 1 rather than the 0 alphabetical order would give.)

2. Only this backend is exposed. `engine/render/d3d11/renderer.cpp:440-451` and `engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp:709-721` both name `"POSITION"`, `"COLOR"`, `"TEXCOORD"` in `D3D1x_INPUT_ELEMENT_DESC` and match against the shader signature by semantic, so an HLSL member reorder is invisible to them. `engine/render/gl/renderer.cpp:426-433` compiles its own GLSL and calls `glBindAttribLocation(program, 0/1/2, "position"/"colour"/"texcoord")` before linking, with a comment saying it did that precisely so "the attribute indices are this file's choice rather than the driver's" — an option SPIR-V does not leave open. `null/` has no shader. So this is not a seam-shaped finding that d3d12/ or gl/ shares; Vulkan is genuinely the only backend whose correctness depends on the text order of `VertexIn`.

3. The silent-failure mechanism is right on the Vulkan side. Vulkan 1.2 §22.1.1 (Attribute Location and Component Assignment) says a shader input with more components than the attribute format takes (0,0,0,1) in the missing ones, and surplus attribute components are ignored. There is no VU requiring component-count agreement — the relevant VUIDs on `VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo` cover a shader input Location having *some* attribute entry and the numeric type (float/int/uint) matching, both of which a swapped `VertexIn` still satisfies. So pipeline creation succeeds, validation is quiet, and the frame renders wrong. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:88-90` does set `skip_tests: '-E RenderPixelTests'` for `x64-debug-vulkan`, so the golden comparison that would catch it does not run in CI.

4. The rule the finding invokes does not hold, and this is where it overreaches. `engine/render/sprite.hlsl:24-33` reads "WHAT A BACKEND DOES OWN IS THE PROFILE AND THE BINDING... The binding is in each backend's renderer.cpp, because it is a call and not a build setting: D3D11 gives the vertex shader its b0 through a constant buffer, D3D12... root constants, and Vulkan as a uniform buffer in a descriptor set. No difference reaches this file." The subject of "No difference" is the three enumerated ways of binding b0, and the claim is that no backend needs a *divergent copy of this source*. That is still true — the three b0 bindings are exactly as described (`vulkan/renderer.cpp:306-311` even argues the push-constant case on those grounds). Nor is the b0 list a "closed enumeration" of bindings: `d3d11/renderer.cpp:440-451` has been a vertex-input binding in a backend's renderer.cpp since long before this commit and sprite.hlsl never enumerated it either. So this is a missing note, not a comment the code contradicts — it does not meet `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md`'s standard ("Each item is a claim that the code no longer matches"), which is the standard the finding cites.

Two further mitigations. The constraint is already written at the site of the edit that would actually desynchronise: `vulkan/renderer.cpp:382-385` says "The locations are the shader's, assigned by dxc in the order the HLSL struct declares its semantics", and anyone adding or moving a vertex attribute must edit that table. And `engine/render/sprite_vertex.h:10-18` is not falsified by this commit — it is about the C++ struct, whose order genuinely is free because Vulkan also uses `offsetof`. The failure the finding describes needs a bare cosmetic reorder of shader semantics, an edit with no motive, reached only by a reader who generalises sprite_vertex.h's paragraph across the language boundary.

*Correction:* The coupling and its silence are real; the rule violation is not, and the severity is one step too high.

Wrong: "in a file that claims no backend difference reaches it" and "a closed enumeration... sealed by 'No difference reaches this file'. A third term now reaches it." sprite.hlsl:32-33's subject is the three ways of binding b0, and its claim is that no backend needs a different copy of this source — still true. Vertex-input binding was never in that enumeration for D3D11 either (d3d11/renderer.cpp:440-451). Nothing in sprite.hlsl is falsified, so this is not a DRIFT.md item and the DRIFT standard the finding leans on does not reach it. Drop that half of the argument.

Also wrong by implication: the finding presents the constraint as stated nowhere useful. It is stated at vulkan/renderer.cpp:382-385, attached to the hardcoded 0/1/2 — the table an editor adding or moving an attribute must open anyway.

What survives, and is worth a note: after 4d91b91, the declaration order of sprite.hlsl:78-83 silently determines SPIR-V input locations for one backend, and the shared file gives no hint of it. Three or four lines above `struct VertexIn` naming vulkan/renderer.cpp:386-403 as the table that must stay in step is the whole fix; no amendment to line 32 is needed, and rewording it as the finding proposes would make a true sentence less true. The `[[vk::location]]` aside is sound — dxc accepts it in -spirv mode, fxc cannot parse the annotation, so it would be the first compiler-conditional line in a source three backends compile, which is the same argument vulkan/renderer.cpp:306-311 already makes about `[[vk::push_constant]]`.

Adjacent and arguably the better-founded item in the same area, which this finding did not raise: sprite_vertex.h:11-13 enumerates "every backend with a vertex buffer" as binding "by semantic (the two Direct3D ones) or by name (gl)" and omits Vulkan, which binds by neither. Its conclusion still holds for Vulkan (offsetof), so the paragraph is incomplete rather than false — but that is a comment 4d91b91 left behind, which is more than can be said for sprite.hlsl:32.

### C32. The swapchain format is allowed to differ from the colour target's, and the present path then chooses vkCmdCopyImage on extent alone, so a surface without B8G8R8A8_UNORM presents every frame with red and blue swapped

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1089`** · minor · `core` · raised by R19, R32, R59 · run id `V8`

> Raised as should-fix; a refuter corrected it to minor.

THREE LENSES (swapchain, pipeline-state, instance-device) independently. device_resources.cpp:1089-1101 picks `VkSurfaceFormatKHR chosen = surface_formats.empty() ? VkSurfaceFormatKHR{ VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM, VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR } : surface_formats[0];` and only upgrades to B8G8R8A8_UNORM/SRGB_NONLINEAR if the loop finds it - so surface_formats[0] stands unchallenged otherwise, including an _SRGB or an RGBA one. The result is stored at 1144 (`this->swapchain_format_ = chosen.format;`) and NEVER READ AGAIN: `grep -n swapchain_format_` gives exactly two hits, the write at 1144 and the declaration at device_resources.h:430. colour_format_ is fixed at VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM (device_resources.h:454), and present() chooses between the two operations on EXTENT alone (1568): equal extents take `vkCmdCopyImage` (1577), unequal take `vkCmdBlitImage` (1593). RULE BROKEN: vkCmdCopyImage between size-compatible but different formats is a raw texel-bit copy with no component conversion (VUID-vkCmdCopyImage-srcImage-01548 requires only size compatibility), where vkCmdBlitImage converts - so the two branches do not mean the same thing unless the formats match, and nothing checks that they do. The file's own paragraph at 1082-1088 argues the opposite case ('NOT THE _SRGB ONE, and the difference is the whole pixel contract ... It would be visible only on screen, only next to another backend'), and the same function already refuses a surface it cannot use, throwing by name when supportedUsageFlags lacks TRANSFER_DST (1030-1038). FAILURE: on a surface offering R8G8B8A8_UNORM but not BGRA - the ordinary Android case, and CLAUDE.md and docs/port/android.md give Android as the entire reason this backend exists - chosen.format is R8G8B8A8_UNORM, the extents agree in the steady state, so every frame takes the vkCmdCopyImage branch and the whole game presents with red and blue exchanged, while read_back_buffer keeps reading the engine-owned colour target and every golden image stays green. With a B8G8R8A8_SRGB surface the copy branch presents raw bytes and the blit branch re-encodes them, so the window visibly changes brightness while it is being drag-resized. If surface_formats[0] is wider than 32 bits (VK_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT on an HDR surface) the copy is not size-compatible and is undefined behaviour. FIX: either refuse a surface that cannot give the engine its own format, throwing beside the usage check at 1030-1038 and naming the formats offered (T6), or gate the copy branch on `this->swapchain_format_ == this->colour_format_` and let every mismatch fall through to the blit, which converts. Either way swapchain_format_ stops being a member nothing reads.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *refuted*, severity `minor`

Every line the finding quotes is accurate, and the mechanism it builds on them is not.

WHAT IS TRUE. device_resources.cpp:1089-1092 is verbatim as quoted (`chosen = surface_formats.empty() ? {B8G8R8A8_UNORM, SRGB_NONLINEAR} : surface_formats[0]`). :1144 is `this->swapchain_format_ = chosen.format;` and a repo-wide grep gives exactly two hits — that write and the declaration at device_resources.h:430 — so the member is genuinely written and never read. colour_format_ is fixed at VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM (device_resources.h:454). present() really does branch on extent alone at :1568, copy at :1577, blit at :1593, with no format term anywhere in the function. The precedent throw for supportedUsageFlags is at :1032-1039 as cited. The Vulkan claims are also right: a copy between size-compatible formats reinterprets bits, a blit converts.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. (1) The mechanism is misread. The finding says "surface_formats[0] stands unchallenged otherwise" and then builds all three failure scenarios out of what element [0] happens to be. But :1093-1101 is a scan of the WHOLE list that breaks on any B8G8R8A8_UNORM + SRGB_NONLINEAR entry, not a check of [0]. Element [0] governs only when that pair is absent from the entire list. Two of the three scenarios named are lists that contain it: a surface that offers B8G8R8A8_SRGB also offers B8G8R8A8_UNORM, and an HDR surface offering R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT offers the 8-bit formats alongside it, not instead of them. In both, the loop takes BGRA8_UNORM, chosen.format == colour_format_, and the copy at :1577 is format-identical. The "visibly changes brightness while it is being drag-resized" and the "undefined behaviour" HDR case therefore never arise.

(2) The one scenario that would reach it — an RGBA-only surface — is offered as "the ordinary Android case", and Android is not reachable from any entry point at HEAD. device_resources.h:8-13 hard-defines VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR and includes <Windows.h> before <vulkan/vulkan.h> so the header compiles for no other WSI; device_resources.cpp:447 pushes VK_KHR_WIN32_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME, :875 builds a VkWin32SurfaceCreateInfoKHR, and :425 is `set_window(HWND, int, int)`. CMakePresets.json has six presets, all x64 Windows. docs/port/android.md's own header reads "Scoping only ... **Nothing here has been built.**" CLAUDE.md gives Android as the *reason* the backend exists, not as a target in the tree. There is no caller, on any platform this repository builds, that can hand this code an RGBA-only surface — that is the missing link.

(3) The "silent, and every golden image stays green" framing is not evidence of a missed check. present() has exactly one caller, vulkan/renderer.cpp:866, and tests/render/ reaches it once (pixel_tests.cpp:1729, "a frame may be read back and then presented"), reading the engine-owned colour target before the present by design — the header at device_resources.h:36-42 states that the pixel contract deliberately never presents. Nothing in the copy/blit path is claimed to be under test, so nothing is being hidden from one.

What is left is smaller than the finding: a member nothing reads, and an invariant the copy branch depends on that no line states. Neither produces a wrong pixel on any configuration this tree can build.

*Correction:* Two things survive, both below should-fix. First, `swapchain_format_` really is dead — written at device_resources.cpp:1144, declared at device_resources.h:430, read nowhere in the repository. Second, the copy branch at :1577 carries an unwritten precondition (swapchain format == colour_format_) that the extent test at :1568 does not express and no comment records, while the paragraph at :1079-1088 explains only the colour-space half of the choice. Stating that invariant — an assert, or the throw beside :1032-1039 naming the formats offered — is a legitimate tidiness item for a backend whose stated purpose is to reach a platform where it will one day matter.

The finding's proposed fix is wrong in its second form and should not be applied as written. "Gate the copy branch on format equality and let every mismatch fall through to the blit, which converts" inverts the sRGB case: vkCmdBlitImage from the UNORM colour target into a B8G8R8A8_SRGB destination applies the linear-to-sRGB encode on write and washes the frame out on EVERY present, where vkCmdCopyImage hands the presentation engine exactly the bytes the engine drew and is the correct operation for an _SRGB destination under SRGB_NONLINEAR. Converting is not always the right answer, so routing mismatches to the blit would turn a latent issue into a live one on the very surface the finding is worried about. Only the first form of the fix — refuse a surface that cannot give the engine its own format — is sound.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

I tried to kill this and could not kill the core of it, though I killed two of its three failure scenarios and its severity.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED IN THE CODE.

1. The fallback exists and is unguarded. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1089-1092` is exactly as quoted: `chosen` is `surface_formats[0]` unless the list is empty, and the loop at `:1093-1101` only overrides it when it finds `B8G8R8A8_UNORM` + `SRGB_NONLINEAR`. Any other first-offered format stands. The comment at `:1079` ("B8G8R8A8_UNORM if it is offered, which on Win32 it always is, and the first thing offered otherwise") shows the fallback is deliberate, not an oversight of intent.

2. The result is written and never read. `:1144` `this->swapchain_format_ = chosen.format;`. `grep -n "swapchain_format_"` over `engine/render/vulkan/*.cpp` and `*.h` returns exactly two hits: that write and the declaration at `device_resources.h:430`. No comparison anywhere. By contrast `colour_format_` (`device_resources.h:454`, fixed at `VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM`) is read at `:805`, `:924`, `:962`. A member written once and read nowhere is direct evidence the format was tracked and then forgotten.

3. The present branch is on extent alone. `:1568-1569` compares `colour_extent_` against `swapchain_extent_`; `:1577` takes `vkCmdCopyImage`, `:1593` takes `vkCmdBlitImage`. The file's own comment at `:1564-1565` confirms the copy branch is the steady state ("They agree whenever the shell is keeping up"), so this is the common path, not the rare one.

4. The Vulkan rule is right, and I state it from the spec rather than from the finding. `vkCmdCopyImage` requires only that the two formats be size-compatible (same texel block size); where they differ, the texel data is copied verbatim with no format conversion. `B8G8R8A8_UNORM` and `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` are both in the 32-bit compatibility class, so such a copy is *legal Vulkan* that silently transposes R and B. `vkCmdBlitImage` by contrast reads source texels to float and writes them through the destination's encoding, i.e. it converts. So the two branches genuinely do not mean the same thing when the formats differ. This is not folklore, and it is not a validation-layer warning — validation would pass a size-compatible copy silently, so the memory note that this backend "was actually checked" with the validation layers would not have caught it either.

5. The tests are blind to it, as claimed. `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1207` reads back `device_resources.colour_target()` — the engine-owned image — never a swapchain image, so every golden stays green regardless of what the present path does.

6. It is not a seam issue, so the "check the other backends" escape does not apply. `d3d12/device_resources.cpp:363` sets `description.Format = this->back_buffer_format_` — DXGI is *told* a format and fails if it cannot honour it. There is no "accept whatever is offered" shape anywhere else in `engine/render/`; it is unique to this file, because Vulkan is the only one of the five that hands you a list.

WHAT I KILLED.

(a) The Android headline is unreachable at HEAD. This backend is hard-wired to Win32: `device_resources.h:9` force-defines `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR`, `device_resources.cpp:447` pushes `VK_KHR_WIN32_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME`, `:875-879` builds a `VkWin32SurfaceCreateInfoKHR` and calls `vkCreateWin32SurfaceKHR`, and `set_window` at `:425` takes an `HWND`. There is no Android build to present anything wrongly. `docs/port/android.md` names Android as the backend's reason but says nothing about surface format (its format discussion at :74-169 is about texture/atlas formats, a different concern).

(b) The HDR / size-incompatibility scenario is flatly wrong. `VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace` is not enabled — `device_resources.cpp:445-462` enables only `VK_KHR_surface`, `VK_KHR_win32_surface`, and `VK_EXT_debug_utils` in debug. Without that extension a driver may report only `VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR`, so `VK_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT` cannot appear in `surface_formats` at all. The claimed undefined behaviour from a non-size-compatible copy cannot occur.

(c) The remaining scenarios need a Win32 driver that omits `B8G8R8A8_UNORM`/`SRGB_NONLINEAR` from its surface format list. Every shipping Windows implementation — the three IHVs, SwiftShader, lavapipe — offers it, so the loop at `:1093-1101` always finds it and the fallback is dead in practice today. The `_SRGB` drag-resize brightness shift is mechanically correct (copy stores raw bytes that the display then sRGB-decodes; blit encodes first, so the two differ) but requires that same absent driver.

WHY IT STILL SURVIVES. The finding's evidence says what the finding says it says, and the defect is in the tree: a deliberately-written fallback accepts an arbitrary format, and the code that consumes it assumes one specific format without checking. That is a real internal inconsistency with a dead member as its fingerprint, invisible to both the goldens and the validation layers, sitting on the exact path the port this backend exists for would take. The proposed fixes are both sound and both supported by the codebase's own precedent: the same function already refuses a surface it cannot use by name at `:1030-1038` (the `TRANSFER_DST` check), which is T6 (PHILOSOPHY.md:106-119, "loud is for broken contracts") applied to this very object. T1's "not a licence for speculative frameworks" (PHILOSOPHY.md:45-47) does not rescue the code — the `surface_formats[0]` fallback *is* the speculative half, and it is the half that is wrong; T1 argues for deleting it and throwing, which is the finding's first option.

*Correction:* Mechanism and code evidence stand; failure scenarios and severity do not.

Severity should-fix -> minor. Not because the code is right, but because the consequence today is nil. The backend builds only for Win32 (device_resources.h:9, device_resources.cpp:447, :879), and no shipping Win32 Vulkan driver omits B8G8R8A8_UNORM/SRGB_NONLINEAR, so the fallback at :1092 is dead in practice and the loop at :1093-1101 always wins. Nothing presents with red and blue swapped on any machine that can run this today. It is a latent trap, not a live bug — but a high-value one, because it is invisible to the goldens (renderer.cpp:1207 reads colour_target(), never a swapchain image) AND to the validation layers (a B8G8R8A8_UNORM -> R8G8B8A8_UNORM copy is size-compatible and therefore legal Vulkan, so nothing warns), and it springs on exactly the port CLAUDE.md gives as this backend's whole reason for existing.

Two of the three failure scenarios are refuted outright:
- Android/R8G8B8A8_UNORM is not reachable at HEAD. There is no Android build; the surface is VkWin32SurfaceCreateInfoKHR from an HWND.
- The HDR VK_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT / non-size-compatible / undefined-behaviour claim is wrong. VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace is not enabled (only KHR_surface, KHR_win32_surface and, in debug, EXT_debug_utils at :445-462), so only VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR formats are reported and a 64-bit float format cannot be in the list. Drop this sentence; it is the weakest part of the finding and invites the whole thing being dismissed.
- The B8G8R8A8_SRGB drag-resize brightness shift is mechanically correct but needs the same absent driver, so it is hypothetical too.

The finding should be restated as what it actually is: swapchain_format_ is written at :1144 and read nowhere (grep gives two hits, that write and device_resources.h:430), which is the fingerprint of a format that was captured and then not honoured; the present path at :1568 branches on extent alone while the two branches differ in meaning whenever the formats differ, because vkCmdCopyImage copies texel bits verbatim between size-compatible formats and vkCmdBlitImage converts. Both proposed fixes are correct and either closes it. The throw option is the better fit: it matches the TRANSFER_DST refusal already in the same function at :1030-1038 and is T6 (PHILOSOPHY.md:106-119) on a broken contract, and it removes the speculative fallback that T1 (PHILOSOPHY.md:45-47) does not license in the first place.

One thing the finding did not claim that strengthens it: this is not a seam issue, so it cannot be deflected as such. d3d12/device_resources.cpp:363 sets description.Format explicitly — DXGI is told a format and fails if it cannot honour it. No other backend has the "accept whatever the platform offers, then assume" shape.

**Adjudicator** — the two disagreed, so a third read the code. *confirmed*

I read the code rather than the refuters. Every line the finding cites is verbatim accurate, and the two refuters agree on all of it — they differ only on whether "unreachable today" kills a defect the code deliberately wrote a branch for.

CONFIRMED IN THE TREE:
- engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1089-1092 — `VkSurfaceFormatKHR chosen = surface_formats.empty() ? VkSurfaceFormatKHR{ VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM, VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR } : surface_formats[0];` and the loop at :1093-1101 overrides it only on an exact B8G8R8A8_UNORM + SRGB_NONLINEAR hit. The comment at :1079-1080 ("...and the first thing offered otherwise") makes the fallback deliberate, not an oversight. Nothing anywhere guarantees a surface list contains BGRA8_UNORM — the comment asserts it, the code does not check it.
- :1144 `this->swapchain_format_ = chosen.format;`. Repo-wide grep gives exactly two hits for the member: that write and the declaration at device_resources.h:430. Nothing reads it. `colour_format_` (device_resources.h:454, fixed B8G8R8A8_UNORM) is read three times (:805, :924, :962) and exposed by an accessor. A member captured once and consumed nowhere is the fingerprint the finding says it is.
- present() branches on extent alone: :1568-1569 compares colour_extent_ against swapchain_extent_, :1577 vkCmdCopyImage, :1593 vkCmdBlitImage. No format term in the function, and the comment at :1562-1567 confirms the copy is the steady state, not the rare path.
- The Vulkan rule is right and I checked it independently of the finding: vkCmdCopyImage between size-compatible formats reinterprets texel bits with no component conversion (both BGRA8_UNORM and RGBA8_UNORM are in the 32-bit compatibility class, so such a copy is legal Vulkan that silently transposes R and B — validation would not warn, which is why the "checked with the validation layers" provenance does not cover it), while vkCmdBlitImage reads to float and writes through the destination encoding. The two branches genuinely do not mean the same thing unless the formats match.
- Nothing in the tree observes the present path: renderer.cpp:1205-1207 reads back `device_resources.colour_target()`, the engine-owned image, never a swapchain image, and device_resources.h:36-42 states the pixel contract deliberately never presents. Every golden stays green whatever the copy does.
- The precedent for the fix is in the same function: the TRANSFER_DST refusal at :1030-1038 throws by name for a surface this backend cannot use. That is T6 on a broken contract, applied to this very object.

WHAT I KILLED, agreeing with both refuters on two points and with Refuter A alone on a third:
- Android is unreachable at HEAD. device_resources.h:9 force-defines VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR, :447 pushes VK_KHR_WIN32_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME, :874-880 builds a VkWin32SurfaceCreateInfoKHR from an HWND, set_window takes an HWND, and all six presets are x64 Windows. docs/port/android.md is scoping only. The headline failure is not producible on anything this repository builds.
- The HDR claim is wrong. create_instance (:445-462) enables only VK_KHR_surface, VK_KHR_win32_surface and, in debug, VK_EXT_debug_utils. Without VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace only SRGB_NONLINEAR formats are reported, so VK_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT cannot be in the list and the size-incompatible-copy undefined behaviour cannot arise. That sentence should be struck.
- Refuter A is right that the finding's second proposed fix is wrong, and I verified the mechanism: blitting the UNORM colour target into a B8G8R8A8_SRGB destination applies the linear-to-sRGB encode on write and washes the frame out, where the raw copy hands the presentation engine exactly the bytes it wants under SRGB_NONLINEAR. So on an _SRGB surface it is the BLIT branch that is wrong, not the copy — the finding has the drag-resize brightness shift real but attributed backwards. Routing all mismatches to the blit would convert a latent trap into a live one.

WHY IT SURVIVES ANYWAY. Refuter A's own correction concedes both surviving items and recommends acting on them (assert or throw), which is a downgrade, not a refutation — an argument that ends "state the invariant or refuse the surface" has not killed the finding. The defect is in the tree as written: the code contains a deliberate fallback branch for a surface that offers something other than BGRA8_UNORM, and the consumer of that branch assumes one specific format without checking. Code that writes a fallback and gets it wrong is defective whether or not the fallback fires today; T1 says the speculative half is the `surface_formats[0]` fallback itself, and deleting it in favour of the throw at :1030-1038 closes the finding and retires the dead member in one move.

### C33. The texture upload's staging buffer is not released on any exception path, in the block whose own comment says every failure must put back what it took

**`engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:230`** · minor · `docs` · raised by R131, R154, R159 · run id `V87`

> Raised as should-fix; a refuter corrected it to minor.

MERGED — three independent lenses (claim-drift-code, conventions, simplify) hit the same block from three angles: the comment's stated invariant, the missing destroy in the catch, and the leak's cost on a retrying loader. Their evidence agrees exactly.

CLAIM: `add_texture_asset` creates a fourth live resource inside its try block and the catch releases only three, so any throw between texture_factory.cpp:230 and :304 leaks a VkBuffer, its host-visible VkDeviceMemory and a permanent mapping.

EVIDENCE, texture_factory.cpp:208-213 — the invariant the block states:

```
		// FROM HERE THE IMAGE IS OWNED BY NOBODY UNTIL THE LAST LINE, so every
		// failure between the two has to put it back. There is no ComPtr in
		// this API and no destructor to lean on: the VulkanTexture that will
		// own all three is not constructed until every one of them exists.
		try
```

:230 `VulkanBuffer staging = create_vulkan_buffer(owner, ..., "A texture's staging copy");` — released only on the success path at :304 `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);`. The catch at :320-331 frees `view`, `memory` and `image` and rethrows; it never names `staging`.

Throwing calls between :230 and :304: `copies.reserve`/`push_back` (:246-269, std::bad_alloc), `device_resources.begin_upload()` (two `check_vk` at device_resources.cpp:1855, 1863) and `device_resources.end_upload(commands)` (check_vk on vkEndCommandBuffer, on vkQueueSubmit, and inside wait_for_gpu, device_resources.cpp:1888-1898).

RULE: the comment above the try states the obligation the block then fails to meet for one of four resources. `VulkanBuffer` is deliberately a plain aggregate with free create/destroy functions — device_resources.h:155-163: "here they are two objects with two lifetimes. Pairing them in one struct is what stops the second from being forgotten" — so the hand-written unwind is the only mechanism and it has to be complete. It also breaks the API's destruction rule the same folder calls out at device_resources.h:110-113 as "the one shape of undefined behaviour this API gives no diagnostic for": vkDestroyDevice with live child objects (VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137).

FAILURE: a device lost or an out-of-device-memory during a manifest walk makes end_upload throw. The catch frees the image, its memory and the (still null) view and rethrows; the staging VkBuffer and its mapped VkDeviceMemory, sized to the whole texture, are leaked with nothing holding a handle. A resource_loader replaying a manifest over a flaky device leaks one host-visible allocation per texture attempted. At shutdown `~DeviceResources` reaches vkDestroyDevice with those live children: a validation error under the layers, undefined behaviour without them.

FIX: hoist `VulkanBuffer staging;` above the `try` and make `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);` the first statement of the catch — it is already null-safe on a zeroed struct — keeping or dropping the early release at :304 as preferred, and amend the comment at :208-211 to say four resources rather than three.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

CONFIRMED as a code defect; the docs framing and the blast radius are both wrong.

THE LEAK IS THERE. texture_factory.cpp:230 declares `VulkanBuffer staging` inside the try opened at :212 and closed at :319. `VulkanBuffer` is a plain aggregate with four data members and no destructor (device_resources.h:164-173), so scope exit on unwind does nothing. The only release is texture_factory.cpp:304 `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);`, on the success path. The catch is at :320 `catch (...)`, freeing `view` (:322-325), `memory` (:326-329) and `image` (:330) before rethrowing at :336 — `staging` is never named. Quoted evidence matches character for character at :208-211, :230 and :304.

THE THROW SITES ARE REAL. `check_vk` throws std::runtime_error on any non-VK_SUCCESS (device_resources.cpp:212-221). Between :230 and :304: `begin_upload()` at :267 check_vks vkAllocateCommandBuffers (device_resources.cpp:1856) and vkBeginCommandBuffer (:1862); `end_upload()` at :303 check_vks vkEndCommandBuffer (:1869) and vkQueueSubmit (:1895), and calls `wait_for_gpu()` which check_vks vkWaitSemaphores (:1684). VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST from vkQueueSubmit or vkWaitSemaphores is exactly the failure this backend's `handle_device_lost` machinery (device_resources.cpp:1265) exists to model. (`copies.reserve` at :241 is a bad_alloc of a dozen structs — not a serious trigger; `push_back` at :264 cannot reallocate after the reserve.)

THE TEARDOWN CONSEQUENCE IS REACHABLE FROM A REAL ENTRY POINT. samples/minimal/main.cpp:38 holds `Application app` as a local, with load_manifest (:45) and run (:47) inside the try and the catch at :48. A throw unwinds `app`, so ~DeviceResources runs and ~VulkanDevice calls vkDestroyDevice at device_resources.cpp:238 with the leaked VkBuffer and VkDeviceMemory still live. That is a true VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137 violation and a validation-layer object-leak report — and per the project's own record the validation layers are how this backend was verified.

THE HAND-UNWIND RULE IS REAL AND THIS IS THE DIVERGENCE. device_resources.h:158-163 (the finding cites :155-163; the quoted sentences are at :162-163) states the pairing rationale, and there is no RAII anywhere on VulkanBuffer, so the catch is the only mechanism. The D3D12 sibling's staging is `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource>` (engine/render/d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:207) and releases itself — which is exactly what texture_factory.cpp:209-210 identifies as absent here ("There is no ComPtr in this API and no destructor to lean on"). The file names the reason it must hand-unwind and then hand-unwinds three of four.

WHAT THE FINDING GETS WRONG. (1) The comment at :208-211 does not state the obligation attributed to it: "the VulkanTexture that will own ALL THREE is not constructed until every one of them exists" scopes it to image/memory/view. It never claims to cover staging, so it is incomplete rather than contradicted — this is not claim-drift and `area: docs` is the wrong label. (2) The accumulation scenario does not exist: engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:78-88 walks the manifest with no catch (the only catch in the file is the sound-bank one at :146-152), so the first throw aborts the walk — at most one leak per walk, not one per texture attempted. Nothing retries either: Application::on_device_restored (engine/app/application.cpp:439) is called from handle_device_lost (device_resources.cpp:1328), itself called from the frame path (:1225, :1417, :1537, :1631), and a throw propagates uncaught through engine/app/ to the sample's main catch. Every reachable trigger is terminal. (3) device_resources.h:110-113 describes the OPPOSITE hazard — "A texture destroyed after the device would be a call into a device that has gone, which is the one shape of undefined behaviour this API gives no diagnostic for" — i.e. a call into a dead device, not a device destroyed with live children, which the layers do diagnose. The VUID violation is genuine; that comment is not evidence for it.

The proposed fix is correct and null-safe: destroy_vulkan_buffer early-returns on a null device (device_resources.cpp:339-343) and guards each handle (:345-359), so hoisting `VulkanBuffer staging;` above the try and making the destroy the first statement of the catch is safe on a zeroed struct and idempotent after the :304 release.

Not checked here but adjacent and worse-shaped: create_vulkan_buffer itself leaks on its own internal failures — `owner.memory_type` throwing at device_resources.cpp:309 leaks result.buffer, and a vkBindBufferMemory (:321) or vkMapMemory (:329) failure leaks both — only the vkAllocateMemory case (:313-320) unwinds. Same-shaped sites also exist unprotected at renderer.cpp:582-599 and :1184-1240.

*Correction:* The defect survives; three things around it do not.

AREA IS WRONG. This is a code defect, not a docs one. The comment at texture_factory.cpp:208-211 is scoped to the image trio — "the VulkanTexture that will own ALL THREE is not constructed until every one of them exists" — and makes no claim about the staging buffer. It is incomplete, not false, so there is no claim-drift here. Amending it to say four is a nice-to-have; adding the destroy is the actual fix.

FAILURE MAGNITUDE IS OVERSTATED. "A resource_loader replaying a manifest over a flaky device leaks one host-visible allocation per texture attempted" does not describe this tree. resource_loader.cpp:78-88 has no catch, so the first throw aborts the entire manifest walk — one leaked staging buffer per walk at most. And no caller retries the walk: the only replay is handle_device_lost (device_resources.cpp:1265) -> on_device_restored (:1328) -> Application::on_device_restored (application.cpp:439) -> reload_device_resources, and a throw from there propagates uncaught out of the frame path, through engine/app/, to the sample's catch at samples/minimal/main.cpp:48, which exits. Every reachable trigger is a terminal run.

THE VUID CITATION'S SUPPORT IS BACKWARDS. device_resources.h:110-113 describes a texture destroyed AFTER the device — a call into a device that has gone — which it correctly calls the shape the API gives no diagnostic for. Destroying the device with live children is the shape the layers DO diagnose. The VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137 violation at device_resources.cpp:238 is genuine on the unwind path; that comment simply is not the rule being broken.

SEVERITY. Strip the retrying-loader narrative and what remains is one leaked staging buffer plus a validation-layer object-leak report at teardown, on a run that is already terminating because an upload failed. That is minor, not should-fix. It is still worth the three-line fix — the folder's stated discipline is hand-unwinding, the D3D12 sibling gets this free from ComPtr (d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:207), and a spurious object-leak report during device-loss testing under the layers is exactly the noise that wastes a reader's time. A reviewer arguing should-fix on discipline grounds alone would not be unreasonable, but the consequence claimed is not the consequence that occurs.

SCOPE THE FIX SHOULD COVER. The same omission is worse-shaped one file over: create_vulkan_buffer unwinds only its vkAllocateMemory failure (device_resources.cpp:313-320) and leaks result.buffer when owner.memory_type throws at :309, and leaks buffer and memory when vkBindBufferMemory (:321) or vkMapMemory (:329) fails. Two more unprotected staging sites sit at renderer.cpp:582-599 and :1184-1240.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

The structural claim is true and I verified every link of it.

LEAK IS REAL. `VulkanBuffer staging` is declared *inside* the try at texture_factory.cpp:230-235, so it is not even nameable from the catch. It is destroyed only on the success path, texture_factory.cpp:304 `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);`. The catch at texture_factory.cpp:320-337 frees `view`, `memory` and `image` and rethrows — no mention of staging. `VulkanBuffer` is a plain aggregate with no destructor (device_resources.h:164-175), so nothing reclaims it.

THE THROWS BETWEEN THEM EXIST. `check_vk` throws std::runtime_error on any non-VK_SUCCESS (device_resources.cpp:212-221). Between :230 and :304 the reachable throws are `begin_upload` at :267 — check_vk on vkAllocateCommandBuffers (device_resources.cpp:1855) and on vkBeginCommandBuffer (device_resources.cpp:1861) — and `end_upload` at :303 — check_vk on vkEndCommandBuffer (device_resources.cpp:1869), on vkQueueSubmit (device_resources.cpp:1892 via the `submitted != VK_SUCCESS` branch), and inside `wait_for_gpu` on vkWaitSemaphores (device_resources.cpp:1683). VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST is a documented return of vkQueueSubmit and vkWaitSemaphores; VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY / VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY of all five. The path is reachable.

THE TEARDOWN CONSEQUENCE STANDS. `~VulkanDevice` calls vkDestroyDevice unconditionally (device_resources.cpp:225-241) with no accounting of children. Vulkan requires that all child objects created on a device be destroyed before the device is (VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137, the current spelling of what was VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-00378) — so a surviving VkBuffer plus its VkDeviceMemory at that point is a real valid-usage violation the layers will report as an object-leak error.

NOT A SEAM QUESTION. The D3D12 backend holds its upload buffer as `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource> staging` (d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:207) and has no try/catch at all — RAII covers every throw. So this shape is specific to the hand-written unwind in vulkan/, which is why the finding is not answered by "the other backends do the same".

But three of the finding's supports do not hold, and one of them is its failure scenario.

(1) THE FAILURE SCENARIO IS UNREACHABLE. There is no retrying loader. `ResourceLoader::reload_device_resources` walks the manifest with no try/catch (resource_loader.cpp:96-108); the "texture" and "font" kinds are registered with lambdas that discard `optional` — `bool /*optional*/` at resource_loader.cpp:35-42 — so the optional-asset catch at resource_loader.cpp:152 covers sound banks only; `DeviceResources::handle_device_lost` calls `notify_->on_device_restored()` bare (device_resources.cpp:1326-1329); `Application::on_device_restored` calls the walk bare (application.cpp:428-439). The only handler above all of this is main's, which shows a MessageBox and returns 1 (samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49-57, samples/minimal/main.cpp:48). So the first throwing texture ends the walk and the process. "One host-visible allocation per texture attempted" is wrong: it is exactly one, once, on a path that is already terminating.

(2) THE COMMENT DOES NOT STATE THE OBLIGATION IT IS SAID TO STATE. texture_factory.cpp:208-211 reads "FROM HERE THE IMAGE IS OWNED BY NOBODY ... the VulkanTexture that will own all three is not constructed until every one of them exists." It names three by name, and they are the three VulkanTexture owns — image, memory, view — which are exactly the three the catch frees. The staging buffer is never owned by VulkanTexture and is outside what that sentence promises. The claim-drift angle of the merge is therefore refuted: comment and code agree.

(3) THE device_resources.h CITATION IS BACKWARDS. Lines 109-113 say "a VkImage is a handle with no reference in it, and vkDestroyImage takes the VkDevice as its first argument. A texture destroyed after the device would be a call into a device that has gone, which is the one shape of undefined behaviour this API gives no diagnostic for." That is about destroying a child *after* the device, not about destroying the device with live children — the opposite direction, and it is the argument for the shared_ptr refcount. It does not support the VUID point; the VUID does, on its own.

One thing the finding missed that bears on its fix: the same class of leak is inside `create_vulkan_buffer` itself (device_resources.cpp:285-334). It unwinds only the vkAllocateMemory failure (:313-318); `owner.memory_type` throwing at :311 leaks the just-created VkBuffer, and a failing vkBindBufferMemory (:320) or vkMapMemory (:330) leaks both. So hoisting `staging` above the try closes the caller's hole but not the callee's.

*Correction:* The leak itself is confirmed; three of the finding's four supports are not.

Failure scenario, replace: there is no retry and no catch-and-continue anywhere between add_texture_asset and main. reload_device_resources (resource_loader.cpp:96-108) has no try/catch, the texture and font kinds discard `optional` (resource_loader.cpp:35-42) so the optional-asset catch at :152 is sound-bank-only, handle_device_lost calls on_device_restored bare (device_resources.cpp:1326-1329), and main catches, message-boxes and returns 1. The cost is one leaked VkBuffer + VkDeviceMemory + mapping, once, on a path that then exits the process — not one per texture on a manifest walk.

Rule citation, drop: the comment at texture_factory.cpp:208-211 says "the VulkanTexture that will own all three", naming the three the catch actually frees. Comment and code agree; there is no claim drift, and the suggested amendment to "four resources" would make the comment less accurate about what VulkanTexture owns, not more. Say instead that the staging buffer sits outside the comment's scope and nothing else covers it.

Rule citation, drop: device_resources.h:109-113 is about destroying a texture after its device — a call into a device that has gone — not about vkDestroyDevice with live children. The VUID stands on its own without that passage.

Consequence that survives: stack unwinding reaches ~VulkanDevice (device_resources.cpp:225-241), which calls vkDestroyDevice with the buffer and its memory still alive — VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137, a validation-layer object-leak error under the layers this backend was checked with, formally undefined without them.

Severity should-fix -> minor: one-line fix, but every consequence lands on an already-fatal exit path where the OS reclaims the allocation, and the only durable artefact is a validation error at teardown. Worth fixing with the finding's own remedy (hoist `VulkanBuffer staging;` above the try, make destroy_vulkan_buffer the first statement of the catch — it is null-safe, device_resources.cpp:337-359), and worth doing in the same pass as the identical gaps inside create_vulkan_buffer at device_resources.cpp:311, 320 and 330, which the finding did not notice and which a fix confined to texture_factory.cpp leaves open.

### C34. add_texture_asset's catch destroys the image and frees its memory while the upload batch that copies into them may still be executing, because end_upload's post-submit wait is a throwing call

**`engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:320`** · minor · `core` · raised by R39, R9 · run id `V11`

> Raised as should-fix; a refuter corrected it to minor.

TWO LENSES (lifetimes, command-buffers). end_upload submits and only then waits: device_resources.cpp:1887 `const VkResult submitted = vkQueueSubmit(...)` succeeds, the GPU begins the vkCmdCopyBufferToImage into `image`, and device_resources.cpp:1902 `this->wait_for_gpu();` is `check_vk(vkWaitSemaphores(...), "The wait for the GPU did not finish")` - it throws. That throw unwinds into texture_factory.cpp:320-336, which immediately runs `if (memory != VK_NULL_HANDLE) { vkFreeMemory(device, memory, nullptr); } vkDestroyImage(device, image, nullptr);` on the destination of a copy that is still in flight. RULE BROKEN: Vulkan valid usage on vkDestroyImage/vkFreeMemory - all submitted commands referring to the object must have completed execution (VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000). The only thing that establishes that here is the very wait that threw, so the catch runs in exactly the state where its own precondition has not been met. FAILURE: a device reset or a host/device OOM during a manifest walk. vkWaitSemaphores returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY or VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, check_vk throws, and the handler frees an image and an allocation the queue is still reading: undefined behaviour, reported by the validation layers as an object destroyed while in use. It is most likely on the path renderer.h:511-543 exists for, because a post-restore reload_device_resources re-uploads every texture at once. FIX: make end_upload's post-submit wait non-throwing - `std::ignore = this->try_wait_for_gpu();` in place of device_resources.cpp:1902 - so that once a batch has gone to the queue, control cannot reach a caller's cleanup with GPU work still referencing what that cleanup is about to destroy. (If the wait's failure must be reported, report it after the free and after the wait, not before.)

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this and could not. Every quoted line is character-accurate and the chain is complete.

THE WINDOW IS REAL. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1887-1888` is exactly `const VkResult submitted = vkQueueSubmit(this->owner_->queue, 1, &submit, VK_NULL_HANDLE);`. The failure branch at 1889-1894 frees the command buffer and rethrows only when the submit itself failed — i.e. when nothing is in flight, which is correct. Past that branch the work is on the queue. The next statement is `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1902` `this->wait_for_gpu();`, and `wait_for_gpu` at 1670-1685 ends in `check_vk(vkWaitSemaphores(this->owner_->device, &wait, UINT64_MAX), "The wait for the GPU did not finish");` — the message matches the finding verbatim. `check_vk` at `device_resources.cpp:212-221` is `if (result == VK_SUCCESS) { return; } throw std::runtime_error(...)`, so any non-success throws. `vkWaitSemaphores` documents VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY, VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY and VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST; UINT64_MAX rules out VK_TIMEOUT. So the throw is reachable.

THE CATCH REALLY DOES DESTROY THE COPY DESTINATION. `add_texture_asset` spans `engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:129-355`. `image` is created at 194-196 and `memory` allocated and bound at 216-219, both before the upload. The copy into `image` is recorded at 284-286 (`vkCmdCopyBufferToImage(commands, staging.buffer, image, ...)`), and `device_resources.end_upload(commands);` is at line 303 — inside the `try` that opens at 212 and closes at 319. The handler is `catch (...)` at 320, and its body is `vkDestroyImageView` (324), `vkFreeMemory(device, memory, nullptr)` (328) and unconditional `vkDestroyImage(device, image, nullptr)` (330), then `throw;` (336). So a throw out of the wait at 1902 unwinds straight into 320 and frees the destination of a copy whose only completion guarantee was the wait that just failed. VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000 and VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-00677 are real and say precisely that all submitted commands referring to the object must have completed.

THE FIX IS THIS CODEBASE'S OWN IDIOM, WHICH KILLS THE "IT'S NOT A RULE HERE" DEFENCE. `bool try_wait_for_gpu() noexcept` is declared at `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:326` and defined at `device_resources.cpp:1688-1702`, returning `vkWaitSemaphores(...) == VK_SUCCESS` and never throwing. The suggested `std::ignore = this->try_wait_for_gpu();` is written verbatim at `device_resources.cpp:381` and `renderer.cpp:280`. Better still, the header comment at `device_resources.h:320-326` enumerates where throwing does more damage than the failure it reports — "two destructors ... and the resize path" — and `end_upload` is not among them. The gap is the codebase's own reasoning not having been applied to this call site.

SCOPE IS CORRECTLY NARROW. `end_upload` has exactly two callers (`renderer.cpp:598` and `texture_factory.cpp:303`). The renderer.cpp one at 592-599 has no handler at all, so a throw there merely leaks — safe. texture_factory.cpp is the only site with a destructive unwind, which is the only site the finding names.

REACHABLE FROM A REAL ENTRY POINT. `add_texture_asset` is called from `engine/render/resource_factory.cpp:77` and `:97`, and directly by `tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:678`, `:1807`, `:1810`. It is the ordinary texture load path, and `engine/render/resource_factory.h:88` documents it as throwing. No link in the chain is missing.

*Correction:* Three things the finding gets wrong or omits; none of them touch the conclusion.

1. ITS "MOST LIKELY" TRIGGER IS ITS WEAKEST HALF, AND THE RANKING IS INVERTED. The finding says "It is most likely on the path renderer.h:511-543 exists for, because a post-restore reload_device_resources re-uploads every texture at once." That path is the least dangerous instance, for two reasons. A post-restore reload runs on a freshly created device, so it is not a device-lost-while-waiting scenario at all; the many uploads only raise the number of exposures. And in a genuine device-lost case the queue is not "still reading" — execution has terminated, a lost device's timeline can never signal, so the completion precondition is unsatisfiable by construction and tearing objects down anyway is the only thing an application can do (validation layers handle that state specially). The sound trigger is the healthy-device one the finding also names: `vkWaitSemaphores` returning VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY or VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY, where the copy genuinely is in flight and the image is genuinely freed under it. The conclusion stands on that half alone.

2. THE PROPOSED FIX IS RIGHT IN DIRECTION BUT INCOMPLETE. Replacing device_resources.cpp:1902 with `std::ignore = this->try_wait_for_gpu();` stops the unwind into the destructive catch, which is the important half. But control then falls to `vkFreeCommandBuffers` at device_resources.cpp:1904, which carries the same requirement (VUID-vkFreeCommandBuffers-pCommandBuffers-00047: all submitted commands must have completed). So in the wait-failed case the non-throwing wait relocates a valid-usage violation rather than removing it — though a command buffer freed early is far less harmful than an image being written by an in-flight copy after its memory is released. Whoever applies this should decide what end_upload does with a false return, not just silence it.

3. AN OMITTED SECONDARY EFFECT, WHICH HAPPENS TO BE PROTECTIVE. On this same unwind the staging buffer leaks: `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging)` at texture_factory.cpp:304 is skipped, the catch at 322-330 does not free it, and `VulkanBuffer` at device_resources.h:164-175 is a plain struct with no destructor. The upload command buffer leaks likewise (device_resources.cpp:1904 skipped). Both are leaks rather than UB — and the staging leak is why only the copy's destination is at risk and not its source.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

THE MECHANICS ARE QUOTED CORRECTLY; THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT.

What is true. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1887-1888` submits, `:1902` then calls `this->wait_for_gpu()`, which at `:1671-1686` ends in `check_vk(vkWaitSemaphores(..., UINT64_MAX), "The wait for the GPU did not finish")`, and `check_vk` (`:212-221`) throws on any non-`VK_SUCCESS`. `vkWaitSemaphores` with an infinite timeout can return `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY`, `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` or `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`, so a throw after the submit is a real code path, and `engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:320-330` does then run `vkFreeMemory` and `vkDestroyImage`. The VUIDs cited exist and say what the finding says (VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000, VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-00677: all submitted commands referring to the object must have completed execution).

WHY IT DIES — 1. THE NAMED TRIGGER IS THE BRANCH WHERE DESTROYING IS LEGAL AND MANDATORY. The finding's failure scenario leads with "a device reset" and points at the device-loss reload path. On `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` the Vulkan spec's Lost Device section is explicit: "When a device is lost, its child objects are not implicitly destroyed and their handles are still valid. Those objects must still be destroyed before their parents or the device can be destroyed... It is still legal to call any API command on the device and child objects." No wait can ever succeed again on that device, so the VU's precondition is permanently unsatisfiable and destruction is the only move the application has — leaking the image instead does not make `vkDestroyDevice` reachable, it makes it illegal.

2. THIS BACKEND'S OWN ACCEPTED RECOVERY PATH DOES EXACTLY WHAT THE FINDING CALLS UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR. `device_resources.cpp:1265-1305` (`handle_device_lost`) calls `on_device_lost` to empty the texture table — destroying every `VkImage` and its memory — then `std::ignore = vkDeviceWaitIdle(...)` at `:1280` (return value discarded, and on a lost device it returns `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`), then destroys the frames, the swapchain, the colour target, the render pass at `:1293`, the upload pool at `:1298` and the timeline semaphore at `:1303`. Same at `:1223-1234`. If the rule bit on the device-lost branch, the backend's central, deliberately documented recovery would be the defect, not one catch block in the texture factory.

3. THE IDENTICAL SHAPE IS AT HEAD IN THE ACCEPTED D3D12 BACKEND. `engine/render/d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:272-273` is `impl.execute_frame_list(); impl.device_resources.wait_for_gpu();` — that `wait_for_gpu` throws (`d3d12/device_resources.cpp:541-554`), and the function has no try/catch at all, so unwinding releases the `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource> resource` and `staging` locals that the just-executed list references. D3D12 does no lifetime tracking for GPU work either. That backend had a dedicated review whose must-fix, should-fix and minor findings were all applied, and which examined this very function's throwing wait at length (`docs/review/d3d12/all-findings.md:492-493`, `:652-711`, `:2491-2574`). So this is a shared load-path idiom of the seam, not something `4d91b91` introduces.

4. THE PROPOSED FIX RELOCATES THE HAZARD RATHER THAN REMOVING IT — which shows the defect was mislocated. With `std::ignore = try_wait_for_gpu()` at `device_resources.cpp:1902`, control returns normally to `texture_factory.cpp:304`, which unconditionally calls `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging)`; that function (`device_resources.cpp:336-360`) unmaps, `vkDestroyBuffer`s and `vkFreeMemory`s the copy's *source* in exactly the same in-flight state (VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-00922). `renderer.cpp:598-599` does the same with the index staging buffer. On the device-lost branch the fix also never establishes the precondition — the image just gets destroyed later by `~VulkanTexture`, after a `try_wait_for_gpu`/`vkDeviceWaitIdle` pair whose failures are ignored at `:381-386`.

5. AND THE FIX FIGHTS A SETTLED DECISION. `d3d12/device_resources.h:134-152` names the non-throwing wait as being for exactly three places — two destructors and `create_window_size_dependent_resources` — "WHERE THROWING DOES MORE DAMAGE THAN THE FAILURE IT REPORTS"; the load path deliberately keeps the throwing form so a failed load is reported (T6). Vulkan mirrors that exactly: `try_wait_for_gpu` is used only at `device_resources.cpp:381` (destructor), `:1223` (swapchain recreate) and `renderer.cpp:280` (destructor). Swallowing it on the load path puts a texture whose upload never completed into the registry and reports nothing.

RESIDUE. The one branch the refutation does not cover is `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY`/`OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` from `vkWaitSemaphores` on a still-live device — there the copy really is in flight and the destroy really is a VU violation. That is a driver host-allocation failure inside a wait, in a process that has just allocated an image, a device allocation, a staging buffer and memcpy'd the pixels into it; nothing in `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp` catches the resulting throw either (its only catch, at `:145-152`, is the optional-sound-bank case), so the process is on its way to a T6 stop. As a code shape it is at most minor, it is shared with `d3d12/texture_factory.cpp`, and point 4 shows it is not fixable at `texture_factory.cpp:320`.

*Correction:* Two things survive, neither at should-fix and neither as stated. (a) A post-submit wait that can fail at all leaves the next statement destroying something the queue may still reference — but that is a property of the shared load-path idiom (`vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:303-304` destroys the staging buffer immediately after `end_upload`; `d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:272-273` releases two ComPtrs on unwind from the same call), reachable only on a wait that returns OOM on a live device, and not localisable to the catch at `vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:320`. Minor at most, and a seam-level observation, not a Vulkan-backend defect. (b) Separately and unmentioned by the finding: when the wait at `device_resources.cpp:1902` throws, the upload command buffer is never freed (`:1904` is skipped, and the free at `:1891` is on the submit-failure branch only) and the staging buffer at `texture_factory.cpp:230` is never destroyed — two leaks on a path that is about to stop the program anyway. Leaks, not undefined behaviour. The finding's central claim — that the catch causes UB on the device-loss path the reload exists for — is wrong: on a lost device destroying child objects is legal per the spec's Lost Device section and is what `handle_device_lost` (`device_resources.cpp:1265-1305`) itself does by design.

**Adjudicator** — the two disagreed, so a third read the code. *confirmed*

Every line both refuters quote is character-accurate, and the mechanism the finding describes does exist — but only on one of the two branches it names, and not where it says the defect lives.

WHAT IS TRUE. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1887-1888 is `const VkResult submitted = vkQueueSubmit(this->owner_->queue, 1, &submit, VK_NULL_HANDLE);`, and the failure branch at :1889-1894 frees the command buffer and rethrows only when the submit itself failed — i.e. only when nothing is in flight. That throw does unwind into engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:320's `catch (...)`, whose body runs vkDestroyImageView (:324), vkFreeMemory (:328) and unconditional vkDestroyImage (:330) on the destination of the vkCmdCopyBufferToImage recorded at :287-289. WHAT IS WRONG — 1. THE HEADLINE TRIGGER IS THE BRANCH WHERE DESTROYING IS LEGAL. The finding leads with "a device reset" and points at the reload_device_resources path. On VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST the spec's Lost Device section makes destruction of child objects legal and mandatory, and this backend already relies on that: DeviceResources::handle_device_lost (device_resources.cpp:1265-1305) calls on_device_lost to empty the texture table — destroying every VkImage and its memory — then `std::ignore = vkDeviceWaitIdle(...)` at :1280 (return discarded, and on a lost device it returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST), then destroys the frames, colour target, render pass (:1293), upload pool (:1298) and timeline (:1303). If the rule bit on the device-lost branch, the backend's documented recovery would be the defect. Refuter A concedes this in its own correction. Only the live-device OOM half survives — a driver host-allocation failure inside a semaphore wait, in a process that is on its way to a T6 stop (engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp's only catch, at :145-152, is the optional-sound-bank case; reload_device_resources at :96-108 catches nothing).

2. THE PROPOSED FIX RELOCATES THE VIOLATION, WHICH SHOWS THE DEFECT IS MISLOCATED. With `std::ignore = try_wait_for_gpu()` at device_resources.cpp:1902, control returns normally to texture_factory.cpp:304, which unconditionally calls `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging)`; that function (device_resources.cpp:336-360) unmaps, vkDestroyBuffers and vkFreeMemorys the copy's *source* in exactly the same wait-failed state (VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-00922). vulkan/renderer.cpp:598-599 does the same with the index staging buffer, and device_resources.cpp:1904's vkFreeCommandBuffers carries VUID-vkFreeCommandBuffers-pCommandBuffers-00047. The catch at :320 is one of four teardowns with the same unmet precondition, not the site of the defect.

3. THE FIX ALSO FIGHTS A DOCUMENTED, SETTLED DECISION, AND REFUTER A READS THE COMMENT BACKWARDS. vulkan/device_resources.h:320-326 says try_wait_for_gpu is "THE SAME WAIT, FOR THE PLACES WHERE THROWING DOES MORE DAMAGE THAN THE FAILURE IT REPORTS — two destructors ... and the resize path", citing d3d12/device_resources.h for the argument. That list is exhaustive by design, not an oversight: the load path deliberately keeps the throwing form so a failed load is reported (T6). It is used at exactly device_resources.cpp:381 (destructor), :1223 (swapchain recreate) and renderer.cpp:280 (destructor). A's "the gap is the codebase's own reasoning not having been applied to this call site" inverts the comment — applying it there would silently register a texture whose upload never completed. That decision came out of the d3d12 review's C5 and G7 (docs/review/d3d12/all-findings.md:652-711, :2491-2574), both of which examined this exact throwing wait and confined the non-throwing form to destructors and resize.

4. IT IS A SHARED LOAD-PATH IDIOM, NOT SOMETHING 4d91b91 INTRODUCES. d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:271-272 is `impl.execute_frame_list(); impl.device_resources.wait_for_gpu();`, that wait throws, and add_texture_asset there has no try/catch at all (only `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource> resource` at :158 and `staging` at :207), so unwinding releases both in flight with no lifetime tracking either. Same shape, at HEAD, after a dedicated review whose must-fix, should-fix and minor findings were all applied.

CONCLUSION. The mechanism is real on one narrow branch, so the finding is not refuted — but it is not should-fix. Its named trigger is the legal case, its fix would move the same violation one line later while regressing a documented T6 decision, and the residue is a seam-wide observation about a post-submit throwing wait that is not fixable at texture_factory.cpp:320. Minor.
