## Confirmed by gap probe — raised after the critics, refuted again before counting

16 findings. Three completeness critics were shown what the lenses had found and what they said they could not check, and named nine probes; these are what the probes came back with, put through the same two refuters.

### G1. create_swapchain's zero-extent (minimised) early return leaves the old swapchain installed, so present()'s two "nothing to present into" guards can never fire and a minimised window ends the frame in a throw instead

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059`** · must-fix · `probe` · raised by P2 · run id `P2.1`

EVIDENCE: create_swapchain, lines 1059-1067:

1059:		if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u)
1060:		{
1061:			// A minimised window. There is nothing to present into and there
1062:			// will be again; present() answers this by doing nothing rather
1063:			// than by refusing, because a shell that keeps drawing while
1064:			// minimised is the ordinary case and not a mistake.
1065:			this->swapchain_extent_ = extent;
1066:			return;
1067:		}

Note what is *not* on line 1065: `this->destroy_swapchain();`. The only place `swapchain_` is ever set to VK_NULL_HANDLE is destroy_swapchain (1204-1209), and create_swapchain reaches it only at line 1140, *after* this early return.

present(), lines 1513-1533:

1513:		if (acquired == VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR)
1514:		{
...
1522:			this->rebuild_swapchain();
1523:			if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)
1524:			{
1525:				this->execute();
1526:				this->frame_index_ = (this->frame_index_ + 1) % FRAME_COUNT;
1527:				return;
1528:			}
1529:
1530:			acquired = vkAcquireNextImageKHR(this->owner_->device,
1531:				this->swapchain_, UINT64_MAX, this->frame().acquired,
1532:				VK_NULL_HANDLE, &image);
1533:		}

and then 1540-1543:

1540:		if (acquired != VK_SUCCESS && acquired != VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR)
1541:		{
1542:			check_vk(acquired, "No swapchain image could be acquired");
1543:		}

rebuild_swapchain (1171-1184) is `vkDeviceWaitIdle` + `create_swapchain()` and nothing else.

WHY WRONG: Two rules. (1) The DRIFT standard this review is held to - "a comment the code does not match is a defect" (docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md, restated in CLAUDE.md). The comment at 1061-1064 states "present() answers this by doing nothing rather than by refusing", and present()'s own comment at 1497 says its `swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE` guard covers "Minimised, or a swapchain that could not be made at this size". Neither is true on the rebuild path: create_swapchain never nulls `swapchain_`, so the guard at 1523 is provably dead code - present() only reaches line 1522 when `swapchain_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE` (checked at 1495), and rebuild_swapchain can only leave it unchanged, replace it with a fresh non-null handle, or throw. (2) The commit message's own claim, lines 26-27: "stale news is answered inside present() because what it invalidates is not what the seam calls the back buffer". It is not answered; it escapes as std::runtime_error. T6 governs what a throw is for, and "the window was minimised" is not a broken contract.

FAILURE: The shell keeps drawing while minimised - Window::pump_until_quit (engine/app/window.cpp:239-247) calls tick() whenever the queue is empty, and WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED takes the on_suspending branch (window.cpp:387-395) without stopping Application::render(), which calls begin_frame/submit/end_frame every iteration. Minimise the window: the Win32 surface now reports currentExtent {0,0} and the presentation engine declares the swapchain out of date. The next end_frame -> present() gets VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR from the acquire at 1509, calls rebuild_swapchain() at 1522, which reaches the branch at 1059 and returns leaving the old 1280x720 swapchain installed and `swapchain_extent_` = {0,0}. The guard at 1523 does not fire. The second acquire at 1530 runs against the same out-of-date swapchain and returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again. Line 1542 throws std::runtime_error("No swapchain image could be acquired: VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR") out of present() -> Renderer::end_frame -> Application::render -> tick -> pump_until_quit, where nothing catches it until samples/minimal/main.cpp:48 - which pops a MessageBox titled "Sample - startup failure" and returns 1. Minimising the sample kills it. The four sibling backends survive this: d3d11/d3d12 ResizeBuffers a std::max(...,1u) size and GL does nothing at all. Secondary consequence if the window is restored between the two acquires so the second one succeeds: `swapchain_extent_` is {0,0} while `swapchain_` is a live full-size swapchain, so present() takes the else branch at 1583 and issues vkCmdBlitImage with dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1} - a degenerate destination region into a full-size image, i.e. a presented frame that was never written.

FIX: Add `this->destroy_swapchain();` as the first statement of the branch at 1060 (and clear `swapchain_format_` with it), so that a zero extent leaves `swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE` and both of present()'s guards mean what their comments say. This is safe on all three callers of create_swapchain, which is exactly why the fix belongs there: rebuild_swapchain has just done vkDeviceWaitIdle (1182), create_window_size_dependent_resources has done one (1229-1234), and handle_device_lost has done one (1276-1279) and has already destroyed the swapchain anyway - so no present is outstanding on the `presentable_` semaphores destroy_swapchain frees. With that line in place the minimised frame takes 1523-1528, executes what it recorded, advances the frame index and returns, which is what 1061-1064 promises.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried to kill this on five fronts and it survived all of them.

1. THE MECHANISM IS AS CLAIMED. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067` returns before ever touching `swapchain_`; the only assignment of `VK_NULL_HANDLE` to it is in `destroy_swapchain` (1205-1208), and `create_swapchain` reaches that only at line 1140, after `vkCreateSwapchainKHR`. So a zero-extent create leaves the previous handle installed and sets `swapchain_extent_ = {0,0}` (1065).

2. THE 1523 GUARD IS GENUINELY DEAD. `present()` reaches 1522 only when `swapchain_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE` (checked 1495). `rebuild_swapchain` (1171-1184) is `vkDeviceWaitIdle` + `create_swapchain` and nothing else — no `destroy_swapchain` — so it can leave the handle unchanged, replace it with a fresh non-null one, or throw out of `check_vk` (1141). It cannot leave it null. Note the early return at 1172-1175 also leaves it unchanged. Confirmed dead.

3. THE SHELL REALLY DOES KEEP DRAWING. `Window::pump_until_quit` (window.cpp:234-250) calls `tick()` whenever the queue drains; `WM_SIZE`/`SIZE_MINIMIZED` (window.cpp:380-395) calls only `on_suspending`, and `Application::on_suspending` (application.cpp:352-364) touches gamepads, focus and audio — nothing that stops rendering. `Application::tick` (254-258) calls `render()` unconditionally and `render()` (280-299) calls `begin_frame`/`submit`/`end_frame` after the first update. `Renderer::end_frame` (vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867) calls `present()` with no guard.

4. NOTHING CATCHES IT. `check_vk` throws `std::runtime_error` for every non-`VK_SUCCESS` (device_resources.cpp:212-221), so line 1542 throws on `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR`. There is no `catch` between there and `main` — `Application::run` (200-206), `tick`, `render` and `pump_until_quit` all have none; `grep catch engine/app/*.cpp engine/render/vulkan/*.cpp` finds only texture_factory.cpp:320. The sample's `catch (const std::exception&)` MessageBox-and-return-1 is the terminus.

5. THE ESCAPE ROUTES I LOOKED FOR DO NOT EXIST. `create_window_size_dependent_resources` (1216-1241) does NOT call `destroy_swapchain` before `create_swapchain` at 1240, so even a size-change route would leave the stale handle installed — and minimise never takes that route anyway: `on_window_moved` (application.cpp:381-386) compares `back_buffer_size()` against `output_size_`, and Vulkan's `back_buffer_size` is `colour_extent_` (vulkan/renderer.cpp:1158-1169), i.e. `output_size_` clamped to >=1 (create_colour_target, 905-913), so that call is a self-comparison returning false. `handle_device_lost` (1276-1283) is the one caller that does destroy first, which is why the 1495 guard is not dead in general — see correction.

The one genuinely driver-dependent link is whether a minimised Win32 window makes acquire/present report `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR`. That does not save the code: `rebuild_swapchain` is called from exactly two places, present's acquire path (1522) and its present path (1641), so the zero-extent branch's own existence presupposes that behaviour. If the implementation reports it, the second acquire at 1530 runs against the same never-recreated swapchain, returns the same error and line 1542 throws — the sample dies on minimise. If it never reports it, the branch is unreachable and the comments at 1061-1064 and 1497-1501 describe a state that cannot occur. Either way the code does not do what it says, and on the implementations the branch was written for it crashes.

*Correction:* Two corrections, neither refuting.

(a) "present()'s two guards can never fire" is too strong. The 1495 guard is reachable — at startup into an already-minimised window (`create_window_size_dependent_resources` runs with `swapchain_` never yet made), and after `handle_device_lost`, which destroys the swapchain at 1283 before reaching `create_swapchain` at 1240. It is the *minimise-while-running* path where 1495 cannot fire. Only the 1523 guard is dead unconditionally.

(b) The finding under-states the non-crash form, which is worse than a race. `swapchain_extent_ = {0,0}` is sticky: it is only ever rewritten at 1145, on a successful create. If the OUT_OF_DATE arrives from the present side (1638-1643) rather than the acquire side, the rebuild happens after the frame, the stale extent is recorded, and if the window is later restored to the size the surviving swapchain already has, nothing triggers another rebuild — so `colour_extent_ != swapchain_extent_` forever and every subsequent present takes the blit at 1583-1594 with `dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1}`, writing nothing into the presented image. A permanently blank window, no throw, no diagnostic. That makes the defect user-visible even where the throw is not reached.

Also worth recording for whoever fixes it: the proposed `destroy_swapchain()` in the branch is safe at all three call sites — `rebuild_swapchain` waits idle at 1182, `create_window_size_dependent_resources` at 1233, and `handle_device_lost` at 1278 before destroying at 1283 — and it introduces no new assumption, since line 1140 already destroys the swapchain and its `presentable_` semaphores after exactly those same waits.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

Confirmed against HEAD. (1) engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067 — the zero-extent branch sets swapchain_extent_ = {0,0} and returns without destroy_swapchain(). (2) swapchain_ is set to VK_NULL_HANDLE in exactly one place, destroy_swapchain at :1208 (verified by grep: only :1143 and :1208 assign it); create_swapchain reaches destroy_swapchain at :1140, after the early return. Every other exit of create_swapchain either throws (:1070 usage-flag throw, :1141 check_vk(created)) or ends at :1143 with a non-null handle. rebuild_swapchain (:1171-1184) is only an owner/device early-return plus vkDeviceWaitIdle (:1181) plus create_swapchain (:1183). So after :1522 the handle is unchanged and non-null — present() reaches :1522 only past the :1495 non-null check — and the guard at :1523 is dead. (3) The retry acquire at :1530-1532 runs on the same swapchain that just returned VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR; :1540-1543 then calls check_vk, which throws std::runtime_error unconditionally for any non-VK_SUCCESS (:212-220). (4) Reach: window.cpp:386-398 takes the on_suspending branch on SIZE_MINIMIZED and never calls on_window_size_changed (the restore branch at :399-407 calls only on_resuming); pump_until_quit (window.cpp:234-247) keeps calling tick(); Application::tick (application.cpp:254-258) calls render() unconditionally, and render() (application.cpp:280-302) runs begin_frame/submit/end_frame every iteration. Renderer::end_frame (vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867) calls present() with no try/catch between it and samples/minimal/main.cpp:48 (grep for catch finds only the two sample mains). grep for "minimi" across engine/render/vulkan/ returns only the comments at :1061-1064 and :1497-1500 — there is no executable minimise handling anywhere in the backend, and no test covers it. (5) Rule: docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:9-10 holds comments in engine/render/ to the seam's own standard, and its listed entries are exactly this shape; the comment at :1061-1064 ("present() answers this by doing nothing rather than by refusing") and the one at :1497-1500 ("Minimised, or a swapchain that could not be made at this size") are both false on the rebuild path, as is the commit message's "stale news is answered inside present()". (6) The proposed fix's safety argument holds: rebuild_swapchain waits idle at :1181, create_window_size_dependent_resources at :1229-1234, handle_device_lost at :1276-1283 (and already destroys the swapchain there).

*Correction:* Two corrections, neither rescuing the code. (a) The sibling-backend mechanism is wrong: on minimise no backend's resize path runs at all, because window.cpp:386-398 never calls on_window_size_changed for SIZE_MINIMIZED — so "d3d11/d3d12 ResizeBuffers a std::max(...,1u) size" is not what saves them. They survive because IDXGISwapChain::Present returns DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED, a success code, and both only test FAILED(hr) (d3d11/device_resources.cpp:396,416; d3d12/device_resources.cpp:472,487). Conclusion unchanged. (b) The throw is driver-conditional, not spec-guaranteed: it needs vkAcquireNextImageKHR at :1509 (or vkQueuePresentKHR at :1627-1641, which routes to the same no-op rebuild) to report VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR for a minimised window. The spec note on VkSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR anticipates maxImageExtent becoming (0,0) when a window is minimised and that no swapchain can then be created — which is why the branch at :1059 exists at all — but it does not mandate that acquire report staleness. What is provable with no driver at all is the dead guard at :1523, the two false comments, and swapchain_extent_ = {0,0} (:1065) left beside a live swapchain, which sends the next present() into the blit at :1583-1596 with a zero-area dstOffsets[1]. Also minor: destroy_swapchain (:1186-1210) does not currently clear swapchain_format_, so the finding's parenthetical is an addition to that function rather than something it already does.

### G2. create_swapchain's zero-extent early return does not release the swapchain it is replacing, so after a minimise present() retries the acquire on a stale swapchain and throws out of the pump

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059`** · must-fix · `probe` · raised by P5 · run id `P5.1`

EVIDENCE: device_resources.cpp:1059-1067 - `if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u) {  // A minimised window. There is nothing to present into and there  // will be again; present() answers this by doing nothing rather  // than by refusing, because a shell that keeps drawing while  // minimised is the ordinary case and not a mistake.  this->swapchain_extent_ = extent;  return; }` - no destroy_swapchain() on this path; the only `destroy_swapchain()` calls in the file are at 388 (teardown), 1140 (after a SUCCESSFUL vkCreateSwapchainKHR) and 1283 (handle_device_lost), and neither caller destroys first (rebuild_swapchain 1171-1184 does vkDeviceWaitIdle then create_swapchain; create_window_size_dependent_resources 1212-1241 does wait / abandon_commands / destroy_colour_target / create_colour_target / create_swapchain). present()'s no-op guard is `if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE)` (1495), and the retry after a rebuild is guarded the same way (1523).

WHY WRONG: The comment at 1061-1064 states the contract this branch is supposed to establish - "present() answers this by doing nothing rather than by refusing" - and present() can only do nothing when `swapchain_` is VK_NULL_HANDLE. The branch sets `swapchain_extent_` to {0,0} but leaves `swapchain_` pointing at the pre-minimise swapchain, so the two halves never meet. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard: a comment the code does not match is a defect. The shell makes it reachable rather than theoretical: Window::pump_until_quit (engine/app/window.cpp:239-247) calls `notify_->tick()` on every iteration where PeekMessage finds nothing, a minimised window produces no messages, and Application::tick/render (application.cpp:254-258, 280-300) has no minimised gate - only `GetFrameCount() == 0`. So end_frame -> present() runs every frame while minimised, and window.cpp:387-398 never forwards a size, so present()'s own out-of-date path is the ONLY thing that can rebuild.

FAILURE: Run MinimalSample on x64-debug-vulkan and click minimise. The client rect is 0x0, so the surface's currentExtent is {0,0} and the live swapchain is out of date (the same premise the comment at 1061 asserts). Next frame: present() at 1509 gets VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR; 1522 rebuild_swapchain() -> vkDeviceWaitIdle -> create_swapchain() -> zero-extent early return, `swapchain_` unchanged; 1523 `swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE` is false, so 1530 re-acquires from the SAME stale swapchain. Nothing can have changed in between - the window can only be resized by messages on this thread and this thread is inside present() - so the second acquire returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again, 1540 is taken and check_vk at 1542 throws std::runtime_error("No swapchain image could be acquired"). It unwinds Renderer::end_frame (renderer.cpp:866) -> Application::render -> tick -> pump_until_quit -> samples/minimal/main.cpp:48, which puts up a MessageBox and returns 1. Minimising the window kills the game. (On a WSI that keeps returning images for a minimised window instead, the same branch leaves `swapchain_extent_` = {0,0} beside images that are still the old size, so the copy/blit test at 1568 takes the blit path with dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1} - bookkeeping that describes a swapchain that does not exist.)

FIX: Call `this->destroy_swapchain();` immediately before `this->swapchain_extent_ = extent; return;` at 1065. Both callers have already done vkDeviceWaitIdle, so the destroy is safe there, and it is what makes present()'s VK_NULL_HANDLE branch - the one the comment names - the branch that actually runs.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried to kill this three ways — the branch, the reachability, and the throw path — and all three hold.

THE BRANCH IS AS QUOTED. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067` sets `swapchain_extent_ = extent` ({0,0}) and returns with no `destroy_swapchain()`. `grep -n "destroy_swapchain"` over the file gives exactly four hits: 388 (destructor), 1140 (after `vkCreateSwapchainKHR`, before the `check_vk` at 1141), 1186 (the definition) and 1283 (`handle_device_lost`). `swapchain_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE` is assigned in exactly one place, `destroy_swapchain` at 1208. So after a zero-extent early return the member still names the pre-minimise swapchain — still owned and still valid, so this is not a leak or a use-after-free, it is a state-contract mismatch, which is what the finding claims.

NEITHER CALLER DESTROYS FIRST. `rebuild_swapchain` (1171-1184) is `vkDeviceWaitIdle` then `create_swapchain`. `create_window_size_dependent_resources` (1212-1241) is try_wait / `vkDeviceWaitIdle` / `abandon_commands` / `destroy_colour_target` / `create_colour_target` / `create_swapchain` — no swapchain destroy anywhere in it. The two call sites where the branch IS correct are the ones where `swapchain_` is already null: first creation (renderer.cpp:763) and `handle_device_lost`, which destroys at 1283 and only then re-enters `create_window_size_dependent_resources` at 1324. That is almost certainly why the branch reads as it does, and it is exactly the two rebuild paths it gets wrong.

THE SHELL REACHES IT. `Window::pump_until_quit` (engine/app/window.cpp:234-249) calls `notify_->tick()` on every iteration PeekMessage finds nothing; a minimised window is quiet. `Application::tick` (application.cpp:254-258) is `timer_.Tick(update); render();` and `Application::render` (280-300) gates only on `GetFrameCount() == 0` before `begin_frame / draw / submit / end_frame`. Minimise does fire `on_suspending` (window.cpp:387-398) but `Application::on_suspending` (application.cpp:352-364) only suspends gamepads, drops focus and suspends audio — it does not stop the loop. This codebase's own history already confirms this: docs/review/all-findings.md:668 and :6823 are the pre-split findings "the main loop never gates on suspend/minimise". `Renderer::end_frame` (vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867) calls `device_resources.present()` unconditionally, and neither `begin_frame` (825-854) nor `open_frame` (664-701) has a size or minimise guard.

AND NOTHING ELSE CAN REBUILD DURING A MINIMISE. window.cpp:387-406: the SIZE_MINIMIZED branch and the restore branch both consume their WM_SIZE without calling `on_window_size_changed` — independently confirmed at docs/review/backend-equivalence/README.md:97 and :171. WM_MOVE (window.cpp:359-368, minimise does move the window to -32000) routes to `Application::on_window_moved` (application.cpp:382-388), which passes `back_buffer_size()` back in, and `DeviceResources::window_size_changed` (1243-1254) early-returns false when the size matches `output_size_`. So `present()`'s own OUT_OF_DATE handling is the only channel, exactly as claimed.

THE THROW ESCAPES. `check_vk` (212-221) throws `std::runtime_error` for any non-VK_SUCCESS, and 1540-1543 routes anything that is not SUCCESS/SUBOPTIMAL into it. There is no try/catch between there and `wWinMain`: `Application::run` (200-206) is `transition_to; pump_until_quit; return exit_code`, and `tick()` is called from the PeekMessage else-branch, not from inside DispatchMessage, so it unwinds normally into samples/minimal/main.cpp:46-56 — MessageBox, return 1.

The only step not provable from this tree is that a Win32 driver returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR for a 0x0 client area. It is the ordinary behaviour (minImageExtent == maxImageExtent == currentExtent == {0,0} means no swapchain of any size is compatible, and the branch at 1059 exists precisely because the author expects to be called in that state), and once one acquire has said it, the retry at 1530 cannot see anything different: `rebuild_swapchain` only waits idle and re-queries, and the window can only change via messages on the thread that is currently inside `present()`. The spec's "may" is the one soft joint, and on the driver that instead keeps handing out images the same branch still leaves `swapchain_extent_ = {0,0}` beside a live swapchain of the old size, so 1568 takes the blit path with `dstOffsets[1] = {0,0,1}` — a degenerate blit that presents nothing. Defect either way; crash on the ordinary way.

*Correction:* Two corrections, neither of which touches the defect.

1. THE PROPOSED FIX IS INCOMPLETE AND REGRESSIVE ON ITS OWN. Adding `this->destroy_swapchain();` at 1065 stops the crash and then strands the window: `present()`'s null branch (1495-1504) executes the frame and returns without ever attempting a rebuild, and the restore-from-minimise WM_SIZE is consumed at window.cpp:399-406 without forwarding a size (docs/review/backend-equivalence/README.md:97). So after restoring, nothing calls `create_swapchain` again — not `window_size_changed` (no size arrives), not `on_window_moved` (application.cpp:382-388 passes the unchanged size, and 1250-1254 returns false), not `present()`. The window presents nothing for the rest of the run until the user happens to drag an edge. 2) present() never retries. device_resources.cpp:1493-1504: `void DeviceResources::present()` opens with `if (this->swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE) { ... this->execute(); this->frame_index_ = (this->frame_index_ + 1) % FRAME_COUNT; return; }`. No capabilities query, no create call. Confirmed by grep: the only calls to `create_swapchain()` are device_resources.cpp:1183 (inside `rebuild_swapchain`, 1171-1184) and 1240 (inside `create_window_size_dependent_resources`, 1212-1241). `rebuild_swapchain` has exactly two call sites, 1522 and 1641, and both are inside present() *past* the 1495 guard (1522 is the VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE branch after vkAcquireNextImageKHR at 1509; 1641 is after vkQueuePresentKHR) — neither can run with a null swapchain. `create_window_size_dependent_resources` has two call sites: device_resources.cpp:1261 (from `window_size_changed`, which early-returns at 1249-1254 when the size matches `output_size_`) and 1324 (inside `handle_device_lost`), plus vulkan/renderer.cpp:763 in create_device.

3) The shell genuinely never delivers the news. engine/app/window.cpp:380-413 — the WM_SIZE arms are `if (self && w_param == SIZE_MINIMIZED)` / `else if (self && self->minimized_)` / `else if (self && !self->in_sizemove_)`, so the restore WM_SIZE is consumed by the second arm (`minimized_ = false; ... on_resuming();`) and the `on_window_size_changed` arm at 408-412 is never reached on a restore. Application::on_resuming (engine/app/application.cpp:366-379) touches timer, pads, input focus and audio only. WM_ACTIVATEAPP (window.cpp:443-455) calls on_activated/on_deactivated only; the WM_POWERBROADCAST resume (476) calls on_resuming. `grep` for on_window_size_changed shows only two producers in the whole tree: window.cpp:410 and window.cpp:429 (WM_EXITSIZEMOVE). The remaining candidate, on_window_moved (application.cpp:381-386), passes `renderer_->back_buffer_size()` back into `window_size_changed` — and vulkan/renderer.cpp:1158-1169 returns `device_resources.colour_extent()`, i.e. the engine-owned 1280x720, so Renderer::window_size_changed (renderer.cpp:768-782) early-returns false on the equality test against `output_size()`. Self-comparison confirmed.

4) Reachability. Application::initialize calls create_window (application.cpp:106) — which constructs Window with the caller's `show_command` (application.cpp:151-168, window.cpp:214-215: `ShowWindow(this->handle_, options.fullscreen ? SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED : show_command)`) — and only afterwards, at application.cpp:118-121, calls `renderer_->create_device(...)` with `resolution_manager_->resolution_ivec()`. A SIZE_MINIMIZED WM_SIZE takes the first arm at window.cpp:387-398 and never corrects the resolution manager, so create_device gets 1280x720, `create_colour_target` succeeds, and `create_swapchain` (called from renderer.cpp:763) sees `currentExtent` {0,0} and returns at 1066. Nothing earlier depends on the extent: the only surface capability query in the file is at device_resources.cpp:1028 inside create_swapchain (grep confirms one occurrence); create_device_resources (863-900) does the surface at 879 and the queue-family support probe at 585, both size-independent. And the frame loop keeps running regardless of minimisation — Application::render (application.cpp:279-300) has no suspend gate, so begin_frame/submit/end_frame run every tick and end_frame reaches present at vulkan/renderer.cpp:866. WM_PAINT outside a sizemove is BeginPaint/EndPaint with nothing drawn (window.cpp:344-357), so the window shows the class brush COLOR_WINDOW+1 (window.cpp:163) forever.

5) It is new with this commit rather than an inherited shell limitation. engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.cpp:238-239 and 277-278 size the swap chain from `m_outputSize` clamped to a minimum of 1, so the other backends launch minimised with a working swap chain and paint on restore. Vulkan is the only one that can end with no presentation object and no route back — which is precisely what device_resources.h:44-47 says ("a Win32 surface reports minImageExtent == maxImageExtent == the window's client area"), making the refusal correct and the never-retrying the defect.

*Correction:* Three refinements, none of which weaken it.

(a) The recovery set is slightly wider than the finding states. It says "WM_EXITSIZEMOVE at window.cpp:422-432 is the one path"; in fact any WM_SIZE arriving while `minimized_` is already false and `in_sizemove_` is false takes the third arm at window.cpp:408-412 — so maximising the window, or a programmatic leave_fullscreen (window.cpp:291), also delivers a differing size and recovers it. Both are still user-initiated resizes; nothing in the ordinary running of the game recovers it.

(b) There is a second reachable route the finding does not list, and it needs no unusual launch: a device loss while the window is minimised. handle_device_lost calls destroy_swapchain (device_resources.cpp:1284) and then create_window_size_dependent_resources at device_resources.cpp:1324, which calls create_swapchain at 1240 with a zero extent — same permanent dead end, on a machine that TDRs during a minimised session.

(c) Severity. The trigger is narrow on its own (launch minimised, or a TDR while minimised), which by itself would read as should-fix. It is must-fix because of the coupling the finding names: the correct fix for the sibling stale-handle finding is to release the swapchain in the zero-extent branch, at which point every ordinary minimise/restore lands here. Whoever fixes that one must fix this one in the same commit or convert a rare blank window into a routine one.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

Every link the finding needs is in the code as it stands at HEAD, and I could not break any of them.

1. The dead end itself. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1059-1067` — `if (extent.width == 0u || extent.height == 0u) { this->swapchain_extent_ = extent; return; }` — returns before `vkCreateSwapchainKHR`, leaving `swapchain_` as it was (VK_NULL_HANDLE on the first call). `present()` at `:1495-1504` then does exactly what the finding quotes: on a null swapchain it calls `execute()`, advances `frame_index_`, and returns — no `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR`, no rebuild attempt.

2. There is no other door in. `grep` for `create_swapchain` in the backend gives four sites: the definition (`:1023`), `rebuild_swapchain` (`:1183`) and `create_window_size_dependent_resources` (`:1240`). `rebuild_swapchain` has exactly two callers, `device_resources.cpp:1522` and `:1641`, both *after* the null-swapchain early return at `:1495`, so neither is reachable while `swapchain_` is null. `create_window_size_dependent_resources` has three callers: `vulkan/renderer.cpp:763` (create_device), `device_resources.cpp:1261` (inside `DeviceResources::window_size_changed`, which early-returns at `:1250-1254` unless the size differs) and `:1324` (handle_device_lost).

3. The shell really does not deliver a size on restore. `engine/app/window.cpp:387-413`: the three WM_SIZE arms are exclusive; the restore arm at `:399-407` sets `minimized_ = false` and calls `on_resuming()` only, and `break`s at `:413` without reaching the `on_window_size_changed` arm at `:408-412`. `Application::on_resuming` (`application.cpp:366-379`) touches timer, pads, focus and audio and never the renderer. Outside `engine/render/`, the only callers of `Renderer::window_size_changed` are `application.cpp:384` (from `on_window_moved`, which feeds it `renderer_->back_buffer_size()` — a self-comparison) and `application.cpp:411` (from `on_window_size_changed`, fed only by window.cpp:410 and window.cpp:429/WM_EXITSIZEMOVE). This shell behaviour is independently documented as confirmed in `docs/review/backend-equivalence/README.md:97` and `:171`.

4. The self-comparison really is one on this backend. `vulkan/renderer.cpp:1158-1169` answers `back_buffer_size()` from `colour_extent()`, i.e. the size the shell last said (1280x720), so `on_window_moved` hands `window_size_changed` the number `output_size_` already holds and `renderer.cpp:778-783` returns false.

5. Startup while minimised reaches the branch. `wWinMain`'s `show_command` flows `samples/minimal/main.cpp:39` -> `application.cpp:106,167` -> `window.cpp:151,214-215` `ShowWindow(handle_, show_command)`; `start /min` and a shortcut set to Run: Minimized both supply SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE. The resulting WM_SIZE is SIZE_MINIMIZED, so `window.cpp:387-398` calls `on_suspending` only and the resolution manager keeps its preset; `application.cpp:114-121` then calls `create_device` with that preset, `set_window` stamps `output_size_` 1280x720 (`device_resources.cpp:425-433`), `create_colour_target` builds a valid 1280x720 image from `output_size_` (`:905-938`), and `create_swapchain` takes the zero-extent return. The zero `currentExtent` for a minimised Win32 window is not folklore — the Vulkan spec's own `VkSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR` note says the extent may become (0,0) when a window is minimised and that no swapchain can then be created, and this file's comment at `:1061-1064` names the case ("A minimised window ... there will be again").

6. The consequence is what is claimed. `Application::render()` (`application.cpp:279-301`) has no minimised gate and runs `begin_frame`/`submit`/`end_frame` every tick; `end_frame` calls `present()` (`vulkan/renderer.cpp:857`), which returns at `:1503` forever. WM_PAINT outside a drag does BeginPaint/EndPaint only (`window.cpp:344-356`) and the class brush is `COLOR_WINDOW + 1` (`window.cpp:164`), so the restored window stays the system window colour for the life of the process. Only a real resize (`window.cpp:422-432`) or a maximise after the restore recovers it.

7. No other backend has this dead end, which is why it is a backend divergence rather than an engine-wide known gap: `d3d11/device_resources.cpp:238-239` and `:277-278` size the swap chain from `m_outputSize` clamped to >= 1, `d3d12/device_resources.cpp:361` likewise, and GL has no swapchain at all — none of them consults the surface, so a minimised launch costs them nothing once restored.

*Correction:* Two things to scope, neither of which rescues the code.

(a) The title reads wider than the reachable set. An ordinary minimise/restore of a running process does NOT reach this today: nothing calls `create_swapchain` on a minimise, so the swapchain survives at its old extent; and if a driver reports OUT_OF_DATE while minimised, `rebuild_swapchain` -> `create_swapchain` returns at :1066 with the OLD `swapchain_` handle still installed, so present keeps trying and recovers on restore. The finding says this itself ("Independent of the finding above"), but a reader should take the reachable triggers as: the process launched minimised, and — a second route the finding does not name — `handle_device_lost()` occurring while minimised, since `device_resources.cpp:1324` runs `create_window_size_dependent_resources` -> `create_swapchain` into the same zero-extent return, and `handle_device_lost` is reachable from the `execute()` that `present()` still calls at `:1501`. Once either happens the state is permanent, and a game calling `set_fullscreen`/`set_resolution` to escape does not help: `enter_fullscreen`'s `ShowWindow(SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED)` (`window.cpp:278`) produces a WM_SIZE the `minimized_` arm at `window.cpp:399-407` swallows.

(b) One driver-dependent detail in the launch-minimised symptom: the `supportedUsageFlags & VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT` test at `device_resources.cpp:1032-1039` runs BEFORE the extent test, so a driver that reports no TRANSFER_DST for a zero-extent surface would make the minimised launch throw out of `create_device` instead of showing a blank window. Blank window or startup throw, the branch is still wrong; the fix the finding proposes (query capabilities in the null-swapchain arm of `present()` and create when the extent is non-zero) addresses both.

Severity confirmed at must-fix: the trigger needs no client code at all, it is unrecoverable within the process except by a manual resize, and the other four backends survive the same launch.

### G5. Renderer::read_back_buffer discards execute()'s documented device-lost answer, then reads and destroys its read-back buffer against a VkDevice that handle_device_lost has already destroyed

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221`** · must-fix · `probe` · raised by P4 · run id `P4.1`

EVIDENCE: renderer.cpp:1184  `VulkanBuffer readback = create_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.owner(),`
renderer.cpp:1221  `device_resources.execute();`   <- bool discarded
renderer.cpp:1224  `device_resources.wait_for_gpu();`
renderer.cpp:1231  `static_cast<const unsigned char*>(readback.mapped);`
renderer.cpp:1240  `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback);`

device_resources.h:287-292  `// ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on // the way out. That is not a courtesy: ...`  `bool execute(VkSemaphore wait = VK_NULL_HANDLE, ...);`

device_resources.cpp:1314-1318  `// Released rather than destroyed: anything still holding one of these - // a texture whose owner has not got round to dropping it - keeps the // old device alive until it does, which is exactly the guarantee COM // gives the D3D12 backend for free.`  `this->owner_.reset();`

device_resources.h:164-175  `struct VulkanBuffer { VkBuffer buffer; VkDeviceMemory memory; VkDeviceSize bytes; void* mapped; };`  (no shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>)
device_resources.cpp:232-241  `// NOTHING WAITS HERE, because whoever gets to this point has already // waited.` ... `vkDestroyDevice(this->device, nullptr);`

WHY WRONG: device_resources.h:287-291 makes execute()'s false return a term of the class's own contract and says in terms that it is "not a courtesy". present() is the only other caller and honours it (device_resources.cpp:1607-1615, "There is nothing left of this frame to present"); read_back_buffer does not. The premise that makes ignoring it look safe - device_resources.cpp:1314-1317's claim that owner_.reset() gives "exactly the guarantee COM gives the D3D12 backend for free" - is only true for VulkanTexture, the one type that holds a shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> (backend.h:106, device_resources.h:100-117). A VulkanBuffer holds four raw handles and nothing else (device_resources.h:164-175), so the D3D12 equivalence claimed here does not hold for the very object read_back_buffer has live on its stack: an ID3D12Resource staged for a read-back does hold a reference on its device, this does not. On top of that, ~VulkanDevice calls vkDestroyDevice while those child objects are still alive, which VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137 forbids.

FAILURE: A client draws a frame and calls read_back_buffer between submit() and end_frame(), which is where renderer.h:473-474 puts it. A TDR or GPU reset makes vkQueueSubmit inside execute() return VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST (device_resources.cpp:1412-1419). handle_device_lost then runs to completion on the stack: Application::on_device_lost empties the texture registry (application.cpp:414-425 -> RenderResources::release_device_resources -> Registry::release_all), which drops the last shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> any texture held; owner_.reset() at device_resources.cpp:1318 therefore runs ~VulkanDevice and vkDestroyDevice while readback.buffer and readback.memory are still alive; a new instance, device, timeline, frames, colour target and swapchain are built, and Application::on_device_restored (application.cpp:428-440) replays the manifest, uploading all 43 textures. execute() returns false. read_back_buffer ignores it: line 1224 waits on the NEW timeline (already signalled), lines 1231-1238 copy width*height*4 bytes out of readback.mapped - a pointer into memory freed by vkDestroyDevice - so the caller's `pixels` gets freed-heap garbage or the read faults; then line 1240 calls vkDestroyBuffer/vkFreeMemory with the NEW VkDevice and handles belonging to the destroyed one. Even in a configuration with no DeviceNotify wired (so a texture keeps the old device alive), line 1240 still crosses two devices.

FIX: Keep the device alive for the duration of the call the way VulkanTexture does, and honour the bool. At the top of read_back_buffer take `std::shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> owner = device_resources.shared_device();`, create the buffer from `*owner` and destroy it with `owner->device`; then replace line 1221 with `if (!device_resources.execute()) { destroy_vulkan_buffer(owner->device, readback); throw std::runtime_error("The back buffer could not be read: the device was lost and has been rebuilt."); }`. renderer.h:377-380 already says a device event surfaces as a throw mid-frame, so a throw is the seam's own vocabulary here; what must not happen is the map read and the destroy running on the far side of a device rebuild.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

Confirmed line by line at HEAD (4d91b91).

execute()'s contract: device_resources.h:287-292 documents the false return as "ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out. That is not a courtesy". The implementation matches exactly: device_resources.cpp:1368-1431 returns true at :1372 (nothing recorded) and :1431 (submitted), and false only at :1414-1419 after vkQueueSubmit gives VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and handle_device_lost() has already returned. So false uniquely means "rebuilt underneath you".

The discard: renderer.cpp:1221 is `device_resources.execute();` with the bool dropped. It is the only call site in the folder that drops it against live state (the other three are device_resources.cpp:1501, :1525, :1607).

The live stack object: renderer.cpp:1184 builds the read-back buffer from device_resources.owner(), which is `const VulkanDevice& owner() const { return *this->owner_; }` (device_resources.h:345) — a bare reference, no refcount. create_vulkan_buffer (device_resources.cpp:286-335) maps HOST_VISIBLE memory at :330 and the struct comment (device_resources.h:170-174) says it is never unmapped, so readback.mapped points into the old device's memory. VulkanBuffer is four raw handles (device_resources.h:164-175) and holds no shared_ptr.

The teardown: handle_device_lost (device_resources.cpp:1265-1328) calls notify_->on_device_lost() at :1275, waits idle, destroys swapchain/colour target/frames/render pass/upload pool/timeline/surface, then owner_.reset() at :1318, then create_device_resources() which does `this->owner_ = std::make_shared<VulkanDevice>()` at :871. notify_ is always non-null: renderer.cpp:263 registers Impl unconditionally; Impl::on_device_lost (renderer.cpp:703-710) destroys its own device-dependent resources and forwards to the seam's DeviceNotify, which Application::on_device_lost (application.cpp:414-425) answers with render_resources_->release_device_resources(). VulkanTexture is the only other holder of shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> (backend.h:91, :104; argued at device_resources.h:101-116), so with the shell wired the last reference goes at :1318 and ~VulkanDevice (device_resources.cpp:225-240) calls vkDestroyDevice with readback.buffer and readback.memory still alive — child objects outliving their device, and its own comment says "NOTHING WAITS HERE, because whoever gets to this point has already waited", which is untrue of this caller.

The consequence back in the caller: renderer.cpp:1231-1238 reads width*height*4 bytes out of readback.mapped, memory freed by vkDestroyDevice, and hands it to the caller as the pixel contract's answer; renderer.cpp:1240 calls destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback), and device() (device_resources.h:335) now returns the NEW VkDevice, so vkUnmapMemory/vkDestroyBuffer/vkFreeMemory (device_resources.cpp:337-360) run with one device's handles on another device. That second half is wrong even when a surviving texture keeps the old device alive.

The asymmetry the finding rests on is real: the safety premise at device_resources.cpp:1313-1317 ("exactly the guarantee COM gives the D3D12 backend for free") holds only for VulkanTexture. The D3D12 twin (d3d12/renderer.cpp:1272-1354) keeps its read-back in a ComPtr<ID3D12Resource>, and its execute_frame_list (d3d12/renderer.cpp:575-589) cannot rebuild a device inline — ExecuteCommandLists returns void. Vulkan's execute() is the only submit behind this seam that can tear the device down under its caller.

Reachability: renderer.h:473 states the call sits between submit() and end_frame(); renderer.h:378 already makes a device event a mid-frame throw, and shared_device() (device_resources.h:330) exists for the pinning half, so the proposed fix is in the backend's own vocabulary. The only in-tree caller today is tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:496, but read_back_buffer is a declared term of the public seam (renderer.h:480) and vkQueueSubmit returning VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST is an ordinary TDR outcome.

Severity calibration: docs/review/d3d12/README.md:89-150 sets the must-fix bar at a seam-reachable state error whose worst case most drivers tolerate. This is worse than that bar — a use-after-free read handed back as pixel data plus a cross-device destroy.

*Correction:* Three details in the write-up are off; none changes the defect or its severity.

1. The failure narrative says line 1224 "waits on the NEW timeline (already signalled)". It does not wait at all: handle_device_lost sets timeline_value_ = 0 (device_resources.cpp:1320-1321), and wait_for_gpu's first guard (device_resources.cpp:1671-1675) returns immediately when timeline_value_ == 0. Execution simply falls through to the bad read at :1231. The mechanism after that is exactly as described.

2. "present() is the only other caller and honours it" is loose. present() calls execute() three times — device_resources.cpp:1501, :1525 and :1607 — and drops the bool at the first two. Those two are benign (both return immediately after), so the point stands at the function level, but the sentence overstates the tidiness of the existing callers.

3. The texture's shared_ptr member is backend.h:104 (constructor parameter at :91), not :106.

One clarification on the second failure branch: notify_ is never null (renderer.cpp:263 registers Impl unconditionally). The case the finding calls "no DeviceNotify wired" is a client that never called Renderer::set_device_notify, so Impl::notify is null (renderer.cpp:707-710) and the texture table is never emptied. That only helps if at least one VulkanTexture is alive; with none, owner_.reset() destroys the device regardless and the full use-after-free applies.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I tried to kill this on four axes — the rule, the code, the reachability, and the consequence — and it holds on all four.

THE RULE, stated precisely and checked:
1. The codebase's own rule. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:287-292` is the declaration of `execute()`, and its comment reads "ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out. That is not a courtesy: ...". That is a term of this class's contract, in its own header, in its own words. `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221` is a bare `device_resources.execute();` with the bool discarded. The only other caller honours it: `device_resources.cpp:1607-1615` checks it and returns with "There is nothing left of this frame to present." So the rule is real and read_back_buffer is the one place that breaks it.
2. The Vulkan rule. `vkDestroyDevice` carries the valid-usage requirement that all child objects created on the device be destroyed first, and the common "-parent" valid usage requires a handle passed to a command to have come from the device passed alongside it (`vkUnmapMemory`, `vkDestroyBuffer`, `vkFreeMemory` all carry it). Neither is folklore; both are Valid Usage in the spec's Fundamentals/common VU sections. `vkQueueSubmit` lists `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` among its return codes, so the trigger is spec-sanctioned too.

THE CODE, verified line by line at HEAD (4d91b91):
- `renderer.cpp:1184` `VulkanBuffer readback = create_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.owner(), ...)` — `owner()` is `device_resources.h:345`, `const VulkanDevice& owner() const { return *this->owner_; }`, a bare reference. No refcount is taken.
- `device_resources.h:164-175` — `VulkanBuffer` is four POD members (`VkBuffer`, `VkDeviceMemory`, `VkDeviceSize`, `void* mapped`). No `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>`. A repo-wide grep for `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>` returns exactly three sites: `backend.h:91`/`backend.h:104` (VulkanTexture's member) and `device_resources.h:424`/`330` (owner_ and shared_device()). So `VulkanTexture` is the *only* type that holds the device alive — which means `device_resources.cpp:1314-1318`'s claim that `owner_.reset()` gives "exactly the guarantee COM gives the D3D12 backend for free" is true for textures and false for the object read_back_buffer has live on its stack. The finding's central asymmetry is confirmed by grep, not by argument.
- `device_resources.cpp:1412-1419`: `vkQueueSubmit` → `if (submitted == VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) { this->handle_device_lost(); return false; }`. The rebuild runs *inline, on this stack*, before `execute()` returns.
- `handle_device_lost` (`device_resources.cpp:1264-1328`): calls `notify_->on_device_lost()` first, then destroys swapchain/colour target/frames/render pass/upload pool/timeline/surface, then `this->owner_.reset()` at 1318, then `create_device_resources()` + `create_window_size_dependent_resources()` and `on_device_restored()`.
- `VulkanDevice::~VulkanDevice` (`device_resources.cpp:225-241`): "NOTHING WAITS HERE" then `vkDestroyDevice(this->device, nullptr);` — with `readback.buffer` and `readback.memory` still alive. That is the vkDestroyDevice VU violation, and the comment's premise ("This object outlives DeviceResources by exactly as long as some texture still names it") is precisely the premise that fails here, because a VulkanBuffer names nothing.
- Back in read_back_buffer: `1224` `wait_for_gpu()`, `1231-1238` reads `readback.mapped`, `1240` `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback)`. `device()` is `device_resources.h:335-338` — it returns `owner_->device`, i.e. after the rebuild, the NEW VkDevice. `destroy_vulkan_buffer` (`device_resources.cpp:337-359`) only short-circuits on `VK_NULL_HANDLE`; a live new device means it really calls `vkUnmapMemory` / `vkDestroyBuffer` / `vkFreeMemory` with the new device and the old handles.

REACHABILITY — the axis most findings die on, and this one does not:
- read_back_buffer always records: `transition_colour` and `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer(device_resources.commands(), ...)` at 1207-1213 open the buffer, so `execute()` at 1221 always reaches `vkQueueSubmit` rather than the `if (!this->recording_) return true;` early-out.
- Nothing between 1221 and 1231 stops the walk. I specifically checked whether `wait_for_gpu()` would throw and save it: `device_resources.cpp:1671-1676` returns immediately when `timeline_value_ == 0`, and `handle_device_lost` sets `timeline_value_ = 0` at 1320. So line 1224 is a no-op after a rebuild and control falls straight into the dangling map read.
- The device-notify chain the failure scenario describes is real: `renderer.cpp:263` `register_device_notify(this)`, `renderer.cpp:703-711` forwards to the seam's `DeviceNotify`, `application.cpp:414-425` `on_device_lost` → `render_resources_->release_device_resources()`, which empties the texture table and drops the last `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>`. So in the shipping configuration the refcount really does reach zero at line 1318.
- And the weaker configuration is not a refuge: with no notify wired, a texture keeps the old device alive, the map read is fine — but line 1240 still hands old handles to a new device. There is no configuration in which this code is correct after a lost submit.
- `renderer.h:473-474` does place the call "BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame()", inside a live frame, and `renderer.h:377-380` does say a device event "surfaces as a throw from a worker mid-frame" — so the finding's proposed vocabulary is the seam's own.

WHY THIS BACKEND AND NOT THE OTHERS (I checked, hoping to find a house pattern that would excuse it): `d3d12/renderer.cpp:1272-1345` has the identical shape — `impl.execute_frame_list(); device_resources.wait_for_gpu();` with no device-lost check — but it is safe for two reasons that do not transfer. `execute_frame_list` (`d3d12/renderer.cpp:575-590`) never rebuilds; D3D12's `handle_device_lost` is only reached from the present/acquire paths (`d3d12/device_resources.cpp:319, 344, 483`). And its `readback` is a `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource>`, which holds a real COM reference on the device. Vulkan is the only backend where the rebuild happens *inside* the call read_back_buffer makes, and the only one whose staging buffer holds no reference. So this is not a shared house pattern being singled out — it is a real divergence introduced by this commit.

*Correction:* Three inaccuracies that survive without changing the conclusion, and one that a reader should not repeat:

1. The headline is loose. "reads and destroys its read-back buffer against a VkDevice that handle_device_lost has already destroyed" is not quite what happens at line 1240 — `device_resources.device()` (device_resources.h:335-338) returns the NEW device, so the destroy crosses two devices rather than using the dead one. The map read at 1231 is the one that touches memory belonging to the destroyed device. The FAILURE paragraph gets both right ("with the NEW VkDevice and handles belonging to the destroyed one"); only the one-line summary blurs them.

2. "line 1224 waits on the NEW timeline (already signalled)" is wrong in mechanism: `wait_for_gpu` returns at device_resources.cpp:1673 without waiting at all, because `handle_device_lost` zeroes `timeline_value_` (device_resources.cpp:1320). This strengthens the finding — there is not even a chance of a throw there to abort the walk — but the stated mechanism is not what the code does.

3. The VUID number should not be quoted as gospel. The rule is real and is what matters ("all child objects created on device must have been destroyed prior to destroying device", plus the common `-parent` valid usage that a handle must come from the device it is passed with), but the specific id has been renumbered across spec revisions and I could not verify VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137 against a spec copy in this read-only tree. Cite the rule, not the number.

4. Worth adding, because it is the part that makes this must-fix rather than should-fix: the cross-device destroy at line 1240 is not merely a leak. Non-dispatchable handles are per-device values a driver is free to reuse, so `vkDestroyBuffer`/`vkFreeMemory` on the rebuilt device may name a live object of the new device rather than nothing at all. That is a use-after-free with a silent, non-local victim, and it fires in *every* configuration — including the no-DeviceNotify one the finding correctly identifies as still broken.

The proposed fix is the right shape: `shared_device()` already exists at device_resources.h:330 and is exactly what `texture_factory.cpp:353` uses to give a VulkanTexture its reference, so holding one for the duration of read_back_buffer is this folder's own established answer rather than a new mechanism.

### G6. Renderer::read_back_buffer discards execute()'s device-lost answer, then reads and frees a VkBuffer belonging to a VkDevice that handle_device_lost has already destroyed, against its replacement

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221`** · must-fix · `probe` · raised by P8 · run id `P8.1`

EVIDENCE: renderer.cpp:1181-1189 — "// Made per call and thrown away: this is not a frame-path function and // a cached read-back buffer would be one more thing to remake on a // device loss. VulkanBuffer readback = create_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.owner(), ...)"
renderer.cpp:1221 — "device_resources.execute();"  (return value discarded)
renderer.cpp:1231 — "static_cast<const unsigned char*>(readback.mapped);"
renderer.cpp:1240 — "destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback);"
device_resources.h:287-291 — "ANSWERS FALSE WHEN THE DEVICE WAS LOST, having rebuilt everything on the way out. That is not a courtesy..."
device_resources.cpp:1415-1418 — "if (submitted == VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) { this->handle_device_lost(); return false; }"
device_resources.cpp:1313-1318 — "// Released rather than destroyed: anything still holding one of these ... this->owner_.reset();"

WHY WRONG: device_resources.h:287-291 makes execute()'s bool a term of this backend's own contract — false means the device was replaced inside the call — and present() honours it (device_resources.cpp:1607, "if (!this->execute(current.acquired, ...))"). read_back_buffer is the one caller that does not. It is also the exact hazard render_resources.h:112-143 and vulkan/device_resources.h:102-118 were written for: "a VkImage is a handle with no reference in it and vkDestroyImage takes the VkDevice as its first argument. A texture destroyed after the device would be a call into a device that has gone, which is the one shape of undefined behaviour this API gives no diagnostic for." Every VulkanTexture was given a shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> to close that hole; this local VulkanBuffer has no such reference, and line 1240 re-reads device_resources.device() *after* the rebuild, so it names the wrong device rather than a dead one. It is also the point where the transliteration from D3D12 breaks: d3d12/renderer.cpp:1296 holds its read-back as `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource> readback`, whose Release is safe across a device replacement because COM holds a reference on the device — the property render_resources.h:132 relies on and vulkan/backend.h:78-88 says had to be supplied by hand.

FAILURE: A client (RenderPixelTests, or any client of the seam) calls submit() then read_back_buffer(). The GPU TDRs, so the vkQueueSubmit inside execute() at device_resources.cpp:1412 returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST. handle_device_lost() runs to completion inside line 1221: notify_->on_device_lost() reaches Application::on_device_lost (application.cpp:414) which calls render_resources_->release_device_resources(), every VulkanTexture is destroyed and drops its shared_ptr, so owner_.reset() at device_resources.cpp:1318 is the last reference and ~VulkanDevice calls vkDestroyDevice — while `readback.buffer` and `readback.memory`, children of that device, are still alive (VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-00378). A new VkInstance/VkDevice is then created and the shell reloads every texture onto it. Control returns to line 1221; line 1231 dereferences readback.mapped, host memory unmapped and freed with the destroyed device (read of freed memory, and no copy ever executed into it so the pixels handed back are garbage even if it does not fault); line 1240 then calls vkUnmapMemory/vkDestroyBuffer/vkFreeMemory with the NEW VkDevice and the OLD device's handles (VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-parent).

FIX: Take and hold the device for the whole call, and check the answer. At the top: `const std::shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> owner = device_resources.shared_device();` then create the buffer from `*owner` and destroy it with `owner->device` at line 1240 — which is the same shared_ptr guarantee VulkanTexture already uses. And branch on execute(): `if (!device_resources.execute()) { destroy_vulkan_buffer(owner->device, readback); throw std::runtime_error("The back buffer could not be read: the device was lost during the copy and has been rebuilt."); }` before the wait and the mapped read, so no destroyed-device memory is ever touched and the caller is not handed a frame that was never copied.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `must-fix`

I read the whole of `Renderer::read_back_buffer` (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1172-1241), `DeviceResources::execute` (device_resources.cpp:1375-1432), `handle_device_lost` (device_resources.cpp:1265-1330), `create_vulkan_buffer`/`destroy_vulkan_buffer` (device_resources.cpp:286-360), the accessors (device_resources.h:330-345), and the callers. Every cited line number is exact and every link in the chain is real.

1. The local has no device reference. `VulkanBuffer` (device_resources.h:164-175) is four POD fields — `VkBuffer`, `VkDeviceMemory`, `VkDeviceSize`, `void* mapped` — and no `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>`. `create_vulkan_buffer` takes `const VulkanDevice&` (device_resources.h:177), and renderer.cpp:1184 passes `device_resources.owner()`, which is `const VulkanDevice&` (device_resources.h:345). No reference is taken. Contrast `VulkanTexture`, which holds `std::shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> owner_` (backend.h:104), handed to it at texture_factory.cpp:353 from `shared_device()` — the only other holder of that shared_ptr in the backend.

The submit is real, not a no-op: renderer.cpp:1206 records through `device_resources.commands()`, so `recording_` is true and execute reaches `vkQueueSubmit` at device_resources.cpp:1412.

3. The device really is replaced inside line 1221, and nothing tears the local down. handle_device_lost calls `notify_->on_device_lost()` (device_resources.cpp:1276) — `notify_` is always set, Renderer::Impl registers itself at renderer.cpp:263. That reaches `Renderer::Impl::on_device_lost` (renderer.cpp:703), which destroys the Impl's own device-dependent objects against the still-old device, then forwards to the seam notify → `Application::on_device_lost` (application.cpp:414-426) → `release_device_resources()`, dropping every VulkanTexture's shared_ptr. `this->owner_.reset()` (device_resources.cpp:1318) is then the last reference, and `~VulkanDevice` calls `vkDestroyDevice` (device_resources.cpp:237-241) while `readback.buffer`/`readback.memory` are alive. `create_device_resources()` at line 1323 then installs a new device. `readback` is a local nobody registered, so nothing in that path frees it.

4. Nothing between the loss and the dangerous lines can save it — and this is the part the finding understates. `wait_for_gpu()` at renderer.cpp:1224 looks like it might throw first, but handle_device_lost sets `timeline_value_ = 0` at device_resources.cpp:1321, and `wait_for_gpu` early-returns on exactly that at device_resources.cpp:1673-1676. It returns silently, so control reaches 1231 and 1240 unconditionally with no exception in between.

5. Both dangerous lines do what is claimed. The buffer is host-visible, so `mapped` is non-null (device_resources.cpp:328-332); renderer.cpp:1231 dereferences it — memory of a destroyed device, and never written, because the submit that would have run the `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` failed. renderer.cpp:1240 calls `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device_resources.device(), readback)`, and `device()` re-reads `owner_` fresh (device_resources.h:335-338), so it is the NEW device; `destroy_vulkan_buffer` only early-outs on `VK_NULL_HANDLE` (device_resources.cpp:339-342), so it proceeds to vkUnmapMemory/vkDestroyBuffer/vkFreeMemory with new device, old handles.

6. The rule invoked is this codebase's own, not an imported one. device_resources.h:102-118 is the argument that the whole `VulkanDevice` refcounted type exists to close exactly this hazard ("A texture destroyed after the device would be a call into a device that has gone, which is the one shape of undefined behaviour this API gives no diagnostic for"), and device_resources.cpp:1314-1318 says the reset is "Released rather than destroyed" precisely so holders survive it — a guarantee this buffer never opted into. The d3d12 contrast is accurate: d3d12/renderer.cpp:1296 is `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource> readback`, whose Release is device-independent.

7. The proposed fix shape is seam-legal: renderer.h:467-471 already permits a backend to refuse a read-back by throwing.

*Correction:* Two imprecisions, neither load-bearing, plus one thing the finding missed in its own favour.

(a) "read_back_buffer is the one caller that does not [honour the bool]" is literally wrong: device_resources.cpp:1501 and 1525 also discard it. Both are inside `present()`'s own no-swapchain paths, where the only statements after them advance `frame_index_` and return, so neither touches a device-owned local afterwards. read_back_buffer is the only *hazardous* discarding caller, which is the substantive claim.

(b) The worst branch of the failure — `vkDestroyDevice` with live children — needs the shell path to drop the last texture reference (application.cpp:425). A client that registers no seam notify and still holds textures keeps the old VkDevice alive through those refs; there the consequence is milder but still a defect: the pixels handed back are garbage because no copy ever executed, and renderer.cpp:1240 still destroys the buffer against the wrong (new) device, leaking the old one and violating VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-parent. Both branches are bugs; only the severity of the worst one depends on the client.

(c) Missed, and it removes the last possible escape: `wait_for_gpu()` at renderer.cpp:1224 cannot throw on the way through, because handle_device_lost zeroes `timeline_value_` (device_resources.cpp:1321) and wait_for_gpu early-returns on exactly that condition (device_resources.cpp:1673-1676). The dangerous lines are reached unconditionally, not merely possibly.

Severity stands at must-fix: undefined behaviour with no diagnostic, in the one API the backend's own headers single out as having none, on a path the backend explicitly contracts for.

*Correction:* Two corrections, neither fatal. (a) The finding UNDERSTATES reachability: Renderer::submit() only records and never submits — the only execute() in engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp is line 1221 (submit() ends at vkCmdEndRenderPass, renderer.cpp:1148-1156) — so for a headless client that draws, submits and reads back, line 1221 is the frame's first and only vkQueueSubmit, i.e. exactly where a TDR caused by the frame's own drawing surfaces. (b) One half of the failure chain is conditional, not certain: vkDestroyDevice-with-live-children occurs only when the last VulkanTexture reference is actually dropped (it is, via Application::on_device_lost at application.cpp:414 -> release_device_resources). A client that keeps a texture alive keeps the old device alive instead — in which case there is no vkDestroyDevice violation, but renderer.cpp:1240 still destroys the buffer against the wrong device (VUID-vkDestroyBuffer-buffer-parent) and leaks the old one, and renderer.cpp:1231 still returns pixels no copy ever wrote. The defect is unconditional; only which flavour of UB you get depends on the client. Minor wording: device_resources.h:287-291 argues the bool specifically for present()'s semaphores, so the load-bearing rule is the Vulkan parent/child requirement rather than that comment, and the vkDestroyDevice VUID number cited is the older spelling.

### G7. `RenderResources`' ordering constraint — the paragraph written by the fix for the review's §2.3 — was renumbered rather than re-derived, and now says the ordering is free on four of five backends when Vulkan is the second backend it is load-bearing on

**`engine/render/render_resources.h:121`** · should-fix · `probe` · raised by P7 · run id `P7.2`

EVIDENCE: render_resources.h:112-123 —
"// CONSTRAINT: A RenderResources OUTLIVES THE Renderer IT WAS FILLED
// AGAINST. This class holds whatever a backend calls a texture, and on
// one of the five that is an ID3D12Resource the GPU may still be
// reading: the only thing that waits for it is ~Renderer::Impl...
// It is stated here rather than only kept, because it costs nothing on
// four of the five backends and is therefore invisible in four
// configurations out of five."

The commit's own diff shows the edit was "three of the four" -> "four of the five" and "one of the four" -> "one of the five", with no re-derivation.

But on Vulkan the ordering is load-bearing in exactly the D3D12 way:
- engine/render/vulkan/render_resources.cpp:26-59 — `VulkanTexture::~VulkanTexture()` calls vkDestroyImageView / vkDestroyImage / vkFreeMemory and waits for nothing; its only guard is that the device still exists.
- engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:266-281 — `Renderer::Impl::~Impl()` is the only wait: `std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu();`
- engine/app/application.h:250-251 — `render_resources_` then `renderer_`, so the renderer (and its wait) dies first. Reverse that and every VkImage is destroyed ahead of the only wait on the shutdown path.
- engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:113, :451-462, :490-509 — VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation and the debug messenger are enabled under `_DEBUG`, and `x64-debug-vulkan` is the only preset that builds this backend.

WHY WRONG: This is the paragraph commit 5825513 added to answer docs/review/d3d12/README.md §2.3, whose whole argument was "it costs nothing on the other three backends, which is why it survived". That premise is what makes the constraint worth writing on the seam rather than merely keeping. It is now false: destroying a VkImage or VkImageView while a submitted command buffer still names it violates VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000 / VUID-vkDestroyImageView-imageView-01026, which is the direct analogue of the debug layer's OBJECT_DELETED_WHILE_STILL_IN_USE that the paragraph cites. The Vulkan-specific paragraph the commit appended at :134-143 addresses only the opposite direction — a texture outliving the *device* — and closes "it is now true by construction on five rather than by luck on four", which reads as though the fifth backend removed a hazard here rather than adding one.

FAILURE: A shell or harness author reads this paragraph to decide member order, and it tells them the ordering matters on one backend (D3D12) and is invisible on the other four. They write a Vulkan-only client — or reorder application.h back to creation order on the reasonable-looking ground that the Vulkan texture already holds its own device reference, which the paragraph directly beneath now says. `Application::render()` ends at `end_frame()` -> `present()` -> `execute()` + `vkQueuePresentKHR`, so the last frame's command buffer is in flight when `~Application` runs; `render_resources_` then dies before `~Renderer::Impl`'s `try_wait_for_gpu()`, and every texture the frame's descriptor sets name is destroyed under it. Under x64-debug-vulkan, which is the only preset that builds this backend, that is a validation error on every ordinary exit of both samples — precisely the §2.3 failure, in the configuration the paragraph says cannot have it.

FIX: Re-derive rather than renumber: "on two of the five that is a resource the GPU may still be reading — an ID3D12Resource, or a VkImage and its view" and "it costs nothing on three of the five backends and is therefore invisible in three configurations out of five", naming the Vulkan diagnostic (VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000, reported by VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation, which engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp enables under _DEBUG) beside the D3D12 one. Keep the appended paragraph — the shared_ptr answers a different, real question — but say that it answers the device-lifetime half and not the in-flight half.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I attacked this at the only place it could die — the claim that the ordering is genuinely load-bearing on Vulkan, not just D3D12 — and it held at every step.

THE RULE, stated from the specification rather than folklore. C:\VulkanSDK\1.4.357.0\share\vulkan\registry\validusage.json gives verbatim: VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000 "All submitted commands that refer to image, either directly or via a VkImageView, must have completed execution"; VUID-vkDestroyImageView-imageView-01026 "All submitted commands that refer to imageView must have completed execution"; VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-00677 "All submitted commands that refer to memory (via images or buffers) must have completed execution". The finding cites the first two correctly; ~VulkanTexture trips all three.

THE TEXT SAYS WHAT THE FINDING SAYS IT SAYS. engine/render/render_resources.h:121-123 reads "It is stated here rather than only kept, because it costs nothing on / four of the five backends and is therefore invisible in four / configurations out of five." `git show 4d91b91 -- engine/render/render_resources.h` is a two-hunk diff of exactly "one of the four"->"one of the five" and "three of the four"/"three ... out of four"->"four of the five"/"four ... out of five", plus the appended :134-143 paragraph. Renumber, not re-derivation, as claimed.

THE HAZARD IS REACHABLE, and I checked each of the four things it needs:
1. The command buffer really names the texture. engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1100 `texture_binding.imageView = run.texture->view();`, :1130 vkUpdateDescriptorSets, :1133 vkCmdBindDescriptorSets, :1142 vkCmdDrawIndexed. The submitted buffer refers to the VkImageView through a bound descriptor set — the exact predicate of 01026/01000.
2. Work is genuinely outstanding at shutdown. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:197 `static const int FRAME_COUNT = 2;` — frames in flight, not a per-frame stall. I read present() end to end (device_resources.cpp:1493-1648): it records the blit, calls execute() (:1607), vkQueuePresentKHR (:1626), then `frame_index_ = (frame_index_ + 1) % FRAME_COUNT` (:1647) and returns. No wait. The only per-frame wait is wait_for_frame (:1652) at the top of the NEXT frame, on frame N-2. So the last submit is in flight when Application::render() returns. This was the argument most likely to kill the finding and it fails.
3. ~VulkanTexture waits for nothing. engine/render/vulkan/render_resources.cpp:26-59: vkDestroyImageView / vkDestroyImage / vkFreeMemory, guarded only by `if (!this->owner_ || this->owner_->device == VK_NULL_HANDLE) return;` at :35-38 — device liveness, never GPU completion.
4. The wait is inside the renderer, on the far side of the table. engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:266 ~Impl, :280 `std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu();`, and device_resources.cpp:370-386 ~DeviceResources does the same plus vkDeviceWaitIdle — both reached only when the Renderer is destroyed. engine/app/application.cpp:62-86 ~Application adds no GPU wait of its own. engine/app/application.h:250-251 declares `render_resources_` then `renderer_`, so today the renderer dies first and the order is kept; reversed, every VkImage, view and allocation the in-flight frame's descriptor sets name is destroyed ahead of the only wait.

So the ordering is load-bearing on two of five backends, not one, and free on three (d3d11, gl, null), not four. The sentence at :121-123 is false as written.

I also confirmed the code at HEAD is correct everywhere — application.h:250, tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:508, tests/render/null_tests.cpp:117, tests/render/renderer_seam_tests.cpp:60 all declare the table first. This is a false statement on a seam header, not a live bug, which is what sets the severity.

*Correction:* Three things the finding overstates, none of which touch its conclusion.

1. "a validation error on every ordinary exit of both samples" is too strong. Whether the layer fires is a race: it reports only while it still tracks the submission as in flight, and the final frame may well have retired before member destruction reaches the table. Say "can be, on any exit where the last frame has not retired". The same caveat already applies to the D3D12 OBJECT_DELETED_WHILE_STILL_IN_USE the paragraph describes, so the two stay symmetric and nothing is lost.

2. The two diagnostics are not equally loud, and the fix's wording should not imply they are. engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:247-249 calls SetBreakOnSeverity, so D3D12 breaks into the debugger. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:135-143 only OutputDebugStringA's the message and returns VK_FALSE ("FALSE, ALWAYS"). A Vulkan violation is a line in the debug output that a reader has to be looking at. That strengthens rather than weakens the case for stating the term on the seam — it is the quieter of the two.

3. The fix is incomplete: it names only render_resources.h. engine/app/application.h:242-249 carries the same claim, uncorrected — "on the D3D12 backend that is an ID3D12Resource the GPU may still be reading" and "It costs nothing on the other three backends, which is why it survived". Commit 4d91b91 did not touch engine/app at all (`git show 4d91b91 --stat -- engine/app/` is empty), so that count was never even renumbered and is now stale by two. Both sites need the same re-derivation.

ADJACENT, needing its own confirmation and not part of P7.2 — but whoever rewrites this paragraph will be standing on it. render_resources.h:115-117 states the hazard as "a shell that declares its table before its renderer releases every texture ahead of the one wait", while :123-124 in the same paragraph says "keeping it means declaring the table BEFORE the renderer", and application.h:240 says "THE TABLE IS DECLARED BEFORE THE RENDERER, so it dies after one". Table-before-renderer is the SAFE order under reverse-declaration destruction, so the first sentence appears to name the safe case as the failure. It predates this commit. Worth a second reader while the paragraph is open.
