### G8. render_resources.h's amended count claims the RenderResources-outlives-Renderer constraint "costs nothing on four of the five backends", but violating it on Vulkan destroys VkImages that submitted commands still reference — exactly the D3D12 cost

**`engine/render/render_resources.h:121`** · should-fix · `probe` · raised by P8 · run id `P8.2`

EVIDENCE: render_resources.h:121-123 (changed by this commit from "three of the four ... invisible in three configurations out of four") — "// It is stated here rather than only kept, because it costs nothing on // four of the five backends and is therefore invisible in four // configurations out of five."
render_resources.h:113-117 — "on one of the five that is an ID3D12Resource the GPU may still be reading: the only thing that waits for it is ~Renderer::Impl, so a shell that declares its table before its renderer releases every texture ahead of the one wait on the whole shutdown path."
render_resources.h:134-143, the new paragraph — "...so a texture OUTLIVING the renderer would be a call into a device that has gone... Every VulkanTexture therefore holds a shared_ptr to the device it was made on"
vulkan/renderer.cpp:266-282 — ~Impl: "std::ignore = this->device_resources.try_wait_for_gpu();"
vulkan/device_resources.cpp:370-386 — ~DeviceResources: try_wait_for_gpu() then vkDeviceWaitIdle

WHY WRONG: The commit bumped the numbers mechanically and added a paragraph covering only one of the two directions. The shared_ptr fixes "texture outlives the device"; it does nothing for the direction the constraint actually guards, which is "texture is destroyed before the wait". On this backend the only GPU waits on the shutdown path are ~Renderer::Impl's try_wait_for_gpu (renderer.cpp:280) and ~DeviceResources' vkDeviceWaitIdle (device_resources.cpp:376). A shell that declared the table after the renderer would run ~VulkanTexture — vkDestroyImageView/vkDestroyImage/vkFreeMemory, vulkan/render_resources.cpp:26-63 — before either, on images a still-executing command buffer samples. That is VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000 and VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-00677: undefined behaviour, with no refcount to soften it, where D3D11 (context bindings are refcounted), GL (deletion is deferred by the implementation) and null are genuinely free. The correct count is three of the five, not four. DRIFT.md's standard is that an argument whose premise is false is a defect, and this premise is what the sentence uses to justify writing the constraint down at all.

FAILURE: A future shell — or a maintainer trimming the ordering comment in application.h on the strength of this sentence — declares RenderResources after Renderer. Under x64-debug-vulkan: the last frame is submitted and presented by end_frame (renderer.cpp:857-866, no CPU wait after the present), the process then exits, ~RenderResources runs first and destroys every VkImage/VkDeviceMemory the in-flight command buffer is still sampling. The validation layers report it; without them it is silent corruption or a driver fault. The comment says that configuration is one of the four where the mistake is "invisible".

FIX: Change "four of the five ... four configurations out of five" to "three of the five ... three configurations out of five", and extend the new paragraph at 134-143 to say that the shared_ptr closes only the outlive direction: on Vulkan, as on D3D12, releasing a texture ahead of the renderer's wait destroys an image the GPU may still be reading, so the constraint is load-bearing on two backends now rather than one.

Destroying the view/image/memory underneath them is VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000 and VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-00677, with no refcount anywhere — VulkanTexture's shared_ptr is to VulkanDevice (vulkan/backend.h:91-104), which keeps the DEVICE alive and tracks nothing about GPU progress.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this and could not. The claim, the mechanism and the consequence all check out at HEAD.

THE RULE. `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:9-10` states the standard the finding invokes: "The comments in `engine/render/` are held to the same standard — `renderer.h` is not a header with comments, it is the specification of the seam". Its entry at `:24` is precedent of exactly this shape — a per-backend sentence on the shared seam counted wrong, "false in two of three configurations", listed as drift. So a count sentence in `render_resources.h` that puts a backend in the wrong column is a defect by this repository's own published standard, not by a reviewer's taste.

WHAT THE SENTENCE CLAIMS. `engine/render/render_resources.h:121-123`: "It is stated here rather than only kept, because it costs nothing on four of the five backends and is therefore invisible in four configurations out of five." "Costs nothing" means *violating* it costs nothing — `engine/app/application.h:243-248` spells the same thought out longhand: "Declared the other way round ... every texture is released ahead of that wait on every normal exit. It costs nothing on the other three backends, which is why it survived." The diff (`git show HEAD -- engine/render/render_resources.h`) changed only the numerals: "three of the four"→"four of the five", "three ... out of four"→"four ... out of five". Vulkan was moved into the free column by arithmetic, with nothing checked.

VULKAN IS NOT IN THE FREE COLUMN.
- `engine/render/vulkan/render_resources.cpp:25-60`, `~VulkanTexture`: guards only on `owner_`/`device` being alive, then calls `vkDestroyImageView` (:43), `vkDestroyImage` (:48) and `vkFreeMemory` (:57). There is no GPU wait anywhere in it.
- Those objects are referenced by submitted work: `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:1099-1130` writes `texture_binding.imageView = run.texture->view()` into a `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_SAMPLED_IMAGE` binding of the set the run draws with.
- Nothing waits after the last submit. `Renderer::end_frame` (`renderer.cpp:856-866`) does `frame_begun = false; device_resources.present();`. `DeviceResources::present` ends in `execute(...)` then `vkQueuePresentKHR` (`device_resources.cpp:1607-1648`), and `execute` (`device_resources.cpp:1368-1432`) calls `vkQueueSubmit(..., VK_NULL_HANDLE)` — no fence, no CPU wait, it only records `frame.timeline_value`.
- The only waits on the shutdown path are `~Renderer::Impl`'s `try_wait_for_gpu` (`renderer.cpp:280`) and `~DeviceResources`' `try_wait_for_gpu` + `vkDeviceWaitIdle` (`device_resources.cpp:381-386`) — and `DeviceResources` is a member of `Renderer::Impl`, so both live inside destroying the renderer. `Application::~Application` (`engine/app/application.cpp:62-86`) does `clear()`, an audio suspend and `CoUninitialize` — no device wait before the member list destructs.

So a shell that declared the table after the renderer would run `~VulkanTexture` on images a still-executing command buffer samples. That is VUID-vkDestroyImage-image-01000, VUID-vkDestroyImageView-imageView-01026 and VUID-vkFreeMemory-memory-00677 — each requires all submitted commands referring to the object to have completed execution. The `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>` (`vulkan/backend.h:104`) keeps the *device* alive; it says nothing about in-flight work, and the folder's own prose confirms it was only ever aimed at the other direction: `vulkan/backend.h:76-84` and `vulkan/device_resources.h:102-118` both argue exactly and only "a texture destroyed after the device would be a call into a device that has gone".

THE NEW PARAGRAPH DOES NOT COVER IT. `render_resources.h:134-143` is about the outlive direction, and its closing "The sentence above still holds on every backend" refers to line 131-132 ("Nothing here needs the renderer to still be alive: a texture releases itself, and an ID3D12Resource holds its own reference on the device"), not to the count at :121-123. I grepped `engine/render/vulkan/` for any statement of the in-flight cost and there is none.

THE OTHER THREE ARE GENUINELY FREE, so "three of the five" is the right number. D3D11 releases a `ComPtr` and the runtime defers destruction behind its own references; GL's `~GlTexture` is `glDeleteTextures` (`engine/render/gl/render_resources.cpp:25-30`), where the spec frees the name immediately and the object only when it is no longer in use; `null/` has no GPU.

The second half of the sentence is wrong too, in the finding's favour: debug builds enable `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` when installed (`vulkan/device_resources.cpp:451-467`), so the mistake is loud in that configuration rather than "invisible" — which is what caught the two defects the commit message credits to the layers.

*Correction:* Three refinements, none of which touch the conclusion.

1. The finding's failure narrative says that without validation layers the breakage is "silent corruption or a driver fault". True, but under `x64-debug-vulkan` with the SDK installed — the only way that preset is normally built — the layers are on (`vulkan/device_resources.cpp:451-467`) and would report it. That makes the sentence's *second* clause wrong as well: the mistake is not invisible in that configuration either. Strengthens rather than weakens the finding.

2. The finding says "the only thing that waits for it is ~Renderer::Impl" is a claim Vulkan breaks. It does not — `~DeviceResources` (`device_resources.cpp:370-386`) is reached only by destroying `Renderer::Impl`, which owns it, so :115-117's structural claim holds on Vulkan unchanged. Only the *count* sentence at :121-123 and the "on one of the five that is an ID3D12Resource" scoping at :113-114 are wrong.

3. Scope: the same false premise is stated in two more places the fix should not leave behind. `engine/render/renderer.h:356-360` — "on one backend it holds resources the GPU may still be reading" — was in this commit's diff (renderer.h changed 87 lines) but that hunk was not touched, and it is now two backends. `engine/app/application.h:243-248` names the D3D12 backend explicitly and ends "It costs nothing on the other three backends"; this commit did not touch application.h at all, so that sentence is pre-existing rather than introduced here — it is now numerically right only by accident, since the set it means is the other four. A fix confined to render_resources.h leaves the seam header itself saying "one backend".

**`engine/render/renderer.h:490`** · should-fix · `probe` · raised by P8 · run id `P8.3`

EVIDENCE: renderer.h:486-491 — "(engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.h says which and why - it is the // only one of the five that HAD such a wrapper to strip ... a device // can be lost on both of them, which is half the backends rather than // one, and the settled note at the foot of this file says so)."
renderer.h:538-543, changed by this commit — "NOT NOWHERE, which is the option the fourth backend closed and the fifth closed again. A device is lost on three of the five rather than on one, so the hazard is most of this seam's configurations..."

The sentence cites the settled note as its authority, and the note now says the opposite: three of five, not "both of them" and not "half". renderer.h is described by CLAUDE.md and by this repository's own review standard as the seam whose comment IS the contract, so a self-contradicting count inside it is the DRIFT defect class exactly.

FAILURE: A reader of the seam header takes "a device can be lost on both of them" as the roster of configurations that need a device-loss path, concludes the Vulkan preset does not, and writes or reviews a shell, a resource kind or a test on that basis — while vulkan/device_resources.cpp calls handle_device_lost from three places and re-enters the shell's on_device_lost/on_device_restored round trip on each. The reader is misled by the seam header and corrected only by the footnote it points at.

FIX: Amend renderer.h:489-491 to "a device can be lost on three of the five, which is most of this seam's configurations rather than one, and the settled note at the foot of this file says so" — matching the note at 538-543 the sentence already cites.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

The commit message claims the sweep ("renderer.h counted four in fourteen places").

The arithmetic is false on either reading of "both of them". Taken as an anaphor to d3d11+d3d12, that is 2 of 5, which is not half. Taken as the roster of device-losing backends, the roster is 3 of 5, so "both" is short by one. Neither is "half the backends".

The Vulkan half of the count is real, not a documentation guess. `engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1415` (vkQueueSubmit), `:1535` (acquire) and `:1629` (present) each test `== VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` and call `handle_device_lost()` on the next line; `:1225` is a fourth call site. `handle_device_lost()` at `:1265-1329` calls `notify_->on_device_lost()`, waits idle, tears down swapchain/colour target/frames/render pass/pool/timeline/surface, resets the device, then `create_device_resources()`, `create_window_size_dependent_resources()` and `notify_->on_device_restored()` — the full shell round trip the finding describes. `grep` for `on_device_lost` across `engine/render/gl/` and `engine/render/null/` returns nothing, so three of five is the correct roster.

The standard invoked is this repository's own, not an imported one. `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:9-12` — "renderer.h is not a header with comments, it is the specification of the seam, and several of its paragraphs are the only place a rule is written down." And `docs/review/d3d12/README.md:425` flagged this very sentence's previous incarnation for the same defect, noting "the project has paid to correct it once already" (`a56d198`); "half the backends" is the language of that fix, now stale in turn. `renderer.h:697-701` states the class in the file itself: "it used to say 'the three backends have three different things to reset' and that sentence went stale on the day the fourth landed."

Adversarial check that failed to kill it: `renderer.h:514` also says "two of the four backends", but that one is explicitly fenced as history by `:518-522` — "(Four was the count when this was settled...)" — added by this commit. `:490` has no such fence, sits in a present-tense parenthesis whose adjacent clause the commit did update, and cites a live note. It is a miss, not preserved history.

*Correction:* Two refinements; neither touches the conclusion.

Mechanism: the finding treats "a device can be lost on both of them" as the false clause. That clause is defensible on its own — "both of them" is an anaphor to the two Direct3D device wrappers under discussion in the preceding sentence, and a device genuinely can be lost on both. What is false at HEAD is (a) the count clause "which is half the backends rather than one" — 2 of 5 is not half, and the real roster is 3 of 5 — and (b) the citation "the settled note at the foot of this file says so", since `:538-541` now says "three of the five" and "most of this seam's configurations". The defect is a stale count and a false self-citation inside the seam specification, not a false statement about D3D11/D3D12.

Failure scenario: overstated. A reader misled by "half the backends" is pointed at the correcting note in the same breath by the sentence's own last clause, so the wrong roster is self-limiting for anyone who follows the pointer. The residual harm is a reader who trusts the summary and does not, plus the loss of the file's standing as a checkable contract — which `renderer.h:697-701` and `DRIFT.md:9-12` treat as the cost that matters.

Severity should-fix is right by this repository's own precedent: the analogous "renderer.h still counts three backends in eight places" sits under "## 3. Should fix" at `docs/review/d3d12/README.md:411`, and its table row `:425` is this exact sentence one generation earlier. The proposed fix wording is correct as written.

So the cross-reference is broken: the note does not say "half", and no scoping rescues the arithmetic — two of five is 40%, the loss-capable set is three of five, two of the three backends that have a device_resources.h is not half either, and both Direct3D backends is all of two rather than half. It was exactly true at four backends (2/4) and went stale on this commit.

The Vulkan half checks out: handle_device_lost() is called from four sites in engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp (1225 via try_wait_for_gpu, 1417, 1537, 1631 — the finding cited 1415/1535/1629, which are the VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST guard lines rather than the calls, and missed 1225), and handle_device_lost at device_resources.cpp:1265 drives notify_->on_device_lost(). So renderer.h:539's "three of the five" is right and renderer.h:490's "half" is wrong.

The rule invoked is a real rule of this codebase. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:11-13 states it: "renderer.h is not a header with comments, it is the specification of the seam, and several of its paragraphs are the only place a rule is written down", and its renderer.h bullet list ends with the same defect class ("`:40`, `:255`, `:328` — 'two backends' / 'a second backend' throughout. Three."). CLAUDE.md's amendment-in-the-same-commit rule makes this a miss of this commit's own pass rather than inherited drift, which the commit message itself frames ("renderer.h counted four in fourteen places").

What does not survive is the weight. This repository has already adjudicated the identical defect: docs/review/d3d12/all-findings.md:645-649 — "The sub-claim about renderer.h:284 ('three backends answered it three ways') stands as drift: four backends answered it, and the same file counts four at :467 and :482-488. It is minor and shares the finding's root cause rather than being separate." Its §4 Minor list carries two more of the same shape (docs/review/d3d12/README.md:601 "The same short list the other two backends keep. Three."; :590 "the four .cpp beside it. Three include it."). A stale backend count in renderer.h is a minor in this review's own vocabulary.

The stated failure is also not reachable in the form claimed. The clause is a parenthesis on the begin_marker/end_marker/set_marker declarations, about which device-wrapper accessors were stripped, not the device-loss roster, and it ends by pointing at the note that has the right number. Decisively, the note it points at exists to remove exactly that per-backend caller decision: renderer.h:546-551 — "'A hazard its configuration may not have' is a statement about a build, not about a caller. LABRADOR_RENDER_BACKEND picks a backend at configure time (T5) over one game source... what varies is which build ever runs the path, never which source has to write it." A reader who wrongly concluded the Vulkan preset never loses a device would still register the same reload_device kind, because the seam settled that the source is identical in every configuration. The harm is a self-contradicting count inside the contract header, which is worth the one-line fix; it is not a mis-written shell, resource kind or test.

The proposed fix text is sound and matches the note it cites.

*Correction:* Two things the finding gets wrong, neither fatal. (1) Severity: this repository has already graded this exact defect class — a stale backend count in renderer.h contradicted by another count in the same file — as minor, at docs/review/d3d12/all-findings.md:647, with two more of the same shape in that review's §4 Minor list (docs/review/d3d12/README.md:590, :601). Should-fix is one grade too high; minor is the calibrated weight. (2) The failure scenario overstates reach. The clause hangs off the debug-marker declarations and is about which device-wrapper accessors were stripped, not the device-loss roster, and it forwards the reader to the note that carries the right number. More to the point, the note it forwards to (renderer.h:546-551) exists precisely to establish that the caller's obligation does not vary per backend — "what varies is which build ever runs the path, never which source has to write it" — so a reader who wrongly concluded the Vulkan preset never loses a device would still write the same reload_device registration. The consequence is a self-contradicting count in the seam header, not a downstream shell/resource-kind/test defect. Also, minor citation slip: vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1415, 1535 and 1629 are the `if (... == VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)` guards; the calls are at 1417, 1537 and 1631, and there is a fourth call site at 1225 reached from the failed try_wait_for_gpu path, so it is four call sites rather than three. The core assertion — that renderer.h:490 says "half the backends" while renderer.h:539, edited by this same commit, says "three of the five", and that line 487 in the same parenthesis was updated while 489-491 were not — is verified true at HEAD, and the proposed one-line amendment is the right fix.

EVIDENCE: engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:38-43 (new in 4d91b91):

```

//    frames and presents none of them - deliberately, because presenting a
```

The Harness comment was updated for it (pixel_tests.cpp:309-313: "ONE CASE CALLS IT ITSELF, AND IT IS THE CASE ABOUT THAT"); the Vulkan header was not. The presented frame is one the case read back (harness.end() at 1761 does submit + read_back_buffer), so "presents none of them" cannot be rescued as "presents none of the ones it reads".

The same sentence is repeated verbatim in the amendment block this commit added to docs/port/android.md:343 ("draws fifty-one frames and presents none of them") and, with the count corrected but the present claim still wrong, in the commit message at line 16 ("draws fifty-three frames and presents none of them").

WHY WRONG: docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard, restated in CLAUDE.md: "a comment the code does not match is a defect", and this file is the one CLAUDE.md and the commit message both name as carrying "the largest decision in the port" — the bullet quoted is the first of the three properties that decision is derived from. FAILURE: A reader deciding whether the engine-owned-colour-target design is still warranted opens engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h — the file CLAUDE.md sends them to — and checks the first premise against tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp. Both halves fail on inspection: the file says fifty-three frames, and `harness.renderer().end_frame()` at pixel_tests.cpp:1767 presents one. ### G11. device_resources.h's commands() comment claims every entry point executes before it returns, which is false for begin_frame and submit and is the exact opposite of the backend's one-buffer-per-frame design

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:275`** · should-fix · `probe` · raised by P6 · run id `P6.2`

EVIDENCE: device_resources.h:270-277


```
		// The frame's command buffer, begun if it is not already recording.
		// Returns the same buffer either way, which is what makes it idempotent
		// WITHIN one operation: the barrier and the clear of a begin_frame are
		// two calls to this and one buffer, as are the transition, the copy and
		// the transition back of a read-back. It is not a way to add to what an
		// earlier entry point recorded - every entry point executes before it
		// returns, so there is never an open buffer between them.
		VkCommandBuffer commands();
```


Contradicted by the code it describes. engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:688 (Impl::open_frame, reached from Renderer::begin_frame at :853) records the clear into `commands()` and never calls `execute()`; engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:982 (Renderer::submit) records the render pass and every draw into `commands()` and never calls `execute()`. `execute()` appears in renderer.cpp only at :1221 (read_back_buffer) — grep confirms those are the only three uses of `commands()` and the only `execute()` in the file. So the buffer is open across begin_frame -> submit -> end_frame, and the single submit is present()'s at device_resources.cpp:1607.

And contradicted by this backend's own prose, device_resources.cpp:1481-1483:


```
		// THE D3D12 BACKEND CANNOT HAVE THIS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ONE LINE OF
		// ITS open_frame: it executes the clear immediately, so its
		// back_buffer_state is true the moment it is written. This backend
		// records the whole frame into one command buffer and submits once,
```


WHY WRONG: docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard, restated in CLAUDE.md: a comment the code does not match is a defect, and this codebase's comments are unusually load-bearing. This one is not decorative — it is the stated premise for the `submitted_` member and for the wait-and-pool-reset branch at device_resources.cpp:1338-1352, i.e. for one of the two defects this commit says the validation layers found. Two comments in the same backend assert opposite frame models, and only one of them is the code.

FAILURE: A maintainer reading commands() takes the stated model — every entry point submits — and concludes that when `present()` calls `this->commands()` at :1546, `recording_` is false and `submitted_` is true on every ordinary frame, so the branch at :1338 fires and `wait_for_frame()` blocks on `frame().timeline_value`, which submit() would just have set to the frame's own submit. Under the documented model every present is a full CPU-blocks-on-its-own-GPU-work stall, FRAME_COUNT = 2 buys nothing, and frames_[1] is dead weight — so the obvious "fix" is to remove the branch or the flag. The code's actual model is the opposite (`recording_` is true on entry to present(), the branch fires only after read_back_buffer's mid-frame execute at renderer.cpp:1221), so acting on the comment removes the only thing that makes reopening the buffer after a read-back legal, which is the VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT hazard the same header documents at :469-479 and which the validation layers already caught once.

FIX: Replace the last sentence with what the backend actually does: the frame's buffer is opened by begin_frame's clear and stays open across submit() until present() executes it, so commands() is idempotent across the whole frame, not within one operation; the one caller that finds it closed mid-frame is read_back_buffer's, which is why `submitted_` and the wait-and-pool-reset exist. That is the sentence device_resources.cpp:1481-1484 already writes for abandon_commands, so the two should agree.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `should-fix`

I tried to kill this and could not — every load-bearing claim verifies.

THE COMMENT, VERBATIM AT HEAD (engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:270-277): "The frame's command buffer, begun if it is not already recording. ... It is not a way to add to what an earlier entry point recorded - every entry point executes before it returns, so there is never an open buffer between them." The final sentence (`:274-276`) is a descriptive claim about the code, not a caller norm, and its stated consequence ("there is never an open buffer between them") is checkable.

IT IS FALSE, AND ITS OWN BACKEND VIOLATES IT THREE TIMES.
- `Renderer::begin_frame` (renderer.cpp:826-854) ends at `:853` with `impl.open_frame()`. `Impl::open_frame` (renderer.cpp:664-701) records `vkCmdClearColorImage` into `this->device_resources.commands()` at `:688`, plus two `transition_colour` calls (`:670`, `:691`) that themselves record via `commands()` (device_resources.cpp:1718). Nothing in that path calls `execute()`. begin_frame returns with the buffer open.
- `Renderer::submit` takes `VkCommandBuffer commands = device_resources.commands();` at renderer.cpp:982 — i.e. it *adds* the render pass and every draw to what begin_frame recorded, the precise thing the comment says commands() "is not a way to" do — and ends at `:1148` with `vkCmdEndRenderPass(commands)` and a `set_colour_layout` call. No submit.
- The frame's only `vkQueueSubmit` is inside `DeviceResources::execute` (device_resources.cpp:1412). `grep -n "vkQueueSubmit"` over `engine/render/vulkan/*.cpp` returns exactly two hits: `:1412` (execute) and `:1887` (`end_upload`, which allocates and submits its own one-shot buffer, not the frame's). In renderer.cpp, `execute()` appears once, at `:1221`, inside `read_back_buffer`. So on an ordinary frame the buffer opened by begin_frame's clear is still recording when `present()` calls `this->commands()` at device_resources.cpp:1546 and is executed only at `:1607`.

CONTRADICTED BY TWO OTHER COMMENTS IN THE SAME BACKEND. device_resources.cpp:1483-1487: "THE D3D12 BACKEND CANNOT HAVE THIS ... it executes the clear immediately ... This backend records the whole frame into one command buffer and submits once". And device_resources.h:467-476 on `submitted_`: "ONE CALLER MAKES IT TRUE AND IT IS THE ONE THE SEAM NAMES. read_back_buffer submits mid-frame and waits ... and end_frame then wants the same buffer again." Both state the model the commands() comment denies.

THE RULE IS THIS CODEBASE'S. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:7-16 sets the standard explicitly — comments in `engine/render/` are "held to the same standard" as the design documents, and "each item is a claim that the code no longer matches" — and CLAUDE.md points at that file as a live work item list. This is not a stale count; it misstates the frame model that the whole backend is organised around.

THE READER-HARM MECHANISM HOLDS. Under the documented model, `submit()` would have flushed, so on entry to `present()` `recording_` would be false and `submitted_` true, and the reopen branch at device_resources.cpp:1338-1352 would fire every frame — `wait_for_frame()` on `frame().timeline_value` that submit had just written (`:1428`), a full CPU stall on the frame's own work, making FRAME_COUNT=2 pointless. That inference really does follow from the comment, and it is the opposite of the code: `recording_` is true on entry to present(), and the branch exists only for read_back_buffer's mid-frame `execute()` at renderer.cpp:1221 — the VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT hazard documented at device_resources.h:472-476.

The finding's proposed FIX targets the right sentence: the earlier half of the comment (idempotence within begin_frame's barrier+clear, and within the read-back's transition/copy/transition) is accurate and should stay.

*Correction:* Three imprecisions, none of which weaken it. (1) Citation drift: the D3D12-contrast prose is at device_resources.cpp:1483-1487, not 1481-1483/1481-1484; the RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT hazard is documented at device_resources.h:467-476, not :469-479. A maintainer following the finding's imagined chain to "remove the branch" would hit that sentence at the site of the edit, so the concrete failure scenario is less reachable than the finding claims. The defect is the false statement itself in the header that renderer.cpp reads, not a live trap.

(b) The finding under-states the scope of the error by focusing on the justification clause. The preceding sentence — "It is not a way to add to what an earlier entry point recorded" — is false on its own terms: renderer.cpp:982's `commands()` in `submit()` adds to the clear that renderer.cpp:688 recorded in `begin_frame`, and device_resources.cpp:1546's adds to both. The fix must replace both sentences, not only the last one; the proposed replacement does.

Also worth noting for whoever fixes it: this is not drift from a later change. `engine/render/vulkan/` arrived whole in 4d91b91, so the sentence was false the day it was written, which is why DRIFT.md's "did not amend" framing does not apply and a straight rewrite is the whole fix.

### G12. The headline comment's claim that the absence of descriptor_slot is "THE ONE LINE THAT DIFFERS FROM THE D3D12 FILE" is false: the file also carries a 43-line VulkanTexture destructor and size() that the D3D12 file does not have, and the descriptor_slot it lacks is fourteen lines, not one

**`engine/render/vulkan/render_resources.cpp:94`** · should-fix · `probe` · raised by P1 · run id `P1.1`

EVIDENCE: render_resources.cpp:94-102 —

```
	// NO descriptor_slot HERE, WHICH IS THE ONE LINE THAT DIFFERS FROM THE
	// D3D12 FILE. ... re-loading one costs exactly
	// the image it makes and the image it destroys.
```


A `diff` of the two files (backend name normalised) reports exactly four differences, of which the descriptor_slot absence is one:

```
  - :3  `#include "engine/math/vector2f.h"` — absent from the D3D12 file
  - :8  `using namespace mattmath;` — absent from the D3D12 file
  - :24-66 the whole `VulkanTexture::~VulkanTexture()` (35 lines, comment included) and `Vector2F VulkanTexture::size() const` — absent from the D3D12 file. `D3d12Texture` declares no destructor at all (d3d12/backend.h:90-109) and its `size()` lives in d3d12/renderer.cpp:132-136.
  - d3d12/render_resources.cpp:33-46 `int RenderResources::Impl::descriptor_slot(...)` — fourteen lines, absent here.
```


The same claim is asserted a second time, citing this file as the authority: texture_factory.cpp:347-350 — "which on this backend costs exactly the image it frees, there being no descriptor slot to give back (render_resources.cpp says why that is the one line differing from the D3D12 file)".

WHY WRONG: docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md sets the standard this repository holds comments to: "The comments in engine/render/ are held to the same standard ... Each item is a claim that the code no longer matches, with the line that contradicts it", and it lists near-identical items as defects (renderer.h `:40, :255, :328` — "'two backends' / 'a second backend' throughout. Three."). CLAUDE.md repeats it for this commit's own subject matter: a backend's headers "state the claim", and the design documents "change by amendment in the same commit as the change that fights" them.

FAILURE: A reader — or a reviewer checking backend equivalence, which is what this paragraph exists to let them do without opening both files — is told the two backends' texture tables are the same file apart from a descriptor slot. They therefore conclude that per-texture teardown is the same on both. It is not, and the difference is the single largest decision the port made about textures: every VulkanTexture carries a `shared_ptr<VulkanDevice>` and frees three objects by hand (`vkDestroyImageView`, `vkDestroyImage`, `vkFreeMemory`, :42-59), where D3D12 releases one ComPtr and needs no destructor. The same paragraph then shortens that three-object cost to "the image it makes and the image it destroys", and texture_factory.cpp:347-348 shortens it again to "exactly the image it frees" — so the one place a reader is sent to learn what a Vulkan re-load costs under-counts it by the allocation and the view that :52-59 and :42-46 actually free, and that :54-56 elsewhere calls out as the thing "every other backend behind this seam has one object here and this one has two".

FIX: Amend :94-102 to a claim the diff supports — e.g. "NO descriptor_slot HERE, WHICH IS THE ONE ENTRY IN THIS LIST THE D3D12 FILE HAS AND THIS ONE DOES NOT; the destructor above is the block that goes the other way, and it is why this file is longer than that one rather than shorter" — and correct the cost sentence to name all three objects a re-load frees. Then amend the cross-reference at texture_factory.cpp:347-350 in the same edit, since it repeats the false half.

*Correction:* The defect survives; four of the finding's supporting arguments do not, and they inflate the severity.

1. "fourteen lines, not one" is the weakest jab and should be dropped. `d3d12/backend.h:132` declares `descriptor_slot` in exactly one line, and "THE ONE LINE" is established house idiom for "the one decisive place" (`d3d11/renderer.cpp:71`, `d3d12/renderer.cpp:113`, `resource_factory.h:69`, `d3d12/device_resources.cpp:376`). What actually fails is the *singularity of the divergence*, not the line count.

2. "the single largest decision the port made about textures" is wrong twice. `engine/render/gl/render_resources.cpp:25-31` defines `GlTexture::~GlTexture()` and `:33-37` defines `GlTexture::size()` in that same file — so a backend texture destructor living in `render_resources.cpp` is the GL shape too, not a Vulkan invention; D3D12 is the outlier for having no destructor at all. And CLAUDE.md and `vulkan/device_resources.h` both place the port's largest decision elsewhere (what a back buffer is).

3. The cost-sentence half — that "costs exactly the image it makes and the image it destroys" (`:99-100`) under-counts by the view and the allocation — is prose shorthand for the texture object, and the full three-object list (`vkDestroyImageView`/`vkDestroyImage`/`vkFreeMemory`) sits forty lines above at `:42-59` in the same file. Worth tidying in the same edit, not a defect on its own.

4. The failure scenario is narrower than stated. A reader at `:94` has the destructor at `:26-60` in the same file, sixty lines up; they are not going to conclude teardown is identical. The genuine exposure is the second-hand citation at `texture_factory.cpp:349-350`, which sends a reader to a claim that is not there to be checked.

Net: a false comparative claim in a shouted comment, echoed in one other file, with correct code underneath and a one-paragraph prose fix. Real by DRIFT.md's standard, but it costs a reader a moment, not an hour — minor, not should-fix. The finding's proposed amendment at `:94-102` plus `texture_factory.cpp:347-350` is the right fix.

WHY WRONG: docs/review/d3d12/README.md §4 raised this exact sentence in its previous form ("THE ONE DESTRUCTOR IN engine/render/ THAT HAS TO DO ANYTHING") and gave the reason it is worth fixing rather than tolerating: "It misdirects exactly the audit §2.2 requires." It finds "the two", follows "the other one is ~Renderer::Impl in renderer.cpp" to the single named sibling, and reports the folder clean. Vulkan's two destructors, which run `try_wait_for_gpu()` and `vkDeviceWaitIdle` for the same reason and would be std::terminate sites if either ever regained a throw, are never visited, because the one document that indexes them says there is nothing else to visit.

"The next teardown audit ... reports the folder clean" treats §2.2 of `docs/review/d3d12/README.md` as a standing recurring process; it is a historical review artifact, and CLAUDE.md itself says `docs/review/` "is the review as written and is not updated as findings are fixed". A reader auditing teardown across `engine/render/` would more likely grep for `~` than trust one file's index. What is actually and only wrong is that a sentence which closes a set — numeral plus a named sole sibling — is false at HEAD, which is the same standard `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md` applies and the same standard the review applied to this very sentence at `README.md:610`.

The mechanism should be strengthened, not softened. The finding frames it as the Vulkan author "seeing the trap and stepping round it locally" — an inference about intent. The commit diff shows something firmer and worse: `4d91b91` explicitly swept counting sentences in all four sibling backends (`d3d11/backend.h:200`, `d3d11/renderer.cpp:810`, `d3d12/render_resources.cpp:56`, `d3d12/renderer.cpp:904` and `:1130`, `gl/renderer.cpp:700`, `null/*`) and says so in its message. This is one omission from an otherwise complete pass, in the one file where a prior review had already paid to get the sentence right.

Minor is the correct severity: comment-only, no behavioural consequence, but checkable, cheap, and in a sentence the project has already fixed once for this exact reason.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

I tried five refutation routes and all failed.

RULE. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:6-16 states the standard the finding invokes, in the project's own words: "The design documents are authoritative on intent and change by amendment in the same commit as the change that fights them ... The comments in `engine/render/` are held to the same standard." Its body is a list of exactly this defect class (renderer.h ":40, :255, :328 — 'two backends' / 'a second backend' throughout. Three."; CLAUDE.md ":114-116 — 'four state objects'"; gl/backend.h ":17-20 — 'its only client is ...'. Three."). So the rule is not folklore; it is written down, and it is about checkable counts in engine/render/ comments specifically.

THE RULE WAS APPLIED BY THE COMMIT UNDER REVIEW. `git show 4d91b91` message: "renderer.h counted four in fourteen places and the other four backends counted each other in nine more." The diff confirms nine count-widening edits in sibling backends, two of them inside d3d12/ itself: engine/render/d3d12/render_resources.cpp:56 ("The same short list the other three backends keep" -> "other four"), engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp:904 ("the longest of the four" -> "of the five") and :1130 ("The four backends have three different things to drop: two clear a vector" -> "The five backends ... three clear a vector"). `git show --stat 4d91b91` lists engine/render/d3d12/render_resources.cpp and engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp and does NOT list engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp. The sweep happened and this sentence was missed.

THE COUNT IS WRONG AT HEAD. engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:50-58 reads "ONE OF THE TWO DESTRUCTORS IN engine/render/ THAT HAS TO SYNCHRONISE WITH A GPU ... The other one is ~Renderer::Impl in renderer.cpp, from the same commit and for the same reason". That is an explicitly closed, explicitly engine/render/-scoped set of two. `grep -n try_wait_for_gpu engine/render/vulkan/* engine/render/d3d12/*` gives four destructor call sites: d3d12/device_resources.cpp:65 (dtor :48), d3d12/renderer.cpp:458 (dtor :440), vulkan/device_resources.cpp:381 (dtor :370, plus vkDeviceWaitIdle at :385), vulkan/renderer.cpp:280 (dtor :266). I checked the only other candidate: gl/renderer.cpp:247 ~Impl does wglMakeCurrent/wglDeleteContext/ReleaseDC and no GPU wait, so it is correctly outside the set. Four, not two.

THE VULKAN SIDE QUALIFIES ON ITS OWN TERMS. vulkan/device_resources.cpp:372-375: "ONE OF THE DESTRUCTORS IN engine/render/ THAT HAS TO SYNCHRONISE WITH A GPU ... Nothing here may be freed while the GPU is still reading it, and this API tracks none of that for you." vulkan/renderer.cpp:271-275: "The wait is inside destroy_device_dependent_resources for the same reason ~DeviceResources has one: nothing may be freed while the GPU is reading it". Both also carry the "AND IT ANSWERS RATHER THAN THROWS ... T6: teardown stays silent" paragraph, i.e. both are the std::terminate-site class the finding names. So the two new members belong to the set the d3d12 sentence enumerates, and the numeral-free wording at :372 is confirmed exactly as quoted.

THE CITED HISTORY AND DOCS CHECK OUT VERBATIM. docs/review/d3d12/README.md:610-614 is word for word as quoted, including "THE ONE DESTRUCTOR IN `engine/render/` THAT HAS TO DO ANYTHING", "It misdirects exactly the audit §2.2 requires", and the prescription "Narrow it to 'the only one that has to synchronise with a GPU' and cross-reference the sibling". §2.2 at :183 is indeed the teardown audit ("both new destructors are `std::terminate` sites"), with Failure scenario B at :218 being teardown specifically — so the audit the finding says would be misdirected is a real, named audit in this repo's own review, not an invented one. `git show 1d6c6ac --stat` confirms it is "Answer instead of throwing on the three paths a throw destroys, not reports" and touched d3d12/device_resources.{h,cpp} and d3d12/renderer.cpp — the commit that wrote the current sentence. The fix's precedent is real too: engine/render/d3d11/backend.h:23-31 reads "EVERY CLIENT OF IT IS IN THIS FOLDER, and that is the rule rather than a count ... This paragraph used to name its clients individually and the list went stale twice".

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED. (a) Scoping — could "THE TWO" be read as within d3d12/? No: the sentence says "IN engine/render/" and the review it answers used the same tree-wide scope. (b) Do the Vulkan destructors merely wait rather than "have to"? Their own comments give the same necessity argument, and vulkan/device_resources.cpp adds vkDeviceWaitIdle on top. (c) Out of scope because the file is untouched? The codebase's stated rule is that the commit that fights a comment is the commit that amends it, and this commit performed that sweep on eight other files. (d) Consequence overstated? The project itself already judged the same misdirection worth fixing at README.md:613. (e) Line numbers wrong? :50 is the first line of the comment, :55-58 is the by-path pointer, both as cited.

*Correction:* Two refinements, neither of which weakens the finding.

1. "the Vulkan file deliberately avoided the count without going back to widen this one" attributes intent that cannot be proven from the tree. What is provable is only the outcome: vulkan/device_resources.cpp:372 has no numeral where its d3d12 sibling at :50 has one, and 4d91b91 amended nine other count sentences (two of them in d3d12/) while leaving this one. Read it as a miss in a sweep the commit otherwise performed, not as a decision.

2. The finding understates the by-path pointer's staleness. At HEAD "The other one is ~Renderer::Impl in renderer.cpp" (:55-56) is ambiguous in a second way: three files in engine/render/ now define Renderer::Impl::~Impl — d3d12/renderer.cpp:440, gl/renderer.cpp:247 and vulkan/renderer.cpp:266 — and only two of those three synchronise with a GPU (gl/renderer.cpp:247 does WGL teardown only). So a reader who resolves the unqualified "renderer.cpp" wrongly lands on a destructor that is not in the set at all. That is an additional argument for the finding's own prescription — replace the list-of-one with the rule — rather than merely renumbering.

Severity minor is correct and matches this repo's own precedent: the previous form of this exact sentence was filed under "## 4. Minor" (docs/review/d3d12/README.md:584, item at :610) and was applied on that basis. Nothing at runtime is wrong; the cost is entirely to the next reader of the teardown set.

### G16. An upload's staging buffer is leaked whenever end_upload throws, including on the index-buffer upload that runs inside handle_device_lost's restore

**`engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:230`** · minor · `probe` · raised by P4 · run id `P4.2`

EVIDENCE: texture_factory.cpp:210-211  `// FROM HERE THE IMAGE IS OWNED BY NOBODY UNTIL THE LAST LINE, so every // failure between the two has to put it back.`
texture_factory.cpp:212  `try`
texture_factory.cpp:230  `VulkanBuffer staging = create_vulkan_buffer(owner,`   <- declared inside the try
texture_factory.cpp:303-304  `device_resources.end_upload(commands);`  `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);`
texture_factory.cpp:320-336  `catch (...) { if (view != ...) vkDestroyImageView...; if (memory != ...) vkFreeMemory...; vkDestroyImage(device, image, nullptr); ... throw; }`   <- staging is out of scope and untouched

renderer.cpp:582-599 (create_device_dependent_resources, the restore path) has the same shape with no try at all:

```
  `VulkanBuffer staging = create_vulkan_buffer(`  ... `this->device_resources.end_upload(upload);`  `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);`
```


device_resources.cpp:1889-1896  `if (submitted != VK_SUCCESS) { vkFreeCommandBuffers(...); check_vk(submitted, "An upload could not be submitted"); }`
device_resources.cpp:1902  `this->wait_for_gpu();`  (check_vk on vkWaitSemaphores)

WHY WRONG: The comment at texture_factory.cpp:210-211 states the rule for this block - every failure between the create and the last line has to put back what was made - and the catch keeps it for the image, the memory and the view but not for the staging buffer, which is created at :230 inside the same try. That is a comment the code does not match, which docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard makes a defect. renderer.cpp:582-599 has no handler at all and is the copy that runs during a device restore.

FAILURE: During handle_device_lost's restore (device_resources.cpp:1326-1329 -> Renderer::Impl::on_device_restored -> create_device_dependent_resources, and then Application::on_device_restored -> ResourceLoader::reload_device_resources replaying 43 textures), an upload submit or wait fails - a second loss during a driver reset storm, or VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY on a machine already short of memory. end_upload throws at device_resources.cpp:1893 or from wait_for_gpu at :1902. On the texture path the catch at :320 frees the image, its memory and its view and rethrows; staging.buffer and staging.memory - one buffer plus an allocation the size of the whole texture's bytes, up to a full font atlas - are never freed and belong to a device that stays alive. On the index-buffer path (renderer.cpp:598) there is no catch: the staging buffer leaks, and Impl::indices is left as a created-but-never-uploaded device-local buffer, so a client that catches the throw and carries on - which renderer.h:377-380 explicitly contemplates for a device event - binds it at renderer.cpp:1008 and draws every subsequent sprite from undefined index data at renderer.cpp:1142.

FIX: Hoist `VulkanBuffer staging;` above the `try` at texture_factory.cpp:212 and add `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);` to the catch at :320 alongside the image cleanup; wrap renderer.cpp:582-599 in the same try/catch (or give VulkanBuffer a small scope guard local to this folder so both sites get it for free).

**Refuter A — read the code.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

The code fact is confirmed at HEAD. texture_factory.cpp:212 opens the try; texture_factory.cpp:230 declares `VulkanBuffer staging = create_vulkan_buffer(owner, ...)` inside it; the success path destroys it at texture_factory.cpp:304 (`destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging);`) immediately after `device_resources.end_upload(commands);` at :303; the `catch (...)` at texture_factory.cpp:320-337 frees view (:322-325), memory (:326-329) and image (:330) and rethrows at :336, and does not and cannot touch `staging`, which is out of scope. renderer.cpp:582-599 is the same sequence with no handler at all: `this->indices` is created at :577, staging at :582, `end_upload(upload)` at :598, `destroy_vulkan_buffer(device, staging)` at :599.

end_upload really can throw. device_resources.cpp:1867-1906: `check_vk(vkEndCommandBuffer(...))` at :1869, and on a failed `vkQueueSubmit` it frees the command buffer then `check_vk(submitted, "An upload could not be submitted")` at :1893, and `this->wait_for_gpu();` at :1902 is a check_vk'd wait. So the throwing path is real, and both upload sites are the only two callers (grep: device_resources.h:401-402, renderer.cpp:592/598, texture_factory.cpp:267/303).

The leak window is in fact WIDER than the finding says, which favours it: between texture_factory.cpp:230 and :304 the `copies` vector at :240-241 can throw bad_alloc and `device_resources.begin_upload()` at :267 can throw from check_vk on vkAllocateCommandBuffers/vkBeginCommandBuffer (device_resources.cpp:1855-1862). After :304 staging is already destroyed and zeroed (destroy_vulkan_buffer nulls buffer/memory/mapped at device_resources.cpp:344-360), so the throw from vkCreateImageView at :317 leaks nothing and the proposed hoist-and-destroy-in-catch fix is double-free-safe.

Where the finding overreaches, twice. (1) The comment argument. texture_factory.cpp:208-211 reads "FROM HERE THE IMAGE IS OWNED BY NOBODY UNTIL THE LAST LINE ... the VulkanTexture that will own all three is not constructed until every one of them exists" - "all three" is image, memory and view, and the catch puts back all three. So this is not a comment the code fails to match and docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard is not engaged; it is an ordinary missing release on an exceptional path. (2) The failure narrative's second half is unreachable. If the throw comes from renderer.cpp:598, then Renderer::Impl::on_device_restored (renderer.cpp:713-721) never reaches `this->notify->on_device_restored()` at :718, so Application::on_device_restored (application.cpp:428-440) never calls reload_device_resources and the texture table stays as Registry::release_all left it (registry.h:138-145 empties every slot, keeping names). Registry::get throws std::out_of_range for a released slot (registry.h:107-114), and DrawList::draw_sprite resolves through it at renderer.cpp:208-209 (`*this->view_->owner->resources->impl()->texture(texture)`). A client that caught and carried on would therefore throw on its first sprite; no run is recorded, so although vkCmdBindIndexBuffer at renderer.cpp:1007-1008 binds the un-uploaded buffer, the run loop at :1020 is empty and vkCmdDrawIndexed at :1142 never executes. Garbage indices and an empty texture table are the same event, so "draws every subsequent sprite from undefined index data" does not happen.

Consequence in practice. There is no catch below main: grep found none in engine/app or engine/render, and the only handlers are samples/minimal/main.cpp:47 and samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49, which print, MessageBox and `return 1`. So in every in-tree configuration the process ends and the OS reclaims the leaked VkBuffer and VkDeviceMemory. The seam does contemplate a client catching and carrying on (renderer.h:376-379), and clients live outside this repo, so the leak is not nothing - but it is bounded at one buffer per failed upload on a path that is already terminal.

Verdict: the defect is really at texture_factory.cpp:230/:320 and renderer.cpp:582-599 and the one-line fix is correct, so it survives, at minor and no higher.

*Correction:* Two claims fail and the finding stands without them. (a) The DRIFT/comment-mismatch framing is wrong: texture_factory.cpp:208-211 scopes itself to "the VulkanTexture that will own all three" - image, memory and view - and the catch at :320-337 puts back exactly those three. This is a missing release, not a comment the code contradicts. (b) The index-buffer consequence is unreachable: a throw at renderer.cpp:598 means renderer.cpp:718's notify->on_device_restored() never runs, so reload_device_resources never refills the table, and Registry::get throws for every released slot (registry.h:107-114) at DrawList::draw_sprite (renderer.cpp:208-209). A carrying-on client throws on its first sprite, records no run, and never reaches vkCmdDrawIndexed at renderer.cpp:1142 - so nothing is ever drawn from the un-uploaded index buffer. One point in the finding's favour that it understates: the leak window is not just end_upload - the `copies` vector at texture_factory.cpp:240-241 and begin_upload at :267 also throw with staging live. Practical severity is capped at minor: no engine-level catch exists (only samples/minimal/main.cpp:47 and samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49, which return 1), so the leak is reclaimed at process exit in every in-tree client.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

I tried to kill this on four fronts — the ownership rule, the throw sites, reachability, and whether anything else reclaims the buffer — and it survived all four.

1. THE LEAK IS MECHANICALLY REAL. `VulkanBuffer` is a plain aggregate of `VkBuffer`/`VkDeviceMemory`/`VkDeviceSize`/`void*` with no destructor (engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h:164-175). `staging` is declared inside the try at engine/render/vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:230 and destroyed only at :304, on the success path. The catch at :320-337 frees `view` (:322-325), `memory` (:326-329) and `image` (:330) and rethrows at :336 — `staging` is out of scope there and is never touched. Nothing else reclaims it: `create_vulkan_buffer` (device_resources.cpp:286-335) registers the buffer in no list — it returns it by value and the caller owns it outright.

2. THE THROW SITES BETWEEN :230 AND :304 ARE REAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. `end_upload` throws at three points: `check_vk(vkEndCommandBuffer(...))` (device_resources.cpp:1868-1869), `check_vk(submitted, "An upload could not be submitted")` after freeing the command buffer (:1889-1894), and `wait_for_gpu()` at :1902, which is not a `try_` variant — it is `check_vk(vkWaitSemaphores(...))` at device_resources.cpp:1684-1685. `vkQueueSubmit` may return VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY / VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY / VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and `vkWaitSemaphores` VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, all per spec. `begin_upload` at texture_factory.cpp:267 also throws (device_resources.cpp:1863-1864), as does the `copies` vector at :241-265.

3. THE INDEX-BUFFER COPY IS UNGUARDED AND ON THE RESTORE PATH. renderer.cpp:582-599 is the same shape with no try at all. `handle_device_lost` (device_resources.cpp:1265) resets the old device, builds a new one, then calls `notify_->on_device_restored()` (:1326-1329); that is `Renderer::Impl::on_device_restored` at renderer.cpp:713-721, which calls `create_device_dependent_resources()` with no handler, reaching the unguarded upload at renderer.cpp:598. I checked whether `noexcept` would turn this into `terminate()` and kill the "client carries on" half — it does not: the four `handle_device_lost` call sites (device_resources.cpp:1225, 1417, 1537, 1631) sit in `create_window_size_dependent_resources`, `execute`, `present` and `present`, and none of those is declared `noexcept` (device_resources.h:255, :292, :306; only `try_wait_for_gpu` at :326 is). So the exception does reach the client. `this->indices` is assigned at renderer.cpp:577 before the upload, so a throw at :598 leaves it a valid device-local buffer with undefined contents, bound at renderer.cpp:1008-1009 and drawn from at renderer.cpp:1142.

4. IT IS A VULKAN-ONLY GAP. The D3D12 equivalent holds its staging in a `ComPtr<ID3D12Resource>` (engine/render/d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:207), so the same throw releases it for free. And the file's own standard is already "put it back": `create_vulkan_buffer` itself destroys its buffer when its own allocation fails (device_resources.cpp:314-319). The catch at texture_factory.cpp:320 frees three of the four things the try created; the fourth is simply missed.

WHAT I COULD NOT SALVAGE FOR THE DEFENCE, and did check: whether the process always dies before the leak matters. samples/minimal/main.cpp:48 does catch and return 1 — but that only converts the leak into the other half of the same defect, since the device is then destroyed with a live `VkBuffer` and `VkDeviceMemory` bound to it, which the spec forbids (all child objects must be destroyed before `vkDestroyDevice`) and which the validation layers this backend was checked under will report. And renderer.h:376-379 puts a client "catching an exception out of its own draw walk and carrying on — and so does a device event" inside the seam's contemplated behaviour, so the surviving-process case is a term of the contract rather than an invention.

*Correction:* Two things the finding gets wrong, neither fatal.

(a) THE COMMENT-DRIFT ARGUMENT IS A MIS-READING AND SHOULD BE DROPPED. texture_factory.cpp:208-211 reads "FROM HERE THE IMAGE IS OWNED BY NOBODY UNTIL THE LAST LINE, so every failure between the two has to put it back... the VulkanTexture that will own all three is not constructed until every one of them exists." Its subject is the image, and "all three" names image, memory and view — the staging buffer is not in its scope. The code matches that comment exactly. So this is not "a comment the code does not match" and docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md's standard is the wrong rule to invoke. The finding stands on better ground without it: the file's own practice (create_vulkan_buffer frees its buffer on its own allocation failure, device_resources.cpp:314-319; the catch frees three of four), the divergence from d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:207's ComPtr, and the Vulkan VU that every child object be destroyed before vkDestroyDevice.

(b) MINOR CITATION SLIP: the sentence contemplating a client that catches a device-event throw and carries on is renderer.h:376-379, not 377-380 — line 380 is `void begin_frame();`.

ON SEVERITY: minor is right for the finding as titled (a staging-buffer leak on an error path that already means OOM or device loss, and which dies with the device). But the two halves are not the same defect and the write-up buries the worse one. renderer.cpp:582-599 is not primarily a leak — it leaves `this->indices` (renderer.cpp:577) a valid device-local buffer holding undefined bytes with no handler anywhere between it and the client, which is a correctness defect on a path renderer.h:376-379 contemplates. Split out on its own it would rank should-fix. I am leaving the overall severity at minor because the trigger is a Vulkan error return on the restore half of a device loss, which this repository's own review records as having no in-process trigger (docs/review/backend-equivalence/TEST-GAP.md:55), so neither consequence is reachable in any test that exists.

## Refuted — raised, then disproved

11 findings. Kept so that nobody spends the budget re-deriving them. R8 is
the one the two refuters split on and an adjudicator killed. R11 is the one
where they split and no adjudicator is recorded; it is filed here on Refuter
B's reading, and because R7 is the same claim about the same line —
`tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:1747` — raised independently and refuted by both
of its own refuters.

### R1. A second VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR from the retry acquire throws out of end_frame instead of skipping the present, which unwinds through a window procedure during a drag-resize

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1540`** · should-fix · `core` · raised by R164 · run id `V10`

present() gives the acquire exactly one retry and makes its failure terminal. device_resources.cpp:1530-1543: `acquired = vkAcquireNextImageKHR(this->owner_->device, this->swapchain_, UINT64_MAX, this->frame().acquired, VK_NULL_HANDLE, &image); } ... if (acquired != VK_SUCCESS && acquired != VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR) { check_vk(acquired, "No swapchain image could be acquired"); }`. RULE BROKEN: device_resources.h:60-63 claims 'out-of-date news is answered inside present() by remaking a swapchain', and the comment at 1513-1521 says the seam 'never hears about it'; a second out-of-date is not answered, it is thrown. renderer.h documents no throw on end_frame, and device_resources.h:320-326 states this repository's own rule for exactly this situation: try_wait_for_gpu exists 'FOR THE PLACES WHERE THROWING DOES MORE DAMAGE THAN THE FAILURE IT REPORTS - two destructors ... and the resize path, which is reached from a window procedure with nowhere above it to catch. Answers false instead.' This path IS reached from a window procedure and does not answer false. It is distinct from the minimised finding and survives that fix, because here rebuild_swapchain succeeds at a non-zero extent and the retry acquire is stale anyway. FAILURE: drag a window edge. While in_sizemove_ is set, engine/app/window.cpp:244-250 renders from WM_PAINT, so present() runs on every paint while the client area changes on every mouse move. The first acquire returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR; rebuild_swapchain builds one at whatever the surface reported at that instant; the user moves one more pixel before the retry at 1530, which returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again; check_vk at 1542 throws std::runtime_error out of Renderer::end_frame -> Application::render -> the WM_PAINT case -> DispatchMessage, with no handler between. VK_ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR (the window destroyed with a frame in flight) reaches the same line with the same result. FIX: treat OUT_OF_DATE and SURFACE_LOST from the retry the way the no-swapchain branch at 1523-1528 already treats a missing swapchain - `this->execute(); this->frame_index_ = (this->frame_index_ + 1) % FRAME_COUNT; return;` - so the frame's work still reaches the GPU, one frame is not presented, and the next present rebuilds. Reserve the throw for results that are not about the surface having moved.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

The quoted code is accurate but both loadbearing legs of the finding — its rule and its failure scenario — fail against the tree.

WHAT IS AT THE LINES. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1509-1543 reads as quoted: first acquire at 1509, `if (acquired == VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR)` at 1513, `rebuild_swapchain()` at 1522, the null-swapchain bail at 1523-1528, the retry acquire at 1530-1532, the device-lost branch at 1535-1539, and `check_vk(acquired, "No swapchain image could be acquired")` at 1542. `check_vk` at 212-221 throws `std::runtime_error` for anything that is not `VK_SUCCESS`. The call chain is real: Renderer::end_frame (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-867) calls `present()`; Application::render (engine/app/application.cpp:299) calls end_frame; Application::tick (application.cpp:254-258) calls render; and engine/app/window.cpp:344-349 calls `notify_->tick()` from WM_PAINT while `in_sizemove_`. So a throw at 1542 would indeed unwind out of a window procedure. That much is right, and it is the only part that is.

LEG 1 — THE RULE IS NOT THIS CODEBASE'S RULE, AND IS CONTRADICTED THREE LINES ABOVE THE CITED LINE. The finding reads device_resources.h:59-63 ("out-of-date news is answered inside present() by remaking a swapchain") as a promise that this branch cannot throw. It is not, and cannot be: the branch it names is already eight throw sites deep. `rebuild_swapchain` (device_resources.cpp:1171-1184) calls `create_swapchain`, which throws at 1028, 1035, 1070, 1074, 1141, 1148, 1151 and 1165. The sentence is about *where out-of-date news is handled* — inside present(), not routed out to `Renderer::window_size_changed` — which is exactly what the comment at 1515-1521 says ("Renderer::window_size_changed never hears about it"). It is not a no-throw guarantee for the function.

The other cited rule, device_resources.h:320-326, names its own scope in the same sentence the finding quotes: try_wait_for_gpu exists for "two destructors, which are implicitly noexcept, and the resize path". `present()` is neither. The resize path honours it at device_resources.cpp:1223-1227 (`if (!this->try_wait_for_gpu()) { handle_device_lost(); return; }`), and the comment there at 1217-1222 gives the reason. The frame path does the opposite by design and everywhere: `check_vk(submitted, "The frame could not be submitted")` at 1420, and `check_vk(presented, "The frame could not be presented")` at 1645 — the latter reached from the identical WM_PAINT stack, in the same function, two dozen lines below the line being complained about. It is the pattern in every backend: engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.cpp:417 and engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:487 both `ThrowIfFailed(hr)` on an unexpected Present result after handling device-removal. If the invoked rule existed, it would condemn five backends' present paths, not this line.

LEG 2 — THE FAILURE SCENARIO CANNOT HAPPEN. The finding requires the window's client area to change between `rebuild_swapchain()` at 1522 and the retry at 1530: "the user moves one more pixel before the retry at 1530". The window cannot change size there. During a drag-resize the modal size loop runs on this same thread, inside DefWindowProc; WM_PAINT is dispatched from that loop (window.cpp:344-349), and while our handler is inside `present()` the thread is not in the loop, so nothing calls SetWindowPos. Win32 gives no way around this: a size change must be processed by the owning thread (WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING / WM_NCCALCSIZE), so even a cross-thread or cross-process SetWindowPos blocks until this thread pumps again. There is no other thread in the picture — engine/core/thread_pool.cpp is the parallel draw and touches no window, and tick() is only ever called from the message thread (window.cpp:246 idle branch, window.cpp:349 WM_PAINT).

So the retry at 1530 runs against a swapchain built moments earlier from `capabilities.currentExtent` (device_resources.cpp:1048), read after `vkDeviceWaitIdle` at 1182, for a window that has been frozen the whole time. It matches. The `0xFFFFFFFF` fallback at 1049-1057 — the one path that could build a swapchain at the *stale* colour extent during a drag — is dead on Win32, as the comment at 1041-1047 states: minImageExtent and maxImageExtent are both the window's client area.

The SURFACE_LOST leg does not rescue it either. It is not a property of the retry at all — a lost surface returns from the *first* acquire at 1509 and reaches 1542 by the identical route, so it is an argument about the policy at 1540, not about the one-retry structure the finding is built on. And it is not reachable from the window-destroyed case it cites: `pump_until_quit` (window.cpp:238-248) only calls tick() in the `else` branch of PeekMessage, and once PostQuitMessage has set the quit flag PeekMessage returns WM_QUIT rather than FALSE, so no frame is rendered after WM_DESTROY.

*Correction:* One thing survives, and it belongs to the finding this one explicitly disclaims. Line 1542 IS reachable with a second VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR — but only by the minimised route, not the drag route. `create_swapchain` returns early for a zero extent at device_resources.cpp:1059-1067, before `destroy_swapchain()` at 1140 and before `this->swapchain_ = fresh` at 1143, so it leaves `swapchain_` holding the OLD handle. `rebuild_swapchain` (1171-1184) does not destroy it either. So when a minimised window drives the first acquire to OUT_OF_DATE, the guard at 1523 does not fire, the retry at 1530 goes to the same stale swapchain, returns OUT_OF_DATE again, and 1542 throws. Nothing gates rendering on minimised state — Application::tick (application.cpp:254-258) has no such check, and the comment at 1497-1500 says drawing while minimised is expected.

That is the minimised defect, reached through the minimised bug's own mechanism. V10 states "It is distinct from the minimised finding and survives that fix, because here rebuild_swapchain succeeds at a non-zero extent and the retry acquire is stale anyway" — and it is the non-zero-extent case that does not exist. Fix the early return at 1059-1067 and there is no reachable second OUT_OF_DATE left. V10 has no independent content; whatever is owed at this line is owed to the minimised finding, and crediting it twice would have a reader hunting a drag-resize race that Win32 does not permit.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

**1. The stated trigger is physically impossible in this shell.** The finding's whole failure scenario is "the user moves one more pixel before the retry at 1530". Trace the thread. `engine/app/window.cpp:344-350` — WM_PAINT while `in_sizemove_` calls `self->notify_->tick()`, which is `Application::tick` (`engine/app/application.cpp:254-258`) → `render()` (`:280-300`) → `Renderer::end_frame` (`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:856-866`) → `DeviceResources::present()`. That is the window's own thread, inside the window procedure. A Win32 window's client area changes only when its owning thread processes a message (WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGED/WM_SIZE from the modal resize loop's own `SetWindowPos`); `SetWindowPos` from any other thread blocks on that thread's pump. That thread is inside `present()`. So between `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR` at `device_resources.cpp:1028` (inside `create_swapchain`, which `rebuild_swapchain` at `:1171-1180` calls) and the retry acquire at `:1530`, the surface's `currentExtent` cannot move. The swapchain the retry acquires from was created microseconds earlier at exactly the extent the surface still reports. The finding's own words — "here rebuild_swapchain succeeds at a non-zero extent and the retry acquire is stale anyway" — are the claim that fails: it is not stale.

**2. The out-of-date news normally arrives at present, and that path already does not throw.** `device_resources.cpp:1633-1640` handles `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR` and `VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR` from `vkQueuePresentKHR` by rebuilding for the next frame, no throw. On a Win32 drag-resize that is where the mismatch surfaces, so the swapchain is normally already rebuilt before the next frame's acquire runs — the acquire branch at `:1513` typically fires zero times per resize, not twice.

**3. Every other backend has the identical shape, and it is accepted.** `engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.cpp:391-423` and `engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:468-489`: handle `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`/`_RESET`, then `ThrowIfFailed(hr)` on anything else — a throw out of `present()`, reached from the very same WM_PAINT-during-drag path. Per the brief, that makes "a throw out of end_frame during a drag" a property of the seam, not of `vulkan/`.

**4. The rule invoked is misquoted in scope.** `device_resources.h:320-326` makes *`try_wait_for_gpu`* non-throwing, and `device_resources.cpp:1216-1223` gives the reason: after a device removal that wait is the first thing to touch the device, so it answers instead of throwing. Two statements later the same function calls `create_swapchain()` (`:1240`), which throws via `check_vk` at `:1028` and `:1141`, and via `std::runtime_error` at `:1035-1040` — in the resize path, from a window procedure. The codebase therefore holds no rule "nothing reachable from a window procedure may throw"; it holds "the wait on the way out answers false". T6 is "loud is for broken contracts", and swapchain creation failure is treated as one throughout this file.

**5. `renderer.h` does not promise a non-throwing `end_frame`.** `engine/render/renderer.h:367-381` explicitly contemplates exceptions escaping the frame path: "A client reaches this by catching an exception out of its own draw walk and carrying on - and so does a device event, which surfaces as a throw from a worker mid-frame." And there *is* a handler above `DispatchMessage`: `samples/minimal/main.cpp:48` and `samples/linesweeper/main.cpp:49` wrap `app.run(...)`.

**6. The SURFACE_LOST variant is not reachable either.** `window.cpp:665-667` — WM_DESTROY posts WM_QUIT; `window.cpp:238-247` calls `tick()` only when `PeekMessage` finds nothing, and WM_QUIT is returned by `PeekMessage` before the queue is empty, so no frame is rendered after the HWND dies. And a genuinely lost surface would throw from `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR` at `:1028` inside `rebuild_swapchain` before line 1542 is ever reached.

**Line-number check:** the finding cites `engine/app/window.cpp:244-250` for the WM_PAINT tick; the actual site is `:344-350` (`:244-250` is inside `pump_until_quit`/`close`).

*Correction:* One true residue, and it belongs to the finding this one disclaims. There IS a reachable route to a second VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR at device_resources.cpp:1540, and it is the zero-extent one: create_swapchain's early return at :1059-1067 fires BEFORE `VkSwapchainKHR previous = this->swapchain_` and before destroy_swapchain() at :1140, so on a minimise it leaves swapchain_ holding the OLD handle. The guard at :1523 (`swapchain_ == VK_NULL_HANDLE`) therefore does not fire, and :1530 retries the acquire against a stale swapchain. That is exactly the minimised finding, so V10's distinctness claim ("survives that fix, because here rebuild_swapchain succeeds at a non-zero extent") is the part that is false — the non-zero-extent mechanism it rests on cannot occur single-threaded, and the only mechanism that can occur is the one it says it is not. Also worth recording for whoever fixes the minimised case: confining a fix to line 1540 would not buy the immunity V10 asks for, because rebuild_swapchain itself throws from :1028, :1035 and :1141 on the same window-procedure path.
