### R2. The swapchain format fallback takes surface_formats[0] unchecked, which is what the comment immediately above it says must not happen - and the steady-state present path copies rather than converts

**`engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1092`** · should-fix · `seam` · raised by R86 · run id `V47`

CLAIM: When no offered surface format is B8G8R8A8_UNORM + SRGB_NONLINEAR, create_swapchain silently takes surface_formats[0] - whatever it is - while colour_format_ stays hard-coded B8G8R8A8_UNORM, and present() then does a raw vkCmdCopyImage between them in the steady state.

EVIDENCE, verbatim and verified at device_resources.cpp:1080-1101:

```
    // NOT THE _SRGB ONE, and the difference is the whole pixel contract. An
    // sRGB swapchain format makes the presentation engine convert what it
    // is handed, so the same bytes would come out lighter here than on the
    // four backends whose buffers are UNORM - and read_back_buffer would
    // still hand back the unconverted colour target, so nothing in
    // RenderPixelTests could see it. ...
    VkSurfaceFormatKHR chosen = surface_formats.empty()
        ? VkSurfaceFormatKHR{ VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM, VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR }
        : surface_formats[0];
    for (const VkSurfaceFormatKHR& candidate : surface_formats)
    { if (candidate.format == VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM && candidate.colorSpace == VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR) { chosen = candidate; break; } }
```


engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1567-1596, present(), verified: when colour_extent_ == swapchain_extent_ it issues vkCmdCopyImage(colour_image_ -> target); otherwise vkCmdBlitImage with VK_FILTER_LINEAR. engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.h: `VkFormat colour_format_ = VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM;` is never derived from the surface.

WHY IT IS WRONG: vkCmdCopyImage between size-compatible formats is a raw texel-block copy - legal between B8G8R8A8_UNORM and R8G8B8A8_UNORM (same 32-bit compatibility class) and performing no channel reorder and no transfer function - whereas vkCmdBlitImage DOES convert. So on an R8G8B8A8 surface the steady-state frame is presented with red and blue transposed, and the same frame changes colour the moment the window is being drag-resized and the blit path is taken instead. This repository's stated habit is the opposite of silent: engine/render/texture_format.h - "A file naming anything else is rejected by name (T6) rather than passed through to fail as a device error" - and twenty lines above this very code, device_resources.cpp:1032-1038 throws by name when the surface will not take a transfer.

FAILURE SCENARIO: The stated reason this backend exists is Android, Linux and MoltenVK (vulkan/backend.h:20-27, docs/port/android.md, CLAUDE.md). Surfaces on those platforms commonly advertise R8G8B8A8_UNORM / R8G8B8A8_SRGB and no BGRA at all. On such a device surface_formats[0] is taken blind: the shell shows every steady-state frame with red and blue transposed and every drag-resize frame in a different, converted colour, while RenderPixelTests and all fifty golden images stay green - read_back_buffer swizzles from the hard-coded BGRA colour target (renderer.cpp:1226-1238) and never looks at the swapchain at all.

FIX: Refuse by name when no candidate is B8G8R8A8_UNORM + SRGB_NONLINEAR, in the same voice as the transfer-dst refusal at :1032-1038; or make colour_format_ follow the chosen surface format and drive read_back_buffer's swizzle from colour_format() instead of from a hard-coded BGRA.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

The mechanism is physically right and the finding is still dead, on three independent counts: the evidence is misquoted by elision, the failure scenario has no surface to happen on, and the proposed fix is the thing this tree names as its own refused anti-pattern.

1. THE QUOTED EVIDENCE IS NOT WHAT IS AT THOSE LINES. The finding says "EVIDENCE, verbatim and verified at device_resources.cpp:1080-1101" and begins its quotation at `// NOT THE _SRGB ONE`. Checked character for character, that range does not start there. device_resources.cpp:1079-1080 reads:

```
    // B8G8R8A8_UNORM if it is offered, which on Win32 it always is, and the
    // first thing offered otherwise.
```

followed by a blank comment line, and only then (1082) `// NOT THE _SRGB ONE...`. The two lines the quotation drops are precisely the ones that state the fallback as intended behaviour. So the headline — "which is what the comment immediately above it says must not happen" — is refuted by the comment itself. The `NOT THE _SRGB ONE` paragraph (1082-1088) is an argument about the loop's SEARCH KEY at 1093-1101 — why it insists on `B8G8R8A8_UNORM` rather than accepting a `_SRGB` entry that a driver also offers — not a prohibition on the `surface_formats[0]` default. Remove the elision and the finding's premise disappears.

2. THE FAILURE SCENARIO CANNOT BE REACHED, AND THE MISSING LINK IS THE SURFACE. The scenario requires "Android, Linux and MoltenVK... surfaces [that] commonly advertise R8G8B8A8_UNORM and no BGRA at all". This backend can only ever hold a Win32 surface: device_resources.h:8-13 defines `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR` and includes `<Windows.h>` unconditionally; device_resources.cpp:446-447 pushes exactly `VK_KHR_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME` and `VK_KHR_WIN32_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME`; :875-879 builds a `VkWin32SurfaceCreateInfoKHR` and calls `vkCreateWin32SurfaceKHR`; :425 is `set_window(HWND, int, int)`. `CMakePresets.json:45-50` has one Vulkan preset, `x64-debug-vulkan`, x64 Windows, and CLAUDE.md:1 says Windows-only. I tried to build the scenario from every entry point that reaches `present()` (device_resources.cpp:1493) — `samples/minimal`, `samples/linesweeper` — and all of them arrive through that Win32 surface; `RenderPixelTests` never calls `present()` at all (device_resources.h:41-44: fifty-one frames, none presented). There is no Android, Linux or Metal target in this tree to construct the case in. docs/port/android.md §3.5 is a document, not code.

3. THE COLOUR-SPACE HALF IS GUARANTEED ON THAT SURFACE, WHICH THE FINDING DOES NOT ACCOUNT FOR. `VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace` is not in the instance extension list (device_resources.cpp:445-447 plus a debug-utils push at :462 under `_DEBUG`). Without it, `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceFormatsKHR` may only report entries whose colorSpace is `VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR`, so the loop's two-part match at :1095-1096 reduces on Win32 to "is `B8G8R8A8_UNORM` offered" — which every Windows ICD answers yes to, Vulkan WSI on Windows sitting on DXGI whose flip-model format is `DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM`. The `surface_formats.empty()` arm at :1089-1091 is also not a hazard: it defaults to BGRA8_UNORM, and the call is required to return at least one format anyway.

4. THE RULE INVOKED CUTS THE OTHER WAY. The `texture_format.h:30-32` quote ("rejected by name (T6) rather than passed through to fail as a device error") is about CONTENT THAT EXISTS — read :20-32, it is a census of the 43 `.dds` files in this repository and its client. It is not a rule about device capabilities on platforms with no build. The tree's actual position on this move is stated in docs/port/android.md §7: "None of these should be amended in advance... Every other row waits for the work that earns it — the surface-loss term §3.4 names included, which is the fifth backend's to write and not this document's to pre-empt. A design document that describes a port that has not happened is the speculative framework this tree refuses, and it would be the second time a comment in `render/` was written in the future tense of a port." The first time was `texture_format.h`'s block-compression paragraph, caught by DRIFT.md and fixed in `a56d198` — the same file the finding quotes.

5. THE SECOND PROPOSED FIX WOULD BREAK THE DESIGN IT MISREADS. "Make `colour_format_` follow the chosen surface format and drive read_back_buffer's swizzle from `colour_format()`" inverts the backend's central decision. device_resources.h:31-64 argues at length that the image the frame is drawn into is NOT a swapchain image, and :450-453 says why its format is fixed: "B8G8R8A8_UNORM, which is what both Direct3D backends' back buffers are and what a Win32 surface always offers. Matching them costs nothing and keeps read_back_buffer's swizzle the same sentence in three files." The colour target is created at that format at :805, :924 and :962, and renderer.cpp:1226-1238 swizzles to match — internally consistent, not a hazard. Letting the presentation engine choose the engine's colour target format would make `read_back_buffer` output driver-dependent and the fifty golden images in `tests/render/golden/` unshareable across the four rasterisers, which is the pixel contract CLAUDE.md describes.

WHAT IS TRUE: `vkCmdCopyImage` (:1577) between size-compatible 32-bit formats is a raw texel-block copy with no channel reorder, `vkCmdBlitImage` (:1593) does convert, and so on a hypothetical RGBA-only surface the two present paths at :1567-1596 would disagree. Correct Vulkan, no subject in this repository.

*Correction:* One small real observation survives, and it is not what was raised: `swapchain_format_` (device_resources.h:430) is assigned at device_resources.cpp:1144 and read nowhere in the tree — grep over engine/, tests/ and samples/ returns only the declaration and that one assignment. It is a dead member. If the chosen surface format ever did need checking against `colour_format_`, the member already in place to check it with is unused; noting that costs a line and commits the tree to nothing. That is minor/cosmetic and the finding does not raise it. Also worth recording for whoever reads V47 next: the surface-format question is real for a future Android port, but it belongs to that port's work item (docs/port/android.md §3.5, §7), and its answer there is more likely "swizzle or blit rather than copy when the formats differ" than the "refuse by name" this finding proposes — refusing to start on a device that offers only RGBA would be worse than presenting on it.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *refuted*, severity `minor`

The finding's code reading is accurate; its rule, its scenario and its severity are not.

1. THE HEADLINE IS CONTRADICTED BY THE COMMENT IT CITES. The finding says the fallback "is what the comment immediately above it says must not happen", and presents its evidence as "verbatim and verified at device_resources.cpp:1080-1101". The quoted block actually begins at :1082 ("// NOT THE _SRGB ONE"). It omits :1079-1080, which are the two lines that state the policy: "// B8G8R8A8_UNORM if it is offered, which on Win32 it always is, and the / // first thing offered otherwise." The code at :1089-1101 does exactly that. The "NOT THE _SRGB ONE" paragraph argues why the *search key* is the UNORM variant rather than the SRGB variant — a choice between two formats a Win32 surface offers side by side — not a prohibition on the fallback. There is no code/comment contradiction; the finding manufactured one by dropping the two decisive lines from a range it claims to quote verbatim.

2. THE FAILURE SCENARIO IS UNREACHABLE FROM ANY CALLER AT HEAD. The scenario is explicitly "Android, Linux and MoltenVK ... surfaces on those platforms commonly advertise R8G8B8A8". This backend builds no such surface. device_resources.cpp:447 pushes VK_KHR_WIN32_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME unconditionally; :875-881 is a VkWin32SurfaceCreateInfoKHR from an HWND; set_window at :425 takes an HWND. CLAUDE.md:3 and README.md:41 say Windows-only, and README.md:53-55 says of Vulkan's platform reach "it is not a platform this repository has yet". On Win32 every shipping ICD (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and the software ones) advertises B8G8R8A8_UNORM + SRGB_NONLINEAR, so the loop at :1093-1101 always overwrites the :1092 initialiser. The value the finding says is "taken blind" never survives on any configuration this tree builds.

3. TWO OF THE THREE NAMED PLATFORMS WOULD NOT EXHIBIT IT ANYWAY. MoltenVK's surface format list always contains B8G8R8A8_UNORM because MTLPixelFormatBGRA8Unorm is *the* CAMetalLayer format — BGRA is the native case on Apple, not the missing one. Mesa's X11/Wayland WSI likewise advertises B8G8R8A8_UNORM/SRGB_NONLINEAR (the X visual is BGRA). Only Android is a real candidate — ANativeWindow's vocabulary is RGBA_8888/RGBX_8888/RGB_565, so the list is typically R8G8B8A8_UNORM, R8G8B8A8_SRGB, R5G6B5 — and Android is precisely the platform that does not build. Reaching it requires rewriting instance extensions, surface creation and set_window's HWND signature; the format question is met by that same edit, not smuggled past it.

4. IT IS THE SEAM'S ASSUMPTION, NOT THIS BACKEND'S. "The back buffer is B8G8R8A8_UNORM" is hard-coded with no negotiation at all in the two backends already accepted: d3d11/backend.h:226 and d3d12/backend.h:289 both construct DeviceResources{ DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM }, d3d11/device_resources.cpp:279 and d3d12/device_resources.cpp:363 feed it straight into the swap-chain description, d3d12/renderer.cpp:776 into the PSO, and nothing anywhere queries what the output supports. The Vulkan version at least searches for it. (The one asymmetry in the finding's favour: DXGI guarantees B8G8R8A8_UNORM for a flip-model swap chain, where Vulkan guarantees nothing about a surface's format list — so the shapes are not literally identical.)

Verified as correct but moot: colour_format_ is hard-coded at device_resources.h:454 and never derived from the surface; swapchain_format_ is stored at :1144 and read nowhere; present() copies when the extents agree and blits with VK_FILTER_LINEAR when they do not (:1567-1596); read_back_buffer swizzles a fixed BGRA layout (renderer.cpp:1226-1238) and never touches a swapchain image. The Vulkan mechanism is also stated correctly: B8G8R8A8_UNORM and R8G8B8A8_UNORM are in the same 32-bit format-compatibility class, so vkCmdCopyImage between them is legal and is a bit-for-bit texel copy with no channel reorder, while vkCmdBlitImage reads texels as RGBA values and does reorder. All of which describes a state the code cannot enter on the platform it compiles for.

*Correction:* What survives is much smaller than what was raised, and it is not a defect in the present path. The residue: line :1092 is an unreached fallback that would be silently wrong if it were ever reached, sitting sixty lines below :1032-1038, where the same function refuses by name when the surface will not take a transfer. A two-line refusal in that same voice, or a comment saying the branch is a placeholder the port must revisit, would cost nothing and would keep the file's habit consistent. That is a minor tidy against a future port, not a should-fix against 4d91b91 — the shell cannot show a transposed frame on any build this repository produces.

Two further corrections for whoever picks it up. (a) The finding's preferred fix — "refuse by name when no candidate is B8G8R8A8_UNORM" — is the wrong answer for the platform it is worried about: on Android it turns a colour bug into a hard failure to start. The right answer there is its own second option, colour_format_ following the chosen surface format with read_back_buffer's swizzle driven from colour_format(), and that belongs in the port commit that also replaces vkCreateWin32SurfaceKHR. (b) Do not carry the finding's MoltenVK claim forward; BGRA is Metal's native surface format, so Apple is the platform least likely to exhibit this.

FAILURE. LunarG ships a new SDK and any of three things reds master with no commit having touched the repository: (a) the silent-install contract changes — it has changed before, from NSIS-style flags to the Qt IFW's `--accept-licenses --default-answer --confirm-command install` at 1.3.216 — and the argument list at ci.yml:135-136 stops meaning anything; (b) the new dxc emits SPIR-V the descriptor-set layout at engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:314-333 no longer matches, or warns where /WX bites; (c) `latest` 404s or serves a partial file during a release rollover. FIX. Pin the version so a bump is a reviewable commit: add `vulkan_sdk_version: '1.3.290.0'` to the x64-debug-vulkan matrix entry and fetch https://sdk.lunarg.com/sdk/download/${{ matrix.vulkan_sdk_version }}/windows/vulkan_sdk.exe, with a comment saying the pin is the build's Vulkan floor made concrete. Once pinned, the installer download can also be cached, which is impossible while the URL floats.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *refuted*, severity `minor`

VERIFIED TRUE: ci.yml:134 is quoted character for character — `Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://sdk.lunarg.com/sdk/download/latest/windows/vulkan_sdk.exe"`. `git blame -L 126,141` confirms lines 126-137 all landed in 4d91b91. compile_shaders.cmake:101-106 is the sole SPIR-V compiler lookup. ci.yml:6-7 is quoted accurately. That much stands. Everything the finding builds on it does not.

(1) THE UNIQUENESS CLAIM — "the only external input to this workflow that is not [pinned by the tree]" — IS REFUTED BY LINE 27 OF THE SAME FILE. ci.yml:27 `runs-on: windows-latest` (blame: 2a75ae52, predates this commit) is a rolling label pinned by nothing in the tree, and it governs strictly more of the build than the SDK does: MSVC, which enforces `/W4 /WX` with zero suppressions on every C++ file; `fxc`, which at compile_shaders.cmake:30-34 and :42-54 compiles engine/render/sprite.hlsl into the byte arrays BOTH Direct3D backends ship; the Windows SDK; and whatever vswhere resolves at ci.yml:141. ci.yml:114 `VCPKG_ROOT=$env:VCPKG_INSTALLATION_ROOT` takes the runner's preinstalled vcpkg, also unpinned by the tree. And ci.yml:107/120/171 use `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/cache@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4` — floating major tags, not SHA pins. The finding lists these as "pinned" while applying to the SDK URL a standard ("re-running CI a year from now does not rebuild it") that `@v4` and `windows-latest` fail identically. The URL is not the exception; it is one of several, and not the largest.

(2) FAILURE MODE (b) IS REFUTED TWICE. First, the descriptor binding is a function of the repository at both ends, not of dxc's defaults: compile_shaders.cmake:130-132 passes `-fvk-b-shift 0 0`, `-fvk-t-shift 1 0`, `-fvk-s-shift 2 0` explicitly, and engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:314-327 writes `bindings[0].binding = 0`, `bindings[1].binding = 1`, `bindings[2].binding = 2` explicitly to match. A version bump cannot silently move them; dxc would have to change the meaning of explicit flags. Second, CI could not observe a mismatch even if one existed: ci.yml:90 gives the vulkan matrix entry `skip_tests: '-E RenderPixelTests'`, and ci.yml:48-56 states the reason — "a runner has a loader and no device". No VkDevice is created, so vkCreateDescriptorSetLayout/vkCreateGraphicsPipelines never run and no validation occurs. A layout/SPIR-V mismatch would pass CI GREEN, the opposite of the claimed "reds master". Third, "warns where /WX bites" is wrong on mechanism: `/WX` is an MSVC flag carried by labrador_settings for C++ compilation; dxc's argument list at compile_shaders.cmake:125-135 contains no warnings-as-errors flag, and its output is a C header holding a byte array (compile_shaders.cmake:14-15, `-Fh` + `-Vn`), which compiles identically under /W4 /WX whatever version emitted it.

(3) "THE SHIPPED SPIR-V" DOES NOT EXIST HERE. `ls .github/workflows/` shows one file; grep for release/publish/deploy finds only ci.yml:80 (`x64-release` preset) and ci.yml:171 (upload-artifact). The only artifact is `golden-actual-${{ matrix.preset }}` gated `if: failure()` at ci.yml:169-175. The SPIR-V compiled in CI is never executed (no device) and never published. SPIR-V that would actually ship is produced on a contributor's machine by whatever SDK they installed. Pinning CI's URL does not make shipped bytecode a function of the repository.

(4) THE FINDING'S OWN PRIMARY RULE ARGUES AGAINST ITS FIX. ci.yml:6-7 reads "Everything this builds is in the repository or in vcpkg.json, so a run here is a real clone of what a new contributor gets." README.md:68 tells a new contributor to install "The [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/)" — no version — and the build's own FATAL_ERROR at compile_shaders.cmake:113-114 repeats the same versionless URL. A new contributor gets latest. CI fetching `latest` is that sentence honoured; pinning to 1.3.290.0 would make CI the only machine in the world building against a version no contributor has, i.e. it breaks the rule cited to justify it.

(5) THE SECOND RULE QUOTE IS MISCITED AND ITS ANTECEDENT IS FALSE. The finding cites "ci.yml:95-99"; the text is at ci.yml:96-101 (95 is blank). It renders it as "a build should not add a supply chain it does not control." What it actually says is "a build that can be done with the tools already on the machine should not add a supply chain to do it" — a preference for vswhere over a third-party action when the tool is already present. The Vulkan SDK is explicitly NOT already on the machine: engine/CMakeLists.txt:174 "THE ONLY BACKEND WHOSE DEPENDENCY IS NOT ALREADY ON THE MACHINE", and ci.yml:58-65 reasons the exception out at length ("IT IS ALSO THE ONE PRESET THAT INSTALLS SOMETHING, and that was decided rather than discovered"). The condition the principle attaches to is false here, so the principle does not govern.

(6) THE PROPOSED FIX MISDESCRIBES THE TREE. It asks for "a comment saying the pin is the build's Vulkan floor made concrete." The build's Vulkan floor is stated in code as `const uint32_t MIN_API_VERSION = VK_API_VERSION_1_2;` at engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:32, enforced at :554, and argued at :25-31 (Android 10 shipped 1.1, MoltenVK reports 1.2). 1.3.290.0 is not that floor; the comment the fix prescribes would be false.

WHAT SURVIVES: only scenarios (a) and (c) — LunarG could change the Qt-IFW silent-install flags at ci.yml:135-136, or `latest` could 404 during a rollover, and either reds the build. That is real, but it is ordinary external-drift hygiene, identical in kind to and smaller in blast radius than `windows-latest`, and it produces a loud immediate step failure rather than a wrong artifact. It is not the claimed defect, which was about bytecode provenance and reproducibility.

*Correction:* A residue survives, far smaller than raised and with a different mechanism. TRUE: ci.yml:134 fetches an unpinned installer, and if LunarG changes the silent-install argument contract or `latest` is briefly unavailable, the step at ci.yml:135-136 fails with no commit having touched the tree. That is a hygiene point about CI robustness — worth a sentence of comment at most.

FALSE and should not be repeated: (i) that this is the only unpinned external input — ci.yml:27 `windows-latest` is a larger one governing MSVC under /WX and the fxc that produces two other backends' shipped bytecode, and ci.yml:107/120/171's `@v4` are floating tags too; (ii) that a dxc change could silently break the descriptor layout — both ends are explicit in the tree at compile_shaders.cmake:130-132 and renderer.cpp:314-327; (iii) that any such breakage would red master — ci.yml:90 skips RenderPixelTests and ci.yml:48-56 says no device exists, so CI never creates a pipeline and such a bug would pass green; (iv) that /WX interacts with dxc — it does not, dxc emits a byte-array header; (v) that CI produces "shipped SPIR-V" — there is no release job, and the only artifact is failure-gated golden frames.

The prescribed fix should NOT be applied as written. Pinning inverts the rule the finding cites: ci.yml:6-7 makes the run "a real clone of what a new contributor gets", and README.md:68 plus compile_shaders.cmake:113-114 send that contributor to a versionless lunarg.com URL. Pinning makes CI diverge from every contributor's machine. And the pin's proposed justification — "the build's Vulkan floor made concrete" — contradicts device_resources.cpp:32, where the floor is VK_API_VERSION_1_2 for a stated reason. If anything is done here, it is a comment at ci.yml:129 recording that `latest` is deliberate because it matches what README.md:68 tells a contributor to install, and that the installer's flag contract is the thing that could drift.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

The one factual observation is true and dies on everything built on top of it. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:134` does fetch `https://sdk.lunarg.com/sdk/download/latest/windows/vulkan_sdk.exe`, and `cmake/compile_shaders.cmake:101-106` does source `dxc` from `$ENV{VULKAN_SDK}/Bin` and nowhere else. Beyond that the finding fails on its central claim, on its rule, on two of its three failure scenarios, and on its fix.

1. THE CENTRAL CLAIM IS FALSE. "the only external input to this workflow that is not [pinned by the repository]". `ci.yml:27` is `runs-on: windows-latest` — a floating GitHub label — and it is the sole supplier of: (a) MSVC, reached through `ci.yml:141`'s `vswhere.exe -latest`, which has the word in it; (b) **fxc**, the shader compiler for three of the five backends, located by `cmake/compile_shaders.cmake:30-34` — `find_program(FXC_EXECUTABLE NAMES fxc DOC ... REQUIRED)`, no HINTS, no version, bare PATH after vcvars; and (c) the vcpkg *binary*, via `VCPKG_INSTALLATION_ROOT` at `ci.yml:114` — `vcpkg.json`'s `builtin-baseline` (d92484e) pins port versions, not the tool that reads them. `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/cache@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (`ci.yml:107,120,171`) are mutable major-version tags GitHub itself moves, not pins in the reproducibility sense the argument needs. So the finding cites "the runner image for fxc and MSVC" as an example of *pinning* when it is the identical mechanism it condemns: a floating upstream label producing a shader compiler that is not a function of the repository. If the argument holds it convicts fxc word for word, and fxc is not raised. This is the build-system form of "if the other backends have the identical shape and are accepted, the finding is about the seam."

2. THE QUOTED RULE SAYS THE OPPOSITE. `ci.yml:6-7`: "a run here is a real clone of what a new contributor gets." `README.md:68-73` tells that new contributor to install "**The [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/)**" — an unversioned link to a download page that serves the latest; CLAUDE.md repeats it unversioned. `latest` at line 134 is *fidelity to* that sentence. The proposed fix has CI build against a frozen 1.3.290.0 while every human builds against today's SDK — CI diverging from the contributor, which breaks 6-7 rather than restoring it. The fix would only satisfy the rule if README's prerequisite were versioned too, and the finding does not propose that.

3. THE SECOND RULE IS MISQUOTED. The finding renders `ci.yml:95-99` as "a build should not add a supply chain it does not control." `ci.yml:96-101` verbatim says two other things: "the runner image's Visual Studio edition is **not this repository's business**" — an explicit refusal to pin the toolchain, the reverse of what is wanted — and "through vswhere rather than a third-party **action**, because a build that can be done with the tools **already on the machine** should not add a supply chain to do it." The Vulkan SDK is not already on the machine; `ci.yml:58-65` says so at length. Clause two does not reach it and clause one argues against the fix.

4. THE EXCEPTION IS ALREADY ARGUED IN PLACE. `ci.yml:58-65` — "IT IS ALSO THE ONE PRESET THAT INSTALLS SOMETHING, and that was decided rather than discovered" — sits directly above the step and explains what it supplies (a SPIR-V dxc, plus the loader in System32 without which the other eleven test executables would not start). The finding presents this as an unnoticed lapse from line 6-7.

5. FAILURE (b) IS WRONG ON ITS OWN TERMS. "warns where /WX bites" conflates two compilers. `/WX` is an MSVC flag carried by `labrador_settings` in `cmake/settings.cmake` and applies to C++; `compile_shaders.cmake:125-135` hands dxc `-nologo -spirv -T -E -fvk-{b,t,s}-shift -Fh -Vn` and no `-WX`, so a dxc warning fails nothing. Its `-Fh` output is an inert byte array. The descriptor half: bindings 0/1/2 at `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:313-327` are matched by the explicit shifts at `compile_shaders.cmake:130-132`; breaking that needs dxc to change the meaning of three documented flags. And CI cannot reach it either way — `ci.yml:90` sets `skip_tests: '-E RenderPixelTests'` and `ci.yml:48-56` explains why (no device, and Vulkan has no in-box software fallback). A layout mismatch is a runtime fault this job never executes, so the SDK version changes nothing about what CI catches.

6. FAILURE (c) IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE FIX. A 404 or partial transfer is an sdk.lunarg.com availability matter; a versioned URL is the same host with the same absence of a checksum, so pinning buys no byte integrity. It also inverts the risk: `latest` self-heals after a rollover, where a pinned version that LunarG withdraws 404s permanently.

7. FAILURE (a) IS A LOUD RED ON THE INSTALL STEP. The 1.3.216 NSIS→Qt-IFW flag change is real history, but that failure mode is one job going red at `ci.yml:135-136` with the installer's own message in the log — the "fail at build, not at run" preference `compile_shaders.cmake:7` cites T5 for. A maintenance event, not a defect in the tree.

8. The bisect argument is true and true of the whole workflow through windows-latest, vswhere `-latest`, fxc and the vcpkg tool. Nothing here claims a hermetic build; T9 (`PHILOSOPHY.md:150-156`) puts the graphics API on the bought side deliberately. Singling out the one line where the floatiness happens to be spelled as a literal URL, while four other floating inputs feed the same job, is aesthetics.

*Correction:* One grain is real and does not rescue the finding: the argument list at ci.yml:135-136 is genuinely coupled to a silent-install contract the tree does not own, and that contract did change once (1.3.216). Worth a sentence in the ci.yml:58-65 comment noting the flags belong to the Qt Installer Framework, if anyone is editing that block anyway. It is not worth a version pin, because the pin costs the ci.yml:6-7 contract — CI would stop building against the SDK README.md:68 sends a contributor to fetch — and buys no integrity without a checksum. If a future round genuinely wants reproducible CI toolchains, the finding to raise is the whole set (windows-latest at ci.yml:27, vswhere -latest at ci.yml:141, the unconstrained fxc at compile_shaders.cmake:30-34, the @v4 tags), argued once against a stated policy, not this one URL in isolation.

### R4. compile_shaders.cmake's file header argues from "on the PATH of every environment that can build this project at all" and lists two bytecode consumers — the same commit made both false

**`cmake/compile_shaders.cmake:10`** · should-fix · `build` · raised by R105 · run id `V69`

CLAIM: 4d91b91 added a second function to cmake/compile_shaders.cmake without amending the file header that now governs both, and the header makes two statements the new function contradicts from inside the same file.

EVIDENCE. cmake/compile_shaders.cmake:9-18, unchanged by this commit:

```
    # WHY NOT CHECKED-IN BYTECODE. A generated artifact in the tree is a file that
    # can disagree with its source and nothing notices. fxc is in every Windows SDK
    # and on the PATH of every environment that can build this project at all,
    # which is the same bet the repository already makes on cl.exe.
    #
    # WHAT COMES OUT is a C header holding a byte array, which the backend includes
    # and hands to whatever its API wants bytecode in - CreateVertexShader on D3D11,
    # a field of D3D12_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_STATE_DESC on D3D12, which has no such
    # call.
```

Ninety lines below, in the same file: "IT IS LOOKED FOR IN THE VULKAN SDK AND NOWHERE ELSE ... A find_program that searched / PATH would pick that one" (76-89) and the FATAL_ERROR at 107-115, "Install the Vulkan SDK (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/) so that VULKAN_SDK is set." CLAUDE.md agrees against the header: the Vulkan SDK "is the only thing in this repository that has to be installed", and ci.yml:58 calls this "THE ONE PRESET THAT INSTALLS SOMETHING".
On the second claim, engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:74-79: "COPIED INTO uint32_t RATHER THAN CAST TO IT. The generated header / declares an unsigned char array, whose alignment is one, and / VkShaderModuleCreateInfo::pCode is a const uint32_t* the loader may / read as words." The third API cannot be handed the byte array at all.

RULE. DRIFT.md's standard (a comment the code does not match is a defect) plus CLAUDE.md's amendment rule: a document "changes by amendment in the same commit as the change that fights it". This commit fought both paragraphs and amended neither.

FAILURE. A reader or a future backend author takes the header at face value — the shader compiler is on the PATH of every environment that can build this project — and stands up a new build environment (a CI job, a container, a fresh machine) with nothing installed. x64-debug-vulkan then dies at configure on the FATAL_ERROR at line 108, which the file's own opening argument says cannot happen. Separately, a reader writing a sixth backend follows "hands to whatever its API wants bytecode in" and casts the unsigned-char array to the word pointer its API wants, reproducing exactly the alignment reliance vulkan/renderer.cpp:74-79 exists to remove.

FIX. Amend both header paragraphs: say the bet is per compiler — fxc and cl.exe come with the toolchain, the SPIR-V dxc is installed and the build says so by name — and extend the consumer list to the third API, noting it is the one that cannot be handed the array directly.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

CLAIM 1 — "the same commit made [the PATH statement] false." It did not, because the statement is about fxc and only about fxc. cmake/compile_shaders.cmake:10-12 reads, character for character: "fxc is in every Windows SDK and on the PATH of every environment that can build this project at all, which is the same bet the repository already makes on cl.exe." The subject is `fxc`. Nothing in 4d91b91 changes where fxc is: the x64-debug-vulkan preset still builds through MSVC after vcvars, so fxc is on that environment's PATH exactly as before. The finding's FAILURE paragraph silently rewrites the subject — "the shader compiler is on the PATH of every environment that can build this project at all" — and then refutes the rewrite. The line does not say "the shader compiler"; it names one executable, and that sentence is true at HEAD.

Nor is the paragraph's argument left unqualified. Its load-bearing first sentence — "A generated artifact in the tree is a file that can disagree with its source and nothing notices" (compile_shaders.cmake:9-10) — applies verbatim to SPIR-V, and this commit restated it for the Vulkan case in engine/render/sprite.hlsl:8-11 ("A second copy of this file under d3d12/ or vulkan/ would be a generated artifact by another name — a file that can disagree with its source and have nothing notice, which is the failure cmake/compile_shaders.cmake refuses to check bytecode in to avoid"). The availability half is the finding's real target, and the commit wrote the per-compiler distinction the FIX asks for in four places, all in this same commit's diff: engine/CMakeLists.txt:173-183 ("THE ONLY BACKEND WHOSE DEPENDENCY IS NOT ALREADY ON THE MACHINE ... fxc and the two Direct3D libraries come with the Visual Studio install and opengl32 comes with Windows, where this needs the Vulkan SDK ... and — the part that actually cost something — a dxc that can emit SPIR-V"); README.md:68-73, the Prerequisites list, which is where someone standing up a build environment actually looks; .github/workflows/ci.yml:58-65, cited by the finding as evidence *against* the header when it is in fact the amendment ("fxc and the Direct3D libraries come with Visual Studio, opengl32 with Windows — where this one needs the Vulkan SDK twice over"); and CLAUDE.md:33-36 (verified added by this commit: `git show 4d91b91 -- CLAUDE.md` adds "this repository that has to be installed: it needs the [Vulkan SDK]"). "This commit fought both paragraphs and amended neither" is false on the diff.

FAILURE SCENARIO 1 IS UNREACHABLE AS WRITTEN. The chain is "a fresh environment with nothing installed ... x64-debug-vulkan then dies at configure on the FATAL_ERROR at line 108." It cannot get there. engine/CMakeLists.txt:183 is `find_package(Vulkan REQUIRED)` and the first `compile_hlsl_to_spirv` call is engine/CMakeLists.txt:192 — CMake evaluates in order, so an environment with no Vulkan SDK fails at find_package (which the comment at :179-182 says fails "by name rather than at the first missing symbol (T6)") and never reaches compile_shaders.cmake:107. Line 108 fires only in the narrow case where FindVulkan succeeded (so VULKAN_SDK is set) but $VULKAN_SDK/Bin/dxc is absent — not "nothing installed" — and when it fires it names the SDK and the download URL (compile_shaders.cmake:113-114). Nothing here costs a reader hours.

CLAIM 2 — the consumer list. compile_shaders.cmake:14-18 says the output is "a C header holding a byte array, which the backend includes and hands to whatever its API wants bytecode in — CreateVertexShader on D3D11, a field of D3D12_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_STATE_DESC on D3D12, which has no such call." Check each clause against the Vulkan backend: "a C header holding a byte array" is true (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:74-76 states the generated header declares an unsigned char array, and create_shader's parameter at :80-81 is `const unsigned char*`, taking SPRITE_VERTEX_SHADER directly at :357-362, which would not compile otherwise). "which the backend includes" is true (renderer.cpp:15-16). "hands to whatever its API wants bytecode in" — Vulkan wants it in `VkShaderModuleCreateInfo::pCode`, and renderer.cpp:96-97 puts it there. The closing promise, "No file is read at run time and nothing has to be deployed beside the executable," is true on Vulkan too. There is no numeral in the sentence: it does not say "two backends", it gives two instances of a generalisation that already covers the third. Compare the precedent the finding does not cite: e92a982 amended this exact sentence *because the old text was false* — "hands straight to CreateVertexShader" named a call D3D12 does not have — and the amendment generalised it precisely so that a struct field counts. Vulkan is the same shape as the D3D12 instance already listed, so it falsifies nothing.

FAILURE SCENARIO 2 IS SPECULATIVE AND SELF-DEFEATING. "A reader writing a sixth backend ... casts the unsigned-char array to the word pointer its API wants." The header says nothing about casting; the only backend for which alignment matters carries the warning at its own call site (renderer.cpp:73-79), which is where a port author copying a backend reads. CLAUDE.md's "Known-absent, on purpose" also states "A sixth is not planned."

RULES INVOKED DO NOT REACH. docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:1 titles itself "Documentation drift in `engine/render/`" and :8-11 scopes its standard to "The comments in `engine/render/`"; cmake/compile_shaders.cmake is not in engine/render/. CLAUDE.md:190-195 scopes the amendment rule to "`docs/design/`". Both are extensions, and in any case both require a claim the code no longer matches — neither paragraph here contains one.

*Correction:* One sliver of the second half is defensible and nothing more. e92a982's amendment of compile_shaders.cmake:14-18 shows this repository does maintain that consumer list as backends land, so extending it to name `VkShaderModuleCreateInfo::pCode` — and that this is the one API which takes words rather than bytes, so the array is copied rather than pointed at (engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:73-96) — would be consistent with the file's own habit. That is a nicety, not a defect: no sentence in the header is false, and the alignment reason is already written where the code that needs it lives. The first half has no residue at all — the fxc sentence is true at HEAD, and the per-compiler distinction the FIX proposes was written in this same commit at engine/CMakeLists.txt:173-183, README.md:68-73, ci.yml:58-65 and CLAUDE.md:33-36.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

I read the file at HEAD, the commit's diff of it, the file's own history, the prior review that already litigated this exact sentence, and every document the commit amended.

CLAIM 1 — "on the PATH of every environment that can build this project at all" was made false. It was not. `cmake/compile_shaders.cmake:10-12` reads "**fxc** is in every Windows SDK and on the PATH of every environment that can build this project at all, which is the same bet the repository already makes on cl.exe." The subject of that sentence is fxc, a specific program, and it is still true of fxc at HEAD: fxc ships in the Windows SDK, the Windows SDK comes with the VS install, and `README.md:64-66` states the same requirement independently. Nothing in 4d91b91 touched fxc's availability. The finding needs the sentence to be a claim about "the shader compiler" generically; it is a claim about one named executable. That is the whole finding's first half, and it dies on the quotation it is built from.

The commit's diff (`git show 4d91b91 -- cmake/compile_shaders.cmake`) is a pure append at `:59-143` — lines 1-18 untouched — and what it appends is 37 lines of header that state the opposite bet in capitals for the second compiler: `:74-86` "IT IS LOOKED FOR IN THE VULKAN SDK AND NOWHERE ELSE, WHICH IS NOT FUSSINESS", and `:107-115` a FATAL_ERROR that names the SDK, explains the two-dxc trap and gives the URL. The exception is in the same file, sixty lines below the paragraph, attached to the function that introduces it.

The failure scenario is therefore not reachable as written. It requires the reader to hit "the FATAL_ERROR at line 108, which the file's own opening argument says cannot happen" — but the opening argument says nothing whatsoever about dxc, and the error the reader hits is `:113-114` "Install the Vulkan SDK (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/) so that VULKAN_SDK is set." A configure-time error that names its own fix and its own download URL costs a reader nothing. And the reader would have had to get there past `engine/CMakeLists.txt:174-182`, the call site, whose comment opens "THE ONLY BACKEND WHOSE DEPENDENCY IS NOT ALREADY ON THE MACHINE ... fxc and the two Direct3D libraries come with the Visual Studio install and opengl32 comes with Windows, where this needs the Vulkan SDK ... a dxc that can emit SPIR-V"; past `README.md:67-72` (Prerequisites, amended in this commit); past `.github/workflows/ci.yml:58-65`; past `docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md:361-367` (amended in this commit), which ends "SPIR-V at build time means the Vulkan SDK, which `cmake/compile_shaders.cmake` states as the tax it is" — routing the reader to the very paragraph at `:74-115` that states it.

The finding also miscites CLAUDE.md as agreeing against the header. `CLAUDE.md:29-40` has the identical two-part structure the cmake file has: fxc and the D3D backends "come with the Visual Studio install", then "**The Vulkan preset is the one exception to that**". It reproduces the split rather than contradicting it.

CLAIM 2 — the two-item consumer list. `:14-18` reads "hands to whatever its API wants bytecode in - CreateVertexShader on D3D11, a field of D3D12_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_STATE_DESC on D3D12, which has no such call." That wording is not an accident and not a count: `git log -p e92a982 -- cmake/compile_shaders.cmake` shows it was changed from "hands straight to CreateVertexShader" to a general clause plus two illustrations — the applied fix to the D3D12 review's finding C13, whose own recommendation at `docs/review/d3d12/all-findings.md:1719-1723` was "say the byte array goes to whatever that API takes a compiled shader in". Unlike every item in DRIFT.md, which without exception cites a count or an exclusivity the code contradicts ("three translation units", "the only client", "two backends", `DRIFT.md:62` "ten test targets"), this sentence asserts neither. Vulkan is a third instance of a general rule, not a counterexample to it: `vulkan/renderer.cpp:357-362` includes the generated header and hands the bytes to what its API wants bytecode in, `VkShaderModuleCreateInfo::pCode`.

"The third API cannot be handed the byte array at all" over-reads its own evidence. `vulkan/renderer.cpp:72-92` says the array is `unsigned char` and `pCode` is `const uint32_t*`, so it cannot be passed *without a conversion* — a memcpy into `std::vector<uint32_t>` at `:91-92`. That is a statement about pointer types; the cmake sentence makes no statement about pointer types, so it cannot be contradicted by one.

The clause about breaking is a description of what the D3D12 file does with its queue, not a promise made here; and "silent" plainly means a layer that is not reporting — which is exactly what :450-467 and :490-515 prevent by probing for VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation and installing a messenger. The finding redefines "silent" as "non-fatal under ctest" and then charges the file with its own redefinition. The second rule cited is misquoted: CLAUDE.md:183 (and PHILOSOPHY.md:616) say "A new public primitive ships with behavioural tests in the same commit." This commit adds no public primitive — it adds a backend behind an unchanged seam.

(2) THE GAP IS NOT UNDISCLOSED — AND THE FINDING'S OWN FALLBACK FIX IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, TWICE. And the commit message says it twice — "both of which passed every assertion in RenderPixelTests" and "A Vulkan mistake is usually silent, so 'the tests are green' is a weaker statement here than on the Direct3D backends" — and records the verification that was actually done: "Both were confirmed by disabling the fix and watching the error come back."

(3) THE SIBLING COMPARISON OMITS THE SIBLING IN THE SAME SITUATION. The task's method is to check the other backends. `grep -rn "glDebugMessageCallback|KHR_debug|debug_callback|EnableDebugLayer" engine/render/` returns exactly two hits: d3d12/device_resources.cpp:98 and gl/renderer.cpp:871, the latter a comment saying KHR_debug "is not wired up". The GL backend — the third backend, the other one CI cannot rasterise, the other one needing a real driver — installs no debug reporting at all and was accepted. Vulkan's messenger is strictly more than the standing precedent for a non-D3D backend, not less.

(4) THE PROPOSED FIX IS PARTLY BARRED AND WHOLLY CONDITIONAL. "expose the count through engine/render/vulkan/backend.h and CHECK it is zero" from tests/render/ breaches the rule CLAUDE.md states as "Nothing outside that folder includes anything from it" (cmake/check_engine_includes.cmake's second pass; CMakeLists.txt:21 sets ENGINE_DIR=engine, so the script would not catch it — the architectural rule would still be broken). One further overstatement: severity is not "discarded" in the sense that matters to a reader — the layer's own message text, printed verbatim at :136, begins "Validation Error:" or "Validation Warning:". Only the callback's branching is dropped.

*Correction:* What survives is a suggestion, not a defect. It is genuinely true that no automated check exists for either validation-only fix, and adding a branch on VK_DEBUG_UTILS_MESSAGE_SEVERITY_ERROR_BIT_EXT at device_resources.cpp:129 (print, then break or count) would turn a developer-machine `ctest --preset x64-debug-vulkan` into a standing gate on both — worth someone's time, at minor. But it is a new gate the commit never claimed, not a broken one: the comment at :113-122 promises reporting rather than failure, CLAUDE.md:183 governs new public primitives rather than fixes, the coverage limit is stated in the test case (pixel_tests.cpp:1750-1754), in the code (device_resources.cpp:1477-1483), in ci.yml and three times in the commit message, and the closest sibling (gl/) ships with no debug reporting at all. The finding's two fallback remedies were already written before it was raised, and its primary remedy is either architecturally barred (a test including vulkan/backend.h) or conditional on an optional SDK install (device_resources.cpp:450-456).

1. THE PROPOSED TEST WOULD PASS WITH THE VERY LINE IT CLAIMS TO PIN DELETED. Delete `vulkan/renderer.cpp:1216-1219` and read twice: read #2 takes `previous = TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL` (`:1191`), calls `transition_colour(TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL)` which is a no-op, and issues `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer(..., VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, ...)` (`:1206-1208`) against an image genuinely in that layout — legal, no validation error, identical bytes. D3D12 is the same shape with `COPY_SOURCE`. The finding's fix ("CHECK the two buffers are equal") therefore cannot fail on either backend, before or after the mutation it proposes. A test that cannot distinguish the two trees pins nothing.

2. THE RESTORE IS NOT OBSERVABLE AT ALL, so no test could pin it. Within the frame: present transitions from the tracked layout (`vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1546-1548` calls `commands()` then `transition_colour(TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL)`), and `d3d12/renderer.cpp:1154` transitions to PRESENT the same way. Across frames: `begin_frame` calls `abandon_recording` -> `abandon_commands`, which ends with `this->colour_layout_ = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;` (`vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1487`, with the paragraph at `:1466-1486` explaining why), and `open_frame` transitions from whatever that is (`vulkan/renderer.cpp:672-673, 692-693`). D3D12 resets `back_buffer_states_[i]` to PRESENT only on real recreation (`d3d12/device_resources.cpp:326, 449`). So the failure scenario's mutation is behaviour-preserving everywhere — which makes the restore defensive tidiness, not an unpinned invariant. The finding has found a line whose deletion is invisible and called that a missing test.

3. THE COVERAGE CLAIM IS FALSE. The finding says the second read is what "runs the very commands() second-opening branch this case was written for". The case already runs it: `read_back_buffer` ends in `device_resources.execute()` (`vulkan/renderer.cpp:1221`), which sets `this->submitted_ = true` (`device_resources.cpp:1422`); the case's own `harness.renderer().end_frame()` (`pixel_tests.cpp:1767`) reaches `present()`, whose `VkCommandBuffer commands = this->commands();` (`device_resources.cpp:1546`) enters the reopen branch at `device_resources.cpp:1336-1351` with `recording_ == false, submitted_ == true` — exactly the wait-and-pool-reset the case's comment at `:1740-1748` says it was written to walk. Nothing more is uncovered.

4. NEITHER RULE SAYS WHAT THE FINDING NEEDS. (a) CLAUDE.md's "A new public primitive ships with behavioural tests in the same commit" — `read_back_buffer` is not new in 4d91b91 (the commit adds `engine/render/vulkan/`; `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md` already cites `renderer.h`'s `read_back_buffer` paragraph against the tree at `57b65b3`, 2026-08-19). (b) The seam does not promise idempotency at all: `engine/render/renderer.h:445-480` says RGBA/row-major/size, "A BACKEND MAY REFUSE", "BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame()", "NOT A FRAME-PATH CALL" — and nothing whatever about reading twice. The "written promise in two backends" is a backend implementation note about layout hygiene, not a seam term. (c) DRIFT.md's standard is stated in its own preamble at `docs/review/backend-equivalence/DRIFT.md:8-17`: "Each item is a claim that the code no longer matches, with the line that contradicts it" — comment contradicting code, not comment lacking a test. The finding invents the standard it convicts on.

5. THE QUOTED SENTENCE IS NOT FALSE IN CONTEXT. `pixel_tests.cpp:1750-1754` reads in full: "WHAT IT ASSERTS IS THAT THE NEXT FRAME IS ORDINARY, because that is the only observable half. What a present does to the buffer it presented is a backend's business and differs - two of the four discard it - so the statement worth pinning is that the frame after one is clean...". The two halves being weighed are the two halves of the *present* (the presented buffer's fate vs. the next frame), and the next sentence names the other one explicitly. The finding substitutes a different pair of halves — read-once vs. read-twice — and then reports the comment as naming only one of them.

*Correction:* Nothing material survives. The one true observation buried in it is the opposite of what it argues: because both backends compute every transition from tracked state (vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1708-1721, d3d12/renderer.cpp:591-597) and begin_frame forgets the tracking entirely (vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1487), the restore at vulkan/renderer.cpp:1216-1219 and d3d12/renderer.cpp:1322 is defensive rather than load-bearing — its deletion changes no byte anywhere. If anyone wants to act on that, the honest note is on those comments ("a caller that reads twice ... gets what it would have got" is upheld by the state tracking, not by this line), not a test case; a test that cannot fail is worse than none (T6).

The read-back is just another entry point in a design that already reopens after every submit.

By contrast the Vulkan branch exists solely for this caller. device_resources.cpp:1338-1352 gates the wait+vkResetCommandPool on `submitted_`, and device_resources.h:467-476 says why: "ONE CALLER MAKES IT TRUE AND IT IS THE ONE THE SEAM NAMES. read_back_buffer submits mid-frame and waits ... A command buffer allocated from a pool without VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT may only be begun from the INITIAL state, so reopening it after a submit is not a begin: it is a wait and a pool reset first." The pool is created without that bit at device_resources.cpp:697-707. So the asymmetry the comment asserts is exactly the asymmetry in the code.

THE OTHER TWO. D3D11's read_back_buffer copies on the immediate context (renderer.cpp:973-977, `context->CopyResource` then `Map`) — no recording object to reopen. GL's is glReadPixels (renderer.cpp:852). Neither has anything to reacquire.

The comment at :1746-1748 never mentions the state-restoration term, so it cannot mislead anyone about where that term is documented; and it names engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp explicitly for the term it does discuss. A sixth-backend author reads renderer.h:473-480 ("BETWEEN submit() AND end_frame()", which predates this commit — git blame dates that block to "Look at what the renderer drew...") and each backend's read_back_buffer; nothing here diverts them.

If the comment at pixel_tests.cpp:1747 were ever tightened it would be to say "the other three needed no wait and no pool reset" rather than "had nothing to answer", but that is a wording preference, not an argument whose premise is false.

Nothing in the other three has that shape.

The Vulkan backend has already written the D3D12 contrast down itself, at engine/render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1483-1487: "THE D3D12 BACKEND CANNOT HAVE THIS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ONE LINE OF ITS open_frame: it executes the clear immediately... A reading that makes the comment contradict itself fifteen lines apart is not the reading to hold it to. Paragraph 1 defines what "written down" means here: "the sequence the seam explicitly permits - draw, submit, read, present - had never been RUN on any backend", because Harness::end stops at the read. That is a coverage claim and the finding identifies no test that ran it before this one.

The two "PUT BACK WHERE IT WAS" paragraphs (d3d12/renderer.cpp:1317-1321, vulkan/renderer.cpp:1210-1214) are promises about RESOURCE STATE and IMAGE LAYOUT restoration — a different term from the command-recording state this paragraph is about, and one both backends state in the same function.

THE RULE. DRIFT.md:8-10 scopes its standard to "the comments in engine/render/", and :14 gives its criterion: "each item is a claim that the code no longer matches, with the line that contradicts it". The disputed comment is in tests/, and no line contradicts it under its own antecedent.

FAILURE SCENARIO UNREACHABLE. A reader chasing read-then-present resource state opens read_back_buffer, which is where both promises live; a sentence in a test file about who has to reset a command pool does not route anyone away from d3d12/renderer.cpp:1317. The reader is told the command-buffer reopen is Vulkan's alone, which is true.

(Separately checked and not load-bearing here: the VUID the comment cites at :1745 is -00050 "must not be in the recording or pending state", where -00049 "must be in the initial state" when the pool lacks RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT is the exact one for a completed ONE_TIME_SUBMIT buffer. *Correction:* The finding's quoted facts are all accurate — D3D12 does submit mid-frame at renderer.cpp:1323, does reopen via open_frame_list() at :561-572 for the PRESENT barrier at :1154-1155, and the "reads and then presents" sentence at :1317-1321 does predate this commit (3dda092). Only the inference fails. The one residual, well below a finding: "had nothing to answer" is compressed enough that a reader could take it as "no other backend closes and reopens a recorder mid-frame", which is untrue of D3D12. The answer to that is one clause, and the backend already carries it at vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1483-1487; a comment being tighter than it could be is not a false premise.

### R8. vulkan/renderer.cpp's same_viewport is Viewport::operator== copied field for field, in a file that already includes the header declaring it

**`engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:40`** · should-fix · `docs` · raised by R157 · run id `V92`

CLAIM: the file-local `same_viewport` duplicates the engine's own `Viewport::operator==` exactly — six terms, same order, same operator — with no mechanism that would ever catch the two drifting apart.

EVIDENCE, renderer.cpp:37-47:

```
		// Whether two viewports are the same pane. A run cannot span a viewport
		// change, so this is what closes one.
		bool same_viewport(const Viewport& left, const Viewport& right)
		{
			return left.x == right.x && left.y == right.y &&
				left.width == right.width && left.height == right.height &&
				left.minDepth == right.minDepth &&
				left.maxDepth == right.maxDepth;
		}
```

Against engine/render/viewport.cpp:78-86:

```
	bool Viewport::operator==(const Viewport& other) const
	{
		return this->x == other.x && this->y == other.y &&
			this->width == other.width && this->height == other.height &&
			this->minDepth == other.minDepth && this->maxDepth == other.maxDepth;
	}
```

Declared at viewport.h:68; `engine/render/vulkan/backend.h:9` already includes "engine/render/viewport.h". The sole use is renderer.cpp:123, `same_viewport(this->open.viewport, this->viewport)`.

RULE: T4's "Not a licence for: copy-paste in the name of readability — duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale." This is not the class docs/review/backend-equivalence/TEST-GAP.md:14 decided to accept: the duplicates it answers with golden images (the pixels-to-clip constant, the index loop, the HLSL/GLSL transliteration) all decide where a pixel goes and are therefore caught by a byte-compare. A batching predicate is not — two backends can disagree about it and produce identical frames, so no golden image can ever see this copy drift.

FAILURE: somebody gives `Viewport::operator==` a tolerance, or adds a seventh field to `Viewport` (the struct is the engine's, not the backend's). Every backend spelling the comparison `a == b` follows; this file keeps comparing six fields exactly and silently batches across a change the rest of the engine considers a change, drawing every sprite after the first in the merged run with the wrong pane. RenderPixelTests catches it only if a case happens to change the new field mid-list.

FIX: delete `same_viewport` and write `this->open.viewport == this->viewport` at renderer.cpp:123. NOTE for the refuter: the gl backend's `same_viewport` (gl/renderer.cpp:35) is NOT an identical copy — it compares four fields and omits minDepth/maxDepth — so it is a separate decision, and the original finding's suggestion to change both in one edit would alter GL's behaviour.

**Refuter A — read the code.** *refuted*, severity `not-a-finding`

I checked every quoted line character for character, then tried to build the failure scenario from a real entry point. The quotes are accurate; the failure scenario is not reachable, and the mechanism it names is factually false at HEAD.

WHAT THE FINDING GETS RIGHT (all verified):
- `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:40-46` is exactly as quoted: six terms, `x, y, width, height, minDepth, maxDepth`, all `==`, all `&&`.
- `engine/render/viewport.cpp:78-86` is exactly as quoted (the real file breaks the line after each `&&`, but the terms and order are identical). Declared `engine/render/viewport.h:66`.
- Sole use is `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:123`, `same_viewport(this->open.viewport, this->viewport)`.
- The header is in scope — though via `engine/render/vulkan/backend.h:10`, not `:9` (`:9` is `sprite_vertex.h`).
- The NOTE about GL is correct: `engine/render/gl/renderer.cpp:35-39` compares four fields and omits minDepth/maxDepth.
- T4's text is quoted accurately from `docs/design/PHILOSOPHY.md:88-90`.
- The TEST-GAP.md:14 reasoning is sound — a batching predicate is indeed invisible to a byte-compare.

WHY IT DIES — the failure scenario's mechanism is false:
The finding's chain is "Every backend spelling the comparison `a == b` follows; this file keeps comparing six fields exactly." No backend spells it `a == b`. I grepped every `==`/`!=` line in engine/, tests/ and samples/ mentioning viewport. `Viewport::operator==` has exactly ONE caller in the entire repository: `Viewport::operator!=` at `engine/render/viewport.cpp:89` (`return !(*this == other);`). And `operator!=` itself has zero callers. Both comparison operators are dead API.

Following each backend to confirm there is no "rest of the engine" to drift from:
- `engine/render/d3d11/renderer.cpp:278-288` — `set_viewport` calls `RSSetViewports` eagerly after a flush. No viewport comparison exists; no batching predicate.
- `engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp:333-345` — same shape: `this->view_->flush()`, then `RSSetViewports`/`RSSetScissorRects`. No comparison.
- `engine/render/null/renderer.cpp:52` — records only; no comparison.
- `engine/render/gl/renderer.cpp:110` — its own four-field `same_viewport`.
- `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:123` — the six-field one under review.
Even `tests/render/viewport_tests.cpp` — the type's own dedicated test file — never invokes either operator; it checks fields individually with `doctest::Approx` (`:129-130`). `tests/render/viewport_manager_tests.cpp:26-33` hand-rolls a fourth, Approx-based comparison rather than using `operator==`.

So both halves of the claimed failure collapse:
- "somebody gives `Viewport::operator==` a tolerance" — that edit changes the behaviour of zero call sites. Nothing follows it, so Vulkan cannot fall behind it.
- "adds a seventh field to `Viewport`" — `operator==` is hand-written field by field, so the seventh field must be added there manually; and that same edit must already visit `d3d11/renderer.cpp:43` `to_d3d_viewport`, `d3d12/renderer.cpp:44` `to_d3d_viewport`, `vulkan/renderer.cpp:1027-1053` (the pane fill in replay) and `gl/renderer.cpp:35`. It is not a one-line change that silently leaves one file behind. The file that would most visibly disagree is GL, which already ignores minDepth/maxDepth today at HEAD.
There is therefore no state of the tree in which the claimed consequence — "drawing every sprite after the first in the merged run with the wrong pane" — occurs.

AND THE PROPOSED FIX HAS AN UNWEIGHED COST:
`operator==` is declared at `viewport.h:66` and defined out-of-line at `viewport.cpp:78`. `cmake/settings.cmake` sets no `/GL`, and nothing in CMakeLists.txt, cmake/ or CMakePresets.json sets `INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION` or `LTCG` — so it is a cross-TU call in every configuration, release included. `same_viewport` is in an anonymous namespace (`vulkan/renderer.cpp:31-32`) and runs once per sprite inside the batching predicate at `:123`, the hot record path. Swapping it for `==` trades an inlinable six-float compare for a function call per sprite. That is precisely the trade T8 governs (`PHILOSOPHY.md:82-86`, "indirection must pay for itself"), the same reasoning CLAUDE.md cites for `Renderer` not being an abstract base. The fix is not free, and the finding does not mention this.

Finally, what a run may batch across is legitimately a backend's own decision, not the engine's — which is exactly why GL compares four fields, D3D11/D3D12 compare none, and Vulkan compares six. The comment at `vulkan/renderer.cpp:38-39` already states what the function is for.

*Correction:* One true observation survives, but it is not this finding and not about this commit: `Viewport::operator==` and `operator!=` (`viewport.h:66-67`, `viewport.cpp:78-90`) are dead API — the only caller of `==` is `!=` itself at `viewport.cpp:89`, and `!=` has none. That predates 4d91b91 and lives in `engine/render/viewport.*`, not in the Vulkan backend. If anyone wants to raise it, the honest framing is "the type's comparison operators are unexercised and untested", which points at deleting them or testing them — not at rewriting `vulkan/renderer.cpp:123`.

Two smaller corrections to the finding as written: the include is at `vulkan/backend.h:10`, not `:9`; and "no mechanism that would ever catch the two drifting apart" is true but vacuous, since `operator==` is unexercised — there is no behaviour to drift from.

**Refuter B — checked the rule.** *confirmed*, severity `minor`

The duplication is real and exact. `engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:40-46` compares x, y, width, height, minDepth, maxDepth with `==` joined by `&&`; `engine/render/viewport.cpp:78-86` compares the same six fields in the same order with the same operators. Same predicate, character-for-character equivalent. The declaration is visible in that TU: `engine/render/vulkan/backend.h:9` includes "engine/render/viewport.h", where `bool operator==(const Viewport& other) const;` is declared at viewport.h:66; `engine/render/viewport.cpp` is listed at `engine/CMakeLists.txt:61` so it links in every preset. Both operands at the sole call site (renderer.cpp:123) are `Viewport` values — `Run::viewport` at `vulkan/backend.h:136` and `View::viewport` at `:162` — so the proposed one-line fix `this->open.viewport == this->viewport` compiles as written. The six-field form is also semantically required here, not over-strict: replay reads the run's depth range at renderer.cpp:1052-1053 before `vkCmdSetViewport` at :1054. T4 is quoted correctly — PHILOSOPHY.md:88-89 reads "**Not a licence for:** copy-paste in the name of readability — duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale." TEST-GAP.md:14 is quoted correctly, and the finding's distinction is sound: a batching predicate produces identical pixels when two backends disagree about it, so the golden set cannot see this copy.

What does not survive is the failure mechanism. The finding says "Every backend spelling the comparison `a == b` follows; this file keeps comparing six fields exactly". No backend spells it `a == b`. `Viewport::operator==` and `operator!=` have **zero call sites in the entire repository** — a repo-wide grep for Viewport equality across engine/, tests/, samples/ and bench/ returns only their own definition at viewport.cpp:78-89 and declaration at viewport.h:66-67. The only two viewport comparisons that exist are the two file-local helpers: `gl/renderer.cpp:35-39` (four fields, minDepth/maxDepth deliberately omitted) and this one. d3d11 and d3d12 never compare viewports at all — they call `RSSetViewports` eagerly from `DrawList::set_viewport` (`d3d11/renderer.cpp:278-288`, `d3d12/renderer.cpp:333-342`) — and null records a viewport per sprite (`null/renderer.cpp:27`). So there is no "rest of the engine" whose behaviour would change and leave this file behind; the drift scenario requires someone to edit an operator nobody calls and expect it to have propagated. Nor is Viewport::operator== itself covered — tests/render/viewport_tests.cpp asserts only field values and pixel_rect(), never equality.

The class is also already accepted in this seam, and in a worse instance: gl/renderer.cpp:35-39 does not merely duplicate engine equality, it *disagrees* with it — it batches across a depth-range change the engine's operator== considers a difference — and that shipped and survived the backend-equivalence audit. The finding's own note is right that GL is a separate decision, but it means the seventh-field hazard is latent in gl/ today and was not treated as should-fix there.

*Correction:* Two corrections, neither of which removes the finding. (1) The mechanism is wrong. The failure scenario rests on "every backend spelling the comparison `a == b` follows" a change to `Viewport::operator==`. Nothing follows it: `operator==`/`operator!=` have zero call sites repo-wide (only viewport.cpp:78-89 and viewport.h:66-67 mention them), d3d11/d3d12 set the viewport eagerly instead of comparing (d3d11/renderer.cpp:278-288, d3d12/renderer.cpp:333-342), null records one per sprite (null/renderer.cpp:27), and gl uses its own four-field helper. So the accurate statement of the defect is "two independent copies of the same comparison exist, and the engine's own copy is dead code", not "this backend will silently lag the engine". A tolerance added to operator== would in any case be the wrong rule for a batching predicate — batching two viewports that differ by an epsilon replays one of them for both — so vulkan's exact comparison is defensible on its own terms; only the seventh-field case is a genuine hazard, and Viewport mirrors D3D11_VIEWPORT (viewport.h:16-17), which has exactly six. (2) Severity drops to minor. Nothing is wrong at HEAD — the predicate is byte-equivalent to the operator and semantically correct for replay (renderer.cpp:1052-1054) — the propagation story does not hold, the fix is one line, and the same class already ships accepted, in a stronger form, at gl/renderer.cpp:35-39, which actively disagrees with engine equality about the depth range. The fix as written (delete same_viewport, use `==` at renderer.cpp:123) is correct and should keep the existing comment at the call site, since "a run cannot span a viewport change" is the part worth reading.

**Adjudicator** — the two disagreed, so a third read the code. *refuted*

I read every cited line. The quotes are accurate: engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:40-46 compares x, y, width, height, minDepth, maxDepth with == joined by &&, and engine/render/viewport.cpp:78-86 compares the same six in the same order. Sole use is renderer.cpp:123. Two small corrections to the finding: the include is engine/render/vulkan/backend.h:10 (line 9 is sprite_vertex.h), and the declaration is viewport.h:66.

The finding dies on two independent grounds, both checked in the tree.

(1) The propagation mechanism is false. The finding's failure rests on "Every backend spelling the comparison a == b follows". No backend spells it that way. A repo-wide grep across engine/, tests/, samples/ and bench/ finds Viewport::operator== named only at its own definition (viewport.cpp:78) and declaration (viewport.h:66); its only caller is operator!= at viewport.cpp:89, and operator!= has zero callers. There is no std::find/std::count/container comparison over Viewport anywhere. Both operators are dead API, and they predate the commit under review (git log -L 78,90:engine/render/viewport.cpp -> 14fd841, "Move Camera and Viewport into render"). The other backends do not compare viewports at all: d3d11/renderer.cpp:278-290 and d3d12/renderer.cpp:333-345 flush and call RSSetViewports eagerly, null/renderer.cpp:22-40 records a viewport per sprite, and gl/renderer.cpp:35-39 has its own four-field helper. So there is no "rest of the engine" for this file to fall behind, and no tree state producing the claimed consequence.

(2) The predicate is not a copy of engine equality, and the fix points the wrong way. Each backend's same_viewport matches exactly what that backend's replay reads out of Run::viewport. Vulkan's replay sets pane.minDepth/pane.maxDepth from the run (renderer.cpp:1049-1050) before vkCmdSetViewport at :1054, so six terms are required. GL never reads depth at all - grep for minDepth/maxDepth/glDepthRange in gl/renderer.cpp returns nothing, only glViewport at :595, :705, :738 - so its four terms are exactly right there. The agreement with Viewport::operator== is structural (Viewport has six fields; Vulkan's replay reads all six), not copy-paste. Under the finding's own tolerance scenario the proposed fix would introduce the bug rather than prevent it: batching two panes that differ by an epsilon replays one of them for both. Refuter B concedes exactly this ("A tolerance added to operator== would in any case be the wrong rule for a batching predicate") and keeps the finding anyway; that concession is the obituary. A finding whose recommended edit is a net risk transfer, not an improvement, is not a finding.

The cost is small but real and unweighed by the finding: same_viewport is in an anonymous namespace (renderer.cpp:31-32) and inlines; Viewport::operator== is defined out-of-line in viewport.cpp with no LTO anywhere in the build (no INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION, LTCG or /GL in cmake/, CMakeLists.txt or CMakePresets.json; settings.cmake sets only /W4 /WX /permissive- /sdl /fp:precise), so the fix trades an inlined six-float compare for a cross-TU call per sprite in the record path - the trade T8 governs.

What survives is true and is neither this finding nor this commit: Viewport::operator== and operator!= (viewport.h:66-67, viewport.cpp:78-90) are unexercised dead API, never invoked even by their own test file - tests/render/viewport_tests.cpp:129-131 checks fields with doctest::Approx, and tests/render/viewport_manager_tests.cpp:29-32 hand-rolls a fourth Approx-based comparison. That points at deleting or testing them in engine/render/viewport.*, not at rewriting vulkan/renderer.cpp:123.
